## 1. Summary

194 findings survived deduplication and went through 3-lens adversarial verification: **174 confirmed**, 15 plausible, 5 refuted.

| Final severity | Confirmed | Plausible |
|---|---|---|
| critical | 11 | 0 |
| high | 41 | 0 |
| medium | 55 | 2 |
| low | 67 | 13 |

**Confirmed critical findings:**

- [R-027](#r-027) Poly->Mono switch promotes a RELEASED note into the mono note stack and re-gates voice 0: stuck note (`plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:1833-1889`)
- [R-028](#r-028) Arp chord slide glides ONE voice N times: the other chord voices never get a note-off (stuck notes) (`plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:1760-1780`)
- [R-029](#r-029) Changing Arp operating mode with notes held or sounding leaves engine voices stuck (and a test enshrines it) (`plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_midi.cpp:158-194`)
- [R-054](#r-054) Delay and reverb go permanently silent after any engine reset (setActive, host preset load) while they are enabled (`plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:243-247, 305-330`)
- [R-064](#r-064) Switching the arp to Off never drains its note-offs: the last arp notes hang in the engine and on the MIDI output (`plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:289-293, 416-434`)
- [R-079](#r-079) FX-tab modulation-type and flanger/chorus group pointers are never nulled on a MainTab switch: dangling setVisible on every later preset load (`plugins/ruinae/src/controller/controller_settings.cpp:50-57`)
- [R-080](#r-080) Toggling Distortion General/Type-specific destroys Dist_Spectral without nulling spectralCurveDropdown_/spectralBitsGroup_ (use-after-free) (`plugins/ruinae/src/controller/controller_view_sync.cpp:59-85, 487-500, 897-912`)
- [R-114](#r-114) ArpIntegration_DisableWhilePlaying_NoStuckNotes is vacuous: it disables the arp after the last gate already closed, hiding a real stuck-note bug (`plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/processor/arp_integration_test.cpp:668-721`)
- [R-134](#r-134) Reverb type change never completes at normal block sizes: processor re-arms the 30 ms crossfade every block (`plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:655 (with plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:689-701, 1137-1145)`)
- [R-147](#r-147) Corrupt or extreme state value for OSC PhaseMod hangs the audio thread forever (unbounded wrapPhase loop) (`plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/osc_params.h:750-751`)
- [R-193](#r-193) Measured (ASan): a ModSourceViewMode switch leaves the ten LFO/Chaos/S&H/Random rate and note-value group pointers dangling, so sync automation and any preset load read freed memory (confirms R-129) (`plugins/ruinae/src/controller/controller_view_sync.cpp:82-84`)

### lints

I ran all 13 lints in sequence with each output in its own log. The 12 repo lints exited 0 with one-line OK output. These were lint-odr (984 definitions scanned, no cross-file name collisions, so the Krate::DSP engine headers are clean), lint-layers, lint-apple-globals, lint-finite-bitmask, lint-nonfinite-symbols, lint-musical-time-truncation, lint-unordered-serialization, lint-allocation-probes, lint-midi-timing-goldens, lint-float-bit-goldens, lint-plugin-editor-baseline and lint-wallclock-tags. I did not open the one-line logs of the other ten, so I'm relying on their exit codes. `uidesc-inventory.js plugins/ruinae/resources/editor.uidesc --check` exited 1 with the verdict `UIDESC DEFECTS {"overlap":38,"out-of-bounds":26}`. ### build

Ran `cmake --build build/windows-x64-release --config Release --target ruinae_tests Ruinae -- -m:2 /nr:false`. Exit code 0, wall clock about 56 s. The build recompiled the Ruinae processor TUs, including processor_state.cpp, and linked ruinae_tests.exe and Ruinae.vst3. Searching the log case-insensitively for "warning" and "error" found nothing, so there were zero compiler warnings and zero errors. The post-build install copied the bundle to the user VST3 folder without error. I did not run the tests, because this step only builds. Outputs are build/windows-x64-release/bin/Release/ruinae_tests.exe and build/windows-x64-release/VST3/Release/Ruinae.vst3.

### pluginval

Ran tools/pluginval.exe --strictness-level 5 --validate on build/windows-x64-release/VST3/Release/Ruinae.vst3. The run took about 3.3 s and exited with code 0, which is a pass. The log shows no FAIL or error blocks, and the last test completed was "Restoring default layout".

### probes

I built a temporary probe file (82 hidden [audit-probe] cases) against the real Ruinae::Processor and ran it sharded at --share 4 (7 workers). The main run took 46 s and a follow-up isolation pass took 10.6 s. The build had zero compiler warnings at -m:2. The run produced 1827 PROBE lines: 1658 ok, 54 suspicious, 115 bad. All of them are in f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/probe-results.txt. The measurements below cover every non-ok line, grouped by cause, plus one summary entry per ok group. The probe file is kept at specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp. The plugins/ruinae tree is clean.

Confirmed defects (measured, then traced in code):
(1) HANG: a 2000-byte garbage state with a valid version-8 header spun one core for more than 9 minutes on the first process() after a note-on. I isolated it to OSC B PhaseMod (param 212). loadOscParams stores the raw float unclamped (osc_params.h:751-752). The oscillator's PM guard only rejects NaN/Inf (polyblep_oscillator.h:203-206), and wrapPhase is a subtract-1.0 loop (phase_utils.h:74-82). The reproduction file is f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/garbage2.bin.
(2) Pitch bend smoothing is advanced once per block. The 5 ms smoother takes 148 ms to reach 90% of the bend at block 64, 1166 ms at block 512, 4665 ms at block 2048, and only gets to +81 of +200 cents 1 s after the event at block 2048 (note_processor.h:60 and :103-104, ruinae_engine.h:841-842).
(3) Switching the arp operating mode to Off mid-note leaves the sounding arp note stuck. One voice is still active 1.5 s later and the MIDI out has one note-on with no note-off. setEnabled(false) queues the note-offs (processor_params.cpp:1138-1139), but arpCore_.processBlock is skipped when the mode is Off (processor.cpp:289-293), so they never drain.
(4) Every non-spectral delay's wet path arrives 6144 samples (128 ms at 48k) late, while the dry path is unshifted and the plugin reports 0 latency. The compensation delay sits on the wet path (ruinae_effects_chain.h:146-150, :955-958, :1209-1220).
(5) The Formant oscillator clamps pitch at 2000 Hz: C7 is 78.7 cents flat (formant_oscillator.h:195, :273).
(6) The SpectralFreeze oscillator is out of tune by -110 to +122 cents. A4 measures exactly -72.85 cents, which is the 1024-point bin centre 421.9 Hz (oscillator_adapters.h:136, :423-466; spectral_freeze_oscillator.h:451-459).
(7) Output depends on host block size for all five delay types and the Hall reverb, even at multiples of 64. It also depends on block size for pitch bend, for mod at blocks smaller than 64, and for mono portamento. The cause in the effects chain is not isolated.
(8) A filter type change mid-note clicks (jump ratio 3.55); setFilterType has no crossfade (ruinae_voice.h:748-763).

Suspicious, cause not found:
- The Spectral delay outputs exactly 0 for a 25 ms blip at feedback 0, while held notes pass.
- The Tape delay hiss alone gives -98 dBFS RMS with no note ever played (tape_delay.h:686-705).
- At feedback 1.2, every delay type still sounds at -1 to -27 dBFS 30 s after release.
- Distortion level changes range from -22 to +18.7 dB against Clean.
- The Comb filter at maximum resonance peaks at +22 dBFS.
- Single voices go over 0 dBFS at velocity 0.8 with the limiter off (Additive +5.3, Particle +4.9).

Clean results:
- Sample accuracy: +1 sample for every offset, with or without effects.
- The arp: all 10 modes balanced, 0 samples of drift over 8 bars, and transport stop, host loop and release all clean.
- MPE tuning and portamento are correct.
- Envelopes, pitch and level agree across 44.1k-192k.
- No NaN anywhere.
- All 168 presets are audible, at or below 0 dBFS, and round-trip. One preset is non-deterministic and within 0.98 dB RMS. For Polymeter_Pulse the saved bytes differ from the loaded bytes.
- No self-noise from any effect except the Tape delay.

The prior findings F001-F042 cover none of these issues.

## 4. Findings by final severity

## 4.1 Confirmed critical (11)

### R-027

**Poly->Mono switch promotes a RELEASED note into the mono note stack and re-gates voice 0: stuck note**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** critical · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:1833-1889`
- **Also flagged by:** gestalt-engine

**Problem.** switchPolyToMono picks the most recent voice with voices_[i].isActive(). isActive() is ampEnv_.isActive() (stage != Idle), so it includes voices in Release whose key is already up. When that voice is not slot 0, it calls voices_[0].noteOn(freq, 0.8f), which gates the envelopes ON for a key nobody is holding. In every case it calls monoHandler_.noteOn(voiceNote, 100), which pushes the released pitch onto the mono note stack as if it were held. No note-off will ever remove it. The other active voices (1..N) get noteOff() but processBlockMono renders only voices_[0], so their releases freeze mid-tail.

**Why it is wrong.** A mode switch must not create a held note out of a released one. Only a voice whose allocator state is Active (key down) may survive into the mono stack. The FR-011 intent is that the most recent HELD note survives.

**Consequence.** Play a chord, let go, and switch Voice Mode to Mono while the release tails ring. Case 1, the newest voice is not slot 0: voice 0 is re-gated at velocity 0.8 and sustains forever with no key held. Case 0, the newest voice is slot 0: the phantom stack entry makes every later mono note-off take the 'returning to held note' branch (dispatchMonoNoteOff:1822-1826), so voice 0 is never released. In both cases the note is stuck until the user presses and releases that exact pitch. The frozen voices 1..N are cut abruptly (a click) and resume as ghost tails on the switch back to Poly.

**Suggested fix.** In switchPolyToMono, choose the survivor only among slots whose allocator_.getVoiceState(i) == VoiceState::Active. Push every Active slot's note into the MonoHandler in timestamp order, so the other held keys survive too. If no slot is Active, transfer nothing and let voice 0 finish its release; do not re-gate it. Fade or render the non-surviving voices to Idle instead of freezing them. Test: in RuinaeEngine, call noteOn(60) and noteOn(64), then noteOff(64), noteOff(60), setMode(Mono), and render 2 s. Expect silence (rms &lt; 1e-4) after the release time. A second case holds 60, plays and releases 64, switches, releases 60, and expects silence.

**Evidence.** ruinae_engine.h:1839-1843 `if (voices_[i].isActive() && noteOnTimestamps_[i] > maxTimestamp)` (no allocator-state check); :1873-1875 `voices_[0].noteOn(freq, 0.8f);`; :1880-1883 `monoHandler_.reset(); monoHandler_.noteOn(voiceNote, 100);`; voice isActive = ampEnv_.isActive() (ruinae_voice.h:335-337), adsr isActive = stage_ != Idle (adsr_envelope.h:266); dispatchMonoNoteOff :1818-1826 only releases when the stack is empty; processBlockMono renders voices_[0] only (:2093-2125). The test (ruinae_engine_test.cpp:533-543) checks only getActiveVoiceCount() &lt;= 1.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I confirmed the defect from source.

1. The survivor search counts released voices. ruinae_engine.h:1839-1844 picks the newest voice with `voices_[i].isActive()`. That is `ampEnv_.isActive()` (ruinae_voice.h:335-337), which stays true through the Release stage. The search never asks the allocator whether the key is still held.

2. Case 1, the newest voice is not slot 0. Lines 1867-1876 call noteOff() on every active voice, then `voices_[0].noteOn(freq, 0.8f)`. That gates voice 0's envelopes on again for a key nobody is holding. In every case where voiceNote >= 0, lines 1880-1884 call `monoHandler_.reset(); monoHandler_.noteOn(voiceNote, 100)`, which pushes that pitch onto the MonoHandler stack (mono_handler.h:148-183, addToStack). No note-off arrives for it, so voice 0 holds at its sustain level until the user plays that exact pitch: pressing it makes removeFromStack + addToStack replace the entry, and releasing it empties the stack.

3. Case 0, the newest voice is slot 0. Voice 0 is not re-gated, so its tail finishes, but the phantom entry stays on the stack. The next mono note-on is a legato push (hadNotesHeld is true). Its note-off then finds the stack non-empty (mono_handler.h:250-263), so dispatchMonoNoteOff (ruinae_engine.h:1815-1826) takes the "returning to a held note" branch and only calls setFrequency. voices_[0].noteOff() is never called, so the note is stuck at the phantom pitch.

4. Nothing in the processor clears notes on a mode change. The only caller is processor_params.cpp:271-272, which calls `engine_.setMode(...)` with no all-notes-off around it. setMode (ruinae_engine.h:385-395) returns early only when the mode is unchanged.

5. The other voices freeze. processBlockMono (ruinae_engine.h:2043-2126) renders only voices_[0]. Voices 1..N, released at lines 1860-1871, are never rendered while in Mono. Their tails stop dead and pick up again after switchMonoToPoly (1891-1897), which leaves the voices untouched.

Every step of the claimed call path matches the code. Severity: a stuck note caused by a common UI action (switching Voice Mode while release tails ring), so "critical" or "high" is defensible; I left it unchanged.

**Note 2.** The defect is confirmed from source. I found no guard, clamp, reset or design note that prevents it.

The survivor is picked without checking whether its key is held.
- ruinae_engine.h:1839-1845 chooses the survivor by `voices_[i].isActive() && noteOnTimestamps_[i] > maxTimestamp`.
- RuinaeVoice::isActive() returns `ampEnv_.isActive()` (ruinae_voice.h:335-337), so a voice in its Release stage still qualifies.
- The allocator keeps the note while a slot is Releasing. Only voiceFinished (voice_allocator.h:293-297) and reset clear it. So `allocator_.getVoiceNote(mostRecentVoice)` at :1856 returns the released pitch (>= 0).
- The function never consults `allocator_.getVoiceState(i)` (voice_allocator.h:424).

Case: survivor is not slot 0. Every active voice gets noteOff() at :1867-1871. Then `voices_[0].noteOn(freq, 0.8f)` at :1872-1876 re-gates voice 0 for a key nobody holds.

Both cases: `monoHandler_.reset(); monoHandler_.noteOn(voiceNote, 100)` at :1880-1885 puts the released pitch on the mono stack. That pitch's note-off already happened in poly mode, so nothing will ever remove it.

Why this sticks in each case:
- Slot 0 survives: voice 0 finishes its release, but the phantom stack entry stays. The next mono note-on retriggers voice 0. Its note-off finds the stack non-empty and takes the "Returning to a held note" branch (:1822-1826, setFrequency only), so voice 0 never releases.
- Slot 0 is re-gated: voice 0 sustains until that exact pitch is pressed and released.

The secondary claim also holds. processBlockMono renders only voices_[0] (:2093-2125). Voices 1..N, which were just sent noteOff, are frozen mid-tail. allocator_.reset() at :1887 forgets them. They resume when Poly mode renders all voices again.

No upstream guard exists:
- setMode (:385-395) calls switchPolyToMono directly.
- The processor calls `engine_.setMode(...)` from the voiceMode atomic (processor_params.cpp:271-272) with no all-notes-off or release beforehand.

The doc comment at :381-383 ("most recent voice survives at index 0") states the intent for a sounding voice. It does not justify turning a released note into a held one.

The only test (ruinae_engine_test.cpp:533-543) holds all three keys down when it switches, and asserts only `getActiveVoiceCount() <= 1`. No test covers a switch during release tails.

The trigger is ordinary user behaviour: change Voice Mode while release tails ring. The result is a sustained stuck note, so critical severity stands.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. The survivor search at ruinae_engine.h:1839-1845 tests only `voices_[i].isActive()`. That is `ampEnv_.isActive()` (ruinae_voice.h:335-337), so a voice in its Release stage still counts. The allocator keeps a released voice's note until voiceFinished (voice_allocator.h:258-280 moves Active to Releasing and keeps the note; :288-302 clears it to -1 only when the voice finishes). So `getVoiceNote(mostRecentVoice)` at :1856 returns the released pitch.

**Case 1 (newest voice is not slot 0).** Every active voice is sent noteOff (:1867-1871), then `voices_[0].noteOn(freq, 0.8f)` (:1875) re-gates voice 0. This is the ordinary result of a released 3-note chord: slots 0, 1 and 2 are in use, so the newest is slot 2. In both cases :1880-1884 then pushes the released pitch onto the MonoHandler stack. After that, voice 0 is released only when dispatchMonoNoteOff sees an empty stack (:1815-1821). A note-off for any other pitch takes the 'returning to held note' branch, because MonoHandler::noteOff (mono_handler.h:224-264) returns isNoteOn=true while the stack is not empty. The result is a held drone (with sustain > 0) and no key down.

**Case 0 (newest voice is slot 0).** Voice 0 is not re-gated, so its release finishes. The next mono note-on sees `hadNotesHeld = true` (mono_handler.h:165-192). With legato on it does not retrigger, so the first note is silent because dispatchMonoNoteOn only calls setFrequency (:1808-1809). Releasing that note returns to the phantom pitch, and voice 0 sustains forever.

**What clears it.** monoHandler_ is reset in only four places: engine reset (:196, reached from setActive at processor.cpp:206 and from preset load at processor_state.cpp:364), the two resets inside switchPolyToMono, and switchMonoToPoly (:1892). No processor*.cpp handles All-Notes-Off / CC123 (grep found nothing). So the note stays stuck until the user presses and releases that exact pitch, switches back to Poly, loads a preset, or the plugin is reactivated.

**Frozen voices 1..N.** processBlockMono renders only voices_[0] (:2093-2125), so voices 1..N stay isActive and are never processed. Their tails are cut off at the switch and resume when switching back to Poly.

**Trigger.** The Voice Mode change goes through engine_.setMode from applyVoiceAndOscParams (processor_params.cpp:271), so a UI click or host automation while release tails ring is enough. The existing test (ruinae_engine_test.cpp:533+) uses held notes only, so it does not catch this.

**Severity.** It needs a mode switch during release tails, but the result is an indefinitely sustained note with no key held. With sustain = 0 it is a silent CPU leak instead. Critical/high stands; no change.

</details>

### R-028

**Arp chord slide glides ONE voice N times: the other chord voices never get a note-off (stuck notes)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** critical · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:1760-1780`

**Problem.** On a Slide step with more than one note (chord lane), ArpeggiatorCore cancels the pending note-offs of the currently sounding chord, sends NO note-offs for them, and sends one legato NoteOn per new chord note. It then replaces currentArpNotes_ with the new notes. Each legato NoteOn reaches dispatchPolyLegatoNoteOn. That function glides the single voice with the highest noteOnTimestamps_ and gives that voice ++timestampCounter_. The second, third and later legato notes therefore find the SAME voice (it is now the newest). They re-glide it and rename its allocator note with setVoiceNote each time. The other voices of the previous chord keep their gates on with their old allocator notes. The arp has forgotten those pitches and will never send them a note-off. The same happens on a chord-to-single-note slide.

**Why it is wrong.** A legato hand-off must map N old notes to N voices, or release whatever it does not glide. The arp's contract (slide = no note-off, the engine re-pitches the sounding notes) only holds if the engine transfers every sounding arp voice. Every arp NoteOn must reach a matching note-off on the engine side.

**Consequence.** In Poly mode (chord lane is enabled in Poly), any pattern that puts Slide on a chord step leaves the previous chord's other voices droning indefinitely. They stop only when the allocator steals them or the same pitch is replayed. Only the last note of the new chord sounds (as a glide); the other new chord notes are never heard.

**Suggested fix.** Make poly legato chord-aware. Collect the gated voices that the arp is sounding (allocator state Active, sorted by timestamp) at the start of a run of legato NoteOns at the same offset. Glide them one-to-one onto the new notes. Release any surplus old voices and allocate fresh voices for any surplus new notes. At minimum, skip voices already re-targeted at this offset, and release the voices that were not re-targeted. Test: an arp processor test with the chord lane at 3 notes and the modifier lane Slide on step 2. Run two steps, stop the arp's input (all keys off, latch off) and render 3 s. Expect silence, and expect the count of engine voices with an active gate to equal the chord size during step 2.

**Evidence.** arpeggiator_core.cpp:1123-1144 `cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes(); // Do NOT emit noteOffs for currently sounding notes ... for (i < result.count) outputEvents[..] = {NoteOn, ... .legato = true}; ... currentArpNotes_[i] = result.notes[i]`; processor_midi.cpp:100-101 ArpNoteOn -> `engine_.noteOn(event.pitch, event.velocity, event.legato)`; ruinae_engine.h:1764-1775 picks max-timestamp active voice, `glideToFrequency(freq); allocator_.setVoiceNote(bestVoice, note); noteOnTimestamps_[bestVoice] = ++timestampCounter_;`. No test drives a legato chord through the engine (grep 'legato' in plugins/ruinae/tests: only ArpIntegration_SlidePassesLegatoToEngine, a single note, audio-present check).

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Confirmed from source. Arp side: dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:1123-1144. On a Slide step with result.count > 1 it calls cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes() (arpeggiator_core.h:1499-1513 removes the pending offs for every note in currentArpNotes_) and emits no NoteOff for the sounding chord. It then emits one ArpEvent NoteOn per new chord note with .legato = true and overwrites currentArpNotes_/currentArpNoteCount_ with the new notes, so the arp no longer tracks the old pitches. It schedules gate offs only for the new notes (1163-1168). Processor side: processor.cpp:342-346 queues each event as an ArpNoteOn carrying .legato = evt.legato, and processor_midi.cpp:100-101 calls engine_.noteOn(pitch, vel, legato). Engine side: ruinae_engine.h:229-232 sends a legato note-on in Poly mode to dispatchPolyLegatoNoteOn. At 1760-1775 that function picks the single isActive() voice with the largest noteOnTimestamps_, glides it, renames it with allocator_.setVoiceNote (voice_allocator.h:415-418, which only stores the note), and stamps it with ++timestampCounter_. The second and third legato notes therefore pick that same newest voice again and re-glide/rename it. The other voices of the old chord keep their gates and their old allocator notes. Later ArpNoteOffs for the new notes (processor_midi.cpp:103-104 -> dispatchPolyNoteOff, ruinae_engine.h:1782-1789) match only the one renamed voice, and only for its final note. The other new-chord notes never got a voice, and nothing ever sends a note-off for the old pitches. The processor has no allNotesOff/panic path: the only engine_.reset() is at processor.cpp:206, the lifecycle path. So the leftover voices stay gated until they are stolen or the same pitch is replayed. A chord-to-single slide leaves the same orphans. The defect is real as described, and critical severity fits a stuck-note bug.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source, and nothing upstream or downstream guards it.

1) Arp side. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:1123-1144, the Slide path with ratchet 1 and result.count > 1, calls cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes() (arpeggiator_core.h:1499-1513 removes the pending offs for every currentArpNotes_ entry). It emits no NoteOff for the old chord, emits one NoteOn with .legato=true per new chord note, then overwrites currentArpNotes_[0..count) and currentArpNoteCount_ with the new notes. After that the arp no longer tracks the old pitches and will never release them.

The chord count is reachable in Ruinae through ArpMode::Chord or the chord lane (arpeggiator_core.cpp:498, :861-877). The ratchet Slide path (:1047-1089) also emits legato chord NoteOns. It appends to currentArpNotes_, so the old pitches stay tracked there, but the voices carrying them were renamed (see 2), so they still do not match.

2) Engine side. processor_midi.cpp:100-101 sends ArpNoteOn to engine_.noteOn(pitch, vel, legato). ruinae_engine.h:229-232 routes Poly + legato to dispatchPolyLegatoNoteOn. At ruinae_engine.h:1760-1779 that function picks the single active voice with the highest noteOnTimestamps_, calls glideToFrequency, then allocator_.setVoiceNote(bestVoice, note), which at voice_allocator.h:415-419 only renames the voice's note. It then sets noteOnTimestamps_[bestVoice] = ++timestampCounter_, so that voice becomes the newest. The 2nd through Nth legato NoteOns of the same chord therefore pick the same voice again and re-glide it. The other voices of the old chord keep their gates and old allocator notes. dispatchPolyNoteOff (:1782-1790) only releases voices by allocator note, so a later arp NoteOff for a new note never reaches them.

The design intent says the opposite: archived spec 073 FR-015 (specs/_archive2_/073-per-step-mods/spec.md:169) requires "each voice glides from the previous pitch to the new pitch". The engine does not do that, so this is not a documented trade-off.

No test covers it. A grep of plugins/ruinae for chord+slide or PolyLegato finds only the implementation and a comment at ruinae_voice.h:314. The arp-core test Slide_ChordMode_AllNotesLegato checks only the legato flags on the events and never drives the engine.

One nuance. If the new chord has exactly the same pitches as the old one (a static triad in Chord mode), the voice that gets glided ends back on its own pitch. The old chord's other voices keep their own matching pitches, and the next NoteOffs release them, so nothing sticks. That case only produces a spurious glide on one voice. Any chord change on a Slide step (the chord lane moving over different arp roots, a pattern that moves the chord, a chord-to-single-note slide) leaves the voices that were not glided gated until a steal or until the same pitch comes back, and only one of the new chord's notes sounds.

Severity stays as filed: it is a real stuck-note path, though it needs Slide on a chord step whose pitches change.

**Note 3.** I traced the whole path and the defect is real.

1. Arp core (dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:1123-1144). On a Slide step with ratchet 1 it calls cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes() (arpeggiator_core.h:1499-1513, which only removes pending offs) and sends no NoteOff for the sounding notes. It sends one NoteOn with legato=true for each new chord note, then overwrites currentArpNotes_[0..count) and sets currentArpNoteCount_ = result.count. The old pitches are forgotten. The previous step kept them sounding: suppressGateNoteOff is set when the next step is a Slide (arpeggiator_core.cpp:1027-1032). Chord -> single works the same way (lines 1145-1157: currentArpNotes_[0] = note, count = 1).

2. Routing (plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:336-346). Each NoteOn is queued as ArpNoteOn carrying .legato. applyTimedEvent (processor_midi.cpp:100-101) calls engine_.noteOn(pitch, vel, legato). In Poly mode, RuinaeEngine::noteOn (ruinae_engine.h:229-232) calls dispatchPolyLegatoNoteOn.

3. Engine (ruinae_engine.h:1760-1776). It picks the active voice with the highest noteOnTimestamps_, glides it, calls allocator_.setVoiceNote(bestVoice, note) (voice_allocator.h:415-419, a plain rename) and stamps it with ++timestampCounter_. The 2nd and 3rd legato NoteOns therefore pick the same voice again. It ends on the last chord note and its allocator note is that last pitch.

Example: old chord C/E/G slides to D/F/A.
- The G voice becomes D, then F, then A.
- The voices still playing C and E keep their gates and their allocator notes C and E.
- The arp later sends NoteOffs only for D, F and A. dispatchPolyNoteOff(D) and (F) find no voice and do nothing. Only A is released.
- C and E have no NoteOff source left. The processor has no engine-level all-notes-off on arp stop or disable: in processor.cpp the only engine_.reset() is at line 206, plus the preset-load reset in processor_state.cpp. They sound until they are stolen, until the same pitch is struck again, or until a reset.
- Only the last new chord note (A) is heard, as a glide. D and F are never heard.

The ratchet>1 slide path (lines 1047-1089) is different: it appends to currentArpNotes_ and keeps the old notes, so it does not leak in the same way. The finding cites the ratchet-1 path, and that path is the one that is wrong.

Impact: the consequence happens as claimed. In Poly mode with arp MIDI dispatch, a chord-lane step of more than one note (or a chord sliding to a single note) on a Slide modifier step leaves (old chord size - 1) voices droning with their gates open after the arp stops. Each such slide leaks more voices, until polyphony fills and steals begin.
- The trigger needs that user configuration. I did not confirm that any factory preset uses Poly + chord + Slide: the generator's slide presets I saw are mono/legato.
- With the MIDI output enabled, the same core behaviour also leaves the old chord pitches stuck on the downstream instrument, because no NoteOff is ever emitted for them.

A stuck note is the highest-impact synth hazard, so I keep the reviewer's severity.

</details>

### R-029

**Changing Arp operating mode with notes held or sounding leaves engine voices stuck (and a test enshrines it)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** critical · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_midi.cpp:158-194`
- **Also flagged by:** voice-management-midi, portability-quality

**Problem.** The processor routes each note-on and note-off by the operating mode at the moment the event arrives, not by where the note-on went. There are three cases. (a) Off/Mod -> MIDI or MIDI+Mod: a key pressed earlier went to the engine as a direct NoteOn. Its release now goes only to arpCore_.noteOff, which never saw the key, so engine_.noteOff is never queued and the voice sustains forever. (b) MIDI -> Off: applyArpParams calls arpCore_.setEnabled(false), which only sets needsDisableNoteOff_. process() skips arpCore_.processBlock whenever the mode is Off, so the cleanup note-offs are never drained, and the engine voices started by ArpNoteOn stay gated. (c) MIDI -> Mod: the core keeps running, but process() drops arp NoteOffs unless the mode dispatches notes, so the sounding arp voices never release.

**Why it is wrong.** Every engine note-on needs a matching note-off whatever parameters change in between. The routing decision must be latched per note, or a mode change must flush the engine (and MIDI out) of the notes the old routing owned. The comment at processor.cpp:294-296 says the disable note-offs are drained, but that code is inside `if (isArpRunning)`.

**Consequence.** A user who switches the arp on, off or between MIDI and Mod while playing gets drones that never stop. Only a preset load or setActive(true) (engine_.reset()) clears them. Automating the arp mode in a DAW does the same on every switch.

**Suggested fix.** Keep a per-pitch record of which sink got the note-on: engine-direct and/or arp. Route the note-off to that sink regardless of the current mode. On any operating-mode change, drain the arp once more (call arpCore_.processBlock with the disable flag even when the new mode is Off) and route its note-offs to the sinks that received the note-ons. Alternatively, release every arp-owned engine voice. Change ArpIntegration_EnableWithExistingHeldNote_NoStuckNotes to require silence after the release, and add MIDI->Off and MIDI->Mod cases with sustain 1.0 that require silence 1 s after the switch.

**Evidence.** processor_midi.cpp:183-193 `const int opMode = arpParams_.operatingMode.load(...); ... if (arpRunning) arpCore_.noteOff(midiPitch); if (!arpDispatchesNotes) queueTimedEvent({... NoteOff ...});`; processor_params.cpp:1139 `arpCore_.setEnabled(arpOpModeParam != kArpOff);`; arpeggiator_core.h:394-396 setEnabled(false) only sets `needsDisableNoteOff_ = true`; processor.cpp:293 `if (isArpRunning) {` wraps the only arpCore_.processBlock call (:330); processor.cpp:361-365 ArpNoteOff queued only `if (isArpDispatchingNotes)`. arp_integration_test.cpp:852-869 releases the direct note after enabling the arp and then `CHECK(audioAfterNoteOff)`, with the comment 'The original engine note should still be sounding ... This is the expected behavior', which enshrines the stuck note.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this finding. The source confirms all three paths.

(a) Off -> MIDI or MIDI+Mod. processor_midi.cpp:183-193 (onNoteOff) and :223-229 (the MPE overload) read the operating mode at the moment the note-off arrives. In MIDI or MIDI+Mod mode, arpDispatchesNotes is true, so the note-off goes only to arpCore_.noteOff(). No engine NoteOff is queued. A note that onNoteOn (:172-176) had sent straight to the engine while the mode was Off therefore never gets an engine note-off. Nothing records which sink received the note-on, and processor_params.cpp has no mode-change handler: grep finds no prevArpOperatingMode or similar variable; only prevArpMode_, prevArpNoteValue_ and the like at :843-978. The test arp_integration_test.cpp:803-870 (ArpIntegration_EnableWithExistingHeldNote_NoStuckNotes) writes this down. Its comments at :849-851 and :866-868 say "no one sent engine_.noteOff(60)", and it then asserts CHECK(audioAfterNoteOff).

(b) MIDI -> Off. processor_params.cpp:1139 calls arpCore_.setEnabled(arpOpModeParam != kArpOff). In arpeggiator_core.h:394-400, setEnabled(false) only sets needsDisableNoteOff_ = true and clears the ratchet counters. The only arpCore_.processBlock call is at processor.cpp:330, inside `if (isArpRunning)` (:293), and isArpRunning = (opMode != kArpOff) (:290). So with the mode Off, the cleanup note-offs are never drained. The comment at :294-296 says they are drained, but the code it sits in cannot run in Off mode. Any arp-issued engine voice still gated at the switch stays gated. The user's own key release then sends a direct engine NoteOff only for the key's own pitch (processor_midi.cpp:191-192). That does not release arp notes at other octaves or other pitches.

(c) MIDI -> Mod. The core keeps running (isArpRunning is true), but processor.cpp:361-365 queues an ArpNoteOff only `if (isArpDispatchingNotes)`, and that is false in Mod mode. Arp voices already started in the engine get no release from the arp. The only release they can get is the same-pitch direct note-off described in (b).

Caveat: ArpIntegration_DisableWhilePlaying_NoStuckNotes (:668-721) expects silence after a disable. I did not run it. It may pass only because the default 80 % gate (arpeggiator_params.h:76) had already closed the arp note before the disable, or because of some engine default. That does not change the code path cited above.

I left the severity unchanged. Stuck drones that only a preset load or setActive clears, triggered by an ordinary mode switch or by automating the mode, justify a high or critical rating.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this. Every path the finding cites is in today's code, and nothing upstream guards it or documents it as intended.

(a) Off/Mod -> MIDI: processor_midi.cpp:183-193 routes onNoteOff by the CURRENT opMode. In MIDI mode it calls only arpCore_.noteOff and never queues TimedEventKind::NoteOff, so a voice started by a direct NoteOn (:172-176, applied as engine_.noteOn at :92-95) gets no engine_.noteOff. The default amp sustain is 0.8 (env_params.h:87, AmpEnvParams(10,100,0.8,200)), so that voice holds for good. arp_integration_test.cpp:852-869 does exactly this sequence and then CHECKs `audioAfterNoteOff`, with the comment "This is the expected behavior". The comment at :850-851 says the note sustains "until the amp envelope naturally releases it", which is false at sustain 0.8. So the test pins the stuck note.

(b) MIDI -> Off: processor_params.cpp:1139 calls arpCore_.setEnabled(false), which only sets needsDisableNoteOff_ (arpeggiator_core.h:394-396). The only arpCore_.processBlock call sits inside `if (isArpRunning)` (processor.cpp:293, call at :330), so the cleanup note-offs are never drained while the mode is Off. The comment at processor.cpp:294-296 says otherwise.

ArpIntegration_DisableWhilePlaying_NoStuckNotes (arp_integration_test.cpp:668-720) passes only because of its timing. The defaults are 120 BPM, a 1/8 step (11025 samples) and an 80 % gate (arpeggiator_params.h:74,76). Step 3 starts at 22050 and its note-off lands at 30870, just before the disable block at about 31232. No arp note is sounding at the switch, so the flush is never exercised.

There is one partial mitigation. Releasing a held key while in Off mode sends engine_.noteOff(pitch), which frees an arp voice only when its pitch equals that key. Octave-shifted or transposed arp notes stay stuck.

(c) MIDI -> Mod: the arp keeps running, but ArpNoteOff is queued only `if (isArpDispatchingNotes)` (processor.cpp:362), so the sounding arp voices never get their note-off.

Nothing documents this as intended. MANUAL.md:950-957 just lists the modes, and the prior findings.json has no matching entry, so this is not a repeat of a fixed F-id. The engine is cleared only by a preset load (processor_state.cpp:364) or by setActive (processor.cpp:206). I keep the severity: any arp mode switch while playing, or automating the mode, leaves drones at the default patch settings.

**Note 3.** I could not refute it. All three paths are confirmed in the source.

(a) Off/Mod -> MIDI or MIDI+Mod: processor_midi.cpp:162-176 sends a note-on directly to the engine (queueTimedEvent NoteOn) when the arp does not dispatch notes. The note-off at :183-193 reads the operating mode at release time. In MIDI or MIDI+Mod it calls only arpCore_.noteOff and queues no engine NoteOff. Nothing records where the note-on went. arp_integration_test.cpp:852-869 releases note 60 after enableArp() and then CHECKs that audio is still present, with the comment "This is the expected behavior". The test enshrines the stuck note.

(b) MIDI -> Off: processor_params.cpp:1139 calls arpCore_.setEnabled(mode != Off). arpeggiator_core.h:394-405 then only sets needsDisableNoteOff_. The only arpCore_.processBlock call is processor.cpp:330, inside `if (isArpRunning)` (:293). That flag is false in Off mode, so the cleanup note-offs and any gate-pending note-offs are never emitted. The comment at :294-296 claims they are drained, which is wrong. The src/processor tree has no allNotesOff, panic or flush fallback (grep found none). ArpIntegration_DisableWhilePlaying_NoStuckNotes passes (I ran it: 2 assertions, all passed), but only by timing. The disable lands at block 61 = sample 31232. At 120 BPM a 1/8 step is 11025 samples with an 80% gate, so the step at 22050 already released at 30870 and the disable falls in the gap between notes. The test never exercises a disable during a sounding note.

(c) MIDI -> Mod: processor.cpp:362 queues ArpNoteOff only `if (isArpDispatchingNotes)`. The core keeps running, but its note-offs for notes started under MIDI are dropped, so those engine voices stay gated.

Impact: with any amp-envelope sustain above 0 the voice drones indefinitely. It clears only on a preset load, setActive(true) (engine_.reset(), processor.cpp:206), a voice steal, or a later engine note-off of the same pitch. Mono mode is no exception. Any user who changes the arp mode while holding keys, or automates the arp mode in a DAW, triggers it.

I am downgrading from critical to high. It is a real, user-reachable stuck note, but there is no crash, no level explosion and no corrupted state. It needs a mode change mid-note, and the user can recover by replaying the pitch or loading a preset.

</details>

### R-054

**Delay and reverb go permanently silent after any engine reset (setActive, host preset load) while they are enabled**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** critical · **Dimension:** effects-chain · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:243-247, 305-330`

**Problem.** RuinaeEffectsChain::reset() forces delayFadeState_/reverbFadeState_ to Off and the alphas to 0, but leaves delayEnabled_/reverbEnabled_ untouched. setDelayEnabled/setReverbEnabled return early when `enabled == delayEnabled_`. The processor re-applies the enable flags every block (processor_params.cpp:557-558), but because the flag already reads true no fade-in is ever started, so processChunk skips the slot (line 840 `if (delayFadeState_ == SlotFadeState::Off)`, line 1077 for reverb) for good. reset() is reached from RuinaeEngine::reset() (ruinae_engine.h:201), which Processor::setActive(true) (processor.cpp:206) and applyPresetSnapshot (processor_state.cpp:364) call. The harmonizer does not have this bug because reset() also clears harmonizerEnabled_ (line 233). git blame puts lines 243-247 and 305-307 in c447b9f5, the F012 remediation (PR #265).

**Why it is wrong.** A reset must leave the chain able to honour the enable flags that are re-applied afterwards. Either the cached enable flags have to be cleared together with the fade state, or the fade state has to be rebuilt from the flags. The F012 fix added the fade state machine but kept the edge-detect guard keyed to a flag that reset() does not clear.

**Consequence.** Two common cases kill the delay and reverb until the user toggles them off and on: a host deactivate/reactivate (sample-rate change, offline bounce, device off/on, some hosts on transport stop) with delay or reverb enabled, and loading a preset through the host (setState) when both the old and the new preset have the delay or reverb on. The patch then plays fully dry. A preset saved in that state still says delay/reverb on.

**Suggested fix.** In reset(), set delayFadeState_ = delayEnabled_ ? On : Off and delayFadeAlpha_ = delayEnabled_ ? 1 : 0 (same for reverb), or set delayEnabled_ = reverbEnabled_ = false so the next setDelayEnabled(true) starts a fade-in. Regression test at processor level: enable the delay and reverb, process, then setActive(false)/setActive(true) (and separately setState of a delay-on preset over a delay-on preset), feed an impulse, and REQUIRE non-zero wet energy at the echo time. Add the same check at chain level: setDelayEnabled(true) -> process -> reset() -> setDelayEnabled(true) -> impulse -> wet > 0.

**Evidence.** ruinae_effects_chain.h:244 `delayFadeState_ = SlotFadeState::Off;` 245 `reverbFadeState_ = SlotFadeState::Off;` (no delayEnabled_/reverbEnabled_ reset; contrast :233 `harmonizerEnabled_ = false;`); :306 `if (enabled == delayEnabled_) return;`; :321 `if (enabled == reverbEnabled_) return;`; ruinae_engine.h:201 `effectsChain_.reset();`; processor.cpp:206 `engine_.reset();` in setActive; processor_state.cpp:364 `engine_.reset();`. MEASURED (clang-cl probe against the chain header plus build/windows-x64-release KrateDSP.lib, probe at the scratchpad fxprobe/probe.cpp): delay wet peak before reset 0.928, after reset + setDelayEnabled(true) 0.000000. Reverb RMS before 0.005460, after 0.000000 (dry passes, 1.000). The only reset test (ruinae_effects_chain_test.cpp:1439) disables delay/reverb right after reset, so it cannot catch this.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The source confirms the defect.

1. ruinae_effects_chain.h:243-247: reset() sets delayFadeState_ and reverbFadeState_ to SlotFadeState::Off and both alphas to 0. It does not touch delayEnabled_ or reverbEnabled_ (declared at :1385-1386). The harmonizer differs: reset() clears its flag at :233 (harmonizerEnabled_ = false).
2. prepare() (:115-199) never touches the enable flags or the fade states either. So the usual host sequence setActive(false) -> setupProcessing (processor.cpp:182 engine_.prepare) -> setActive(true) (processor.cpp:206 engine_.reset()) leaves the flag true and the fade state Off.
3. setDelayEnabled (:305-306) and setReverbEnabled (:320-321) return early when `enabled == delayEnabled_` / `reverbEnabled_`. Re-applying true therefore never starts a FadingIn.
4. The processor re-applies the flags every block: processor.cpp:251 applyParamsToEngine() -> processor_params.cpp:256 applyGlobalFilterAndFxEnableParams() -> :557-558 engine_.setDelayEnabled / setReverbEnabled (ruinae_engine.h:626-627 forwards to the chain). These calls hit the early return.
5. processChunk keys only on the fade state. :840 skips delay processing when the state is Off, the wet mix at :968 is gated the same way, and :1077 skips the whole reverb slot. The state can only leave Off through the two setters, so the delay and reverb stay silent until the user turns them off and on again.
6. The preset path is affected as well. processor_state.cpp:364 calls engine_.reset() inside applyPresetSnapshot, which runs from processor.cpp:236. When the delay or reverb was already on before the load and is on in the new preset, the atomic does not change, so there is no edge and the slot stays dead. applyPresetSnapshot restores only the reverb type (:369 setReverbTypeDirect) and does nothing to the enable or fade state.
7. Test coverage: ruinae_effects_chain_test.cpp:1439 calls chain.reset() and then immediately runs setDelayEnabled(false) and setReverbEnabled(false) (:1442-1443), so it cannot catch this. The other reset test at :150 checks only the delay type.

The one partial mitigation is that the very first activation is unaffected, because delayEnabled_ starts false and the first block produces the edge. Every reactivation after processing with the delay or reverb on fails, and so does every preset load where the slot was on before and stays on. Hosts commonly cycle setActive on sample-rate or device changes, on offline bounce and on project reload. With the patch's delay and reverb silently dead, critical is the right severity.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source and found nothing elsewhere that guards against it.

The chain: ruinae_effects_chain.h:243-247 reset() sets delayFadeState_ and reverbFadeState_ to Off and both alphas to 0. It never touches delayEnabled_ or reverbEnabled_, which are declared at :1385-1386, and those two are written only at :307 and :322. The harmonizer differs: reset() clears harmonizerEnabled_ = false at :233.

setDelayEnabled at :306 and setReverbEnabled at :321 both start with `if (enabled == xEnabled_) return;`, so passing true again after a reset never starts a fade-in. processChunk skips the delay when delayFadeState_ is Off (:840). Reverb is gated by `if (reverbFadeState_ != SlotFadeState::Off)` (:1077). No other code moves the fade states out of Off: the only writes are :244-245, :310/312 and :325/327, plus tickSlotFade.

The callers: ruinae_engine.h:201 calls effectsChain_.reset() inside reset(). Processor::setActive(true) at processor.cpp:206 calls engine_.reset(). applyPresetSnapshot at processor_state.cpp:364 also calls engine_.reset(), and afterwards it re-applies only the reverb type (:369) and the arp sentinels. It does not clear any delay or reverb enable cache. processor_params.cpp:557-558 passes the atomic values straight to engine_.setDelayEnabled/setReverbEnabled (ruinae_engine.h:626-627), with no toggle in between. So once the chain has been enabled, any later reset leaves delayEnabled_ true and the fade state Off for good.

Why it can look correct: on the first activation the flags still hold their initial false, so the first enable works. The bug shows from the second reset on, for example a reactivation or a host setState while the effect is on.

Test coverage: the only reset test that processes audio afterwards, ruinae_effects_chain_test.cpp:1439, calls setDelayEnabled(false)/setReverbEnabled(false) right after reset() (:1442-1443), so it never checks re-enabling. The other reset test (:150) only checks the delay type.

I found no design note, upstream clamp or test that makes this intentional or unreachable. A host deactivate/reactivate and a host preset load are both common. I did not re-run the reviewer's measurement (delay wet 0.928 before the reset, 0.0 after), but it agrees with the code path above. The critical severity stands: the patch silently plays dry and no error is shown.

**Note 3.** The defect is real, and the claimed consequence follows directly from the source.

1. reset() clears the slot fade state but not the cached enable flags. ruinae_effects_chain.h:244-247 sets delayFadeState_ and reverbFadeState_ to Off and both alphas to 0. delayEnabled_ and reverbEnabled_ (members at :1385-1386) are never touched in reset() (:205-264). The harmonizer is handled differently: :233 sets harmonizerEnabled_ = false.

2. The setters only act on a change. setDelayEnabled returns early at :306 (`if (enabled == delayEnabled_) return;`), and setReverbEnabled does the same at :321. Only these setters ever move the fade state to FadingIn (:310, :325).

3. While the fade state is Off, nothing runs. In processChunk, :840 skips all delay processing, :968 skips the delay dry/wet mix, and :1077 skips reverb processing and its mix. The fade state cannot leave Off without a setter call that changes the flag. Since delayEnabled_ still reads true, the slots stay silent until the user toggles the parameter off and on.

4. prepare() does not recover it. :115-199 never touches delayEnabled_, reverbEnabled_ or the fade states. Processor::setupProcessing (processor.cpp:182) therefore cannot undo it either.

5. The reachable paths are confirmed:
   - Processor::setActive(true) calls engine_.reset() (processor.cpp:206). RuinaeEngine::reset() calls effectsChain_.reset() (ruinae_engine.h:201).
   - applyPresetSnapshot calls engine_.reset() unconditionally on every state load (processor_state.cpp:364). Afterwards it re-applies only the reverb type (:369) and the arp sentinels, not the enable flags.
   - processor_params.cpp:557-558 re-applies setDelayEnabled/setReverbEnabled every block from the atomics. If the delay or reverb was already enabled, that call hits the early return, so no fade-in starts.

6. Impact: the first activation after construction works, because both flags start false (:1385-1386), so the first per-block setter call starts a fade-in. Every later case kills the wet path whenever the slot was enabled beforehand:
   - setActive(false) then setActive(true), which hosts do on a sample-rate or buffer change, offline bounce, device restart, and some on transport stop.
   - A preset or state load (host setState or the plugin's own preset browser, both through applyPresetSnapshot) while delay or reverb is on and the new preset also has it on.

   After that the patch plays fully dry: a 100 % loss of the delay and reverb wet signal (the quoted probe measured a delay wet peak of 0.928 before and 0.000 after). The parameter and the UI still show the effect as on, and the effect stays dead until the user toggles it.

Delay and reverb are used by a large share of synth presets, and this triggers on routine host actions without any warning. Critical severity is justified, so no adjustment.

</details>

### R-064

**Switching the arp to Off never drains its note-offs: the last arp notes hang in the engine and on the MIDI output**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** critical · **Dimension:** arpeggiator · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:289-293, 416-434`
- **Also flagged by:** shared-dsp-contracts, gestalt-processor

**Problem.** applyArpParams ends with arpCore_.setEnabled(arpOpModeParam != kArpOff) (processor_params.cpp:1139). setEnabled(false) only sets needsDisableNoteOff_ (arpeggiator_core.h:394-400); the NoteOffs are emitted by the NEXT processBlock() (arpeggiator_core.cpp:35-41, emitPanicNoteOffs). process() calls arpCore_.processBlock only inside `if (isArpRunning)` (processor.cpp:293), and isArpRunning is false as soon as the mode is Off, so the cleanup is never drained. The comment at processor.cpp:294-296 claims the opposite. Pending gate NoteOffs are frozen too, because the jump-ahead loop never runs. No engine allNotesOff exists anywhere in plugins/ruinae/src.

**Why it is wrong.** FR-017, cited in the code, requires every arp NoteOn to get a matching NoteOff. The core's contract is that a disable is discharged by the next processBlock(). Ruinae's Off branch skips that call, so the contract cannot be met.

**Consequence.** With the default 80 % gate an arp note is sounding about 80 % of the time. Turning Arp Off (MIDI or MIDI+Mod to Off), or automating it off, leaves that voice at the amp sustain level (default 0.8) indefinitely while the user plays the synth directly. With MIDI Out on, the downstream instrument also receives the NoteOn with no NoteOff. The note is released only when the arp is turned on again and its frozen pending-off finally runs, or when the user plays and releases the same pitch.

**Suggested fix.** When the operating mode changes to Off, run one arpCore_.processBlock() for that block and route its NoteOffs to the engine and MIDI out. The routing must be decided by the PREVIOUS mode, because the notes were dispatched under it. Alternatively, track the previous mode and call the drain whenever it was a dispatching mode. Regression test: in MIDI mode, hold one key at gate 100-200 % so a note is guaranteed to be sounding, switch to Off mid-gate, and REQUIRE silence within release time and a NoteOff on outputEvents. The existing ArpIntegration_DisableWhilePlaying_NoStuckNotes (arp_integration_test.cpp:668-721) passes only by timing. With its 1/8, 80 %, 512-sample schedule (steps at 512, 11537, 22562, offs at 9332, 20357, 31382), the last note is already released at sample 31382, before the disable block at 31744, so no note is sounding when it disables.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:293 `if (isArpRunning) { // FR-017: setEnabled(false) queues cleanup note-offs internally. The processBlock() call below drains them`, and the else branch at :416 only writes playhead sentinels. processor_params.cpp:1139 `arpCore_.setEnabled(arpOpModeParam != kArpOff);`. arpeggiator_core.h:395-396 `if (enabled_ && !enabled) { needsDisableNoteOff_ = true;`. arpeggiator_core.cpp:36-40 `if (!enabled_) { if (needsDisableNoteOff_) emitPanicNoteOffs(...); return eventCount; }`, which is reachable only through processBlock. Grep for allNotesOff/requestPanic under plugins/ruinae/src: no hits.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the claim through the code and could not refute it.

1. processor_params.cpp:1138-1139 calls `arpCore_.setEnabled(arpOpModeParam != kArpOff)` from applyParamsToEngine(), which processor.cpp:251 calls before the arp block. arpeggiator_core.h:394-400: on an enabled-to-disabled change, setEnabled only sets `needsDisableNoteOff_ = true` and clears the ratchet counters. It emits no events.

2. arpeggiator_core.cpp:31-41: the NoteOffs are emitted only inside processBlock(). Path (c) `if (!enabled_) { if (needsDisableNoteOff_) emitPanicNoteOffs(...); return eventCount; }` runs when processBlock is called.

3. processor.cpp:289-293: `isArpRunning = (arpOpMode != kArpOff)`, and `arpCore_.processBlock(arpCtx, arpEvents_)` (line 330) is only inside `if (isArpRunning)`. The else branch at 416-434 only writes the playhead sentinel output params. In the first block after Off, the operating mode is already kArpOff, so processBlock is never called and the queued panic NoteOffs are never drained. Pending gate NoteOffs stay frozen in pendingNoteOffs_. The comment at processor.cpp:294-296 says the opposite of what the code does.

4. Nothing else releases the notes. A case-insensitive grep for OperatingMode, allNotesOff, releaseAll and panic under plugins/ruinae/src finds only the atomic loads and the param registration: no mode-change handler, no previous-mode tracking, no engine all-notes-off. Even if the arp were drained later, its routing at processor.cpp:342/362 is gated by the CURRENT mode (`isArpDispatchingNotes`), so in Off mode the NoteOffs would not reach the engine or MIDI out either.

5. Partial mitigation, which does not refute the finding: in Off mode, processor_midi.cpp:180-193 sends a user key release straight to the engine as a NoteOff for that pitch. A stuck arp note is therefore freed if the user later releases the same pitch. That does not happen with latch on (keys already released, the arp still sounding), with octave range above 1, with transposed or ratcheted pitches, or for the MIDI output: user NoteOffs in Off mode are never written to data.outputEvents. So the downstream instrument keeps an unmatched NoteOn.

6. The test at arp_integration_test.cpp:668-721 does not exercise the bug. Its comment (693-695) says "the processBlock() inside disableArp() drains them", which is the same wrong belief, and its pass depends on whether a note is sounding when the disable block runs. The code path confirms the defect.

Severity stays as filed: a stuck note on an ordinary mode switch (always reachable with latch on), plus an unmatched NoteOn on the MIDI output, is a top-tier synth defect.

**Note 2.** The defect is confirmed from source. Nothing elsewhere guards it.

1) The disable is only queued. processor_params.cpp:1139 calls `arpCore_.setEnabled(arpOpModeParam != kArpOff)`. In arpeggiator_core.h:394-405, setEnabled(false) only sets needsDisableNoteOff_ = true and clears the ratchet state; it emits nothing.

2) Only processBlock drains it. arpeggiator_core.cpp:36-41 is the `if (!enabled_) { if (needsDisableNoteOff_) emitPanicNoteOffs(...); return eventCount; }` branch, and it is reachable only through processBlock.

3) process() skips that call when the arp is Off. processor.cpp:289-293 computes isArpRunning = (arpOpMode != kArpOff) from the same atomic that applyArpParams just used, and calls arpCore_.processBlock (:330) only inside `if (isArpRunning)`. The else branch at :416-434 only writes the playhead sentinels. So in the block where the mode becomes Off, and in every later block, the queued panic NoteOffs and any pending gate NoteOffs are never emitted. Nothing routes them to queueTimedEvent(ArpNoteOff) or to outputEvents. The comment at :294-296 ("The processBlock() call below drains them") cannot be true for this transition, because the code it sits in does not run when the mode is Off.

4) No other path exists. A grep for operatingMode in plugins/ruinae/src/processor finds only reads: processor.cpp:289, processor_params.cpp:868, and processor_midi.cpp:162/183/205/223. Nothing tracks the previous mode and nothing does an engine-wide note release when the mode changes.

5) Released keys only partly help. After the switch to Off, processor_midi.cpp:191-193 sends a host NoteOff straight to the engine. That releases an arp voice only if its pitch equals the released key. Notes moved by the octave range, the pitch lane or the chord lane, latched notes, and the MIDI-out copies all stay stuck.

6) The existing test does not pin the case. ArpIntegration_DisableWhilePlaying_NoStuckNotes (arp_integration_test.cpp:668-721) relies on the comment at :693-695, which says the processBlock inside disableArp() drains the NoteOffs. The processor path never makes that call when the mode is Off, so the test can pass only when no arp note is sounding at the moment of the disable, which is the timing argument the finding makes.

The bug is reachable through ordinary automation or a UI change of Arp Mode to Off while keys are held or latched. I keep the severity: it leaves stuck notes in the engine and on the MIDI output.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the defect from source.

1. The disable is never discharged.
   - processor_params.cpp:1139 calls `arpCore_.setEnabled(arpOpModeParam != kArpOff)`.
   - setEnabled(false) at arpeggiator_core.h:394-406 only sets `needsDisableNoteOff_ = true` and clears the ratchet state. It emits nothing.
   - The NoteOffs come only from processBlock: arpeggiator_core.cpp:36-40 (`if (!enabled_) { if (needsDisableNoteOff_) emitPanicNoteOffs(...); return eventCount; }`).
   - processor.cpp:289-293 computes `isArpRunning = (arpOpMode != kArpOff)` from the same atomic, in the same block, and calls `arpCore_.processBlock` (processor.cpp:330) only inside `if (isArpRunning)`.
   - The else branch at processor.cpp:416-434 only writes the playhead sentinel values. So in the block that switches to Off, and every block after it, the queued panic NoteOffs are never drained. The comment at processor.cpp:294-296 is wrong.
   - processor.cpp is the only caller of processBlock in plugins/ruinae/src. A grep for operatingMode/kArpOff/setEnabled found no other transition handling. setActive (processor.cpp:206-207) calls arpCore_.reset(), which clears needsDisableNoteOff_ without sending anything.

2. The engine cannot release the note any other way.
   - In MIDI and MIDI+Mod modes the physical keys go only to arpCore_. processor_midi.cpp:168-176 shows `!arpDispatchesNotes` gating the direct engine NoteOn, so the engine holds only the arp's ArpNoteOn voices.
   - After the switch to Off, onNoteOff (processor_midi.cpp:180-193) sends a direct engine NoteOff for the released physical pitch only.
   - The arp voice is therefore released only if its pitch equals a key the user later releases.
   - Nothing reaches the MIDI output in Off mode: output events are written only inside the isArpRunning block (processor.cpp:347-377).

3. Magnitude, with the claim narrowed.
   - Default case (latch Off, octave range 1, no pitch lane, keys still held at the switch): the arp note is one of the held pitches, so releasing the keys afterwards sends a matching NoteOff to the engine. The stuck voice then ends at key release; it is not held indefinitely. The user still hears a single arp note sustained in place of the chord while the keys are held.
   - Cases where the note hangs indefinitely in the engine:
     - Latch Hold or Add (keys already released, pattern still running).
     - Octave range above 1, a pitch lane, transpose or spice, where the arp pitch is not a held key.
     - Sequencer source mode.
     - In mono mode the stuck pitch stays in MonoHandler's note stack.
   - With MIDI Out on, the downstream NoteOn never gets a NoteOff in every case, because Off mode forwards nothing.
   - Probability: with an 80 % gate, a note is sounding at roughly 80 % of switch instants.

4. Test coverage.
   - ArpIntegration_DisableWhilePlaying_NoStuckNotes (arp_integration_test.cpp:668-721) cannot catch this. disableArp() (lines 277-281) only sends kArpOperatingModeId=0 and processes one block.
   - About 61 blocks of 512 samples (~31.2k samples) run before the disable. With 1/8-note steps of ~11025 samples and an 80 % gate, the last gate-off (about 30.9k–31.4k samples depending on the first step's offset) lands at or before the disable block, so no note is sounding when it disables.
   - The test passes on timing alone, as the finding says.

Severity: keep critical. The finding is real and reachable through ordinary use (toggling Arp Off with latch on, octave range above 1, or MIDI Out). In the default held-key case it lasts only until key release, which narrows the claimed consequence but does not refute it.

</details>

### R-079

**FX-tab modulation-type and flanger/chorus group pointers are never nulled on a MainTab switch: dangling setVisible on every later preset load**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** critical · **Dimension:** ui-wiring · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/controller/controller_settings.cpp:50-57`
- **Also flagged by:** prior-audit-regressions

**Problem.** verifyView caches eight raw view pointers from the Tab_Fx template: noModulationGroup_, phaserControlsGroup_, flangerControlsGroup_, chorusControlsGroup_, flangerRateGroup_, flangerNoteValueGroup_, chorusRateGroup_ and chorusNoteValueGroup_ (controller_verify_view.cpp:942-981). onTabChanged's 'FX tab residents' block nulls harmonizerVoiceRows_, the delay groups, the phaser rate groups and the spectral pointers, but none of these eight. Only willClose clears them (controller.cpp:701-708). When the user leaves the FX tab, UIViewSwitchContainer removes and forgets the Tab_Fx template, and the eight pointers keep pointing at freed CViewContainers.

**Why it is wrong.** The project invariant, written in the controller.cpp:724-727 comment and in the prior audit F001-F003, is that every cached view pointer is nulled on every path that destroys its template. A dangling non-null pointer passes every `if (ptr)` guard. F003 fixed the MOD-tab residents. The FX-tab groups that were added for flanger and chorus were never added to onTabChanged, so this is the same defect class, reintroduced.

**Consequence.** Repro: open the FX tab, switch to SOUND, MOD or SEQ, then load a preset from the host (setComponentState -> syncAllViews). syncAllViews unconditionally calls flangerControlsGroup_->setVisible(...) and the other setters on freed memory (controller_view_sync.cpp:826-836): a crash or heap corruption. The same happens on host automation of Modulation Type, Flanger Sync or Chorus Sync (controller_view_sync.cpp:410-425), or on any browser preset load (loadComponentStateWithNotify -> syncAllViews).

**Suggested fix.** Null all eight pointers in onTabChanged's FX block, next to delayTimeGroup_ and phaserRateGroup_. Extend mod_source_view_teardown_test.cpp with a test that shows Tab_Fx, switches the MainTab container to index 0, calls notifyTabChangedForTest, and asserts that every FX-group pointer is null. Expose a count accessor similar to modSourceViewPointerCount(). Better: a test that walks every custom-view-name in each Tab_* template and asserts that onTabChanged clears it.

**Evidence.** controller_settings.cpp:50-57 FX block: `harmonizerVoiceRows_.fill(nullptr); delayTimeGroup_ = nullptr; delayNoteValueGroup_ = nullptr; phaserRateGroup_ = nullptr; phaserNoteValueGroup_ = nullptr; spectralCurveDropdown_ = nullptr; spectralBitsGroup_ = nullptr;` (no flanger/chorus/noModulation/phaserControls). verify_view.cpp:952-953 `} else if (*name == "FlangerControlsGroup") { flangerControlsGroup_ = container;`. editor.uidesc:2515 `<template name="Tab_Fx"` contains custom-view-name NoModulationGroup (2572), PhaserControlsGroup (2581), FlangerControlsGroup (2683), FlangerRateGroup (2705), ChorusControlsGroup (2767), ChorusRateGroup (2789). controller_view_sync.cpp:835 `if (flangerControlsGroup_) flangerControlsGroup_->setVisible(modType == 2);` runs inside syncAllViews.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The defect holds in today's code.

1. Where the pointers are cached: controller_verify_view.cpp:942-981 stores eight raw CView* pointers when verifyView meets the NoModulationGroup, PhaserControlsGroup, FlangerControlsGroup, ChorusControlsGroup, ChorusRateGroup, ChorusNoteValueGroup, FlangerRateGroup and FlangerNoteValueGroup containers. The members are declared at controller.h:385-396.

2. Where the views live: all eight custom-view-names are inside `<template name="Tab_Fx">` (editor.uidesc:2515; Tab_Seq starts at 3317). They are at uidesc lines 2572, 2581, 2683, 2705, 2716, 2767, 2789 and 2800. They are direct children of Tab_Fx, not of a nested switch. Tab_Fx is one of the pages of the MainTab UIViewSwitchContainer (editor.uidesc:4313-4318, `template-switch-control="MainTab" template-names="Tab_Sound,Tab_Mod,Tab_Fx,Tab_Seq"`). Switching away from it tears that template down.

3. The teardown hook leaves them set: setParamNormalized(kMainTabTag) calls onTabChanged (controller_view_sync.cpp:64-67). The FX block of onTabChanged, controller_settings.cpp:50-57, nulls only harmonizerVoiceRows_, delayTimeGroup_, delayNoteValueGroup_, phaserRateGroup_, phaserNoteValueGroup_, spectralCurveDropdown_ and spectralBitsGroup_. None of the eight pointers is nulled there. A grep for every one of them in plugins/ruinae/src finds a nulling assignment only in willClose (controller.cpp:701-708). No other per-tag reset exists either: the type-specific resets at view_sync.cpp:68-84 cover only the Osc A/B PW knobs, the distortion spectral pointers and the mod-source views.

4. Where the stale pointers are used: syncAllViews calls syncVisGroup on flangerRateGroup_/flangerNoteValueGroup_ and chorusRateGroup_/chorusNoteValueGroup_ (controller_view_sync.cpp:826-827). It then calls setVisible on the four modulation-type groups, guarded only by `if (ptr)` (controller_view_sync.cpp:833-836). setParamNormalized does the same for kFlangerSyncId, kChorusSyncId and kModulationTypeId (view_sync.cpp:410-425) whenever bulkParamLoad_ is false (the early return is at line 88). A freed pointer is non-null and passes every one of these guards.

5. The repro holds: open the FX tab, switch to another tab, then load a preset or receive host automation of Modulation Type, Flanger Sync or Chorus Sync. That calls setVisible on freed CViewContainers. This is the same class of defect as F001-F003. The project's own comment at controller.cpp:724-727 says this exact pattern causes use-after-free on the setComponentState -> syncAllViews path. The existing test mod_source_view_teardown_test.cpp covers only the MOD-tab residents (lines 189-190), so nothing tests the FX groups.

Severity: a use-after-free on a common user path (visit FX, then load a preset). Critical stands; no change.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source. I could not find anything that guards against it, makes it intentional or makes it unreachable.

1. The views live in a template that gets destroyed. The main tab container is a UIViewSwitchContainer with template-switch-control="MainTab" and template-names="Tab_Sound,Tab_Mod,Tab_Fx,Tab_Seq" (editor.uidesc:4313-4318). Tab_Fx starts at editor.uidesc:2515 and the next template, Tab_Seq, starts at :3317. The groups sit inside that range: NoModulationGroup (2572), PhaserControlsGroup (2581), FlangerControlsGroup (2683), ChorusControlsGroup (2767). No nested switch container keeps them alive.

2. verifyView caches raw pointers and takes no reference: noModulationGroup_, phaserControlsGroup_, flangerControlsGroup_, chorusControlsGroup_, chorusRateGroup_, chorusNoteValueGroup_, flangerRateGroup_ and flangerNoteValueGroup_ (controller_verify_view.cpp:942-981, plain assignments, no remember()). They are declared as raw CView* in controller.h:385-396.

3. onTabChanged's "FX tab residents" block (controller_settings.cpp:50-57) nulls only harmonizerVoiceRows_, delayTimeGroup_, delayNoteValueGroup_, phaserRateGroup_, phaserNoteValueGroup_, spectralCurveDropdown_ and spectralBitsGroup_. None of the eight pointers is nulled anywhere in onTabChanged (lines 14-81). A grep shows the only other place they are nulled is willClose (controller.cpp:701-708).

4. onTabChanged is the only hook for a MainTab switch. setParamNormalized calls it when tag == kMainTabTag (controller_view_sync.cpp:64-67). The comment at controller_view_sync.cpp:59-63 itself says that skipping this nulling leaves pointers dangling and causes a use-after-free in syncAllViews.

5. The dangling pointers are dereferenced from paths that do not depend on the FX tab being visible:
- setParamNormalized for kFlangerSyncId, kChorusSyncId and kModulationTypeId (controller_view_sync.cpp:410-425). These run on host automation or on any parameter update.
- syncAllViews (controller_view_sync.cpp:826-827 through syncVisGroup, and the setVisible calls at 833-836). syncAllViews runs on state load.
Every one of these sites uses an `if (ptr)` guard, and a non-null dangling pointer passes it.

6. There is no test for this. mod_source_view_teardown_test.cpp covers only the MOD-tab mod-source pointers (F001-F003, modSourceViewPointerCount). Nothing asserts that the FX-group pointers are null after notifyTabChangedForTest.

The only mitigation is that verifyView re-populates the pointers when the user returns to the FX tab. Until then they dangle. Repro: open the FX tab, switch to another tab, then load a preset or automate Modulation Type, Flanger Sync or Chorus Sync. That is a use-after-free on the UI thread in a common user flow, so critical severity is justified.

**Note 3.** The defect is confirmed from source.

1. All eight groups live in Tab_Fx. editor.uidesc:2515 opens `<template name="Tab_Fx"`, and NoModulationGroup (2572), FlangerControlsGroup (2683), FlangerNoteValueGroup (2716) and ChorusNoteValueGroup (2800) are declared inside it. Tab_Fx is one of the MainTab UIViewSwitchContainer's `template-names="Tab_Sound,Tab_Mod,Tab_Fx,Tab_Seq"` (editor.uidesc:4315). VSTGUI's switch container removes and releases the old template's views when the index changes.

2. verifyView caches raw CView* pointers to these groups (controller_verify_view.cpp:942-981, e.g. 953 `flangerControlsGroup_ = container;`). They are declared as raw `VSTGUI::CView*` members (controller.h:385-395). The controller registers no view listener: a grep for viewWillDelete, registerViewListener and IViewListener in src/controller finds nothing.

3. The only tab-switch hook is setParamNormalized(kMainTabTag) -> onTabChanged (controller_view_sync.cpp:64-66). Its "FX tab residents" block (controller_settings.cpp:50-57) nulls only harmonizerVoiceRows_, delayTimeGroup_, delayNoteValueGroup_, phaserRateGroup_, phaserNoteValueGroup_, spectralCurveDropdown_ and spectralBitsGroup_. noModulationGroup_, phaserControlsGroup_, flangerControlsGroup_, chorusControlsGroup_, flangerRateGroup_, flangerNoteValueGroup_, chorusRateGroup_ and chorusNoteValueGroup_ are not nulled there. They are nulled only in willClose (controller.cpp:701-708).

4. The dangling pointers are dereferenced in two places:
   - setComponentState (controller.cpp:291-301) always calls syncAllViews(), which at controller_view_sync.cpp:826-836 calls syncVisGroup(kFlangerSyncId/kChorusSyncId, ...) and `if (flangerControlsGroup_) flangerControlsGroup_->setVisible(...)`. The same happens on browser preset loads (controller_presets.cpp:384).
   - When bulkParamLoad_ is false, setParamNormalized for kFlangerSyncId, kChorusSyncId and kModulationTypeId (controller_view_sync.cpp:410-425) calls setVisible through the same pointers. This covers host automation of those parameters while another tab is showing.

   A freed non-null pointer passes every `if (ptr)` guard. The result is a use-after-free virtual call: an access violation or heap corruption.

Impact: the trigger is ordinary use. Open the FX tab, switch to any other tab, then load a preset from the host or the browser, or automate Modulation Type, Flanger Sync or Chorus Sync. No unusual host or settings are needed. Returning to FX repopulates the pointers, so the window is "FX was visited and is not currently shown", which is the common case. The project already treats this class of bug as a crash: the comments at controller.cpp:724-727 and controller_view_sync.cpp:59-63 describe it, and prior audit fix F003 covered the MOD-tab residents. Critical severity stands.

### R-080

**Toggling Distortion General/Type-specific destroys Dist_Spectral without nulling spectralCurveDropdown_/spectralBitsGroup_ (use-after-free)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** critical · **Dimension:** ui-wiring · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/controller/controller_view_sync.cpp:59-85, 487-500, 897-912`
- **Also flagged by:** ui-wiring, gestalt-controller

**Problem.** SpectralCurveDropdown and SpectralBitsGroup live in the Dist_Spectral template. That template is instantiated only inside the nested Distortion_TypeSpecific switch, which itself sits inside the DistortionViewMode (tag 10017) UIViewSwitchContainer. The pointer-nulling hooks in setParamNormalized cover kMainTabTag, kOscA/BTypeId, kDistortionTypeId and kModSourceViewModeTag. Nothing handles kDistortionViewModeTag (10017), so flipping the IconSegmentButton from Type-specific back to General destroys Dist_Spectral and leaves both pointers dangling.

**Why it is wrong.** Every template switch that destroys a cached view must null the cached pointer, which is the F002 lesson. The view-mode switch is a second destruction path for the same views, and it has no hook.

**Consequence.** Repro: select the Spectral distortion type, click Type-specific (Dist_Spectral is created and cached), click General (it is destroyed), then load a preset. syncAllViews calls spectralCurveDropdown_->setAlphaValue/setMouseEnabled on freed memory (view_sync.cpp:904-911): a crash or heap corruption. Host automation of Distortion Spectral Mode does the same (view_sync.cpp:492-499).

**Suggested fix.** In setParamNormalized, null spectralCurveDropdown_ and spectralBitsGroup_ when tag == kDistortionViewModeTag, next to the kDistortionTypeId hook. Or give the views a removed-callback, as ModRingIndicator does (controller_mod_matrix.cpp:337-340), so that any destruction path clears them. Add a lifecycle test: show Tab_Sound, set DistortionType to Spectral, drive the DistortionViewMode switch 1->0, then assert both pointers are null, or call syncAllViews under ASan.

**Evidence.** view_sync.cpp:74-77 `if (tag == kDistortionTypeId) { spectralCurveDropdown_ = nullptr; spectralBitsGroup_ = nullptr; }`: no kDistortionViewModeTag branch anywhere in 59-85. editor.uidesc:1376-1381 Distortion_TypeSpecific holds the switch `template-names="Dist_Clean,Dist_Chaos,Dist_Spectral,..."`. :1421 `custom-view-name="SpectralCurveDropdown"`, :1426 `custom-view-name="SpectralBitsGroup"`. :3956-3968 IconSegmentButton `control-tag="DistortionViewMode"` drives `template-names="Distortion_General,Distortion_TypeSpecific"`. view_sync.cpp:904-905 `if (spectralCurveDropdown_) { spectralCurveDropdown_->setAlphaValue(...)`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the claim through the source and it holds.

1. Where the pointers are cached: controller_verify_view.cpp:645-646 stores the SpectralCurveDropdown view as a raw pointer (`spectralCurveDropdown_ = view`). controller_verify_view.cpp:1036-1037 does the same for SpectralBitsGroup (`spectralBitsGroup_ = container`). Nothing removes them when the view is destroyed: no listener and no remember/forget.

2. Where the views live: editor.uidesc:1414-1434 puts both custom views in the Dist_Spectral template. Dist_Spectral is created only by the nested UIViewSwitchContainer in Distortion_TypeSpecific (editor.uidesc:1376-1382, switched by DistortionType). Distortion_TypeSpecific is itself one page of the outer UIViewSwitchContainer at editor.uidesc:3965-3969 (`template-names="Distortion_General,Distortion_TypeSpecific"`, `template-switch-control="DistortionViewMode"`), which the IconSegmentButton at :3956-3962 drives.
