(3) The per-sample loop (ruinae_voice.h:516-527) computes effectiveCutoff = filterCutoffHz_ * semitonesToRatio(filterEnvAmount_*env + keyTrackSemitones + cutoffMod + brightnessOffset) and calls setActiveFilterCutoff(effectiveCutoff), which is setFrequency(effective) again.
(4) SelfOscillatingFilter::setFrequency (self_oscillating_filter.h:430-441) sets needsKick_ = true whenever resonance_ > 0.9 and |newFreq - frequency_| > 10 Hz. The base->effective write pair therefore re-arms the kick at the start of every 64-sample sub-block whenever the two cutoffs differ by more than 10 Hz. A per-sample sweep faster than 10 Hz/sample re-arms it every sample.
(5) process() (self_oscillating_filter.h:273-278) answers needsKick_ with filter_.reset(), which clears the ladder state, plus a +1.0 impulse. So the oscillation really is wiped and re-seeded.
(6) Resonance above 0.9 is the normal self-oscillation region: remapResonanceForSelfOsc (ruinae_voice.h:1645-1655) maps Q > 10 to above 0.9.
No upstream clamp, setActive reset or design comment makes the kick-on-frequency-change heuristic intentional for this two-writer pattern. It is a standalone-filter heuristic (meant for a glide or MIDI pitch change) that the voice's alternating base/effective writes trigger periodically. The trigger conditions are ordinary: any key tracking away from C4, any filter-env amount, MPE brightness away from 0.5, or a voice cutoff route. The quoted probe numbers are consistent with this mechanism (a 689 Hz = 44100/64 impulse train, levels down 15-20 dB). The existing voice test renders with key track 0 and no envelope, so effective == base and the test never exercises the alternation. High severity is justified: one of the 13 filter types is broken in its normal melodic use.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the defect from source. It is a real, audible consequence, and it also fires on factory presets.

The code path, each step read:
(1) ruinae_engine.h:846-907. processBlock runs a kModSubBlock grid and calls processBlockPoly/processBlockMono once per sub-block.
(2) ruinae_engine.h:1957-1963 (poly) and 2054-2058 (mono). Each sub-block they call voices_[i].setFilterCutoff(modCutoff), where modCutoff = the base voiceFilterCutoffHz_ times the AllVoice offset. The call is unconditional, and the comment at 1948-1952 says so on purpose.
(3) ruinae_voice.h:766-770. setFilterCutoff stores filterCutoffHz_ and then immediately calls setActiveFilterCutoff(filterCutoffHz_).
(4) ruinae_voice.h:1408-1409. That case calls filterSelfOsc_->setFrequency(base).
(5) ruinae_voice.h:519-527. The per-sample loop then calls setActiveFilterCutoff(effectiveCutoff), which includes keyTrackSemitones, filterEnvAmount_*env, the voice cutoff route and the MPE brightness offset.
(6) self_oscillating_filter.h:430-437. setFrequency sets needsKick_ whenever resonance_ > 0.9 and |newFreq - frequency_| > 10 Hz. So the base write (prev = effective) and the first effective write (prev = base) both arm the kick.
(7) self_oscillating_filter.h:273-278. process() answers needsKick_ with filter_.reset() plus filterInput += 1.0f. ladder_filter.h:175-184 shows that reset() zeroes state_ and tanhState_, so the oscillation is destroyed and re-seeded at the start of every sub-block, a periodic pattern at sampleRate/64.

The threshold is reachable: remapResonanceForSelfOsc (ruinae_voice.h:1645-1651) maps Q 10 to 0.9, so any Q above 10 enables the kick gate.

Impact: this is not hypothetical. tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:5269-5271 is a factory preset with filter type 12 (Self-Osc), cutoff 440, resonance 18 and keyTrack 1.0. At :8059-8066 another uses resonance 25 and keyTrack 1.0. For every note except C4 the effective cutoff differs from the base by far more than 10 Hz (key track 1 at C5 doubles it), so both presets are periodically wiped and re-kicked. A fast filter-env sweep (more than 10 Hz per sample) also re-kicks per sample through the per-sample writes alone.

I did not re-run the reviewer's probe. Its numbers (-14.8 dB at Q 20, -20 dB at Q 30, a 689 Hz = 44100/64 impulse train) are consistent with the code: a full ladder state clear plus a unit impulse once per 64 samples.

Severity: high stands. It is a gross audible artefact, a level loss plus a sub-block-rate buzz, on the self-oscillating type's intended melodic use and in shipped presets. It is limited to one of the 13 filter types, so I did not upgrade it.

</details>

### R-010

**Pitch-bend smoother is advanced one sample per engine processBlock call, so bend settles in seconds and its speed depends on host block size and event count**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:841-842 (with dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/note_processor.h 99-108, 60; smoother.h 88-89)`
- **Also flagged by:** voice-management-midi, shared-dsp-contracts, spec-conformance, gestalt-engine

**Problem.** RuinaeEngine::processBlock calls noteProcessor_.processPitchBend() exactly once per call. processPitchBend() does a single OnePoleSmoother::process(), i.e. it advances ONE sample of a smoother configured for the audio sample rate (5 ms, coeff = exp(-5000/(5*44100)) = 0.9776). The bend ratio used by every voice (getFrequency, ruinae_engine.h:2012) therefore moves 2.2 % of the remaining distance per host block / per MIDI segment.

**Why it is wrong.** A smoother configured in samples must be advanced once per sample (or advanceSamples(numSamples) once per block, which OnePoleSmoother provides). Stepping it per call turns a 5 ms time constant into ~203 calls to reach 99 %, which scales with the buffer size, violating the block-size independence the engine's 64-sample mod grid was built for.

**Consequence.** Settling time to 99 % = ln(0.01)/ln(0.9776) = 203 calls: 0.59 s at 128-sample buffers, 2.36 s at 512, 9.4 s at 2048 (44.1 kHz). Releasing the bend wheel leaves the pitch sliding back for seconds; the same performance renders differently at different buffer sizes and with different numbers of note events splitting the block (renderEngineSegments calls processBlock per segment).

**Suggested fix.** Advance the smoother by the segment length: e.g. NoteProcessor::processPitchBend(size_t numSamples) using bendSmoother_.advanceSamples(numSamples) (or per mod sub-block inside the 64-sample loop so voices see a stepped-but-timely bend). Test: set bend +1 then render 50 ms at block sizes 32 and 1024; require voice 0 frequency within 0.1 cent of the bent target and identical between block sizes.

**Evidence.** ruinae_engine.h:841-842 `// Step 6: Process pitch bend smoother once per block  [[maybe_unused]] auto bendValue = noteProcessor_.processPitchBend();` ; note_processor.h:99-104 `/// Advance the pitch bend smoother by one sample. /// Call once per audio block ... float smoothedBend = bendSmoother_.process();` ; note_processor.h:60 `bendSmoother_.configure(smoothingTimeMs_, sampleRate_);` ; smoother.h:88-89 `coeff = exp(-5000.0 / (smoothTimeMs * sampleRate))`. Engine tests only check 'should not crash' (ruinae_engine_test.cpp:940-945).

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The defect is real, and I traced it through the source as follows.

1. Where the smoother is stepped. `RuinaeEngine::processBlock` begins at plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:783. Lines 841-842 call `noteProcessor_.processPitchBend()` once, before the 64-sample sub-block loop that starts at line 846. It is not called inside that loop, and no other site in plugins/ruinae/src calls processPitchBend or advanceSamples on the bend smoother. I grepped for `noteProcessor_.`, which turns up only prepare/reset/setPitchBend/processPitchBend/setPitchBendRange/setTuningReference/setVelocityCurve/getFrequency/mapVelocity.

2. One call is one sample. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/note_processor.h:103-107 has processPitchBend() run `bendSmoother_.process()` once. Its doc comment (lines 99-100) says "Advance ... by one sample. Call once per audio block". The smoother is configured in samples: note_processor.h:60 has `configure(smoothingTimeMs_ (5ms), sampleRate_)`, and prepare() at line 73 calls setSampleRate(sampleRate). Ruinae never calls setSmoothingTime. In smoother.h:89 the coefficient is `exp(-5000/(timeMs*sampleRate))`, which gives about 0.9776 at 44.1 kHz. OnePoleSmoother::process() (smoother.h:195) moves one sample per call. The class already provides `advanceSamples(numSamples)` at smoother.h:241, but nothing here uses it.

3. Who reads the result. In the poly path, ruinae_engine.h:2012-2014 sets each voice's frequency with `noteProcessor_.getFrequency(voiceNote)`, and that reads the cached currentBendRatio_. The mono path and note-ons read the same cache at lines 1735, 1772, 1801 and 1873.

4. Calls per buffer. processor_midi.cpp:120-148 (renderEngineSegments) calls `engine_.processBlock` once for each event-delimited segment. So the smoother moves one step per segment, and both the buffer size and the number of note events in a buffer change how fast the bend settles.

The finding's numbers check out. Reaching 99% takes about 203 calls, which is about 2.4 s at 512-sample buffers and 44.1 kHz. To fall below kCompletionThreshold = 1e-4 (smoother.h:55) takes about 406 calls. Output therefore depends on block size, which contradicts the block-size independence that the modGridPhase_ comment at lines 819-825 claims for the 64-sample grid. A pitch-bend release audibly slides for seconds.

I am keeping the severity at high.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source; I found no guard elsewhere and no design note that would refute it. ruinae_engine.h:841-842 calls `noteProcessor_.processPitchBend()` exactly once per processBlock, before the 64-sample sub-block loop (846+). processPitchBend (note_processor.h:103-108) makes one `bendSmoother_.process()` call. OnePoleSmoother::process (smoother.h:195-209) is a single-sample step, `current = target + coeff*(current-target)`, with coeff = exp(-5000/(timeMs*sampleRate)) (smoother.h:89). The smoother is configured for the real audio rate: NoteProcessor constructor at :60 and prepare(sampleRate) at :70-74, called from ruinae_engine.h:148. Ruinae never calls setSmoothingTime (grep across plugins/ruinae/src), so the 5 ms default applies and coeff is about 0.9776 at 44.1 kHz. The bend therefore covers 2.2% of the remaining distance per processBlock call, and the claimed figures follow: about 203 calls to 99%, i.e. ~2.4 s at 512-sample blocks. The settle time also depends on block size and on how many segments the event queue cuts the block into. Nothing compensates for this. The smoother already provides advanceSamples (smoother.h:234-252), whose own comment says it is "Essential for correct smoothing when processing once per audio block", but Ruinae does not use it. The shared header's comment "Call once per audio block" (note_processor.h:100) does not make this intentional: the same doc says the call advances "by one sample" and that smoothing is 5 ms, so the comment contradicts the configured time constant rather than documenting a design choice. The only pitch bend source is processor_midi.cpp:110 -> engine.setPitchBend, and the bend reaches the voices via getFrequency (ruinae_engine.h:1735/1772/1801/1873/2012). The tests do not pin the timing: ruinae_engine_test.cpp:941-949 only checks that nothing crashes, and ruinae_engine_integration_test.cpp:336-341 only requires rms > 0. The prior audit's findings.json has no pitch-bend finding, so this is new rather than a repeat. Severity stays high: pitch bend is a primary performance control, bend release lags audibly by seconds at common buffer sizes, and renders differ with block size.

**Note 3.** The defect is real, and the consequence happens as claimed.

1. plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:841-842 calls `noteProcessor_.processPitchBend()` once per processBlock call. This is outside the kModSubBlock loop that starts at line 846, and nothing compensates for the number of samples in the call.
2. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/note_processor.h:99-108: processPitchBend() makes exactly one `bendSmoother_.process()` call. The doc comment says "Advance the pitch bend smoother by one sample. Call once per audio block", which contradicts itself. Lines 60 and 70-74 configure the smoother at 5 ms and the audio sample rate. No Ruinae source calls setSmoothingTime (grep of plugins/ruinae/src), so it stays at 5 ms.
3. dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/smoother.h:89 computes coeff = exp(-5000/(5*44100)) = 0.97758 at 44.1 kHz. process() (lines 195-209) is a single step: current = target + coeff*(current-target). advanceSamples(N) exists at lines 241-252, and its comment says it is "Essential for correct smoothing when processing once per audio block". The engine does not use it.
4. Every voice reads the bend through getFrequency, which uses the cached currentBendRatio_ (note_processor.h:156-159; ruinae_engine.h:1873, 2012). So the stepped bend is the pitch you hear.
5. processor_midi.cpp:120-148: renderEngineSegments calls engine_.processBlock once per segment between timed events. PitchBend is one of those timed events (lines 109-110), so every note event and every bend message adds a smoother step. Dense bend streams therefore glide faster than sparse ones, and the rate also changes with host buffer size.

Quantified (one segment per buffer): reaching 99% takes ln(0.01)/ln(0.97758) ≈ 203 calls. That is 0.59 s at 128 samples, 2.36 s at 512 and 9.4 s at 2048 (44.1 kHz). At 96 kHz the coefficient is 0.98965, which needs about 443 calls, so it is even slower. A full ±2 st bend with one 512-sample buffer moves only 2.2%, about 4.5 cents, in the first 11.6 ms. Releasing the wheel leaves the pitch audibly sliding back for seconds instead of 5 ms, and the same performance renders differently at different buffer sizes and event densities.

Bend is a core performance control, and the error is audible in every host, so severity stays high. The earlier test reference (an engine test that only checks for no crash) agrees that nothing covers the timing.

</details>

### R-011

**Mono mode ignores pitch bend and the Tuning Reference: the voice frequency is overwritten every 32 samples from MonoHandler's hard-coded A4 = 440 Hz glide**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:2108-2117 (with dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/mono_handler.h 305-308, 509-513)`
- **Also flagged by:** voice-management-midi, shared-dsp-contracts, spec-conformance

**Problem.** processBlockMono sets voices_[0].setFrequency(glidingFreq) for every 32-sample chunk, where glidingFreq = monoHandler_.processPortamento(). MonoHandler converts its semitone ramp with semitoneToFrequency() = kA4FrequencyHz * semitonesToRatio(s - 69), i.e. fixed 440 Hz, and applies no bend. NoteProcessor (which holds both the bend ratio and the 400-480 Hz tuning reference) is never consulted in the mono path; the only engine uses of bend/tuning are setPitchBend/setTuningReference forwarding and getFrequency in the poly path.

**Why it is wrong.** Pitch bend and A4 reference are global pitch settings and must apply in every voice mode. The poly path multiplies noteProcessor_.getFrequency (A4 ref * bend ratio); the mono path bypasses it.

**Consequence.** In Mono mode (the mode for leads/basses where bend is used most) the pitch wheel does nothing and a 432/442 Hz tuning reference is silently ignored, so a mono patch is out of tune with a poly patch in the same project.

**Suggested fix.** In processBlockMono multiply the glide frequency by noteProcessor_'s bend ratio and by (a4Reference/440), or give MonoHandler the reference and feed the semitone value through NoteProcessor. Test: Mono mode, tuning 432 Hz, bend +1 with range 2: voice frequency of note 69 must be 432*2^(2/12) after the smoother settles; compare to the poly path.

**Evidence.** ruinae_engine.h:2113-2117 `for (size_t s = 0; s < chunk; ++s) { glidingFreq = monoHandler_.processPortamento(); } voices_[0].setFrequency(glidingFreq);` ; mono_handler.h:511-512 `static float semitoneToFrequency(float semitones) noexcept { return kA4FrequencyHz * semitonesToRatio(semitones - static_cast<float>(kA4MidiNote));` ; grep of ruinae_engine.h for Bend/TuningReference: only lines 594-597, 842, 1617-1624. ruinae_engine_test.cpp:1054-1055 'tuning reference forwards' asserts nothing.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the mono path in the source, and the defect is real.

1. Mono render: in ruinae_engine.h:2108-2117, processBlockMono runs for each 32-sample chunk while voice 0 is active. It calls `glidingFreq = monoHandler_.processPortamento()` for every sample, then `voices_[0].setFrequency(glidingFreq)`. Nothing in this function reads noteProcessor_.

2. Where that frequency comes from: in mono_handler.h:305-310, processPortamento returns `semitoneToFrequency(portamentoRamp_.process())`. The Precise and Quantized glide branches also go through semitoneToFrequency (lines 505, 567, 586, 621). At lines 511-512 that function is `kA4FrequencyHz * semitonesToRatio(semitones - kA4MidiNote)`. The 440 Hz reference is fixed. MonoHandler has no setter for a tuning reference and no bend term; a grep for Reference and Bend in mono_handler.h finds only the spec comment.

3. The voice keeps whatever it is given: in ruinae_voice.h:304-308, setFrequency assigns `noteFrequency_ = freq` and calls updateOscFrequencies(). So each chunk replaces the bend- and tuning-aware frequency that dispatchMonoNoteOn set at ruinae_engine.h:1801-1809 with `noteProcessor_.getFrequency(note)`. That correct pitch lasts at most until the first chunk.

4. Contrast with poly: at ruinae_engine.h:2009-2014, "Step 7a: Update frequency with pitch bend" calls `voices_[i].setFrequency(noteProcessor_.getFrequency(voiceNote))` every block. Bend and tuning only reach the engine through setPitchBend (594-597), setPitchBendRange and setTuningReference (1617-1624), and processPitchBend (842). All of these feed noteProcessor_, which the mono render never reads. dispatchMonoNoteOff at 1824-1825 also uses monoHandler_.processPortamento().

Result: in Mono mode the pitch wheel has no audible effect after the first 32 samples, and any A4 reference other than 440 Hz is ignored. Pitch bend is a core performance control in mono lead and bass use, so I keep the severity at high. The tuning-reference part only shows when a user changes it from the 440 default.

**Note 2.** The defect is real, and I found nothing that guards it, documents it as intended, or tests it.

Mono path, plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:2108-2117: for each 32-sample chunk the code calls monoHandler_.processPortamento() and then voices_[0].setFrequency(glidingFreq). It never touches noteProcessor_.

The shared DSP header confirms the hard-coded reference. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/mono_handler.h:305-310, processPortamento() returns semitoneToFrequency(...), or the quantized or precise glide variants, which also use semitoneToFrequency (lines 505, 567, 586, 621). semitoneToFrequency at :511-512 is `kA4FrequencyHz * semitonesToRatio(semitones - kA4MidiNote)`. That is fixed at 440 Hz, and MonoHandler has no tuning or bend input (a grep for tuning in that header finds nothing).

The voice does not apply bend either. The only pitch entry in plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h is setFrequency at :304; a grep for bend in that file finds nothing.

NoteProcessor holds both missing factors. In note_processor.h:156-158, getFrequency = midiNoteToFrequency(note, a4Reference_) * currentBendRatio_, with a4Reference_ clamped to 400-480 Hz at :140.

The poly path applies them every block. ruinae_engine.h:2009-2014 is commented "Update frequency with pitch bend" and calls voices_[i].setFrequency(noteProcessor_.getFrequency(voiceNote)).

In mono mode the correct frequency survives only briefly. dispatchMonoNoteOn at :1801-1809 does use noteProcessor_.getFrequency, but processBlockMono overwrites it on the first chunk, so it lasts until the next chunk boundary at most.

The inputs are wired all the way in, so nothing upstream compensates. processor_midi.cpp:110 calls engine_.setPitchBend, and processor_params.cpp:766 and :769 forward the bend range and tuning reference. In the engine these reach only noteProcessor_ (:594-597, :1617-1624), and noteProcessor_.processPitchBend() runs once per block at :842. Every use of the result is in the poly path or at the mono note-on.

Nothing marks this as a design decision. MANUAL.md:1056-1058 describes Pitch Bend Range and Tuning Reference as global settings with no mono exception. No code comment calls the mono path bend-exempt, and specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json has no bend or tuning finding, so this is new, not a repeat of an F-id.

Result: in Mono mode the pitch wheel and a non-440 Hz tuning reference have no lasting effect on the sounding pitch. The high severity stands: a core performance control fails in the mode where it is used most.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. ruinae_engine.h:2108-2117: processBlockMono advances monoHandler_.processPortamento() through each 32-sample chunk and calls voices_[0].setFrequency(glidingFreq) unconditionally whenever voice 0 is active. mono_handler.h:305-310: processPortamento (ConstantTime) returns semitoneToFrequency(ramp), and :511-512 semitoneToFrequency = kA4FrequencyHz * semitonesToRatio(s - 69), so it is a fixed 440 Hz reference with no bend; the Precise/Quantized paths (:505, :567, :586, :621) use the same function. With portamento time 0 the ramp still returns the target, so it is not limited to glide settings. The bend and the A4 reference live only in NoteProcessor (note_processor.h:156-158 getFrequency = midiNoteToFrequency(note, a4Reference_) * currentBendRatio_). The engine calls getFrequency in the poly per-block update (ruinae_engine.h:2010-2014) and once at the mono note-on (:1801). The bend-aware frequency set at :1806/:1809 is overwritten by the first chunk at :2117 (at most 32 samples later). dispatchMonoNoteOff (:1824-1825) also uses the 440-based processPortamento. setPitchBend (:594-598) only feeds noteProcessor_. The processor's pitch-bend path goes processor_midi.cpp:110 -> engine_.setPitchBend, and the tuning path goes processor_params.cpp:769 -> setTuningReference; neither has a mono-specific route. RuinaeVoice has no global bend input; it only has per-note MPE expressionTuning (ruinae_voice.h:1167, :1600). No Ruinae test covers bend or tuning in mono mode (a grep of the tests for mono+bend/tuning found nothing). Impact: in Mono voice mode the pitch wheel has no audible effect at any range (a ±2 st default up to 24 st is lost). A 432 Hz reference leaves mono patches 31.8 cents sharp of poly patches, and 442 Hz leaves them 7.9 cents flat. This hits every host and sample rate as soon as voice mode is Mono. Losing a core performance control in the lead/bass mode justifies High.

</details>

### R-016

**SpectralFreeze oscillator goes permanently silent after any voice reset (setActive / host preset load)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** voice-signal-path · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/selectable_oscillator.h:114-119`
- **Also flagged by:** shared-dsp-contracts

**Problem.** SelectableOscillator::reset() calls active_->reset() unconditionally. When the active type is SpectralFreeze this reaches SpectralFreezeOscillator::reset(), which sets frozen_ = false (spectral_freeze_oscillator.h:187). processBlock then writes zeros for as long as frozen_ is false (:338-341). Only the adapter's prepare() re-freezes, via initSpectralFreeze (oscillator_adapters.h:135-137, 429-441). RuinaeVoice::reset() (ruinae_voice.h:198-200) resets both oscillators. RuinaeEngine::reset() (ruinae_engine.h:189-192) resets every voice and runs from Processor::setActive(true) (processor.cpp:206) and applyPresetSnapshot (processor_state.cpp:364). Re-selecting the same type afterwards is a no-op (selectable_oscillator.h:134-136), so nothing re-freezes it.

**Why it is wrong.** setType itself already refuses to reset SpectralFreeze because 'reset() would clear its frozen state' (selectable_oscillator.h:151-155). reset() breaks the same invariant. A voice reset should restore a playable state, not leave an oscillator type that outputs silence until the next sample-rate change.

**Consequence.** Patches that use SpectralFreeze on OSC A or OSC B lose that oscillator after any re-activation in which the type is still selected: a host transport restart, a bounce or render, a buffer-size change, or a bypass toggle in some hosts. Factory presets 'Frozen Spectral' (two SpectralFreeze oscillators, so fully silent) and 'Spectral Wash' (oscB.type = 8, tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:6913, 8604-8607) are affected. Loading a SpectralFreeze preset over another one through the host's setState also kills it. Measured with a standalone probe that compiles ruinae_voice.h against the built KrateDSP: RMS 0.69147 before voice.reset(), 0.00000 after reset + noteOn.

**Suggested fix.** Make the reset path preserve or re-arm the frozen spectrum. Options: OscillatorAdapter&lt;SpectralFreezeOscillator>::reset() re-runs initSpectralFreeze() (the freeze buffer is fixed-size, so this needs no allocation), or SpectralFreezeOscillator::reset() clears only phase/OLA state and keeps frozen_. Regression test (ruinae_voice_test or engine test): select SpectralFreeze, noteOn, render, voice.reset() (and engine.reset()), noteOn again, then REQUIRE RMS > 0.1. A processor-level variant does setActive(false)/setActive(true) with a SpectralFreeze preset.

**Evidence.** selectable_oscillator.h:115-118 `void reset() noexcept { if (active_) { active_->reset(); } }`; :151-155 'NOT for SpectralFreeze, which was freeze-initialized in prepare and reset() would clear its frozen state'; spectral_freeze_oscillator.h:187 `frozen_ = false;`, :338-341 `if (!frozen_) { std::fill_n(output, numSamples, 0.0f); return; }`; processor.cpp:206 `engine_.reset();` in setActive(true). Probe output: `P1 SpectralFreeze RMS before reset=0.69147 after reset=0.00000`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. I traced every link in the claimed path in source.

- **The oscillator reset.** `selectable_oscillator.h:115-119`: `reset()` calls `active_->reset()` with no type check. `setType` at :151-155 deliberately skips the reset for SpectralFreeze, because "reset() would clear its frozen state". So the code's own comment states the invariant that `reset()` breaks. Re-selecting the same type is a no-op (:134-136).
- **The adapter.** `oscillator_adapters.h:153-155`: `reset()` forwards straight to `osc_.reset()`, with no re-freeze. The only call to `initSpectralFreeze()` is in `prepare()` at :135-137, and that function (:429-441) is the only caller of `osc_.freeze()`.
- **The oscillator itself.** `spectral_freeze_oscillator.h:184-199`: `reset()` sets `frozen_ = false` and zeroes `frozenMagnitudes_`. `processBlock` at :337-341 then writes zeros whenever `!frozen_`.
- **The voice.** `ruinae_voice.h:198-200`: `reset()` calls `oscA_.reset()` and `oscB_.reset()`. Nothing else in `ruinae_voice.h` re-freezes; a grep for "freeze" finds no match. The voice only calls `prepare`, `processBlock`, `setType`, `setParam`, `setPhaseMode` and `setFrequency` on the oscillators (:135-136, 391-394, 639-668, 1610-1611).
- **The engine.** `ruinae_engine.h:189-191`: `reset()` resets every voice.
- **The processor.** `processor.cpp:206`: `setActive(true)` calls `engine_.reset()`. `processor_state.cpp:364`: `applyPresetSnapshot` calls `engine_.reset()` before the new parameters reach the engine. If the old and new presets both use SpectralFreeze, the later `setType` is a no-op and nothing re-arms the freeze.

**Host order makes it worse than "any re-activation".** `setupProcessing` (`processor.cpp:182`, `engine_.prepare`) re-freezes the spectrum, and the `setActive(true)` that follows (:206) clears it at once. So a buffer-size or sample-rate change, which runs setupProcessing and then setActive, also silences an oscillator that has SpectralFreeze selected.

**First activation is not affected.** On a fresh instance the active type is still the default when `setActive` runs. The non-active SpectralFreeze slot keeps its freeze from `prepare`, so selecting the type later works.

**No test covers reset followed by playback for this type.** The only SpectralFreeze reset test is the lifecycle test at `dsp/tests/unit/processors/spectral_freeze_oscillator_test.cpp:161`, which tests the raw oscillator.

The finding's quoted probe result (RMS 0.69 before the reset, 0.00 after) matches what the code does. High severity stands: a selected oscillator goes fully silent on a common host action and stays silent until the next prepare.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source. Nothing upstream guards it, and no code comment, spec or test makes it intentional.

1. dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/selectable_oscillator.h:115-119: reset() calls active_->reset() whatever the type is. The comment at :151-155 says SpectralFreeze must not be reset because "reset() would clear its frozen state", and setType at :153 skips it for that reason. reset() has no such guard. setType returns early when the type is unchanged (:134-136), so selecting the same type again does not re-arm the freeze.
2. oscillator_adapters.h:153-155: OscillatorAdapter::reset() just calls osc_.reset(). The only re-freeze is initSpectralFreeze() (:429-441), and only prepare() calls it (:135-137).
3. spectral_freeze_oscillator.h:184-207: reset() sets frozen_ = false and zeroes frozenMagnitudes_. processBlock (:337-341) then writes zeros while !frozen_. Only freeze() (:268) sets it back to true.
4. ruinae_voice.h:198-200: RuinaeVoice::reset() resets oscA_ and oscB_. ruinae_engine.h:189-192: RuinaeEngine::reset() resets every voice.
5. processor.cpp:203-206: setActive(true) calls engine_.reset(). processor.cpp:182: prepare runs only in setupProcessing. processor_state.cpp:364: applyPresetSnapshot also calls engine_.reset().

The normal VST3 order is setupProcessing (prepare, which freezes) and then setActive(true) (reset, which unfreezes). So when SpectralFreeze is the active OSC A/B type at activation, for example restored through setState, the oscillator is silent from the first activation onward, not only after a re-activation. The only voice reset() in tests is at ruinae_voice_test.cpp:119, and the SpectralFreeze cases in that file (:1666, 1754, 1838, 2179) do not appear to cover a reset while SpectralFreeze is active. No recovery path exists short of another setupProcessing (prepare). The quoted probe (RMS 0.69 before reset, 0.00 after) matches this code exactly. Severity "high" fits: a whole oscillator type, and factory presets built on it, go silent in normal host use.

**Note 3.** The defect is real, and I found no code path that refutes it. I traced the full chain in source.

1. dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/selectable_oscillator.h:115-119: reset() calls active_->reset() for any active type.
   - The SpectralFreeze exception exists only in setType (:151-155), whose comment says "reset() would clear its frozen state".
   - setType returns early when the type is unchanged (:134-136).
2. oscillator_adapters.h:153-155: the adapter's reset() forwards straight to osc_.reset().
   - Only prepare() re-freezes, through initSpectralFreeze() (:135-137, :429-441).
3. spectral_freeze_oscillator.h:187: reset() sets frozen_ = false.
   - It also zeroes frozenMagnitudes_ (:191).
   - processBlock then fills the output with zeros while !frozen_ (:338-341).
   - Nothing on the note path calls freeze() again.
4. plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:198-200: RuinaeVoice::reset() calls oscA_.reset() and oscB_.reset().
   - ruinae_engine.h:189-192: RuinaeEngine::reset() resets every voice.
5. The engine reset runs from two places:
   - processor.cpp:206, Processor::setActive(true).
   - processor_state.cpp:364, applyPresetSnapshot, where it runs before the new preset's type atomics are applied in process().

Impact check:
- setupProcessing (processor.cpp:182) calls engine_.prepare, which re-freezes every slot.
- SelectableOscillator::prepare keeps activeType_ (:105). So the usual VST3 sequence (setActive(false), setupProcessing, setActive(true)) re-freezes the slot and then kills it at once, whenever SpectralFreeze is the selected type at that moment. That sequence is used for offline bounces, buffer-size and sample-rate changes, and some hosts' bypass and transport handling.
- The first activation after instantiation is safe, because the type is still the default PolyBLEP when reset runs. setType(SpectralFreeze) later in process() skips the reset.
- After the slot is killed, switching away and back does not recover it. setType skips reset for SpectralFreeze but never re-freezes, so the oscillator stays silent until a prepare in which SpectralFreeze is not the active type at reset time. In practice it stays dead for the session.
- A preset load over a patch that already uses SpectralFreeze kills it the same way, because the reset hits the old type.

The quoted probe (RMS 0.69 before reset, 0.00 after) matches this code exactly. For a patch with SpectralFreeze on both oscillators, the voice outputs nothing at all, which is total loss of sound. High severity is justified, so no adjustment.

</details>

### R-017

**SpectralMorph mix mode delays the oscillator signal 1024 samples against the VCA and replays the previous note's tail at the next note-on**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** voice-signal-path · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:397-429, 539, 612-623, 369-372`

**Problem.** In SpectralMorph mode the oscillator mix passes through a 1024-point SpectralMorphFilter whose output is the input delayed by getLatencySamples() = fftSize = 1024 samples (spectral_morph_filter.h:244-246, 456-458; prepared at ruinae_voice.h:149). The amp envelope is not delayed: its value is stored per sample (output[i] = ampEnvVal, :539) and multiplied onto the delayed signal (:622-623). When the amp envelope reaches Idle the voice early-outs (:369-372) without draining the morph FIFO, and noteOn deliberately does not reset spectralMorph_ (:256-261). The last ~1024 samples of the previous note therefore sit in the FIFO and come out under the next note's attack.

**Why it is wrong.** The VCA, filter envelope and every per-sample modulation must act on the samples they were computed for. A 23 ms (44.1 kHz) offset means the attack shapes stale or empty FIFO content, and the real onset arrives after the attack has finished. A new note must not contain audio from the previous note.

**Consequence.** With a 1 ms attack, the onset in SpectralMorph mode comes at sample 1138, against 7 in CrossfadeMix (probe), so attacks shorter than ~23 ms do not shape the onset. The last 23 ms of every note is never heard. A second note whose inputs are silent (both OSC levels at 0) outputs RMS 0.697 over its first 1024 samples, which is the previous note replayed at full level, against 0.0148 in CrossfadeMix. Every note on a reused voice starts with a fragment of whatever that voice played before.

**Suggested fix.** Either reset spectralMorph_ (and the other FIFO stages) at noteOn when the voice was idle, or keep the voice alive until the FIFO has drained. Also delay the amp-envelope / VCA gain by the morph latency in SpectralMorph mode, for example with a 1024-sample gain delay line pre-allocated in prepare(). Regression test: SpectralMorph mode, note 1 at full level, release to idle, set both OSC levels to 0, note 2, then REQUIRE RMS of note 2's first 1024 samples &lt; 1e-3. A second test asserts that onset time in SpectralMorph equals onset time in CrossfadeMix within a few samples, or that the attack shape is preserved.

**Evidence.** ruinae_voice.h:425-429 `spectralMorph_->processBlock(oscABuffer_.data(), oscBBuffer_.data(), spectralMorphBuffer_.data(), numSamples); std::copy(... mixBuffer_.data());`; :539 `output[i] = ampEnvVal;`; :622-623 `const float ampLevel = output[i] * expressionVolume_; output[i] = sample * ampLevel;`; spectral_morph_filter.h:456-457 `return fftSize_;`. Probe: `P3 mode=Crossfade onset=7 ... note2(silent input) rms[0,1024)=0.01484` vs `P3 mode=SpectralMorph onset=1138 ... note2(silent input) rms[0,1024)=0.69747`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the claimed path through the source and it holds. I did not re-run the quoted probe.

(1) The latency is 1024 samples. ruinae_voice.h:149 calls spectralMorph_->prepare(sampleRate, 1024). In spectral_morph_filter.h, getLatencySamples() returns fftSize_ (:456-457). processBlock pushes each hop into blockFifo_ and pops exactly numSamples per call (:290-315). popBlockFifo (:516-528) outputs warmupRemaining_ = fftSize_ zeros after a reset (resetBlockFifo :501-507), then FIFO content. So in SpectralMorph mode, mixBuffer_ (ruinae_voice.h:425-429) holds the oscillator mix delayed by 1024 samples.

(2) The VCA is not delayed. The amp envelope is advanced per sample on the current timeline (:464), stored as output[i] = ampEnvVal (:539), and multiplied onto the delayed sample at :622-623. No delay compensation exists in the voice.

(3) Stale content survives into the next note.
- processBlock early-outs when !ampEnv_.isActive() (:369-372), before spectralMorph_->processBlock. The STFT input buffers and the output FIFO are frozen with the last ~1024 samples of oscillator input.
- That content is pre-VCA, at oscillator level: the OSC levels are applied to the inputs (:417-422), but the amp envelope is not.
- noteOn (:227-288) resets the LFO and TranceGate but never spectralMorph_. setMixMode (:718-720) does not reset it either.
- The engine calls voices_[i].noteOn(freq, vel) directly without voice.reset() (ruinae_engine.h:1738 poly, :1806 mono). voice.reset() is called only from the engine's reset path (:191).
- Result: the first ~1024 output samples of the next note on that voice are the previous note's oscillator tail, scaled by the new attack envelope. With a short attack and sustain 1 they come out at full level. This is consistent with the quoted RMS of 0.697 for note 2 with silent inputs.

(4) There is no test covering this. The [spectral-morph] tests in ruinae_voice_test.cpp (:1244-1440, :2431) only skip the warm-up latency and compare RMS; none checks onset alignment with the amp envelope or replay across notes.

Mitigating point: the base latency is acknowledged in a test comment (:1271), so the VCA-misalignment half could be called an accepted design limitation. The stale-tail replay is unambiguously a bug (audio from the previous note at full oscillator level on every reused voice), so high severity stands.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this. The source confirms each step of the mechanism, and nothing upstream guards against it.

1. **The morph output is delayed by 1024 samples.** spectral_morph_filter.h:244-250 says the output is "the morphed stream delayed by exactly getLatencySamples()". Each frame's hop is pushed into blockFifo_ at :307-312 and popped per chunk at :315. getLatencySamples() returns fftSize_ at :456-457, and the voice prepares it with 1024 at ruinae_voice.h:149.

2. **The VCA is not delayed.** The amp envelope value is stored per sample at ruinae_voice.h:539 (`output[i] = ampEnvVal`). It is multiplied onto the morph-delayed mixBuffer_ at :622-623 with no compensating delay. The mixBuffer_ is filled from spectralMorphBuffer_ at :425-429.

3. **The FIFO is not drained or cleared between notes.** processBlock returns early when the amp envelope is idle (:369-372), so it never processes again and the FIFO keeps its contents. noteOn (:227-288) resets the LFO and the TranceGate but not spectralMorph_. spectralMorph_->reset() is called only from prepare() (:187) and voice reset() (:204). setMixMode (:718-720) does not reset it either.

4. **The engine does not reset a reused voice.** dispatchPolyNoteOn calls `voices_[event.voiceIndex].noteOn(freq, vel)` directly (ruinae_engine.h:1738). The engine's other voice.reset() call (:191) sits in its own reset path, not in note dispatch.

5. **The stale content comes out at full level.** The FIFO holds the pre-VCA oscillator mix, so the previous note's last ~1024 samples come out under the new note's attack at full level. This matches the quoted probe: RMS 0.697 in SpectralMorph against 0.0148 in CrossfadeMix.

**Context lens.** The CHANGELOG (plugins/ruinae/CHANGELOG.md:22) documents only that the mixer "plays every sample, always 1024 samples (23 ms at 44.1 kHz) behind the oscillators". The test comments at ruinae_voice_test.cpp:1271, :1528 and ruinae_engine_integration_test.cpp:1780 do the same: they acknowledge the latency and warm up past it. No document, comment or test treats these as intended:
- the amp envelope being misaligned with the delayed signal;
- the previous note replaying at the next note-on.

The voice test at :1255-1291 skips 44100 warm-up samples, so it cannot catch either effect. Several factory presets use the SpectralMorph mixer (specs/ruinae-preset-redesign/plan-*.md), so this is reachable in a real host.

**Severity stays high.** Every reused voice in this mode starts with a 23 ms fragment of an earlier note, and attacks shorter than ~23 ms no longer shape the onset.

**Note 3.** The defect is real, and it has the claimed impact at the claimed severity.

(1) The latency is real. SpectralMorphFilter::processBlock (dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/spectral_morph_filter.h:251-318) pushes the input into the STFTs, writes each finished hop into blockFifo_, and pops numSamples per call. popBlockFifo (:516-528) outputs warmupRemaining_ = fftSize_ zeros after a reset (:506), so output n = input n-1024. getLatencySamples() returns fftSize_ (:456-457). The voice prepares the filter at 1024 (ruinae_voice.h:148-149).

(2) The VCA is not delayed. The amp-envelope value is stored per sample in output[i] (ruinae_voice.h:539) and multiplied onto the morph output, which comes from :425-429 and passes through the filter, distortion and DC blocker (:612-623). Nothing compensates for the morph latency, so the attack shape is applied to samples that are 1024 samples older.

(3) Stale state carries over to the next note. processBlock returns early when !ampEnv_.isActive() (:369-372), so the STFT input rings, the OverlapAdd buffer and blockFifo_ are frozen, still holding the last ~1024 pre-VCA oscillator samples of the previous note. noteOn (:227-288) resets only the LFO and the trance gate, never spectralMorph_. The only resets are in voice.reset() (:204) and prepare (:187). The engine calls voice.reset() only from RuinaeEngine::reset() (ruinae_engine.h:189-191), not when a voice is allocated or stolen.

(4) How audible it is. On the next note the stale samples come out first. They are raw oscillator output at full level: the previous note's release envelope was applied after the morph, so it never touched the samples still in the FIFO. The new attack ramps the VCA open over them. With a short attack (1 ms is about 44 samples), roughly the first 23 ms (1024 samples at 44.1 kHz, 5.3 ms at 192 kHz) of every note on a reused voice plays the previous note's pitch or timbre at nearly full level. The quoted probe RMS of 0.697 for a silent-input note 2, against 0.0148 in Crossfade mode, fits a full-scale saw/morph signal. The real onset arrives about 1024 samples late (probe: sample 1138 vs 7), so attacks shorter than ~23 ms do not shape it. The filter-envelope and per-sample cutoff modulation (:519-536) are likewise misaligned with the signal by 1024 samples.

(5) Who hits it. Kicking in once each of the 16 voices has played a note, it affects anyone who selects Mixer Mode = SpectralMorph (kMixerModeId, a user-facing dropdown) and plays more than 16 notes, or fewer in mono mode, where one voice is reused for every note. No existing test resets the morph or checks for stale content at note-on. The Crossfade&lt;->SpectralMorph steps at audit_probes.cpp:1350-1355 test mode switching, not reuse.

The severity stays high: a guaranteed, audible ~23 ms fragment of the previous note at full level at every reused-voice note-on in a shipped mix mode, plus a 1024-sample envelope misalignment.

</details>

### R-018

**Note velocity never reaches the VCA: loudness ignores velocity, the velocity curve and arp velocity/accent lanes**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** voice-signal-path · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:233, 470-479, 621-623`
- **Also flagged by:** voice-signal-path, spec-conformance

**Problem.** The engine computes the voice velocity as noteProcessor_.mapVelocity(vel).amplitude (ruinae_engine.h:1736-1738, 1802-1803) and passes it to voice.noteOn(freq, vel). The voice stores velocity_ (:233) and uses it only as a mod-router source (:476) and in the self-oscillating filter's noteOn (:281-282). The VCA is ampEnv * expressionVolume_ (:622). The amp envelope never gets velocity scaling either: no setVelocity/setVelocityScaling call exists anywhere under plugins/ruinae/src (grep finds none).

**Why it is wrong.** MANUAL.md:1008 says the arp Velocity lane 'Determines how hard each note is played', and MANUAL.md:1057 documents a Velocity Curve setting that maps MIDI velocity. Both assume velocity affects level. A synth whose amplitude ignores key velocity by default, with no velocity-to-amp destination in the per-voice matrix (VoiceModDest has no Amp/VCA destination), cannot play dynamically.

**Consequence.** Every note plays at the same level whatever its velocity. The Velocity Curve parameter, the arp Velocity lane, Accent Velocity and Humanize velocity are inaudible unless the user builds a per-voice route from Velocity to a timbral destination, and even then the level stays the same. The SelfOscillating filter is the only path where velocity changes level, so filter types behave inconsistently.

**Suggested fix.** Apply velocity at the VCA, for example ampLevel = ampEnv * lerp(1, velocity_, velSensitivity) * expressionVolume_, or enable ADSREnvelope velocity scaling for the amp envelope with a 'Velocity -> Amp' sensitivity parameter (default 100% to match the manual). Regression test: two noteOns at velocity 127 and 32 with otherwise identical settings must differ in steady-state RMS by the expected curve ratio.

**Evidence.** ruinae_voice.h:233 `velocity_ = std::clamp(velocity, 0.0f, 1.0f);`, :622 `const float ampLevel = output[i] * expressionVolume_;`; ruinae_engine.h:1736-1738 `float vel = noteProcessor_.mapVelocity(...).amplitude; voices_[event.voiceIndex].noteOn(freq, vel);`; grep `VelocityScaling|setVelocity\(` under plugins/ruinae/src finds no matches; MANUAL.md:1008 'Determines how hard each note is played'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the claim through the source and could not refute it.

1. Engine to voice. ruinae_engine.h:1736-1738 (poly) and :1802-1806 (mono) compute `vel = noteProcessor_.mapVelocity(...).amplitude` and pass it to `voices_[i].noteOn(freq, vel)`. Poly legato (:1771-1775) passes no velocity at all, only a glide.
2. Inside the voice. ruinae_voice.h:233 stores `velocity_ = clamp(velocity,0,1)`. It is read in only two places:
   - :476, as the `velocity_` argument to `modRouter_.computeOffsets`.
   - :281-282, the SelfOscillating filter's noteOn.
   The amp envelope is gated at :274 with no velocity. Its value is copied into `output[i]` at :464/:539, and the VCA at :622-623 is `ampLevel = output[i] * expressionVolume_; output[i] = sample * ampLevel`. `expressionVolume_` is reset to 1.0 on every noteOn (:250) and changes only through MPE kVolumeTypeID (:1174).
3. Shared ADSR. dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/adsr_envelope.h:543 sets `velocityScalingEnabled_ = false` by default, and :443 sets `peakLevel_ = velocityScalingEnabled_ ? velocity_ : 1.0f`. A grep for `setVelocityScaling|setVelocity(` under plugins/ finds calls only in Membrum (drum_voice.h:163/436) and none anywhere in Ruinae. So the amp envelope always peaks at 1.0.
4. Downstream. In the engine voice loop (ruinae_engine.h:2018-2028) the voice output is multiplied only by the pan gains. processor_midi.cpp:93-101 passes velocity straight into engine_.noteOn and applies no velocity gain anywhere else.

Result: with no per-voice route configured, loudness does not depend on note velocity, and so it does not depend on the Velocity Curve or the arp velocity/accent lanes either. The only exception is the SelfOscillating filter type.

Small correction to the finding: there is no Amp/VCA destination, but a user can still make velocity change level by routing Velocity to the OscALevel or OscBLevel destination. ruinae_voice.h:495-503 implements this and ruinae_voice_test.cpp:2101-2127 exercises it. That is a workaround that has to be configured by hand, not a default. The core defect stands.

No test asserts that velocity changes level. ruinae_voice_test.cpp:1070 checks only velocity to filter cutoff, and ruinae_engine_integration_test.cpp:626 merely comments "Low velocity" without asserting anything about level. The prior audit (specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json) has no matching finding, so this is not a repeat. specs/Ruinae.md:159 says only "Consider adding velocity scaling option"; nothing documents a deliberate choice to ignore velocity. MANUAL.md:1008 ("Determines how hard each note is played") and :1057 (Velocity Curve) describe velocity-dependent dynamics that the code does not deliver. I see no reason to change the high severity: by default every note plays at the same level, whatever its velocity.

**Note 2.** The defect is real. I found no clamp, no other code path and no documented design decision that gives velocity a fixed effect on loudness.

- **Voice:** ruinae_voice.h:233 stores `velocity_`. It is read only at :281-282 (SelfOscillating filter noteOn) and :476 (`modRouter_.computeOffsets`, as a mod source). The VCA at :539 takes `output[i] = ampEnvVal`, and :622-623 applies `ampLevel = output[i] * expressionVolume_`, with `expressionVolume_` reset to 1.0 at :250.
- **Envelope:** the shared ADSREnvelope supports velocity scaling (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/adsr_envelope.h:217-224, :443 `peakLevel_ = velocityScalingEnabled_ ? velocity_ : 1.0f`). It defaults off (:543 `velocityScalingEnabled_ = false`), and nothing in the voice turns it on. The voice only sets attack, decay, sustain and release at :156-160.
- **Engine:** in ruinae_engine.h, velocity is used only at :1736-1737 and :1802-1803 (`mapVelocity(...).amplitude`, passed to `voice.noteOn`) and at :245 (Transient source). Nothing scales the voice sum by velocity.
- **Mod destinations:** VoiceModDest (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_mod_types.h:50-62) has no Amp/VCA destination.
- **No design decision says otherwise:**
  - The retired spec 041 FR-020 (specs/_archive2_/041-ruinae-voice-architecture/spec.md:205) only says the VCA is `output *= ampEnv.process()`. The code matches it, but it does not say velocity must not change loudness.
  - specs/Ruinae.md:159 says "Consider adding velocity scaling option", which was never done.
  - MANUAL.md:1008 says the Velocity lane "Determines how hard each note is played".
  - The preset generator assumes velocity changes level. tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:438 reads "Rising velocity lane -> genuine crescendo as the arp ascends", but that preset only adds a Velocity->FilterResonance route (:447), so with this code it has no crescendo.
- **Tests:** none checks loudness against velocity. The only velocity tests check the filter-cutoff route (ruinae_voice_test.cpp:1070), the OscLevel routes (:2101-2127) and that the curve setting is forwarded (ruinae_engine_test.cpp:1059).

One correction to the finding: "even then the level stays the same" is overstated. A user can set the OSC A/B level to 0 and route Velocity -> OscALevel/OscBLevel at +1, because the voice computes `effectiveOscALevel = clamp(oscALevel_ + offset)` (ruinae_voice.h:496-506). That does make level follow velocity, but before the filter and distortion, so it is not a clean VCA. By default, every factory preset and every note ignores velocity for loudness. Severity stays as stated.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. ruinae_voice.h:233 stores `velocity_` and nothing else. Velocity is read in three places only: the self-oscillating filter's noteOn (:281-282), the mod-router source argument (:476), and reset (:191/:211). The amp envelope is gated with no velocity (:274, a grep finds no setVelocity call in the voice), its value is stored in output[i] (:539), and the VCA is `ampLevel = output[i] * expressionVolume_` (:622-623). expressionVolume_ is reset to 1.0 at noteOn (:250) and is only set by MPE Volume (:1174).

The engine applies no velocity gain either. ruinae_engine.h:1736-1737 and :1802-1803 pass the mapped velocity only into voice.noteOn. The poly mix at :2018-2028 multiplies by pan gains only, and the mono path (:2119) uses the same voice.

The impact is real. A velocity-127 note and a velocity-32 note play at the same level (0 dB difference, where a linear velocity-to-amp mapping would give about 12 dB). The Velocity Curve (engine :1627), the arp Velocity and Accent lanes and Humanize velocity are therefore inaudible as loudness on the internal engine. Factory presets assume otherwise. tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:440-447 builds a rising velocity lane ("velRise8") and comments "Velocity adds resonance bite so the crescendo ALSO sharpens tonally". That only adds timbre to a crescendo that never happens in level. MANUAL.md:1008 ("Determines how hard each note is played") contradicts the behaviour.

One sub-claim is overstated. The finding says that even with a per-voice route the level stays the same. That is wrong. VoiceModDest has OscALevel and OscBLevel (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_mod_types.h:58-59), and the voice applies them as `clamp(oscALevel_ + offset, 0, 1)` (ruinae_voice.h:496-506). A user who lowers the osc level and routes Velocity -> OscA/B Level does get velocity-dependent level. So a workaround exists, but it is not the default, and with the default osc level of 1.0 a positive amount saturates. Arp velocity also still reaches the MIDI output bus for external synths.

The core defect stands: by default, and in every factory preset, the internal synth ignores velocity. That is significant for a playable instrument, so the high severity is reasonable.

</details>

### R-030

**Ruinae has no IMidiMapping: pitch bend, channel aftertouch and every MIDI CC never reach the plugin in AU or SDK-conforming VST3 hosts**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_midi.cpp:245-248`

**Problem.** The only path for pitch bend is onPitchBend, which the shared dispatcher calls for Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent. The VST3 SDK defines that event as OUTPUT-only. VST3 hosts and the SDK's own AU wrapper deliver pitch bend, channel pressure and CCs only as parameter changes through IMidiMapping::getMidiControllerAssignment. Ruinae's controller does not implement IMidiMapping (no hit anywhere under plugins/ruinae/src), so those messages are dropped before they reach Ruinae. Nothing calls engine_.setAftertouch either, so the per-voice 'Aftertouch' mod source offered in the voice matrix is always 0. There is also no kPolyPressureEvent handling.

**Why it is wrong.** Per ivstevents.h:127, LegacyMIDICCOutEvent 'is reserved for generating MIDI CC as output event'. Input controllers are mapped through IMidiMapping, which Profundum, Vorago and Disrumpo implement (profundum controller.cpp:918-939 maps kPitchBend to kPitchBendId). The AU wrapper drops pitch bend and aftertouch when midiMappingCache is empty (auwrapper.mm:2231-2258).

**Consequence.** The pitch-bend wheel does nothing in Logic and GarageBand (AU) and in hosts that follow the SDK. The 'Pitch Bend Range' setting (MANUAL.md:1056) has no audible effect there. The Aftertouch voice mod source (mod_matrix_types.h:217) is permanently dead. The sustain pedal and mod wheel are ignored. The MPE tests call proc.onPitchBend() directly, so none of this is covered.

**Suggested fix.** Implement Vst::IMidiMapping on the Ruinae controller. Map kPitchBend and kAfterTouch (and optionally the mod wheel) to hidden, automatable, non-persisted parameter IDs. Handle them in processParameterChanges by calling engine_.setPitchBend(2*v-1) and engine_.setAftertouch(v); use each point's sample offset or the timed queue. Consider handling kPolyPressureEvent per note. Tests: (1) getMidiControllerAssignment(0, 0, kPitchBend) returns kResultOk and an ID; (2) a parameter change on that ID moves the rendered pitch of a held A4 by the bend range (FFT peak within 1 Hz of 440*2^(2/12)); (3) a parameter change on kAfterTouch drives a voice route Aftertouch -> FilterCutoff.

**Evidence.** processor_midi.cpp:245-248 `void Processor::onPitchBend(float bipolar) { queueTimedEvent(... PitchBend ...)}`; midi_event_dispatcher.h:149-159 pitch bend decoded only from `case Steinberg::Vst::Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent`; ivstevents.h:127 'This kind of event is reserved for generating MIDI CC as output event'; grep 'IMidiMapping|getMidiControllerAssignment' in plugins/ruinae/src finds nothing (it hits disrumpo/profundum/vorago/shared midi_cc_manager); auwrapper.mm:2231-2232 `if (midiMappingCache.empty ()) return result;` before `case kPitchBendStatus` / `case kAfterTouchStatus`; grep 'setAftertouch' finds only ruinae_engine.h:602 (definition) and ruinae_voice.h:1149, so there is no caller.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The finding holds up against the source.

1. **Only pitch-bend input path.** In processor_midi.cpp:51-66, processEvents hands each event to Krate::Plugins::dispatchMidiEvents. onPitchBend (processor_midi.cpp:245-248) is the only producer of TimedEventKind::PitchBend, and applyTimedEvent (lines 109-110) turns that into engine_.setPitchBend. The shared dispatcher decodes pitch bend only under `case Steinberg::Vst::Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent` (midi_event_dispatcher.h:149-159).

2. **That event is output-only by spec.** extern/vst3sdk/pluginterfaces/vst/ivstevents.h:127 says: "This kind of event is reserved for generating MIDI CC as output event for kEvent Bus during the process call."

3. **No IMidiMapping in Ruinae.** A grep for IMidiMapping, getMidiControllerAssignment and kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent under plugins/ruinae finds only the new audit probe (tests/audit/audit_probes.cpp:183). The Controller class (controller.h:72-74) derives from EditControllerEx1, VST3EditorDelegate and IControlListener. Its DEFINE_INTERFACES block (controller.h:220-223) exposes only IEditController and IEditController2. plugin_ids.h has no parameter for pitch bend, aftertouch or mod wheel; the only related ID is kSettingsPitchBendRangeId=2200 (line 750).

4. **AU wrapper drops these messages without a mapping.** auwrapper.mm:2231 returns early when midiMappingCache is empty. That check comes before the kPitchBendStatus case (line 2242) and the kAfterTouchStatus case (line 2253). The CC paths at lines 2375, 2391 and 2399 are gated the same way.

5. **Aftertouch is never set.** setAftertouch exists only as definitions: ruinae_engine.h:602 forwards to ruinae_voice.h:1149, which writes aftertouch_. The voice reads that value at ruinae_voice.h:478, but nothing in plugins/ruinae/src calls setAftertouch. The voice therefore always sees 0. engine.setModWheel (ruinae_engine.h:612) also has no caller from the processor.

**Severity.** Some hosts do send legacy CC events as input, so the effect depends on the host. It is total in AU hosts (Logic, GarageBand) and in VST3 hosts that follow the SDK and route these messages through IMidiMapping. Pitch bend is a core synth control and the Aftertouch mod source is dead everywhere, so "high" is appropriate.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. Every link in the claim checks out in the code:
- processor_midi.cpp:245-248: onPitchBend queues a PitchBend TimedEvent, and applyTimedEvent (line 109-110) calls engine_.setPitchBend. That is the only path pitch bend takes to the engine. processEvents (line 51-68) hands every event to Krate::Plugins::dispatchMidiEvents.
- plugins/shared/src/midi/midi_event_dispatcher.h:149-163: pitch bend is decoded only from `case Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent` with controlNumber == kPitchBend. The dispatcher has no kPolyPressureEvent case, and no aftertouch or CC case other than pitch bend; those events fall to default, which does nothing.
- extern/vst3sdk/pluginterfaces/vst/ivstevents.h:127: "This kind of event is reserved for generating MIDI CC as output event for kEvent Bus during the process call."
- extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/auwrapper/auwrapper.mm:2231-2232: `if (midiMappingCache.empty ()) return result;` comes before `case kPitchBendStatus` (2242) and `case kAfterTouchStatus` (2253). In the AU build, pitch bend and channel pressure are therefore dropped unless the controller provides an IMidiMapping. The wrapper turns poly pressure into kPolyPressureEvent (2220-2227), but Ruinae's dispatcher ignores that event too.
- Grepping plugins/ for IMidiMapping or getMidiControllerAssignment finds hits in vorago, profundum, disrumpo and shared midi_cc_manager, and none under plugins/ruinae/src.
- Grepping for setAftertouch finds only the definitions (ruinae_engine.h:602, ruinae_voice.h:1149) and unit tests that call the engine or voice directly (ruinae_engine_test.cpp:959, ruinae_voice_test.cpp:1884, ...). No processor code calls it, so the voice Aftertouch mod source is always 0 in the plugin.
- No design decision covers this: there is no hit for IMidiMapping or LegacyMIDICC in specs/Ruinae.md, ruinae-roadmap.md, arpeggiator-roadmap.md or specs/ruinae-*. The prior audit's findings.json has no pitch-bend or aftertouch finding, so this is new and not a repeat of an F-id.

Some VST3 hosts (Reaper, for example) do send legacy CC events as input, so pitch bend works there. That does not change the result for the AU wrapper (Logic, GarageBand) or for hosts that follow the SDK and only use IMidiMapping. High severity stands: the pitch wheel is a core synth control, and the Aftertouch mod source cannot be reached at all.

**Note 3.** I could not refute this finding. Each link in the claim checks out in the source.

1. **Pitch bend has only one input path, and it is the output-only event.** processor_midi.cpp:51-66 sends every host event through Krate::Plugins::dispatchMidiEvents. In plugins/shared/src/midi/midi_event_dispatcher.h:149-163 the only branch that decodes pitch bend is `case Steinberg::Vst::Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent` with controlNumber == kPitchBend, which then calls onPitchBend (processor_midi.cpp:245-248). The SDK says this event is output-only: extern/vst3sdk/pluginterfaces/vst/ivstevents.h:127 reads "This kind of event is reserved for generating MIDI CC as output event for kEvent Bus during the process call."

2. **No IMidiMapping exists.** I grepped `IMidiMapping|getMidiControllerAssignment|kPitchBend` under plugins/ruinae. It finds nothing in src/. The only hit is the audit probe at tests/audit/audit_probes.cpp:184, which injects the legacy event directly. controller.h:72-74 declares `class Controller : public Steinberg::Vst::EditControllerEx1, public VSTGUI::VST3EditorDelegate, public VSTGUI::IControlListener`, with no IMidiMapping.

3. **The AU wrapper drops the messages.** In auwrapper.mm, poly pressure is turned into an event at lines 2222-2228. After that, `if (midiMappingCache.empty ()) return result;` at 2231-2232 returns before the kPitchBendStatus case (2242) and the kAfterTouchStatus case (2253) can run. Ruinae has no mapping, so its cache is empty, and pitch bend, channel pressure and all CCs are discarded in Logic and GarageBand. Poly pressure does arrive as a kPolyPressureEvent, but the dispatcher's switch has no case for it (default: break at line 165), so it is ignored too.

4. **Aftertouch is never fed.** The grep for setAftertouch finds only the definitions (ruinae_engine.h:602-606 and ruinae_voice.h:1149) and unit tests. No processor code calls it, so the voice Aftertouch mod source always reads 0.

5. **The documented feature does nothing.** MANUAL.md:1056 documents "Pitch Bend Range | Range of the MIDI pitch bend wheel in semitones". The only integration coverage is mpe_test.cpp:357-384, which calls t.proc.onPitchBend() directly and skips the host path.

**Impact.** The pitch wheel is silently dead, not wrong by a few cents. The bend is missing in full: with the default range, ±2 semitones (±200 cents). This is certain in every AU host, because of the wrapper code above. It also applies to VST3 hosts that send controllers as parameter changes through IMidiMapping, as the SDK specifies; hosts do not normally send kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent as input. Per-note MPE tuning via NoteExpression still works, so MPE controllers keep per-note bend.

**Severity.** High stands. Pitch bend is a basic synthesizer feature and is documented in the manual. The part about the mod wheel and sustain pedal is weaker: Ruinae never claims to support them, and grep finds no mod-wheel or sustain handling at all. That part is a missing feature, not a regression. The pitch bend and aftertouch failure alone justifies high.

**Prior audit.** specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json does not mention IMidiMapping or pitch bend, so this is a new finding, not a repeat of an F-id.

</details>

### R-031

**Mono 'Portamento Time' is dead: applyArpParams overwrites it every block with the arp Slide Time (60 ms default)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:780, 1032`
- **Also flagged by:** shared-dsp-contracts, duplication-drift, spec-conformance, gestalt-processor

**Problem.** applyAuxModSourceParams (called at :261) sets engine_.setPortamentoTime(monoModeParams_.portamentoTimeMs). applyArpParams runs next (:262) and unconditionally calls engine_.setPortamentoTime(arpParams_.slideTime), whatever the arp mode. RuinaeEngine::setPortamentoTime writes the MonoHandler's glide time and every voice's portamento time. The last writer wins, so the mono glide always uses Slide Time.

**Why it is wrong.** The Mono Portamento Time parameter (0-5000 ms, default 0, mono_mode_params.h:19) must control mono glide. Arp slide time should only govern arp slide steps, and only when the arp dispatches notes.

**Consequence.** Out of the box (arp Off, portamento 0), Mono mode glides 60 ms on every overlapping note: hadNotesHeld makes enableGlide true (mono_handler.h:204-206). The user cannot remove the glide or lengthen it with the Portamento knob; only the hidden arp Slide Time changes it.

**Suggested fix.** Keep two separate times. The MonoHandler gets the mono portamento; RuinaeVoice::setPortamentoTime (poly legato slide) gets slideTime. If arp slide in Mono must use slideTime, pass the time with the legato note-on instead of overwriting the global. Test: a processor test with Mono mode, portamento 0 and arp Off. Hold 60 and press 72: the rendered pitch reaches 72 within 1 ms (no 60 ms glide). With portamento 500 ms, the pitch at 250 ms is between the two notes.

**Evidence.** processor_params.cpp:261-262 `applyAuxModSourceParams(); applyArpParams();`; :780 `engine_.setPortamentoTime(monoModeParams_.portamentoTimeMs.load(...));` (inside applyAuxModSourceParams, starting :748); :1032 `engine_.setPortamentoTime(arpParams_.slideTime.load(...));` (applyArpParams :832, no mode check); ruinae_engine.h:1588-1594 sets monoHandler_ and all voices; arpeggiator_params.h:99 `slideTime{60.0f}`; mono_mode_params.h:19 `portamentoTimeMs{0.0f}`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Confirmed from source. processor.cpp:251 calls applyParamsToEngine() on every process() block, without condition. processor_params.cpp:261-262 calls applyAuxModSourceParams() and then applyArpParams(). Line :780, inside applyAuxModSourceParams (starts :748), calls engine_.setPortamentoTime(monoModeParams_.portamentoTimeMs). Line :1032, inside applyArpParams (starts :832), calls engine_.setPortamentoTime(arpParams_.slideTime). That call is not inside the `arpOpModeParam != kArpOff` branch at :868-869 and is not gated by a change check, so it runs every block whatever the arp mode is. The comment at :1031 says "Forward slide time to engine for both Poly and Mono portamento (FR-034)". ruinae_engine.h:1588-1595 writes monoHandler_.setPortamentoTime(ms) and each voice's setPortamentoTime(ms), so slideTime is always the last value written. The engine uses the MonoHandler glide at ruinae_engine.h:1824 and :2115 (monoHandler_.processPortamento()). In mono_handler.h:202-212, every note after the first glides when notes overlap (hadNotesHeld). With PortaMode::Always it also glides on staccato notes, and Always is the default: mono_mode_params.h:20 portaMode{0}, and mono_handler.h:709 sets PortaMode::Always. updatePortamentoTarget (:496-501) glides whenever portamentoTimeMs_ > 0. The defaults are mono_mode_params.h:19 portamentoTimeMs{0.0f} and arp slideTime 60 ms, so with the arp Off the mono glide is 60 ms instead of 0 and the Mono Portamento Time knob has no effect. No test covers the knob's effect: param_flow_test.cpp:152 only checks that kMonoPortamentoTimeId does not crash, and arp_integration_test.cpp checks only the arp core's slide time. This is a real user-facing bug in a core mono-synth control, so the high severity stands.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. The source confirms it, and no clamp, mode gate, test or documentation makes it intentional.

1. The call order is fixed. processor.cpp:251 calls applyParamsToEngine() on every process() block. processor_params.cpp:261-262 runs applyAuxModSourceParams() and then applyArpParams(), in that order.
2. The first write is the mono Portamento value. processor_params.cpp:780 calls engine_.setPortamentoTime(monoModeParams_.portamentoTimeMs).
3. The second write is the arp Slide Time, and it runs whatever the arp mode is. processor_params.cpp:1032 calls engine_.setPortamentoTime(arpParams_.slideTime), commented "Forward slide time to engine for both Poly and Mono portamento (FR-034)". It sits outside the `arpOpModeParam != kArpOff` branch (:869-964), so nothing gates it on the arp mode.
4. The engine applies the time to both mono and poly paths. ruinae_engine.h:1588-1594 writes monoHandler_.setPortamentoTime(ms) and also every voice's setPortamentoTime. The last writer wins, so the MonoHandler always holds slideTime.
5. The mono path glides with that time. mono_handler.h:203-206: overlapping notes set enableGlide = true whatever the PortaMode. updatePortamentoTarget (:496-501) then glides whenever portamentoTimeMs_ > 0, so with the default 60 ms Slide Time it glides even when Portamento is 0. ruinae_engine.h:2115 drives voice 0 from monoHandler_.processPortamento().
6. The defaults match the finding: mono_mode_params.h:19 sets portamentoTimeMs to 0, and the finding cites arpeggiator_params.h:99 for slideTime 60.

Context check:
- The FR-034 comment covers forwarding Slide Time for arp slide steps. It does not say the mono Portamento knob is meant to be overridden.
- MANUAL.md:262 describes Portamento as "Glide time between notes (0 = instant...)". MANUAL.md:1033 describes Slide Time as "Portamento time for steps marked as slides". So the documented design contradicts the code.
- No test pins the current behaviour. param_flow_test.cpp:152 only sends kMonoPortamentoTimeId and checks there is no crash. arp_integration_test.cpp checks Slide Time on the arp core only.
- The prior audit (specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json) has no matching finding, so this is not a repeat of an F-id; its only portamento entry is the unrelated stale-glide-on-voice-reuse issue.

Net effect: the user-facing mono Portamento knob does nothing. Mono legato always glides at Slide Time, 60 ms by default. The defect is real, and high severity fits.

**Note 3.** The defect is real and has the claimed consequence. Mono mode can never use the Portamento Time knob, and with default settings it glides 60 ms on every note after the first.

Evidence:
- processor.cpp:251 calls applyParamsToEngine() on every process() block.
- processor_params.cpp:248-263 runs applyAuxModSourceParams() at :261 and then applyArpParams() at :262.
- processor_params.cpp:780 calls engine_.setPortamentoTime(monoModeParams_.portamentoTimeMs).
- processor_params.cpp:1032 then calls engine_.setPortamentoTime(arpParams_.slideTime) with no check of arp enable or mode. The comment above it reads "Forward slide time to engine for both Poly and Mono portamento (FR-034)".
- ruinae_engine.h:1588-1595 writes that time to monoHandler_.setPortamentoTime and to every voice. The arp value is written last, so it is the one in effect when the block renders.
- The mono render reads monoHandler_.processPortamento() (ruinae_engine.h:1824 and :2115). The glide time it uses is therefore always slideTime (default 60 ms per the finding's citation of arpeggiator_params.h:99). monoModeParams_.portamentoTimeMs (0-5000 ms, default 0, mono_mode_params.h:19) has no audible effect.

Impact:
- mono_handler.h:199-212 turns glide on for every note after the first when notes overlap (:204-206).
- portaMode defaults to 0, which is Always (mono_mode_params.h:20; mono_handler.h:709 `PortaMode::Always`). So staccato notes glide too (:209). That is worse than the finding states: in default Mono mode, every note after the first glides 60 ms, not only overlapping ones.
- updatePortamentoTarget glides whenever portamentoTimeMs_ > 0 (:498/:501). Slide Time defaults to 60, so the user's portamento of 0 never snaps the pitch.
- Setting Portamento to 5000 ms changes nothing.
- For a 60 -> 72 jump, that means a full octave glided over about 2646 samples at 44.1 kHz. This is clearly audible.

Test coverage: param_flow_test.cpp:152 sets kMonoPortamentoTimeId only to check that processing does not crash. No test checks the resulting glide, so nothing catches the bug.

The defect affects every host and every sample rate whenever Mono mode is used. A user-facing control is dead and it produces an unwanted pitch glide by default. High severity is justified.

</details>

### R-038

**Trance Gate free-run Rate knob is overridden to 4 Hz on every active voice each 64-sample sub-block**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** modulation · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:1972-1979, 2065-2070, 1317-1325, 2212`

**Problem.** processBlockPoly/processBlockMono forward the All-Voice Gate Rate destination unconditionally as setTranceGateRate(baseTranceGateRateHz_ + offset*50). baseTranceGateRateHz_ is only written by RuinaeEngine::setTranceGateRate, which the processor never calls: it pushes the rate through setTranceGateParams(tgp) (processor_params.cpp:390,402), and that path does not update baseTranceGateRateHz_. The member therefore stays at its 4.0f initializer, and every sub-block resets each active voice's gate to 4 Hz plus the offset, overriding the rate that setParams applied at the top of the block.

**Why it is wrong.** The Trance Gate Rate parameter (0.1-100 Hz, kTranceGateRateId) must set the free-run step rate. The All-Voice Gate Rate destination must add to that base. Here the base is a constant. TranceGate::setRate (trance_gate.h:180-183) and setParams (153-171) both call updateStepDuration, so the last writer wins, and the last writer is the engine with 4 Hz. In tempo-sync mode (the default, trance_gate_params.h:27) setRate only stores rateHz, so the All-Voice Gate Rate destination does nothing at all in sync mode. This most likely appeared when the F007 fix made the forwarding unconditional: before that, the override only ran when the offset was non-zero.

**Consequence.** With the gate in free-run mode, every Rate setting other than 4 Hz is ignored on sounding voices, so the gate always steps at 4 Hz. The default rate is 4 Hz (trance_gate_params.h:23), which hides the bug. The existing processor-level test 'TranceGate rate parameter propagates in free-run mode' (trance_gate_param_flow_test.cpp:256-288) compares the energy of two consecutive windows of a 1-hot 16-step pattern. At a constant 4 Hz the second window still has less energy, so the test passes without proving the rate took effect. Modulating All-Voice Gate Rate in sync mode is silently inert.

**Suggested fix.** Keep baseTranceGateRateHz_ in sync with the user value: set it in RuinaeEngine::setTranceGateParams (baseTranceGateRateHz_ = clamp(params.rateHz)), or have applyTranceGateParams call engine_.setTranceGateRate. For sync mode, decide on a sync-aware offset (scale the step duration) or document the destination as free-run only. Add a processor test: free-run, numSteps 2 with pattern 1,0, Rate 0.5 Hz vs 20 Hz. Measure the gate period from the output envelope zero-crossings and require it to match 1/rate within 5%.

**Evidence.** ruinae_engine.h:1973-1977 `float modRate = std::clamp(baseTranceGateRateHz_ + allVoiceTranceGateOffset * 50.0f, 0.1f, 100.0f); ... voices_[i].setTranceGateRate(modRate);`; ruinae_engine.h:1317-1319 setTranceGateParams only loops voice.setTranceGateParams; :2212 `float baseTranceGateRateHz_ = 4.0f;`; grep setTranceGateRate|baseTranceGateRateHz_ under plugins/ruinae finds no processor caller; processor_params.cpp:390 `tgp.rateHz = tranceGateParams_.rateHz.load(...)`, :402 engine_.setTranceGateParams(tgp); trance_gate.h:179-183 `setRate ... (only effective when tempoSync is off)`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the full path and the defect is real.

1. Nothing in the processor writes `baseTranceGateRateHz_`. It is declared `float baseTranceGateRateHz_ = 4.0f;` (ruinae_engine.h:2212) and only `RuinaeEngine::setTranceGateRate` assigns it (ruinae_engine.h:1321-1324). A grep across plugins/ruinae finds that setter called only in tests (ruinae_engine_test.cpp:1129/1153; voice_mod_all_targets_test.cpp calls the voice-level setter). The processor calls only `engine_.setTranceGateParams(tgp)` (processor_params.cpp:402, with `tgp.rateHz` loaded at :390). `RuinaeEngine::setTranceGateParams` (ruinae_engine.h:1317-1318) just loops `voice.setTranceGateParams(params)` and never touches `baseTranceGateRateHz_`.

2. The engine overrides the rate on every sub-block, whatever the offset. processBlockPoly (ruinae_engine.h:1972-1979) computes `modRate = clamp(baseTranceGateRateHz_ + allVoiceTranceGateOffset*50, 0.1, 100)` and calls `voices_[i].setTranceGateRate(modRate)` on every active voice. processBlockMono does the same for voice 0 (ruinae_engine.h:2065-2070). Comment lines 1948-1952 confirm this forwarding is deliberately unconditional.

3. The last writer wins. `RuinaeVoice::setTranceGateRate` calls `tranceGate_.setRate(hz)` (ruinae_voice.h:1098-1100). `TranceGate::setRate` writes `params_.rateHz` and calls `updateStepDuration()` (trance_gate.h:180-183).
