So the counter is pulled to the wrong place at every block, and the error depends on block size. Nothing in the sync touches `swingStepCounter_` parity, so the parity is never re-anchored to the grid.

The committed golden shows the same pattern. Lines 1-16 of plugins/ruinae/tests/fixtures/ruinae_factory_Tape_Shuffle_golden_midi.txt are not a long/short alternation:
- noteOn times run 0, 7310, 14781, 21930 and then 22058. That is noteOn 72 followed by noteOn 60 128 samples later, with no noteOff 72 in between.
- The same flam repeats at 43973 and 44115 (142 samples apart).

The test that generates this golden advances `projectTimeMusic` every block (ruinae_byte_identical_post_lane10_test.cpp:282, 354, 368), so it runs the per-block sync path and locks this behaviour in.

Every swung tempo-synced arp in a DAW that reports ppq is affected: swing timing is lost and flams appear. High severity is justified.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source. I found no guard, design note or test that excuses it.

- Swing-unaware math: in dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.h:1035-1036, syncToMusicalPosition computes stepFraction on a 1-step straight grid (`calculateMusicalStepPosition(projectTimeMusic, noteValue_, noteModifier_, 1)`). Lines 1041-1043 then multiply that fraction by currentStepDuration_ and use the result to overwrite sampleCounter_ (1049-1051).
- currentStepDuration_ is already swung: calculateStepDuration (h:1099-1112) makes it baseDuration*(1+swing) on even swingStepCounter_ steps and baseDuration*(1-swing) on odd ones. It is recomputed that way at every step in arpeggiator_core.cpp:260/284/302/659/701/750/774/784/1328.
- Result: with swing above 0, a straight-grid fraction gets scaled onto a long or short duration, and nothing in the sync realigns swingStepCounter_ parity. swingStepCounter_ is only reset at h:292/344/413 and cpp:84/95/247. The re-anchor is therefore wrong whenever swing is above 0, and where it lands depends on where the block boundaries fall.
- Called every block: plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:325-327 calls it on every playing block that has a valid ppq. Gradus does the same at plugins/gradus/src/processor/processor.cpp:238.
- No test covers swing: the only per-block sync regression test, arpeggiator_core_dawloop_test.cpp:370-418, runs 1/8 notes with no swing at all. The other sync tests at :203, :273 and :345 pass ppq 0.0.
- Not documented as intentional: the comment at h:1020-1028 says sync "only adjusts timing within the current step" and says nothing about swing.
- The golden shows it: plugins/ruinae/tests/fixtures/ruinae_factory_Tape_Shuffle_golden_midi.txt lines 7-8 have `[21930] noteOn 72` then `[22058] noteOn 60`, 128 samples apart. Lines 15-16 have `[43973] noteOn 72` then `[44115] noteOn 60`, 142 apart. The inter-onset intervals are irregular (7310, 7471, 7149, 128, ...). That matches the claimed flams, and the byte-compared golden pins them in place.

Severity stays high: this distorts the timing of every swung tempo-synced arp preset in any host that reports ppq, in both Ruinae and Gradus, because the core is shared.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the defect and its impact from the source and the committed golden. I did not re-run the reviewer's probe.

How the code goes wrong:
- processor.cpp:325-327 calls arpCore_.syncToMusicalPosition(projectTimeMusic) on every block where the transport is playing and the ppq value is valid.
- arpeggiator_core.h:1035-1036 computes stepFraction on the straight grid, using noteValue_/noteModifier_ with a 1-step pattern.
- h:1041-1043 multiplies that fraction by currentStepDuration_, which is the swung duration. calculateStepDuration (h:1099-1112) makes it base*(1+swing) on even swingStepCounter_ and base*(1-swing) on odd.
- h:1049-1051 then overwrites sampleCounter_. swingStepCounter_ is left untouched.
- arpeggiator_core.cpp:136 and :257-284 fire the next step when sampleCounter_ reaches currentStepDuration_.

So every block start moves the counter to a point that has no relation to the swung position. Example: 2000 samples into a long step, the straight fraction 2000/base is multiplied by the long duration, and the counter jumps ahead.

Measured consequence (committed golden, plugins/ruinae/tests/fixtures/ruinae_factory_Tape_Shuffle_golden_midi.txt):
- The preset is 1/8T at 120 BPM with swing 22 % (tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:9969-9971).
- The 1/8T step is 7350 samples at 44.1 kHz, so the expected swing alternates 8967 and 5733 samples.
- The golden NoteOns are at 0, 7310, 14781, 21930, 22058, 29353, 36838, 43973, 44115. The intervals are 7310, 7471, 7149, 128, 7295, ... There is no long/short alternation; the gaps sit near the straight 7350 with jitter.
- There are double triggers 128 and 142 samples apart (21930 noteOn 72 then 22058 noteOn 60, with 72 still held until 26057). These are audible flams with overlapping notes.

The golden is produced exactly the way a DAW would drive the plugin: ruinae_byte_identical_post_lane10_test.cpp:274-282 and :353-356 set kPlaying, advance projectTimeMusic per 512-sample block, and use 120 BPM. So the byte-identical test locks the broken timing in.

Scope and severity:
- It triggers in every host that reports kPlaying with a valid ppq (all DAWs) for any tempo-synced arp with swing > 0.
- Simple hosts without transport do not call the sync and are unaffected, and swing 0 is unaffected.
- The swing parameter does nothing during DAW playback, and flams appear, on factory presets. High severity is justified.

</details>

### R-067

**Single-note arp steps with gate over 100 % are cut by the previous step's stale NoteOff when the pitch repeats (measured: 150 % gate plays as 50 %)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** arpeggiator · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:1230-1257`

**Problem.** The single-note emission path emits NoteOn and appends to currentArpNotes_ without cancelling the earlier step's pending gate NoteOff for the same pitch. The chord path (:1178) and ratchet path (:1059) were fixed for exactly this (GMF-005), but this path was not. With gate > 100 % and a pitch that repeats on consecutive steps (one held key with octave range 1, Random mode repeats, pinned steps, a pitch lane of zeros on a single note), step N-1's pending off fires mid-step N and releases the note just struck. The engine allocator retriggers the same voice on the repeat, so the stale off releases it.

**Why it is wrong.** Gate length is defined per note from its onset (calculateGateDuration). The chord/ratchet code comment (cpp:1054-1059) states the rule: 'addPendingNoteOff does not dedup, so a leftover would fire mid-step and cut the note this step re-strikes'.

**Consequence.** Measured (probe, one held key, 1/8 at 120 BPM, gate 150 %): ON@0 ON@11025 OFF@16537 ON@22050 OFF@27562 ON@33075 OFF@38587 ... Every note after the first sounds for 5512 samples (50 % gate) instead of overlapping legato. Gate 101-200 % on a single held key, the classic legato setting, audibly turns staccato in Ruinae and in Gradus/MIDI Out. The dsp tests cover only chord and ratchet (arpeggiator_core_core_test.cpp:3707, 3775).

**Suggested fix.** In the single-note branch, before emitting the NoteOn, cancel pending offs for result.notes[0]. If that pitch is in currentArpNotes_, emit its NoteOff at humanizedSampleOffset first and remove it, mirroring the chord path. Add a 'GMF-005 single note' test: one held note, gate 150 %, REQUIRE each NoteOn-to-NoteOff duration equals the first.

**Evidence.** arpeggiator_core.cpp:1235-1255 `if (eventCount < maxEvents) { outputEvents[eventCount++] = ArpEvent{.type = NoteOn ...}; if (currentArpNoteCount_ < 32) currentArpNotes_[currentArpNoteCount_++] = result.notes[0]; if (!suppressGateNoteOff) scheduleGate(result.notes[0], gateDuration, 0); }`, with no cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes, unlike :1178. Probe: 'B single note gate150 (step=11025): ON@0 ON@11025 OFF@16537 ON@22050 OFF@27562 ON@33075 OFF@38587'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute the defect: the source shows the behaviour the finding describes.

1. **The single-note branch never cancels or releases the earlier note.** dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:1230-1257 (the result.count==1, non-slide, ratchetCount==1 path) emits the NoteOn (:1236-1240), appends the pitch to currentArpNotes_ (:1247-1249) and calls scheduleGate (:1254). It does not call cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes() and emits no NoteOff for notes still sounding. The other paths do cancel first: the chord path at :1178, ratchet at :1059 (with the comment at :1054-1058 naming exactly this hazard), and slide at :1125.

2. **Pending offs are not deduplicated, and a stale one releases the pitch.** addPendingNoteOff (arpeggiator_core.h:1260-1281) appends unconditionally. When a pending off reaches zero, the emit loop (h:1237-1249, and the in-block variant at h:1524-1535) emits a NoteOff for that pitch and calls removeFromCurrentArpNotes. Nothing in fireStep (cpp:419-1257) between the step start and the single-note branch touches pendingNoteOffs_ for a pitch that repeats.

3. **Gate over 100 % is a legal setting.** kMaxGateLength = 200.0f (h:176), and calculateGateDuration (h:1158-1163) returns stepDuration * gate%. For 1/8 at 120 BPM and 44.1 kHz that is 11025 * 1.5 = 16537. So the off for the note struck at 0 lands at 16537, inside the step that re-struck the same pitch at 11025. The quoted probe trace (ON@0 ON@11025 OFF@16537 ...) matches this arithmetic exactly.

4. **The engine turns the stale off into a release.** VoiceAllocator same-note retrigger (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_allocator.h:238-242, retriggerNote at :843) restarts the existing voice rather than starting a second one. The stale NoteOff therefore releases the note that was just struck, about 5512 samples (50 % of the step) after its onset.

5. **The tests do not cover this case.** The gate > 100 % tests in arpeggiator_core_core_test.cpp (:636-687 at 150 %, :692+ at 200 %) hold three distinct pitches (48, 52, 55) in Up mode, so pitches never repeat on consecutive steps. The GMF-005 tests at :3718 and :3786 use ArpMode::Chord. None runs single-note emission with a repeating pitch.

Severity: high is reasonable. The effect is an audible gate shortening (150 % plays as 50 %) on a common configuration, one held key with a long gate. It reaches Ruinae's engine and the shared Gradus / MIDI-out path, but it causes no stuck notes or crash, so I am not upgrading it.

**Note 2.** The defect is real and nothing else in the code guards against it. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp, the single-note branch (lines 1230-1257) emits a NoteOn, appends the pitch to currentArpNotes_ (1247-1249) and calls scheduleGate (1254). It never calls cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes() and never releases the notes still sounding. Every other note-emitting path does: ratchet at 1059 (whose comment at 1054-1058 explains why), slide at 1125, chord at 1178 (comment at 1173-1177), and the rest, tie and euclidean paths at 645, 687, 738 and 769. The pending-off store does not dedup. addPendingNoteOff (arpeggiator_core.h:1260-1283) appends blindly, and emitDuePendingNoteOffs (h:1231-1256) releases by pitch and calls removeFromCurrentArpNotes. With gate > 100 %, step N-1's pending off for pitch p is therefore still queued when step N strikes p again, and it fires at onset(N-1) + 1.5 steps, which is half a step into note N. calculateGateDuration (h:1158-1163) multiplies the step by gateLengthPercent_, and setGateLength (h:443-444) allows up to kMaxGateLength, so values above 100 % are a supported setting. The quoted probe timeline matches this arithmetic: 11025 + 16537 = 27562, an OFF 5512 samples after ON@22050. The existing tests do not cover it. arpeggiator_core_core_test.cpp:636-687 and 692-745 use three distinct pitches (48/52/55) in Up mode, so the stale off always hits a different pitch, and the GMF-005 tests at 3718 and 3786 cover only the chord path. No code comment or test describes the single-pitch truncation as intended. Severity: downgrade to medium. The bug only shows when the same pitch repeats on consecutive steps: one held key with octave range 1, occasional Random/Walk repeats, pinned or zero-offset pitch lanes. Distinct-pitch overlap, the usual >100 % gate case, works. The suggested fix, mirroring the chord path, would make a repeated pitch sound about 100 % of a step (released at the next onset), not 150 % overlapping legato, because MIDI cannot overlap the same pitch. The finding's 'instead of overlapping legato' framing overstates what a fix restores, but 50 % instead of about 100 % is still a real, audible inconsistency with the chord and ratchet paths.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:1230-1257: the single-note branch (result.count == 1, no ratchet, no slide) emits the NoteOn, appends the pitch to currentArpNotes_ (:1247-1249) and calls scheduleGate (:1254). It does not call cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes, and it does not release the previous note. The chord path (:1178) and the ratchet path (:1059) both cancel first, and their GMF-005 comments (:1054-1058, :1173-1177) describe exactly this hazard.

addPendingNoteOff (arpeggiator_core.h:1260-1283) appends with no dedup by pitch. When a pending off comes due (h:1236-1250, h:1523-1536), it emits NoteOff(note) and calls removeFromCurrentArpNotes. So with gate g > 100 % and pitch P repeated on step N, the off that step N-1 scheduled fires (g-100) % of a step into step N.

Ruinae passes that NoteOff unchanged to the engine as ArpNoteOff (plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:361-365). The engine's VoiceAllocator handles the repeated NoteOn(P) as a same-note retrigger of the existing voice (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_allocator.h:238-242, 843). The stale NoteOff(P) therefore releases the voice that was just re-struck. Every repeated-pitch note after the first sounds for (g-100) % of a step instead of g %. At 1/8 note, 120 BPM, 44.1 kHz (step 11025 samples):
- gate 150 %: 5512 samples instead of 16537, matching the quoted probe (OFF at 16537, 27562, 38587 = onset + 5512).
- gate 101 %: about 110 samples, which is essentially a blip.

The MIDI output and Gradus get the same NoteOn, NoteOn, NoteOff sequence, and most receiving synths cut the note the same way.

Triggers: one held key with octave range 1 (any mode), Chord-mode arp with one key, Random/Walk repeats, pinned steps, and a pitch lane that maps consecutive steps to the same note.

Existing tests do not catch it. arpeggiator_core_core_test.cpp:636-687 and :692-740 test gate 150 % / 200 % overlap only with three distinct held notes, where pitches never repeat on adjacent steps. The GMF-005 tests (:3707, :3775) cover only chord and ratchet. Gate above 100 % on a single held note is the standard legato setting, and here it gives staccato or near-silent notes. High severity is appropriate.

</details>

### R-068

**Retrigger = Beat resets the pattern every block when the host gives no musical position: the arp repeats only its first note (measured)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** arpeggiator · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:269-275, 304-310`

**Problem.** transportPositionSamples is filled only when kProjectTimeMusicValid is set; otherwise it stays at the BlockContext default 0 (block_context.h:78). Ruinae still runs the arp in that case: simple hosts are forced to isPlaying=true at :308-310. With Retrigger = Beat, detectBarBoundary computes `0 % barSamples == 0` and reports a bar boundary at offset 0 of EVERY block (arpeggiator_core.h:1128-1139). The core then runs selector_.reset() and resetLanes() each block (cpp:244-248). The same happens in a DAW that reports a stopped ppq (constant position at a bar line, e.g. 0) before the first play press, while hostSupportsTransport_ is still false.

**Why it is wrong.** Retrigger Beat must reset once per bar (FR-023). A position that never advances is not a bar boundary every block. Without musical time the boundary is unknowable and must be skipped, or synthesised from an internal sample clock.

**Consequence.** Measured (probe, Up over 60/64/67, 1/16, Retrigger Beat, ctx without ppq): the NoteOns are '60 60 60 60 60 60 60 60 60 60'. With ppq valid they are '60 64 67 60 64 67 ...'. Every lane is pinned at step 0 too. Hosts without ppq include standalone hosts and the user's own host class. The Ruinae arp test fixture (arp_integration_test.cpp:217-219) also never sets kProjectTimeMusicValid, so no processor test exercises real bar detection.

**Suggested fix.** In the processor, when !projectTimeMusicValid, run a free-running sample counter for transportPositionSamples while the arp runs, or tell the core there is no position (e.g. transportPositionSamples = -1, which detectBarBoundary already treats as invalid at h:1129-1131). Also derive the boundary from ppq directly instead of the truncated samplesPerBar (block_context.h:140-149). Regression test: processor with kPlaying|kTempoValid and no ppq, Retrigger Beat, three held notes, REQUIRE more than one distinct pitch in 2 s.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:269-275 `if (pc->state & kProjectTimeMusicValid) { ... blockCtx.transportPositionSamples = ppqToSamples(...); }` with no else. arpeggiator_core.h:1128-1139 `const int64_t blockStart = ctx.transportPositionSamples; ... remainder = blockStart % barSamplesI64; if (remainder == 0) barBoundarySample = 0;`. Probe: 'C retrigger Beat, no ppq, Up 60/64/67 notes: 60 60 60 60 60 60 60 60 60 60' / 'C' ... ppq valid: 60 64 67 60 64 67 60 64 67 60'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this finding. I confirmed the full path from source but did not re-run the probe.

1. The position is never set without musical time. processor.cpp:254 default-constructs BlockContext, and transportPositionSamples defaults to 0 (block_context.h:78). It is assigned only inside `if (pc->state & kProjectTimeMusicValid)` (processor.cpp:269-275), which has no else branch. When processContext is null it also stays 0. No other Ruinae code sets it for the arp: a grep finds only processor.cpp:273, the per-segment offset in processor_midi.cpp:137 (engine segments, not the arp ctx) and ruinae_engine.h:808.

2. The arp still runs in that case. arpCtx copies blockCtx (processor.cpp:304), and isPlaying is forced to true while hostSupportsTransport_ is false (:308-310). arpCore_.processBlock(arpCtx, ...) is called once per block at :330. syncToMusicalPosition and the loop detection are skipped because projectTimeMusicValid is false (:315, :325), so nothing replaces the position.

3. The core finds a bar boundary in every block. In arpeggiator_core.cpp:126-127, Retrigger Beat calls detectBarBoundary(ctx). In arpeggiator_core.h:1122-1149, blockStart = 0 passes the `< 0` guard, remainder = 0 % barSamples = 0, so barBoundarySample = 0 and offset 0 is returned for every block (barSamples is nonzero whenever tempo is set).

4. That boundary resets the pattern every block. In the main loop, samplesUntilBar = 0 always wins (cpp:201-221), and the BarBoundary branch calls selector_.reset(), sets swingStepCounter_ = 0 and calls resetLanes() (cpp:244-248). A 1/16 step (about 5512 samples at 120 BPM, 44.1 kHz) is much longer than a typical block, so each step fires in a block whose start just reset the selector. Every step therefore plays the first note and every lane stays at step 0, which matches the quoted '60 60 60 ...' measurement.

5. The setting is reachable in Ruinae: arpCore_.setRetrigger(retrigger) is wired at processor_params.cpp:977.

The same thing happens when a stopped DAW reports a constant ppq on a bar line before the first play while hostSupportsTransport_ is still false.

Severity: no change. The trigger needs a non-default Retrigger mode and a host or state without musical time, but when it happens the Beat mode does not work at all.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source and found no guard, comment or design note that makes it intentional.

1. The position is never filled without ppq. plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:254 declares `BlockContext blockCtx;`. Lines 269-275 set `transportPositionSamples = ppqToSamples(...)` only under `kProjectTimeMusicValid`, and there is no else branch. dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/block_context.h:78 defaults `transportPositionSamples = 0`.

2. The arp still runs in that state. At processor.cpp:300-310, `hostSupportsTransport_` turns true only after the host has reported kPlaying at least once. Until then `arpCtx.isPlaying = true` is forced. `syncToMusicalPosition` and `notifyTransportLoop` (lines 315-327) are skipped without ppq, but `arpCore_.processBlock(arpCtx, ...)` at line 330 still runs.

3. A bar boundary is reported at offset 0 of every block. arpeggiator_core.cpp:126-127 calls `detectBarBoundary(ctx)` when Retrigger = Beat. In arpeggiator_core.h:1128-1139, `blockStart = 0`, which is not below 0, so the `< 0` guard does not reject it. Then `remainder = 0 % barSamples = 0`, so `barBoundarySample = 0`, which is less than blockSize, and offset 0 is returned for every block.

4. Each block resets the pattern. arpeggiator_core.cpp:201-221 gives BarBoundary priority. Lines 244-248 then run `selector_.reset(); swingStepCounter_ = 0; resetLanes();` every block. A 1/16 step at 120 BPM is about 5512 samples, which spans many blocks. Every step therefore fires right after a reset and plays the first note, which matches the quoted measurement of '60 60 60 ...'.

5. The same failure is reachable in a DAW. A stopped DAW that reports a constant ppq of 0 and has never reported kPlaying gets `transportPositionSamples = 0` and a forced `isPlaying = true`. That is the common case of auditioning the arp live before pressing play.

6. Nothing guards or documents this:
- The only per-segment adjustment, processor_midi.cpp:137, applies to engine segments, not to arpCtx.
- MANUAL.md:967 says only "Beat: Restart on beat" and does not mention that host time is required.
- The only Retrigger Beat use in the Ruinae tests, arp_integration_test.cpp:501, is a state round-trip test.
- The arp fixture (arp_integration_test.cpp:217-219) never sets kProjectTimeMusicValid, so no processor test exercises bar detection with or without ppq.

This does not repeat a known prior finding. Severity stays high because the Beat retrigger mode is broken in a reachable host state.

**Note 3.** The defect is real and the claimed consequence follows from the code.

1. processor.cpp:269-275 sets blockCtx.transportPositionSamples only when kProjectTimeMusicValid is set, and there is no else branch. block_context.h:78 defaults it to 0. Ruinae does not keep an internal sample clock. If data.processContext is null, the position is also 0.
2. processor.cpp:308-310: when hostSupportsTransport_ is false (the host has never reported kPlaying), arpCtx.isPlaying is forced to true, so the arp runs. processor.cpp:330 passes arpCtx to arpCore_.processBlock.
3. arpeggiator_core.cpp:126-127 calls detectBarBoundary when the retrigger mode is Beat. In arpeggiator_core.h:1128-1139, blockStart is 0, so remainder = 0 % barSamples = 0 and barBoundarySample = 0. That is less than blockSize, so a boundary is reported at offset 0 of every block. barSamples is never 0 here: tempo defaults to 120 and the time signature to 4/4 (block_context.h:69-71, 140-149).
4. arpeggiator_core.cpp:244-248 runs selector_.reset(), swingStepCounter_ = 0 and resetLanes() at that boundary. The step clock (sampleCounter_) is not reset, so steps still fire on time. But a 1/16 step at 120 BPM is about 5512 samples, which is longer than any normal block. Each step therefore fires in a block whose selector was reset at sample 0, and the arp plays only the first note. The lanes stay at step 0, as the reviewer measured. Only when two steps fall inside one block would the second note be reached.

Impact:
- Retrigger defaults to Off (arpeggiator_params.h:79, retrigger{0}).
- Factory presets do set Beat: tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:553 and :1413 (retrigger = 2).
- A host that never supplies ppq (bare or standalone hosts) breaks the arp completely in Beat mode.
- A DAW is affected too. Before the first play press, hostSupportsTransport_ is false and the arp is forced to run. A stopped DAW usually reports a valid ppq at the playhead, and at bar 1 (the playhead on a newly opened project) ppqToSamples(0) = 0 hits the same bug. So auditioning those Beat presets with the transport stopped plays a single repeated note.

The arp then produces only its first note, so its function is lost for that configuration. I keep the severity at high.

</details>

### R-069

**Arp skip events are sent with IMessage from process(), and every lane gets the velocity lane's step**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** arpeggiator · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:379-386 (sendSkipEvent at plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_messaging.cpp:113-130)`
- **Also flagged by:** ui-wiring, prior-audit-regressions, gestalt-processor

**Problem.** For each kSkip event, process() calls sendSkipEvent 6 times. Each call mutates a pre-allocated IMessage and calls sendMessage(), which is ComponentBase::sendMessage -> getPeer()->notify(message), synchronously on the audio thread (vstcomponentbase.cpp:119-123). There are two possible outcomes. (1) The host connects directly: the controller's notify then runs handleArpSkipEvent -> setSkippedStep -> view->invalid() (controller_arp.cpp:19-40) on the audio thread, racing the UI thread's draw of the same view. (2) The host uses the SDK ConnectionProxy: it discards non-UI-thread messages (connectionproxy.cpp:75-77), so the feature never works. In addition, the step sent is the core's velocity-lane index (`.note = velStep`, arpeggiator_core.cpp:676/716/760), but it is broadcast to the gate, pitch, ratchet, modifier and condition lanes, which have their own lengths and speeds. Chord (6) and inversion (7) lanes get nothing, because the processor allocates and sends only lanes 0-5 (processor_messaging.cpp:118) while the controller handles 8 (controller.h:524).

**Why it is wrong.** The audio thread must not make synchronous host calls or run VSTGUI code. The processor's own comment at processor.cpp:211-214 moves the handshakes off the audio thread for this exact reason. A skip highlight must show the skipped step of each lane.

**Consequence.** Possible data race or crash in VSTGUI (invalid() from the audio thread; on macOS setNeedsDisplay off the main thread). Host-dependent locking/latency spikes in process(). In SDK-proxy hosts the skip highlight is silently dead. Where it works, lanes whose length differs from the velocity lane flash the wrong step, and chord/inversion lanes never flash.

**Suggested fix.** Publish skip events through a lock-free per-lane atomic (step plus sequence counter) or the DataExchange API, and let the controller's 30 fps timer read it, as the playheads already do. Have the core report per-lane step indices for a skip (or let the controller derive them) and cover all 8 lanes. Test: a processor test with a connected mock peer that records the calling thread / asserts sendMessage is never called inside process().

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:382-385 `const int step = static_cast<int>(evt.note); for (int lane = 0; lane < 6; ++lane) { sendSkipEvent(lane, step); }`. processor_messaging.cpp:127-129 `attrs->setInt("lane", ...); attrs->setInt("step", ...); sendMessage(msg);`. vstcomponentbase.cpp:121-122 `if (message != nullptr && getPeer () != nullptr) return getPeer ()->notify (message);`. connectionproxy.cpp:75-77 'We discard the message if we are not in the UI main thread'. controller_arp.cpp:34-39 `targetLane->setSkippedStep(step); ... view->invalid();`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The finding is correct. I checked every link in the path against source:

1. Audio-thread send: process() runs the arp block inside the audio callback (plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:221, arp block at 293-387). For each ArpEvent::Type::kSkip it loops `for (int lane = 0; lane < 6; ++lane) sendSkipEvent(lane, step);` (processor.cpp:379-385).

2. Synchronous host call: sendSkipEvent (processor_messaging.cpp:113-130) has only one guard, editorOpen_ at line 115. After that it calls attrs->setInt twice and then `sendMessage(msg)` at line 129. The Processor does not override sendMessage (the grep finds no override in plugins/ruinae/src). That makes it ComponentBase::sendMessage (extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstcomponentbase.cpp:119-123): `return getPeer ()->notify (message);`. That is a synchronous call into the peer, made from the audio thread.

3. The plugin's own rules contradict this. The comment at processor.cpp:211-214 and the doc comments at processor.h:188 and processor.h:364 say that sendMessage() is a synchronous host call that must not run on the audio thread.

4. The two host outcomes:
   - If the host connects the components directly, Controller::notify handles "ArpSkipEvent" (controller.cpp:414-428) and calls handleArpSkipEvent. That calls targetLane->setSkippedStep and then view->invalid() (controller_arp.cpp:34-40), so VSTGUI code runs on the audio thread.
   - If the host uses the SDK ConnectionProxy, it drops any message sent off the UI thread (connectionproxy.cpp:75-77). The skip highlight then never appears.

5. Wrong step index: the core sets `velStep = velocityLane_.currentStep()` (arpeggiator_core.cpp:486). All three kSkip emit sites send `.note = static_cast<uint8_t>(velStep)` (arpeggiator_core.cpp:676, 716, 760). The processor broadcasts that single index to lanes 0-5, but gateStep and ratchetStep are tracked separately (arpeggiator_core.cpp:487-488). Any lane whose length differs from the velocity lane therefore flashes the wrong step.

6. Missing lanes: the processor allocates only 6 skip messages (processor.h:255 `std::array<..., 6>`, processor.cpp:68), and sendSkipEvent rejects lane >= 6 (processor_messaging.cpp:118). The controller expects kArpLaneCount = 8 (controller.h:524), with chordLane_ and inversionLane_ at indices 6 and 7 (controller_arp.cpp:25-29). Those two lanes never receive a skip event.

Every part of the claim is confirmed.

On severity: the editorOpen_ guard (processor_messaging.cpp:115) limits the problem to times when the editor is open. Within that window the defects are real: a host call on the audio thread, VSTGUI invalid() in direct-connect hosts, and a dead feature in proxy hosts. High is a reasonable rating, so I see no reason to change it.

**Note 2.** I could not refute the finding. Every part of it holds in the source.

1. A host call on the audio thread. processor.cpp:379-386 sits inside process(), in the arp event loop that starts at :334. For each kSkip event it calls `sendSkipEvent(lane, step)` for lanes 0-5. processor_messaging.cpp:113-130 returns early only when the editor is closed (`editorOpen_`, :115). Otherwise it calls setInt twice and then `sendMessage(msg)` (:129). That is a synchronous call to the peer's notify(). No queue, atomic or timer handoff exists anywhere in that path.
   - The controller's notify handles "ArpSkipEvent" at controller.cpp:414-428 and calls handleArpSkipEvent. That function (controller_arp.cpp:19-40) runs `targetLane->setSkippedStep(step)` and `view->invalid()` on whatever thread made the call. With a direct connection, that is the audio thread.
   - The processor's own comment at processor.cpp:211-214 calls synchronous host sendMessage() calls on the audio thread a defect. It moved the handshakes to setActive for that reason, and the test "One-time controller handshakes are sent from setActive, not process" (voice_route_rt_safety_test.cpp:477-496) enforces that move.
   - The only skip-related RT test, voice_route_rt_safety_test.cpp:448-475, only checks that the attribute keys are created in advance so setInt does not allocate. Its comment at :456 admits that sendSkipEvent "runs inside the arp loop on the audio thread". No test, spec comment or doc records the synchronous send itself as an accepted design decision.
   - The editorOpen_ gate means the send only happens while the editor is open, which is exactly when the race on the view exists. So it is no mitigation.

2. Every lane gets the velocity lane's step. All three kSkip emits in arpeggiator_core.cpp (:672-677, :712-717, :756-761) set `.note = static_cast<uint8_t>(velStep)`. The processor sends that one index to lanes 0-5 (velocity, gate, pitch, ratchet, modifier, condition; order from controller_arp.cpp:25-29). Lane lengths are independent, so the gate and pitch lanes' current steps differ from velStep whenever their lengths differ, and those lanes flash the wrong step.

3. Chord and inversion lanes never get a skip. processor.h:255 holds only 6 messages, sendSkipEvent rejects `lane >= 6` (processor_messaging.cpp:118), and the loop runs `lane < 6` (processor.cpp:383). The controller accepts up to kArpLaneCount lanes, including chordLane_ and inversionLane_ (controller_arp.cpp:21-29; controller.cpp:423).

I did not open the SDK's vstcomponentbase.cpp or connectionproxy.cpp in this pass, so the claim that a ConnectionProxy discards these messages is unverified here. It is not needed: the direct-connection path is enough to confirm the RT and threading defect.

I keep the severity at high. It is an audio-thread call into the host and into VSTGUI invalidation, which can race the UI thread's draw (on macOS, setNeedsDisplay off the main thread), plus a functional bug in the skip display.

**Note 3.** I confirmed every part of the claim from source.

(1) The skip messages are sent from the audio thread. processor.cpp:379-386 runs inside process() (the function starts at :221 and the arp block at :293-330). For each kSkip event it loops over lanes 0-5 and calls sendSkipEvent(lane, step). processor_messaging.cpp:113-130 returns early only if the editor is closed (editorOpen_, :115) or the lane/step is out of range. Otherwise it sets "lane" and "step" on the pre-allocated skipMessages_[lane] and calls sendMessage(msg) (:129). In the SDK, vstcomponentbase.cpp:119-123 shows that sendMessage is getPeer()->notify(message), a direct call, so the host's connection code runs on the audio thread. The processor's own comment at processor.cpp:211-214 calls this exact pattern a defect: it moved the handshake sendMessage calls into setActive for that reason. This site was left behind.

(2) There are two outcomes, and both are bad.
- The SDK ConnectionProxy (connectionproxy.cpp:71-77) discards messages that do not arrive on the UI thread, so in those hosts the feature does nothing.
- A host that connects directly runs Controller::notify on the audio thread (controller.cpp:414-428). That calls handleArpSkipEvent, which calls setSkippedStep and view->invalid() (controller_arp.cpp:34-39). This writes view state and triggers VSTGUI invalidation off the UI thread while the UI thread may be drawing the same view. That is a data race. On macOS, invalidating a view off the main thread is not allowed.

(3) Every lane gets the velocity lane's step. arpeggiator_core.cpp:486 captures velStep = velocityLane_.currentStep(). The kSkip events at :676, :716 and :760 carry .note = velStep. The lanes advance independently, each with its own speed accumulator and length (advanceLaneBySpeed, :505). Yet processor.cpp:382-384 sends that one index to all six lanes. When the lane lengths or speeds differ, the gate, pitch, ratchet, modifier and condition lanes highlight the wrong step.

(4) Chord and inversion never flash. skipMessages_ holds only 6 entries (processor.h:255), and sendSkipEvent rejects lane >= 6 (processor_messaging.cpp:118). The controller maps 8 lanes, including chordLane_ and inversionLane_ (controller_arp.cpp:25-29).

Impact: the bug needs the editor to be open and a skip to occur (a probability or condition step that skips), so it is not on every block. When it does fire, there are up to 6 synchronous host calls per skip event inside process(). The worst case is a UI-thread race or crash in hosts that connect directly, and the feature is silently dead in hosts that use the proxy. The wrong-step and missing-lane display errors happen in every host where the message gets through.

No existing test catches this. skip_event_test.cpp only round-trips message attributes, and voice_route_rt_safety_test.cpp only checks that the messages are pre-allocated. Neither checks which thread the message is sent from.

High severity fits: this is a real-time rule violation on the audio thread plus a cross-thread UI race. The UI correctness errors add to it.

</details>

### R-070

**setActive, setupProcessing and preset loads reset the arp without note-offs, stranding MIDI Out notes downstream (Gradus fixed this, Ruinae did not)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** arpeggiator · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_state.cpp:363-365 (also plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:185, 207)`
- **Also flagged by:** lifecycle-state, gestalt-processor

**Problem.** applyPresetSnapshot calls arpCore_.reset(), and setActive(true) and setupProcessing call arpCore_.reset()/prepare(). reset() zeroes currentArpNoteCount_, pendingNoteOffCount_, needsDisableNoteOff_ and panicRequested_ (arpeggiator_core.h:289-306) without emitting anything. engine_.reset() silences the internal voices, but NoteOns already written to data.outputEvents (MIDI Out on, processor.cpp:347-358) never get a NoteOff. Ruinae never calls requestPanicNoteOff()/prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff(), which the core provides for exactly this (h:261-286, 675-676). Gradus uses them (gradus processor.cpp:122, 140-143).

**Why it is wrong.** Every MIDI NoteOn sent to the host must be matched. The core documents that a plain prepare()/reset() 'clears panicRequested_ and the currentArpNotes_ list the panic would have released, so notes already emitted to a MIDI output bus are stranded downstream'.

**Consequence.** With Arp MIDI Out routed to another instrument, a preset change, a sample-rate or buffer reconfiguration, or a bypass/deactivate while the arp plays leaves hanging notes on the downstream synth.

**Suggested fix.** In setActive(false), call arpCore_.requestPanicNoteOff() and set a pendingDeactivateFlush_. In setupProcessing, use prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff when one is pending. In applyPresetSnapshot, run a processBlock-style panic drain into outputEvents (or emit NoteOffs for the core's sounding notes) before reset(). Test: MIDI mode with midiOut on, play until a NoteOn is out, then setState / setActive(false)+setActive(true), and REQUIRE a balancing NoteOff on outputEvents in the next process().

**Evidence.** processor_state.cpp:364-365 `engine_.reset(); arpCore_.reset();`. processor.cpp:206-207 `engine_.reset(); arpCore_.reset();` and :185 `arpCore_.prepare(sampleRate_, ...)`. arpeggiator_core.h:296-299 `currentArpNoteCount_ = 0; pendingNoteOffCount_ = 0; needsDisableNoteOff_ = false; panicRequested_ = false;`. Grep for requestPanicNoteOff in plugins/ruinae/src: no hits. gradus/src/processor/processor.cpp:122 `arpCore_.requestPanicNoteOff();`, :141 `prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the code and the defect is real.

(1) The note-on side. processor.cpp:330 calls arpCore_.processBlock. At processor.cpp:342-359, in MIDI or MIDI+Mod mode with midiOut on, each arp NoteOn is written to data.outputEvents->addEvent. The only NoteOffs Ruinae ever sends to that bus come from arp NoteOff events (processor.cpp:361-377), and those only come from the core's currentArpNotes_ / pendingNoteOff state.

(2) The reset side. arpeggiator_core.h:289-306 reset() sets currentArpNoteCount_=0, pendingNoteOffCount_=0, needsDisableNoteOff_=false and panicRequested_=false. It emits nothing. prepare() (h:255-259) calls reset(). Ruinae calls that path in three places:
- processor_state.cpp:364-365: applyPresetSnapshot runs `engine_.reset(); arpCore_.reset();`. It runs on the audio thread, drained at the top of process() (processor.cpp:235-237), before any arp processBlock in that block.
- processor.cpp:185: setupProcessing calls arpCore_.prepare(...).
- processor.cpp:206-207: setActive(true) calls `engine_.reset(); arpCore_.reset();`.

setActive(false) (processor.cpp:203-218) does nothing for the arp, so no flush is requested before deactivation either. After any of these resets the core's note list is empty. A later setEnabled(false) or transport stop has nothing to release, so NoteOns already sent downstream never get a NoteOff.

(3) The fix exists but Ruinae does not use it. Grepping plugins/ for requestPanicNoteOff, prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff and pendingDeactivate finds them only in Gradus: gradus processor.cpp:110-124 and 140-141 (pendingDeactivateFlush_), with the regression test gradus tests/unit/processor/set_active_flush_test.cpp. There are no hits in plugins/ruinae. The core's own comment at h:261-270 describes this exact stranding.

The engine's internal voices are cleared by engine_.reset(), so the hang only affects downstream instruments fed by the arp's MIDI Out. That needs MIDI Out turned on in MIDI or MIDI+Mod mode, which is a narrower setup, but in that setup the hang is deterministic on every preset load or host reconfigure. I left the severity unchanged.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source; I found no guard elsewhere. (1) processor_state.cpp:363-365: applyPresetSnapshot calls `engine_.reset(); arpCore_.reset();` with no note-off drain beforehand. It runs at the top of process() (processor.cpp:235-237), before the arp block. (2) processor.cpp:203-219: setActive(true) calls `arpCore_.reset()`, and setActive(false) does nothing for the arp. (3) processor.cpp:185: setupProcessing calls a plain `arpCore_.prepare()`, which calls reset(). (4) arpeggiator_core.h:289-299: reset() zeroes currentArpNoteCount_, pendingNoteOffCount_, needsDisableNoteOff_ and panicRequested_ and emits nothing. The core's own comment at h:261-270 says a plain prepare() leaves notes already sent to a MIDI output bus "stranded downstream", and it provides prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff (h:271-286) and requestPanicNoteOff (h:675-678) to prevent that. (5) Ruinae declares a MIDI Output event bus (processor.cpp:64). It writes kNoteOnEvent to data.outputEvents when midiOut is on in MIDI or MIDI+Mod mode (processor.cpp:347-358), and NoteOffs only from arp events (366-377). Once the core's note list is cleared, the matching NoteOff is never produced. (6) Grepping plugins/ruinae/src for requestPanicNoteOff, prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff and pendingDeactivate finds nothing. Gradus does handle it: gradus processor.cpp:110-124 (requestPanicNoteOff + pendingDeactivateFlush_) and :140-141 (prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff). (7) No code comment or test treats this as a design decision. engine_.reset() only covers Ruinae's own voices, not the downstream MIDI bus. The defect is real, but only when Arp MIDI Out is enabled (it defaults to off, arpeggiator_params.h:130) and routed to another instrument. Stranded notes there are a real stuck-note bug, so I keep the high severity.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the defect from source. The impact is real, but it only appears with an opt-in setting, so I am downgrading it.

Code read:
- plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_state.cpp:363-365: applyPresetSnapshot runs `engine_.reset(); arpCore_.reset();` and emits nothing. It is called from process() at processor.cpp:235-237, before the arp block runs.
- plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:203-219: setActive has a branch only for state==true (`engine_.reset(); arpCore_.reset();`). setActive(false) records no note-off obligation.
- plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:185: setupProcessing calls the plain `arpCore_.prepare()`.
- dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.h:255-259: prepare() calls reset().
- arpeggiator_core.h:289-306: reset() zeroes currentArpNoteCount_, pendingNoteOffCount_, needsDisableNoteOff_ and panicRequested_.
- arpeggiator_core.h:261-286: the core's own comment describes exactly this stranding and provides prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff for it. requestPanicNoteOff is at h:675.
- A grep of plugins/ finds no requestPanicNoteOff or prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff call under plugins/ruinae/src. The only arpCore_ reset/prepare/setEnabled calls in Ruinae are processor.cpp:185, processor.cpp:207, processor_state.cpp:365 and processor_params.cpp:1139.
- plugins/gradus/src/processor/processor.cpp:104-149 has the fix: requestPanicNoteOff() and pendingDeactivateFlush_ in setActive(false), the reset skipped on reactivation, and prepareRetainingPanicNoteOff in setupProcessing.
- In Ruinae, NoteOns reach data.outputEvents at processor.cpp:347-358 when midiOutEnabled is on in MIDI or MIDI+Mod mode. Their matching NoteOffs come only from arp events (processor.cpp:366-376). Once reset() empties the core's sounding-note list, no NoteOff is ever produced for those notes.
- The comment at arp_integration_test.cpp:727 says reset "sends note-offs for sounding notes". The code shows reset() emits nothing.

Impact:
- Ruinae's own audio is unaffected, because engine_.reset() silences its voices.
- The stuck notes occur only on the downstream instrument fed by Ruinae's MIDI Out.
- That requires two settings: Arp MIDI Out turned on, which defaults to OFF (arpeggiator_params.h:130 `midiOut{false}`), and the operating mode set to MIDI or MIDI+Mod.
- In that setup, a preset change while the arp is playing is a common action and strands every sounding arp note indefinitely. A host deactivate/reactivate (sample-rate or buffer change, or a host that deactivates on bypass) does the same.
- Downstream, the result is an infinitely held note until the user sends a panic or all-notes-off.

Verdict: the defect is real and causes the stated consequence. For Gradus, MIDI Out is the main path. For Ruinae it is a secondary, default-off feature on an instrument whose main output is audio. Medium severity fits better than high.

</details>

### R-082

**Removing a global mod route shifts the grid but leaves curve/smooth/scale/bypass per slot; emptied slots are reset with performEdit only**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** ui-wiring · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/controller/controller_mod_matrix.cpp:149-157, 268-322`
- **Also flagged by:** gestalt-controller

**Problem.** ModMatrixGrid::removeRoute shifts each whole ModRoute up one slot, including curve, smoothMs, scale and bypass (mod_matrix_grid.h:198-207), then fires the route-removed callback. pushAllGlobalRouteParams re-pushes only source, destination and amount for each slot. The detail parameters of each slot (1324+slot*4 .. +3) keep their old per-index values. For slots that are now empty, the inactive branch calls performEdit(0/0/0.5) without setParamNormalized, so the controller's own Parameter objects still hold the removed route's source, destination and amount.

**Why it is wrong.** A route's identity covers all seven fields. Shifting only three of them recombines one route's source with another route's curve, scale and bypass in the DSP. The controller is responsible for its own parameter values: hosts do not echo performEdit back through setParamNormalized, which is why every other edit path here calls setParamNormalized first.

**Consequence.** Repro: route 0 = LFO1->Cutoff, route 1 = LFO2->Reso with Bypass on or Scale x4. Delete route 0. The processor now plays LFO2->Reso unbypassed at x1 (slot 0's detail params) while the grid shows it bypassed. The emptied last slot keeps its stale source param in the controller. The next syncModMatrixGrid (re-entering the MOD tab, editor reopen, or host automation of any mod-matrix param) and rebuildRingIndicators show a ghost route the processor does not have, and the host's parameter list reports the stale values.

**Suggested fix.** In pushAllGlobalRouteParams, push all seven fields for every slot (curve/3, smoothMs/100, scale/4, bypass), and call setParamNormalized before performEdit in the inactive branch too, with defaults curve 0, smooth 0, scale 2/4, bypass 0. Test: wire a ModMatrixGrid to a Controller, add two global routes with different bypass and scale, removeRoute(0), then assert that getParamNormalized for slot 0's bypass and scale equals the shifted route's values and that slot 1's source param is 0.

**Evidence.** mod_matrix_grid.h:201-205 `globalRoutes_[i] = globalRoutes_[i + 1]; ... globalRoutes_[kMaxGlobalRoutes - 1] = ModRoute{};` then :206-207 `routeRemovedCallback_(activeTab_, slot);`. controller_mod_matrix.cpp:281-306 active branch pushes only sourceId/destId/amountId. :307-319 `// Inactive slot: reset to defaults` `beginEdit(sourceId); performEdit(sourceId, 0.0); endEdit(sourceId);` (no setParamNormalized). syncModMatrixGrid (:205-262) and rebuildRingIndicators (:384-416) read getParameterObject(...)->getNormalized().

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this finding. The source confirms it.

1. The grid moves whole routes. In plugins/shared/src/ui/mod_matrix_grid.h:198-207, removeRoute copies each ModRoute (all seven fields) one slot up in the global tab, clears the last slot with ModRoute{}, and then calls routeRemovedCallback_(activeTab_, slot).

2. The controller re-pushes only three of the seven fields. For tab 0, the callback at plugins/ruinae/src/controller/controller_mod_matrix.cpp:149-157 calls pushAllGlobalRouteParams() and nothing else. In pushAllGlobalRouteParams (:268-322):
   - Active slots (:281-306) push only the source, destination and amount IDs.
   - No path ever pushes the curve, smooth, scale or bypass IDs. Those are 1324+ (plugin_ids.h:520, kModMatrixDetailBaseId), and the processor handles them per slot (parameters/mod_matrix_params.h:97-98 and :279-280).
   - So the processor's slot-i detail parameters keep the removed route's per-index values while slot i now holds a different route's source, destination and amount.
   - The grid itself holds the shifted detail values, so the grid display and the DSP disagree.

3. Emptied slots are reset without setParamNormalized. The inactive branch (:307-319) calls beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit with 0, 0 and 0.5 and never calls setParamNormalized. The controller's own Parameter objects therefore keep the stale source, destination and amount.
   - syncModMatrixGrid (:205-262) and rebuildRingIndicators (:384-416) build their state from getParameterObject(...)->getNormalized().
   - Both run on later updates: controller_view_sync.cpp:544-548 handles any mod-matrix tag, and :933-936 runs on a full view sync.
   - Either one can bring back a ghost route, because route.active = dspSrcIdx > 0 (:262 and :415).

4. No test covers this path. The only removeRoute tests are in plugins/ruinae/tests/integration/mod_matrix_grid_test.cpp (:170, :672, :747, :866, :1054). They exercise the grid on its own with stub callbacks and never wire it to the Controller.

One correction to the finding: its claim that every other edit path calls setParamNormalized first is not quite true. The grid's ParameterCallback (:55-61) calls only performEdit. This does not affect the defect.

I kept the severity at high. Deleting a route silently changes what plays for the routes after it (bypass, scale and curve come from the wrong route), and stale controller state can bring a deleted route back.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source. I found nothing that guards it, documents it as intended, or tests it.

1. Every field of a route shifts. plugins/shared/src/ui/mod_matrix_grid.h:198-207 removeRoute copies whole ModRoute structs: `globalRoutes_[i] = globalRoutes_[i + 1]`, then clears the last slot with `ModRoute{}`. That moves curve, smoothMs, scale and bypass along with the rest, and then it calls routeRemovedCallback_(activeTab_, slot).

2. Only three of those fields are pushed back to the parameters. The global-tab callback (controller_mod_matrix.cpp:149-157) calls pushAllGlobalRouteParams. That function (:268-322) pushes only sourceId, destId and amountId per slot, and it never touches modSlotCurveId, modSlotSmoothId, modSlotScaleId or modSlotBypassId. A grep shows the grid writes the detail IDs only from per-slot interactive edits (mod_matrix_grid.h:916-1043), never on removal.

3. The processor reads the detail values per slot. plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/mod_matrix_params.h:96-120 handles IDs 1324-1355 (Curve/Smooth/Scale/Bypass) and stores each slot's values. After removeRoute(0), slot 0 plays route 1's source, destination and amount with route 0's curve, smooth, scale and bypass. The grid's model shows route 1's own detail values. So the sound and the display disagree.

4. Emptied slots are reset without updating the controller. The inactive branch (:307-319) calls beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit with 0, 0 and 0.5 but no setParamNormalized. The active branch (:289, 297, 303) does call setParamNormalized. syncModMatrixGrid (:205-262) and rebuildRingIndicators (:384-416) read getParameterObject()->getNormalized(). On those paths the controller's Parameter objects still hold the removed route's source, unless the host happens to echo performEdit back to the controller.

5. No coverage and no prior record. The only removeRoute tests (plugins/ruinae/tests/integration/mod_matrix_grid_test.cpp:170, 672, 747, 866, 1054) exercise the grid alone, with empty or no-op callbacks. None wires a Controller or checks parameter values. specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json has no matching finding (no hit for removeRoute, pushAllGlobalRouteParams or shift), so this is new, not a repeat of an F-id.

Severity: I recommend a downgrade from high to medium. The bug is a UI/state desync that needs a specific user action: deleting a non-last route whose detail settings differ from the route below it. The audio stays bounded: bypass, scale and curve change how strongly one route modulates, with no NaN, crash or stuck note. The ghost route in an emptied slot appears only in the controller's view or state. The processor got source = None for that slot through performEdit, so nothing extra is heard.

**Note 3.** I confirmed this in the source. In plugins/shared/src/ui/mod_matrix_grid.h:198-207, removeRoute copies whole ModRoute structs (source, dest, amount, curve, smoothMs, scale, bypass, active) up one slot, clears the last slot, and then calls routeRemovedCallback_. In controller_mod_matrix.cpp:149-157, the removed-callback for tab 0 only calls pushAllGlobalRouteParams(). That function (:268-322) pushes only sourceId, destId and amountId for each slot. It never touches modSlotCurveId, modSlotSmoothId, modSlotScaleId or modSlotBypassId.

The processor reads those per-slot detail atomics. processor_params.cpp:488-494 loads slot.curve, slot.scale, slot.bypass and slot.smoothMs and calls engine_.setGlobalModRoute(i, src, dst, amt, curve, scaleMul, bypass, smoothMs). So after a shift, slot i plays route i+1's source, destination and amount with route i's old curve, scale, bypass and smooth. Example: route 1 was bypassed at Scale x4, route 0 was live at x1. After deleting route 0, route 1's source becomes live at x1 in the DSP, while the grid still shows it bypassed. The reverse case turns a live route silent, or gives it 4x modulation depth (about 12 dB). The saved processor state (processor_state.cpp:58-61) then stores this mixed-up patch, so the change persists.

In the inactive branch (:307-319), only beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit are called, with no setParamNormalized. The controller's Parameter objects therefore keep the removed route's source, destination and amount. syncModMatrixGrid (:205-262) and rebuildRingIndicators (:384-416) read getParameterObject()->getNormalized(). Both are re-run from controller_view_sync.cpp:544-548 on any later mod-matrix param change, and syncModMatrixGrid also runs at wireModMatrixGrid (:189) when the editor reopens. Each of these brings back a ghost route that the processor does not have. The active branch avoids this because it calls setParamNormalized first (:289, :297, :303). Within this call, suppressModMatrixSync_ hides the mismatch until the next sync.

No test covers this at the controller level. mod_matrix_grid_test.cpp only exercises the grid with no-op callbacks (:843-869).

Impact: every deletion of a route that is not the last one, when any later route has non-default detail values, silently changes the sound. Every deletion also leaves stale controller params in the vacated slot. Because the impact is audible and persists in saved state, I keep the severity at high.

</details>

### R-091

**Per-sample cutoff updates re-arm SelfOscillatingFilter's kick: every sample with a >10 Hz cutoff step wipes the ladder state and injects a +1.0 impulse**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** shared-dsp-contracts · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:523-527, 1409`

**Problem.** The voice recomputes cutoff per sample (filter envelope, key track, mod routes, MPE brightness) and calls setActiveFilterCutoff → filterSelfOsc_->setFrequency(hz) every sample. SelfOscillatingFilter::setFrequency sets needsKick_ whenever resonance > 0.9 and |newFreq − frequency_| > 10 Hz (self_oscillating_filter.h:435-437). The next process() then does filter_.reset() and adds +1.0 to the input (L273-277). frequencyRamp_.setTarget is also restarted every sample.

**Why it is wrong.** setFrequency is designed as an occasional note-pitch setter (a kick on a significant pitch change), not a per-sample modulation input. A per-sample sweep creates a 'significant change' on every sample above a few kHz (a 0.0035-semitone step is already 10 Hz at 5 kHz).

**Consequence.** Two audible effects with the Self-Osc filter type at the resonances that make it self-oscillate (Q ≥ ~10 → 0.9 remap): (1) any filter-envelope or LFO sweep through the upper range produces trains of full-scale clicks; (2) the oscillation is repeatedly cleared (filter_.reset), so the tone stutters. The impulses are multiplied by up to 5x output gain (L299-303).

**Suggested fix.** Feed per-sample modulation through a non-kicking path: add setCutoffModulation() or a `kickOnChange=false` overload that only updates the ladder cutoff, and keep setFrequency for note-on. Alternatively update the self-osc frequency at block rate with a kick threshold in semitones relative to the note. Test: SelfOsc type, Q 20, filter env amount +48 st, attack 50 ms, then REQUIRE the max per-sample |Δoutput| stays below 0.2 during the sweep.

**Evidence.** ruinae_voice.h:527 `setActiveFilterCutoff(effectiveCutoff);` (inside the per-sample loop L460), L1409 `if (filterSelfOsc_) filterSelfOsc_->setFrequency(hz);` self_oscillating_filter.h:435-437 `if (resonance_ > 0.9f && std::abs(newFreq - frequency_) > 10.0f) { needsKick_ = true; }` L273-277 `if (needsKick_ && resonance_ > 0.9f) { ... filter_.reset(); filterInput += 1.0f;`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the code path and the defect is real.

1. Per-sample cutoff update. plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:460-536: inside the per-sample loop, effectiveCutoff = filterCutoffHz_ * semitonesToRatio(filterEnvAmount_*filterEnvVal + keyTrack + cutoffModSemitones + brightness) (L519-524). The loop then calls setActiveFilterCutoff(effectiveCutoff) (L527) and processActiveFilter (L536) on every sample. For RuinaeFilterType::SelfOscillating, setActiveFilterCutoff calls filterSelfOsc_->setFrequency(hz) (L1408-1409), and processActiveFilter calls filterSelfOsc_->process(input) (L1474-1475).

2. Kick re-arm. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/self_oscillating_filter.h:430-441: setFrequency sets needsKick_ = true when resonance_ > 0.9f and |newFreq - frequency_| > 10 Hz. It then stores frequency_ = newFreq, so the 10 Hz threshold applies to each per-sample step, not to the change since note-on. It also calls frequencyRamp_.setTarget every sample.

3. Kick action. In the same sample, process() (L273-278) runs filter_.reset(), which clears the ladder state and therefore the running oscillation, and adds filterInput += 1.0f. In the self-oscillation region the output is then multiplied by up to kSelfOscGain = 5.0 (L149, L299-303).

4. Reachability. remapResonanceForSelfOsc (ruinae_voice.h:1645-1655) maps any Q above 10 to a normalized value above 0.9, so the gate opens across the whole upper third of the Q range, which is the range where this filter type does what it is for.

How often it fires: the per-sample step is f*ln2/12*dSt, about 0.0578*f*dSt Hz.
- A filter envelope of +48 st with a 5 ms attack is 0.218 st/sample at 44.1 kHz, so the step passes 10 Hz above about 800 Hz.
- A 50 ms attack passes it above about 8 kHz.
- Envelope decay segments, fast LFO routes and MPE brightness jumps do the same.
In those cases the filter is reset and given an impulse on every sample, so the oscillation is wiped and replaced by a train of impulses.

Test coverage: the only voice test of this type (plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/ruinae_voice_test.cpp:2500-2523) uses a static 440 Hz cutoff with no modulation, so it does not cover this case.

Severity: I left it at high. The defect is real and audible, but only with the SelfOsc filter type at Q above 10 under fast cutoff modulation. That is the type's main use (enveloped self-oscillating plucks), so I see no reason to downgrade it.

**Note 2.** The finding holds up in source, and I found nothing upstream that guards it.

How it happens:
- ruinae_voice.h:460-527 recomputes effectiveCutoff for every sample from the filter envelope, key track, the voice mod-route offset and MPE brightness, then calls setActiveFilterCutoff(effectiveCutoff) on every sample.
- For the SelfOscillating type, setActiveFilterCutoff (L1408-1409) calls filterSelfOsc_->setFrequency(hz) directly. The comparison, ramp and kick logic all live inside the shared DSP filter, with no change gate on the voice side.
- In self_oscillating_filter.h:430-441, setFrequency sets needsKick_ = true whenever resonance_ > 0.9f and |newFreq - frequency_| > 10 Hz. It then calls frequencyRamp_.setTarget.
- The next process() (L273-277) sees needsKick_ with resonance > 0.9. It calls filter_.reset(), which clears the ladder state, and adds +1.0 to the input. L299-303 then applies up to kSelfOscGain = 5.0 (L149).
- remapResonanceForSelfOsc (ruinae_voice.h:1645-1655) maps Q >= 10 to above 0.9. That is exactly the "musical Q" range the test at ruinae_voice_test.cpp:2511-2544 expects to oscillate, and factory presets use Q 18-25. So the kick condition is live in normal use.

Arithmetic check: with a +48 st filter-envelope amount over a 50 ms attack at 44.1 kHz, each sample moves about 0.022 st. That step exceeds 10 Hz above about 7.9 kHz, so every sample above that kicks and resets the filter. A faster attack, an LFO route or MPE brightness lowers that threshold. A static cutoff never triggers a kick, so the bug only appears under modulation, which matches the claim.

What I checked for a refutation:
- No code comment or doc says per-sample setFrequency is intended. The filter's own comment ("If frequency changes significantly, kick-start oscillation") describes an occasional pitch-change setter.
- The voice keeps no previous-cutoff value and does no rate limiting before L1409.
- The only Ruinae test for this filter type (ruinae_voice_test.cpp:2511) holds the cutoff fixed at 440 Hz with no envelope amount, so no test pins or covers sweep behaviour.
- The audit probe at audit_probes.cpp:1342 only switches the filter type.

I did not run a render, so the audible size of the clicks is unmeasured. The mechanism, though, is confirmed line by line, and the high severity rating is reasonable.

**Note 3.** I could not refute this finding. The source confirms each step of the claimed chain.

1. ruinae_voice.h:460-536: inside the per-sample loop, the cutoff is rebuilt every sample. It is filterCutoffHz_ * semitonesToRatio(filterEnvAmount_*filterEnvVal + keyTrack + cutoffMod + brightness) (L519-523). Line 527 then calls setActiveFilterCutoff(effectiveCutoff) on every sample with no change check.
2. ruinae_voice.h:1408-1409: for RuinaeFilterType::SelfOscillating, that call goes straight to filterSelfOsc_->setFrequency(hz).
3. self_oscillating_filter.h:430-441: setFrequency sets needsKick_ = true whenever resonance_ > 0.9f and |newFreq - frequency_| > 10 Hz. It also calls frequencyRamp_.setTarget every time.
4. self_oscillating_filter.h:273-278: on the next process(), if needsKick_ && resonance_ > 0.9f, it runs filter_.reset(), which clears the ladder state, and adds +1.0 to the input. The output is then multiplied by up to kSelfOscGain = 5.0 (L149, L299-303).
5. ruinae_voice.h:1645-1651: remapResonanceForSelfOsc maps Q 10 to exactly 0.9, so any user Q above 10 meets the resonance_ > 0.9 gate.

How often it fires: at 44.1 kHz the kick re-arms on every sample where the per-sample cutoff step exceeds 10 Hz.
- A filter-envelope attack of +48 st over 50 ms moves about 0.0218 st per sample, a ratio step of about 0.126%. Kicks fire on every sample once the cutoff passes about 7.9 kHz.
- A fast pluck envelope (+48 st, 1 ms attack) moves about 1.09 st per sample. Kicks fire above about 155 Hz, so nearly the whole attack is a run of reset-plus-impulse samples.
- Envelope decay segments and fast LFO or mod-matrix sweeps at high cutoffs trigger it the same way.
- Slow sweeps at low cutoffs do not trigger it. A 1 Hz LFO of ±24 st only reaches the 10 Hz step size at cutoffs far above the clamp. So the reviewer's "any sweep through the upper range" is overstated, but common filter-envelope settings do hit it.

Consequence: each kick wipes the ladder state, which cuts off the oscillation, and injects a full-scale impulse that is amplified up to 5x. That is an audible click or buzz train in the self-oscillation mode this filter type exists for.

Scope: it needs the user to choose the Self-Osc filter type with Q above 10 plus a moving cutoff. Default settings are not affected. Within that mode the defect is audible and easy to hit, so I left severity unchanged at high.

</details>

### R-113

**SC-004b golden MIDI fixtures pin stuck MIDI-out notes on Slide steps (5 goldens end with note-ons that never get a note-off)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/ruinae_byte_identical_post_lane10_test.cpp:362-438 (verifyPreset); fixtures/ruinae_factory_{Acid_Gate,Acid_Line_303,Arp_Filter_Sweep,Arp_Self_Modulator,Ratio_Stutter}_golden_midi.txt`

**Problem.** The goldens are produced by the processor itself (RUINAE_REGEN_GOLDENS=1 rewrites them from captured output, :202-217, :417-422), and compareMidiGolden only checks equality with that capture. No independent invariant is checked. A node scan of all 46 fixtures (the sequence releases every key at 45 s and runs to 60 s) found 5 goldens with unbalanced note-ons. Acid_Gate: 361 on / 271 off, pitch 76 last event noteOn@1956938. Acid_Line_303: 361/271, 64 held. Arp_Filter_Sweep: 376/329, pitches 79, 83 (from 438896 = 9.9 s) and 86 held forever. Arp_Self_Modulator: 381/286, 5 pitches held. Ratio_Stutter: 230/219. All five presets use kStepSlide in their modifier lane (generator :10111-10114, :9244-9248).

**Why it is wrong.** On a Slide step the core cancels the previous note's pending off and emits a legato NoteOn without a NoteOff (arpeggiator_core.cpp:1123-1158), then replaces currentArpNotes_ with the new note (:1156-1157). The engine handles this through the legato flag. The MIDI-out branch (processor.cpp:347-358) drops the flag and emits a plain kNoteOnEvent, so the previous pitch never gets a NoteOff on the output bus. Transport stop and panic only release currentArpNotes_, so the old pitch is also never released at the end. Every note-on sent to a host must eventually get a matching note-off. The golden treats the stuck notes as the expected output, and a regeneration bakes them in again.

**Consequence.** With Arp MIDI Out enabled, any slide preset leaves notes stuck on the downstream instrument (Arp_Filter_Sweep strands pitch 83 after 10 s). The regression test fails any fix, because the event count changes, so the bug is protected.

**Suggested fix.** Emit a NoteOff for the outgoing pitch(es) before or at the legato NoteOn on the MIDI-out path, or carry legato as overlapping notes and release the old pitch at the new onset. In verifyPreset add an invariant that runs before the golden compare and also in regen mode, so an unbalanced golden can never be written: for every pitch, onCount == offCount and the last event after the 45 s release is noteOff. Add processor test ArpMidiOut_SlideStep_EveryNoteOnHasNoteOff (arp_integration_test.cpp): modifier lane {Active, Active|Slide}, midiOut=1, capture outputEvents for 4 bars, release keys, and REQUIRE per-pitch balance. Regenerate the 5 goldens after the fix.

**Evidence.** node scan output: 'Acid_Gate: on=361 off=271 stuckAtEnd=90 ... last event noteOn 76@1956938'; 'Arp_Filter_Sweep ... 79@1916889 83@438896 86@1959130'; 'Arp_Self_Modulator ... 71@1971329 75@407210 78@655747 68@427906 90@1950674'. processor.cpp:351-358 'e.type = kNoteOnEvent; ... e.noteOn.noteId = -1; data.outputEvents->addEvent(e);' with no use of evt.legato. arpeggiator_core.cpp:1124-1126 '// Slide: suppress previous noteOffs ... cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes(); // Do NOT emit noteOffs for currently sounding notes'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Confirmed from source and from my own scan of the fixtures.

1. The core emits a legato NoteOn and no NoteOff on a Slide step. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:1123-1158 the isSlide branch calls cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes() at :1125, which drops the previous note's scheduled off. The comment at :1126 reads "Do NOT emit noteOffs for currently sounding notes". The branch then emits NoteOn{.legato=true} (:1133-1138 for a chord, :1148-1153 for a single note) and overwrites currentArpNotes_ (:1142-1144, :1156-1157). After that the old pitch is no longer tracked, so the transport-stop and disable releases that walk currentArpNotes_ cannot release it.

2. The MIDI-out path ignores the legato flag. In plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:342-358, evt.legato goes only to queueTimedEvent for the engine (:346). The output event at :348-358 is a plain kNoteOnEvent with noteId -1 and no NoteOff for the outgoing pitch. The NoteOff branch (:361-377) forwards only NoteOff events the core actually emitted, so the slid-from pitch never gets a NoteOff on the output bus.

3. The fixtures pin this. I ran a node scan (scratchpad scan.js) over plugins/ruinae/tests/fixtures. Exactly five goldens are unbalanced:
- Acid_Gate: 361 on / 271 off
- Acid_Line_303: 361 / 271
- Arp_Filter_Sweep: 376 / 329
- Arp_Self_Modulator: 381 / 286
- Ratio_Stutter: 230 / 219

These match the finding. The last event for several pitches is a noteOn that never gets an off, even though the keys are released at 45 s and the capture runs to 60 s:
- Acid_Gate: `[1956938] noteOn 76`
- Arp_Filter_Sweep: `[438896] noteOn 83`, `[1916889] noteOn 79`, `[1959130] noteOn 86`
- Ratio_Stutter: `[1971160] noteOn 60`

4. The test checks no independent invariant. plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/ruinae_byte_identical_post_lane10_test.cpp:362-438 (verifyPreset) has two paths. In regen mode it writes the captured output straight to the golden (:417-421). Otherwise it only calls compareMidiGolden(actual, golden) (:431-437). It never checks per-pitch on/off balance, so the golden protects the stuck-note behaviour, and any fix that adds NoteOffs changes the event count and fails the test.

The defect is a real stuck MIDI-out note with Arp MIDI Out enabled on Slide presets, and the regression test pins it. Severity high stands.

**Note 2.** I confirmed this from the source and by scanning the fixtures myself. (1) The core's Slide path, dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:1123-1158, calls cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes() (header :1499-1513). That removes every pending NoteOff for the old notes. The core then emits a NoteOn with legato=true and no NoteOff, and overwrites currentArpNotes_[0] and currentArpNoteCount_ (:1156-1157 single note, :1141-1144 chord). After that the old pitch has no output NoteOff, no pending NoteOff and no tracking entry, so the transport-stop and disable flush cannot release it either. (2) processor.cpp:336-358 passes evt.legato to the engine queue (:346), where it means glide without retrigger. The MIDI-out branch (:347-358) ignores evt.legato and writes a plain kNoteOnEvent with noteId=-1. The NoteOff branch (:361-377) only forwards NoteOffs the core actually emits. So on the output bus the previous pitch is never released. (3) The golden is the processor's own output-bus capture: ruinae_byte_identical_post_lane10_test.cpp:327-351 reads data.outputEvents, :404-409 forces kArpMidiOutId=1, and :417-422 writes that capture as the golden when RUINAE_REGEN_GOLDENS=1. :431-437 then checks only equality with the golden; there is no per-pitch balance check. (4) My own node scan of all 46 fixtures found exactly the five files the finding names: Acid_Gate 361 on / 271 off, Acid_Line_303 361/271, Arp_Filter_Sweep 376/329, Arp_Self_Modulator 381/286, Ratio_Stutter 230/219. In each, specific pitches have more on than off (e.g. Arp_Self_Modulator 71x42, 90x31). The other 41 fixtures balance. (5) I found nothing that makes this intentional for MIDI out. The archived spec 073 FR-003/FR-015 says legato tells the *receiving engine* to suppress retrigger and glide. specs/arpeggiator-roadmap.md:546 says "No noteOff until next note", which means the old note should still end when the next one starts, not that it is never released. Gradus has no legato handling. specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json has no slide or legato entry, so this is new, not a repeat of an F-id. The stuck-note bug itself is in processor.cpp:347-358, and the golden test pins it in place. Severity high is justified: the stuck notes reach the host's downstream instrument and never stop. MIDI Out is opt-in, so it does not affect the internal sound.

**Note 3.** I could not refute this. I confirmed it in the source and by counting the goldens. (1) dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:1123-1158: on a Slide step, cancelPendingNoteOffsForCurrentNotes() runs, a NoteOn with .legato=true is emitted, and no NoteOff is emitted for the sounding note (the comment at :1126 says so). currentArpNotes_[0] is then overwritten with the new pitch (:1156-1157), so the old pitch is no longer tracked and the transport-stop/disable cleanup cannot release it later. (2) plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:343-346 forwards evt.legato to the engine queue, but the MIDI-out branch at :347-358 builds a plain kNoteOnEvent and ignores evt.legato. No NoteOff for the outgoing pitch is sent on the output bus. (3) The goldens are captured from that same output bus: ruinae_byte_identical_post_lane10_test.cpp:329-351 reads data.outputEvents after kArpMidiOutId is forced to 1.0 (:404-409). Regen mode writes the capture straight to the golden (:417-422). Otherwise compareMidiGolden only checks equality with the stored file (:431-437). No per-pitch balance invariant exists anywhere. (4) An awk scan of all 46 fixtures matches the reviewer's numbers and finds exactly these 5 unbalanced files: Acid_Gate on=361/off=271 (pitch 76 last event noteOn @1956938); Acid_Line_303 361/271 (64 last noteOn @1940400); Arp_Filter_Sweep 376/329 (79 @1916889, 83 @438896, 86 @1959130, each last event a noteOn); Arp_Self_Modulator 381/286 (68, 71, 75, 78, 90 last noteOn); Ratio_Stutter 230/219 (60 last noteOn @1971160). The input sequence releases every key at 45 s (:163-165), and these noteOns get no later noteOff before 60 s. Impact: with Arp MIDI Out on in MIDI or MIDI+Mod mode, any slide step hangs the previous pitch on the downstream instrument indefinitely; in Arp_Filter_Sweep, pitch 83 is held from about 10 s. The trigger needs MIDI Out, which is opt-in, but a stuck note on a host's downstream instrument is a user-facing failure and the golden locks it in, so high severity stands. One nuance: the root defect is in processor.cpp:347-358, not the test file. The test-gap is the reason the defect has stayed protected.

</details>

### R-115

**ArpIntegration_EnableWithExistingHeldNote_NoStuckNotes asserts that the stuck note keeps sounding**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/processor/arp_integration_test.cpp:803-870`

**Problem.** The test plays C4 with the arp Off, switches the arp to MIDI, and releases the key. It then CHECKs that audio is STILL present (CHECK(audioAfterNoteOff), :869). The comments state that the engine never receives the note-off, and the test treats that as correct ('no duplicate note-offs or stuck notes from the transition'). It renders only 3 blocks and never asserts the note ever ends.

**Why it is wrong.** onNoteOff routes by the CURRENT op mode (processor_midi.cpp:180-193). A key pressed in Off or Mod mode gets an engine NoteOn (:172-176). If it is released after a switch to MIDI or MIDI+Mod, the release goes only to arpCore_ (:188-189) and never to the engine (:191). The default amp sustain is 0.8, so that voice is stuck forever. The test turns this stuck-note bug into a requirement: any fix that releases the direct voice turns it red.

**Consequence.** A user who toggles the arp on while holding a key gets a hanging voice. The suite blocks the fix.

**Suggested fix.** Invert the assertion. After the note-off, render release time plus 10 blocks and REQUIRE 10 consecutive silent blocks. Fix the routing: track which pitches were sent straight to the engine (a 128-bit set filled at :174) and always send their NoteOff to the engine whatever the current mode. Add the reverse case ArpIntegration_DisableWithHeldKey_KeyReleasesCleanly (MIDI→Off with a key held).

**Evidence.** test :866-869 '// The original engine note should still be sounding because the note-off went to the arp (not the engine). This is the expected behavior ... CHECK(audioAfterNoteOff);'; processor_midi.cpp:191-193 'if (!arpDispatchesNotes) { queueTimedEvent({... NoteOff ...}); }'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Confirmed from source. The test and the routing code do what the finding says. One part of the consequence is wrong.

1. The test puts the arp in MIDI mode. ArpIntegrationFixture::enableArp (arp_integration_test.cpp:270-274) sets kArpOperatingModeId to 1/3, which maps to kArpMIDI (arpeggiator_params_test.cpp:67-71).

2. The note-off never reaches the engine. Processor::onNoteOn (processor_midi.cpp:158-177) queues an engine NoteOn only when the mode is not MIDI or MIDI+Mod (:172-176). Processor::onNoteOff (:180-194) also routes by the CURRENT mode. In MIDI mode it calls only arpCore_.noteOff (:188-189) and skips the engine NoteOff (:191-193). The MPE overloads (:201-217 and after) do the same.
