**Global LFO rate clamps at 20 Hz although the Rate parameter spans 0.01-50 Hz**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** modulation · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/lfo_params.h:30, 64-75`

**Problem.** The LFO Rate parameter maps 0-1 to 0.01-50 Hz (logMapFromNormalized) and displays up to 50 Hz (MANUAL documents 0.01-50 Hz). The LFO primitive clamps frequency to kMaxFrequency = 20 Hz in setFrequency and in tempo sync (lfo.h:35, 213-214, 517).

**Why it is wrong.** The DSP must honour the documented and displayed range. The top ~11% of the knob (normalized ~0.89-1.0, 20-50 Hz) does nothing.

**Consequence.** Users setting 30 or 50 Hz for audio-rate-ish wobble get 20 Hz while the display shows 50 Hz. The same cap silently slows fast tempo-synced values (e.g. 1/64 at high BPM).

**Suggested fix.** Raise LFO kMaxFrequency to 50 Hz (check other consumers), or limit the Ruinae parameter range to 20 Hz. Test: set LFO1 Rate normalized 1.0 and measure the LFO1 period from getModulationOffset over many sub-blocks (expect 50 Hz).

**Evidence.** lfo_params.h:30 `rateHz{1.0f};       // 0.01-50 Hz`, :68-70 `logMapFromNormalized(value, 0.01, 50.0)`; lfo.h:35 `inline constexpr float kMaxFrequency = 20.0f;`, :213-214 `frequency_ = std::clamp(hz, kMinFrequency, kMaxFrequency);`

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Confirmed from source. plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/lfo_params.h:68-70 maps the normalized Rate to logMapFromNormalized(value, 0.01, 50.0), and handleLFOParamChange (:111-112) stores that value in params.rateHz. plugin_ids.h:442 also documents kLFO1RateId as 0.01-50 Hz. processor_params.cpp:430/447 passes rateHz unchanged to engine_.setGlobalLFO1Rate/2Rate. ruinae_engine.h:486/488 forwards to globalModEngine_.setLFO1Rate/2Rate. modulation_engine.h:417/435 calls lfo1_.setFrequency(hz)/lfo2_.setFrequency(hz) directly, with no other rate path. dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/lfo.h:213-214 then clamps: `frequency_ = std::clamp(hz, kMinFrequency, kMaxFrequency);`, and :35 sets kMaxFrequency = 20.0f. Tempo sync is clamped the same way at :517. The log map puts 20 Hz at normalized log(2000)/log(5000) ≈ 0.892, so roughly the top 11% of the knob produces no change in the LFO rate while the parameter value (and its display) reads up to 50 Hz. I found nothing between the parameter and the primitive that rescales or bypasses the clamp, so the finding is correct as stated. Medium severity is appropriate: the rate is silently capped and the displayed value is wrong, but it causes no instability or safety problem.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding, and nothing upstream or downstream lifts the cap.

The path, checked in source:
- **Parameter range:** `plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/lfo_params.h:68-71`. `lfoRateFromNormalized` returns `logMapFromNormalized(value, 0.01, 50.0)`. `handleLFOParamChange` (`:111-112`) stores that value unclamped in `rateHz`.
- **Documented range:** the comment at `lfo_params.h:30` and the one at `plugin_ids.h:442` (`kLFO1RateId = 1000, // 0.01-50 Hz`) both give 0.01-50 Hz. `MANUAL.md:492` says "LFO speed. 0.01–50 Hz in free mode".
- **Call chain:** `processor_params.cpp:430` calls `engine_.setGlobalLFO1Rate(lfo1Params_.rateHz.load())`. That goes to `ruinae_engine.h:486` `setGlobalLFO1Rate` -> `globalModEngine_.setLFO1Rate(hz)`, then to `modulation_engine.h:417` `setLFO1Rate(float hz) { lfo1_.setFrequency(hz); }` (LFO 2 is the same, at `:435`).
- **The cap:** in `dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/lfo.h:213-214`, `setFrequency` does `frequency_ = std::clamp(hz, kMinFrequency, kMaxFrequency)`, and `lfo.h:35` sets `kMaxFrequency = 20.0f`. The tempo-sync path clamps to the same 20 Hz at `lfo.h:517`.

So every rate between 20 and 50 Hz plays at 20 Hz. On the log map that is the top ln(50/20)/ln(5000) ≈ 10.8 % of the knob, which matches the finding's ~11 %.

I found nothing that marks this as intended: no code comment, no MANUAL note, no test pinning 20 Hz, and no entry in `specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json` (a grep for `kMaxFrequency` and "50 Hz" found nothing). It is a mismatch between the parameter range and what the DSP accepts. Medium severity fits: no crash or output hazard, but the top tenth of a documented control does nothing.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the defect from source.

**The parameter range is 0.01-50 Hz.** plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/lfo_params.h:68-75 maps the Rate parameter with `logMapFromNormalized(value, 0.01, 50.0)`, and the comment at :30 says "0.01-50 Hz".

**The value reaches the LFO primitive unchanged.** processor_params.cpp:430 and :447 call `engine_.setGlobalLFO1Rate` / `setGlobalLFO2Rate` with `rateHz`. ruinae_engine.h:486 and :488 forward to `globalModEngine_.setLFO1Rate` / `setLFO2Rate`. modulation_engine.h:417 and :435 call `lfo1_.setFrequency(hz)` / `lfo2_.setFrequency(hz)`, and `lfo1_` is a `Krate::DSP::LFO` (modulation_engine.h:21 includes primitives/lfo.h; the member is declared at :830).

**The primitive clamps at 20 Hz.** lfo.h:35 sets `kMaxFrequency = 20.0f`. lfo.h:214 applies `frequency_ = std::clamp(hz, kMinFrequency, kMaxFrequency)`, and :517 applies the same clamp to `tempoSyncFrequency_`.

**How much of the knob is dead:** 20 Hz sits at normalized log(2000)/log(5000) ≈ 0.892. Above that, the top 10.8% of the knob does nothing, and the displayed value (up to 50 Hz) can be 2.5x the real rate.

**Tempo sync is affected too.** The shared note-value list (plugins/shared/src/ui/note_value_ui.h:21-27) offers 1/64T, 1/64, 1/64D, 1/32T and 1/32. At 120 BPM:
- 1/64T is 48 Hz and becomes 20 Hz.
- 1/64 is 32 Hz and becomes 20 Hz.
- 1/32T is 24 Hz and becomes 20 Hz.
- 1/32 reaches 20 Hz from 150 BPM up and stays at 20 Hz.

So those divisions silently stop following the tempo and drift against the grid. 1/64T is already clamped from 50 BPM up.

**Severity stays medium.** It is a real mismatch between what the user sees and what the DSP does, and it breaks tempo lock for the fastest note values. It does not cause instability, stuck notes or NaN, so medium is the right level.

</details>

### R-049

**Arp Rate modulation in tempo-sync mode abandons host grid lock and pins slow note values to 0.5 Hz on any non-zero offset**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** modulation · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:885-908`
- **Also flagged by:** arpeggiator, portability-quality, gestalt-processor

**Problem.** When tempoSync is on and the ArpRate offset is non-zero, the code converts the note value to Hz, calls arpCore_.setTempoSync(false) and setFreeRate(clamp(hz, 0.5, 50)). syncToMusicalPosition is then a no-op (arpeggiator_core.h:1030 `if (!tempoSync_ ...) return;`), so the arp free-runs off the host grid while any route is non-zero, and snaps back to sync whenever the offset returns to exactly 0. Note values slower than 2 s (e.g. 1/1 at 60 BPM = 0.25 Hz, the dotted and 2/1-4/1 entries) are clamped up to 0.5 Hz, so a 0.001 offset makes the arp 2x-8x faster.

**Why it is wrong.** A tempo-synced arp must stay phase-locked to the host transport, and modulation should scale the step duration within sync. A tiny offset must produce a tiny rate change, not a jump caused by a clamp.

**Consequence.** With any LFO/Macro route to Arp Rate, a synced arp drifts against the DAW grid and jumps back each time the offset crosses 0. Slow synced patterns double or more in speed as soon as a route is added.

**Suggested fix.** Keep tempoSync on and pass a duration scale to the core (e.g. setRateScale(1+0.5*off) applied in calculateStepDuration), or at least apply the clamp only to the modulated result relative to the base. Test: 1/1 note value at 60 BPM, ArpRate offset 0.001. The step duration must stay within 0.1% of 4 s, and syncToMusicalPosition must keep step starts on the host grid.

**Evidence.** processor_params.cpp:885 `if (rateOffset != 0.0f && tempoSync) {`, :896-897 `arpCore_.setTempoSync(false); arpCore_.setFreeRate(std::clamp(effectiveHz, 0.5f, 50.0f));`; arpeggiator_core.h:438-440 setFreeRate clamp; :1030 `if (!tempoSync_ || currentStepDuration_ == 0) return;`

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. I checked each step of the claim against the source and it holds.

1. Override branch. In processor_params.cpp:885-897, applyArpParams() runs the branch `if (rateOffset != 0.0f && tempoSync)` whenever the arp is not off (:869). It reads noteValue (:887) and computes baseDurationMs with dropdownToDelayMs(noteIdx, tempoBPM_) (:888). It then divides by scaleFactor = 1 + 0.5*offset (:891-894), calls `arpCore_.setTempoSync(false)` (:896) and calls `arpCore_.setFreeRate(std::clamp(effectiveHz, 0.5f, 50.0f))` (:897). Any offset other than exactly 0 takes this path. When the offset returns to 0, the else branch at :904 calls setTempoSync(true), so the arp snaps back to sync.

2. Lost grid lock. In processor.cpp, applyParamsToEngine() is called at :251, before the arp block. Then :325-326 calls `arpCore_.syncToMusicalPosition(...)`, and arpeggiator_core.h:1030 returns early with `if (!tempoSync_ || currentStepDuration_ == 0) return;`. setTempoSync (arpeggiator_core.h:427-429) only sets the flag. So while the override is active, the step clock is never realigned to PPQ. calculateStepDuration (:1095-1096) then takes the free-rate branch, `sampleRate_ / freeRateHz_`, so the steps free-run off the host grid.

3. 0.5 Hz floor. The clamp floor is 0.5 Hz both in the processor (:897) and in setFreeRate (arpeggiator_core.h:438-440, kMinFreeRate). The dropdown in note_value.h:160-177 contains slow values: 1/2D is 3 beats, 1/1 is 4 beats, and 2/1 and up are longer. At 60 BPM, 1/1 is 4000 ms, which is 0.25 Hz; it is clamped to 0.5 Hz, so the step becomes 2 s. A 0.001 offset should have changed the duration by 0.05%, but the step halves instead. At 120 BPM, 2/1 (4 s) shows the same jump. The Ruinae note-value parameter is clamped to kNoteValueDropdownCount (arpeggiator_params.h:248-250), and the 21-entry comment covers indices 0-20, which include 1/1 (index 19) and 1/1D (index 20). So these slow values are reachable even if the 2/1-4/1 entries are not exposed.

4. Test gap. The covering tests in arp_mod_integration_test.cpp:523-576 (ArpRateTempoSync_PositiveOffset) and :578 onward (ArpRateTempoSync_NegativeOffset) use a short note value with offset ±1. They check only that the step interval is shorter or longer than unmodulated. Neither test runs with transport/PPQ, uses a slow note value or uses a small offset, so neither the clamp jump nor the lost grid lock is covered.

The FR-014 comment shows the free-rate override was a deliberate design, but nothing in the stated architecture says that losing grid lock or clamping slow values was intended. Medium severity is reasonable: this is a timing/musical defect with no crash, stuck note or NaN.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. The code does what the reviewer says, and I found nothing that guards against it or documents it as intended.

What the code does:
- processor_params.cpp:885-897: when tempoSync is on and rateOffset != 0.0f, the code takes baseDurationMs = dropdownToDelayMs(noteIdx, tempoBPM_), works out effectiveHz = 1000 / (baseDurationMs / (1 + 0.5*off)), then calls arpCore_.setTempoSync(false) and setFreeRate(std::clamp(effectiveHz, 0.5f, 50.0f)).
- :902-904: when the offset is exactly 0, sync is switched back on.
- arpeggiator_core.h:173-174 sets kMinFreeRate = 0.5. setFreeRate (:438-440) clamps to that same range.
- syncToMusicalPosition (:1029-1030) returns early when !tempoSync_. So while any non-zero offset is active, the arp runs free off the host grid. It goes back into sync only when the offset is exactly 0.

Slow note values are reachable:
- core/note_value.h:124-177 has 30 dropdown entries, up to 4/1D (24 beats). The plugin clamps noteValue to kNoteValueDropdownCount-1 (arpeggiator_params.h:1281).
- At 60 BPM, 1/1 = 4000 ms = 0.25 Hz. A 0.001 offset gives about 0.2501 Hz, which the clamp raises to 0.5 Hz: twice as fast.
- At 120 BPM, any value longer than 2 s (2/1, 3/1, 4/1 and their dotted forms) jumps to 0.5 Hz. 4/1D jumps by 24x.
- In true sync mode the core computes the step duration from the note value without this Hz clamp. So the jump comes only from the override path, not from a design limit.

Nothing protects against it:
- The design notes in specs/arpeggiator-roadmap.md:916 say only "Rate modulation handles both free-rate and tempo-sync modes". They do not mention leaving the grid or clamping slow values.
- The code comment at :886 calls the path a "Tempo-sync override" but says nothing about the clamp.
- The tests do not pin the correct behaviour:
  - arp_mod_integration_test.cpp:523-627 (T015/T016) use only dropdown index 6, which is 1/16T and not "1/16" as the comment says, at 120 BPM with offset ±1.
  - They check the step interval loosely (fewer than 11 or more than 11 blocks), behind an `if` that can let them pass vacuously.
  - No test covers note values slower than 2 s, small offsets, or grid alignment while modulated.
  - tempoBPM_ also feeds the override, so the effect depends on the host tempo.

Severity stays medium: the timing is wrong whenever a route to Arp Rate is active and a slow synced note value is chosen.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the defect in source, and the claimed consequences can happen.

1. The tempo-sync override exists. plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:885 enters the override branch whenever `rateOffset != 0.0f && tempoSync`. Lines 888-895 convert the note value to Hz with dropdownToDelayMs, line 896 calls `arpCore_.setTempoSync(false)`, and line 897 calls `setFreeRate(std::clamp(effectiveHz, 0.5f, 50.0f))`. setFreeRate (arpeggiator_core.h:438-440) clamps to kMinFreeRate/kMaxFreeRate again.

2. Grid lock is lost. processor.cpp:325-327 calls `arpCore_.syncToMusicalPosition(blockCtx.projectTimeMusic)` on every playing block, and that call is what keeps sync mode on the host grid. arpeggiator_core.h:1030 returns early with `if (!tempoSync_ || currentStepDuration_ == 0) return;`, so while any offset is non-zero the per-block re-sync is skipped. calculateStepDuration (arpeggiator_core.h:1086-1097) then takes the free-rate branch, `static_cast<size_t>(sampleRate_ / freeRateHz_)`. That value is a truncated duration derived from a float Hz value, so the arp drifts against the transport. A continuous LFO or Chaos route rarely gives exactly 0.0f, so in practice the arp stays unsynced for as long as the route exists. When the offset does reach 0, lines 902-904 restore tempoSync, and the next block's syncToMusicalPosition snaps the counter back to the grid, which can shorten or lengthen the step in progress.

3. The clamp distortion is real and affects selectable values. The Ruinae arp noteValue parameter covers all 30 dropdown entries (arpeggiator_params.h:249, clamp to kNoteValueDropdownCount-1). note_value.h:137-177 maps them up to 4/1D (24 beats). Any step longer than 2 s maps below 0.5 Hz and is clamped up to 0.5 Hz:
   - At 120 BPM: 1/1 (2 s) is exactly at the edge. 2/1 (4 s) plays 2x faster, 4/1 (8 s) 4x and 4/1D (12 s) 6x.
   - At 60 BPM: 1/1 (4 s) plays 2x faster, 4/1D (24 s) 12x.
   So a tiny offset such as 0.001 produces a 2x-12x jump in rate, not a 0.05% change.

The tests in plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/processor/arp_mod_integration_test.cpp (ArpRateTempoSync_PositiveOffset/NegativeOffset, lines 523-628) cover the override branch. From their setup they appear to use short note values (the defaults) where the clamp does not bind, and they do not check grid lock against projectTimeMusic, so neither consequence is caught.

I did not run a measurement. The verdict rests on reading the code above. Medium severity is appropriate: the bug appears only when a mod route targets Arp Rate while sync is on, but it then breaks grid lock in every host with a playing transport, and slow note values change speed by large factors.

</details>

### R-050

**Sidechain analysis ignores bus activation: a host buffer on the inactive aux bus switches Env/Pitch Follower and Transient to analysing silence**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** modulation · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:471-489`
- **Also flagged by:** gestalt-processor

**Problem.** process() treats data.inputs[0] as a connected sidechain whenever it has channel pointers. It does not check whether the aux bus was activated (the bus is added default-inactive at :58-62, and the processor has no activateBus override and never reads isActive() or silenceFlags). The engine then uses the sidechain instead of self-analysis and turns off note-triggered transients (ruinae_engine.h:832-839).

**Why it is wrong.** VST3 hosts may pass buffers for deactivated buses (the API sizes inputs by all buses). The sidechain should override self-analysis only when the bus is active (Bus::isActive()) and ideally not silent.

**Consequence.** In such hosts, without any routing by the user, Env Follower, Pitch Follower and Transient routes go dead (they analyse zeros, and transients no longer fire on note-on). The kSidechainActive indicator also reports 'active'.

**Suggested fix.** Gate on audioInputs[0]->isActive() (store the flag in activateBus) before using the buffers. Test: processor with an inactive aux bus but valid zero buffers, Transient -> Master Volume route, note-on. The Transient offset must be > 0 after the note.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:475-482 `if (data.numInputs > 0 && data.inputs) { const auto& scBus = data.inputs[0]; if (scBus.numChannels >= 2 && scBus.channelBuffers32 && ...) { ... sidechainActive = true; }`; :62 `0 /* not default-active ... */`; grep activateBus/silenceFlags under plugins/ruinae/src/processor: none; ruinae_engine.h:835 `globalModEngine_.setTransientAudioDetection(sidechainConnected);`

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute the finding; the code does what it describes. processor.cpp:58-62 adds the stereo kAux "Sidechain" input with flags 0, so the bus starts inactive. At processor.cpp:475-488, process() sets sidechainL/R and sidechainActive=true whenever data.inputs[0] has 2 channels with non-null channelBuffers32[0] and [1], or 1 channel with a non-null [0]. It never checks whether the bus is active or reads silenceFlags. A grep for activateBus, isActive and silenceFlags under plugins/ruinae/src finds only voice and envelope isActive() calls, so nothing in the processor checks bus state. The pointers reach renderEngineSegments (processor.cpp:509), which calls engine_.setSidechainInput per segment (processor_midi.cpp:144). In ruinae_engine.h:832-839, sidechainConnected = sidechainL_ != nullptr. When it is true, the engine analyses the host buffer instead of previousOutput, calls setTransientAudioDetection(true), and stops calling triggerTransient for note-ons. The precondition is real: the SDK's ivstaudioprocessor.h:191-193 says that for an inactive bus the buffer addresses are "safe to be null". That allows null but does not require it. Steinberg's own HostProcessData::createBuffers (public.sdk/source/vst/hosting/processdata.cpp:112-152) allocates real sample buffers for every bus from getBusInfo, whether or not the bus is active. So a host built on the reference helper passes non-null, typically zeroed, buffers on the inactive aux bus. In that case Env Follower, Pitch Follower and Transient analyse silence, note-on transients stop, and kSidechainActiveId reports 1 (processor.cpp:491-503). No test covers an inactive aux bus: the only kSidechainActive hits in the tests are ID-range checks in controller_params_test.cpp:397-427. Medium severity is appropriate: modulation routes go silently dead, but there is no crash or unsafe output.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. The code matches the claim, and at least one real host path reaches it.

1. **The code matches the claim.** processor.cpp:471-489 sets sidechainL/R and `sidechainActive = true` whenever `data.inputs[0]` has `numChannels >= 1` and non-null `channelBuffers32`. That is the only condition. The bus is added default-inactive at processor.cpp:58-62, and the comment there says "host activates when user routes audio". A grep for activateBus, isActive and silenceFlags under plugins/ruinae/src/processor finds no code that tracks bus activation; the only hits are a `setupProcessing` signature, setBusArrangements, and a header comment. renderEngineSegments (:509) passes the pointers into the engine. At ruinae_engine.h:832-835 the engine sets `sidechainConnected = sidechainL_ != nullptr`. It then analyses the sidechain instead of previousOutputL_, and calls `setTransientAudioDetection(true)`, which turns off the transients that note-ons would otherwise fire (:836).

2. **The VST3 spec allows non-null buffers on an inactive bus.** extern/vst3sdk/pluginterfaces/vst/ivstaudioprocessor.h:191-193 says the host "must always supply an array for the channel buffers, regardless if the bus is active or not. However, if an audio bus is currently inactive, the actual sample buffer addresses are safe to be null." The word is "safe", not "must". So a null pointer is not a reliable signal that the bus is inactive.

3. **A real host path passes non-null buffers.** Steinberg's own hosting helper, public.sdk/source/vst/hosting/processdata.cpp:112-158 (HostProcessData::createBuffers), allocates `new Sample32[bufferSamples]` for every channel of every bus from getBusInfo, whether or not the bus is active. These buffers are also uninitialised, so the plugin may analyse garbage rather than silence. Hosts built on this helper (the SDK's audiohost and editorhost, among others) therefore send Ruinae a non-null sidechain while the bus is inactive. The AU wrapper (auwrapper.mm:1535-1546) does pass nullptr for inactive inputs, so the AU build is not affected.

4. **Nothing guards it or documents it as intended.** The CHANGELOG (line 233) says the plugin "Falls back to analyzing the synth's own output when no sidechain is connected", so the fallback is the intended behaviour, and here it does not happen. The engine tests at ruinae_engine_integration_test.cpp:1925-1968 only show that the engine treats a non-null silent sidechain as connected. No processor test covers an inactive bus that has buffers. processor_bus_test.cpp:42 only checks setBusArrangements.

The consequences follow from the code: Env Follower, Pitch Follower and Transient analyse the inactive bus's buffers, transients stop firing on note-ons, and kSidechainActive reports active. Medium severity fits: whether it happens depends on the host, but the result is silently broken modulation.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. processor.cpp:58-62 adds the Sidechain aux input with flags 0, so it starts inactive. processor.cpp:475-488 sets sidechainL/R and sidechainActive = true whenever data.inputs[0] has numChannels >= 1 and non-null channel pointers. Nothing checks bus activation or silenceFlags: a grep for activateBus, isActive() and silenceFlags under plugins/ruinae/src/processor finds no matches. renderEngineSegments (processor_midi.cpp:144-145) passes those pointers to engine_.setSidechainInput. At ruinae_engine.h:832-839, sidechainConnected = sidechainL_ != nullptr does three things: it replaces the self-analysis input (previousOutputL_/R_) with the sidechain buffer, it calls setTransientAudioDetection(true), and it skips the note-on triggerTransient(pendingTransientLevel_) path.

The claimed host behaviour is real and comes from the SDK itself. ivstaudioprocessor.h:188-193 says numChannels must always match the bus arrangement and the channel-buffer array must be supplied "regardless if the bus is active or not". It only says the sample addresses of an inactive bus are "safe to be null", which is permitted, not required. The SDK's own hosting helper, public.sdk/source/vst/hosting/processdata.cpp:115-152 (HostProcessData::createBuffers), allocates real sample buffers for every bus from getBusInfo without checking activation. So any host or test harness built on that helper hands Ruinae non-null sidechain pointers while the aux bus is inactive. Those buffers come from `new Sample32[]` and are not zeroed, so they may hold silence or stale or uninitialised data, not reliably zeros.

The consequence holds as stated. Env Follower and Pitch Follower analyse the dead aux buffer instead of the synth's own output. Transient stops firing on note-on because the note-on trigger is skipped at :836. kSidechainActiveId reports 1 (processor.cpp:493-503).

No test covers this. processor_bus_test.cpp only checks bus-arrangement acceptance (lines 42-45), and nothing tests an inactive aux bus with valid buffers.

Severity stays medium. The defect silently disables three mod sources in affected hosts, but it does not corrupt audio, crash, or leave stuck notes. The output stays NaN-protected downstream, and hosts that pass null pointers for inactive buses are not affected.

</details>

### R-058

**Spectral delay FFT Size control changes fftSize_ without re-preparing: analysis size never changes, phase-advance term and reported latency go wrong**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** effects-chain · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:613-617`
- **Also flagged by:** shared-dsp-contracts, spec-conformance

**Problem.** setDelaySpectralFFTSize calls spectralDelay_.setFFTSize(512..4096) on every block (processor_params.cpp:621). setFFTSize only rewrites fftSize_ and is documented 'Caller must call prepare() after this' (spectral_delay.h:468-477). The STFT/OLA, spectra, bin delay lines and hopSize_ keep the prepare-time size. fftSize_ is still read in readDelayedSpectrum's expected phase advance (`2pi*bin*hopSize_/fftSize_`, :718-719), with the stale hopSize_, and in getLatencySamples (:604-605). The next setupProcessing then prepares the delay at whatever size was last selected, so targetLatencySamples_ (chain :150) and the compensation-line length depend on session history.

**Why it is wrong.** An FFT-size change must either reallocate (off the audio thread, followed by a latency/state update) or not be offered as a live parameter. Mixing a new fftSize_ with the old hop gives an expected per-hop advance off by a factor of 2-4. Unless the offset is a multiple of 2pi, the wrapped deviation then produces a wrong advance, so the phase-locked fractional-frame reads (pass 3) project phases incorrectly.

**Consequence.** Choosing 512, 2048 or 4096 does not change the spectral resolution. It corrupts the phase projection of fractional frame delays (smeared or phasey echoes) and makes the reported latency and the comp-delay length differ from the real path, and from one session to the next.

**Suggested fix.** Either drop the FFT Size parameter, or pre-prepare one SpectralDelay per size (or the max size with a runtime-selected active size) and switch via the existing delay crossfade. Never let setFFTSize change fftSize_ outside prepare(). Test: set FFT index 3 on a prepared chain, render a 300 ms delay of a 1 kHz tone with base delay at a fractional frame, and compare the echo spectrum and level with index 1 (no smearing, and latency identical to the real echo offset).

**Evidence.** ruinae_effects_chain.h:616 `spectralDelay_.setFFTSize(kFFTSizes[clamped]);` (no prepare); processor_params.cpp:621 called each block; spectral_delay.h:471-476 sets fftSize_ only, comment 'Caller must call prepare() after this'; :135 `hopSize_ = fftSize_ / 2;` only in prepare; :718-719 `expected = kTwoPi * bin * hopSize_ / fftSize_`; :605 `return fftSize_;`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I confirmed the finding from source.

1. ruinae_effects_chain.h:613-617: setDelaySpectralFFTSize only calls spectralDelay_.setFFTSize(kFFTSizes[clamped]). It never calls prepare.
2. processor_params.cpp:621 sits inside Processor::applyDelayParams (:564). That is reached through applyParamsToEngine (processor_params.cpp:257), which process() calls every block (processor.cpp:251). So fftSize_ is rewritten on the audio thread every block.
3. spectral_delay.h:468-477: setFFTSize only rounds fftSize_ to a power of two. Its own comment says "Caller must call prepare() after this".
4. In spectral_delay.h, hopSize_ (:135), the STFT and OLA objects (:138-143), the spectra (:147-152) and the frame rate (:159) are set only in prepare(), at :132.
5. The live fftSize_ is still read in readDelayedSpectrum at :718-719 (`expected = kTwoPi*bin*hopSize_/fftSize_`). The hop there is stale, so the expected advance per hop changes by 2x or 4x while the real frame geometry does not.
6. getLatencySamples at :604-605 returns fftSize_. The chain's prepare at ruinae_effects_chain.h:124 and :150 sizes targetLatencySamples_ and the compensation lines (:153-159) from whatever FFT size was selected last. The latency therefore depends on the selection history, while the real path keeps the size from the previous prepare until the next one.

The only other uses of fftSize_ are at prepare time, so the fault is not a buffer overrun. It shows up as a wrong phase projection, an FFT Size control that does nothing audible to resolution until the next prepare, and a latency report that disagrees with the real path. The medium severity is appropriate.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source. ruinae_effects_chain.h:613-617 setDelaySpectralFFTSize calls only spectralDelay_.setFFTSize(kFFTSizes[clamped]). processor_params.cpp:621 calls it on every parameter apply from process(). spectral_delay.h:468-477 setFFTSize only rewrites fftSize_, and its comment says "Caller must call prepare() after this". hopSize_, the STFT/OLA, the spectra and the bin delay lines are sized only in prepare() (spectral_delay.h:132-152). The chain prepares the spectral delay only in its own prepare() (ruinae_effects_chain.h:124), so a live change never re-sizes the analysis, and the resolution stays at the prepare-time size. fftSize_ is still read live at spectral_delay.h:718-719 (`expected = kTwoPi*bin*hopSize_/fftSize_`), with the stale hopSize_. out.advance[bin] = expected + deviation (:731), so a wrong expected value picks a different 2pi-aliased representative of the advance. Pass 3 scales that advance by the fractional distance (:771, `out.phase[bin] += stepFromNearer * out.advance[bin]`), so fractional-frame reads get a wrong phase whenever index != the prepare-time size. Example: prepared at the default 1024 (kDefaultFFTSize, :90, hop 512), then set to 2048: expected is pi*bin/2 instead of pi*bin. Nothing guards against this. No processor code calls prepare on an FFT-size change, and no test covers setDelaySpectralFFTSize. The editor exposes the control (editor.uidesc:1871), and MANUAL.md:813 promises "better frequency resolution but more latency", so this is not an intentional no-op. Latency: targetLatencySamples_ = spectralDelay_.getLatencySamples() + harmonizer PV (chain :150) is computed only in prepare(), from whatever fftSize_ the last applied parameter left. The compensation-line length and engine latency therefore depend on session history: the first setupProcessing gives 1024+5120, a later re-prepare after the user picked 4096 gives 4096+5120. The test at ruinae_effects_chain_test.cpp:1097 pins 6144 only for the default. One sub-claim is overstated. The processor does not override getLatencySamples (no match in plugins/ruinae/src/processor), so nothing is "reported" to the host wrongly. Inside one prepare, the cached targetLatencySamples_ matches the real spectral path, because fftSize_ was consistent at prepare time. The core defect stands: the FFT Size control does not change the resolution, it corrupts the phase projection, and the latency changes across re-prepares. Medium severity is appropriate.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the core defect from source. The latency part of the claim is wrong.

Confirmed:
1. The parameter goes live without a re-prepare. ruinae_effects_chain.h:613-617 calls `spectralDelay_.setFFTSize(kFFTSizes[clamped])` and never calls prepare. processor_params.cpp:621 calls it from applyParamsToEngine on every process() (processor.cpp:251). spectral_delay.h:470-477 only rewrites fftSize_, with the comment "Caller must call prepare() after this".
2. Only prepare() sizes the processing. Line 135 sets `hopSize_ = fftSize_/2`, and lines 138-169 size the STFT/OLA, the spectra and the per-bin delay lines. The only prepare caller is setupProcessing (processor.cpp:182 -> chain :124). So between prepares, choosing 512/2048/4096 does not change the spectral resolution.
3. Session history decides which size is used. setState only stores the atomic (delay_params.h:819). A project saved at 4096 is prepared at the object's current fftSize_ (1024 by default, :1030) and then runs with the mismatched value until the host calls setupProcessing again. Whether a session gets real 4096 resolution therefore depends on whether its host re-runs setupProcessing.
4. The phase-advance term is wrong. :718-719 computes `expected = 2pi*bin*hopSize_/fftSize_` from the stale hop (512) and the new fftSize_. That gives 2pi*bin, 0.5pi*bin or 0.25pi*bin instead of pi*bin. The wrap at :720-721 only keeps advance congruent mod 2pi, so the advance is off by 2pi*m, where m depends on the bin. Pass 3 (:767-771) multiplies it by stepFromNearer, which ranges over [-0.5, 0.5]. That is a phase error up to pi*m for any fractional-frame delay. A whole-frame delay (frac=0) is unaffected.

Impact:
- For a stationary tone with Spread 0, the error is a constant rotation per peak region, so it is mostly inaudible.
- It turns into phase discontinuities between frames (OLA cancellation or smearing) when peaks move (transients, pitch changes) or when Spread gives the bins of one region different fracs.
- So the "smeared or phasey" consequence is real but depends on the material.

Wrong part: the latency claim.
- The processor does not override getLatencySamples, so no FFT-dependent latency reaches the host.
- The chain's targetLatencySamples_ (:150) and the comp lines (:153-160) are set in the same prepare() that sizes the STFT. They always match the real spectral path. Between prepares, both stay at the old size, and spectralDelay_.getLatencySamples() (:604-605) is only read at prepare.
- What does vary from session to session is the effective FFT size (and with it the comp length).

No ruinae test covers FFTSize (grep of plugins/ruinae/tests finds nothing).

Severity: I keep medium. The control is effectively inert, saved sessions sound different depending on the host's call order, and the phase projection is corrupted. The latency sub-claim is overstated, but it does not change the severity.

</details>

### R-059

**Modulation-slot crossfade re-targeted mid-fade: A->B->A crossfades an instance with itself (processed twice per block, then reset); A->B->C cuts B**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** effects-chain · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:343-354, 1304-1314, 1361-1374`
- **Also flagged by:** prior-audit-regressions, gestalt-engine

**Problem.** startModCrossfade, called directly from processParameterChanges (processor_params.cpp:197) on every kModulationTypeId point, overwrites incomingModType_ and resets modCrossfadeAlpha_ to 0 while a fade is running. If the new target equals activeModType_, processModulationSlot calls processModEffect for the same Phaser/Flanger/Chorus instance twice per block, once into tempL_ and once in place, so its LFO and delay state advance twice. completeModCrossfade then resets activeModType_'s effect, which is the one that stays active. If the new target is a third type, the half-faded-in B vanishes in one sample (alpha jumps back to 0) and its state is left stale for next time.

**Why it is wrong.** Re-targeting a crossfade must continue from the current mix (e.g. swap roles and use alpha' = 1 - alpha when returning to the active type, or finish/fast-track the running fade as setDelayType does at :410-413). It must never process one stateful instance twice per block or reset the effect that remains active.

**Consequence.** A click when the user scrolls through the Modulation Type dropdown, or automation flips it within 30 ms. Returning to the original type also restarts the phaser/flanger/chorus from reset, which is an audible discontinuity, and during the fade the effect is processed with double-rate state.

**Suggested fix.** In startModCrossfade: if crossfading and incoming == activeModType_, swap active/incoming and set alpha = 1 - alpha. If incoming is a third type, complete the current fade first (fast-track like setDelayType) and then start the new one. Test: process a sine through the chain, start Phaser->Chorus, one block later start ->Phaser, and assert the max per-sample step stays below 2x the dry sine's natural step.

**Evidence.** :347 `if (modCrossfading_ && incoming == incomingModType_) return;` (no check for incoming == activeModType_); :350-351 `incomingModType_ = incoming; modCrossfadeAlpha_ = 0.0f;`; :1312/:1314 processModEffect(activeModType_) and processModEffect(incomingModType_); :1363-1370 reset outgoing = activeModType_ then `activeModType_ = incomingModType_`. MEASURED (probe, 0.3-amp 110 Hz sine, 512 blocks, Phaser active, startModCrossfade(Chorus) at block 10, startModCrossfade(Phaser) at block 11): max per-sample step 0.0624 vs a natural sine step of 0.0047 (13x), against 0.0071 in the steady-phaser blocks before the switch.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute the finding. The source shows the behaviour it describes. In ruinae_effects_chain.h:343-354, startModCrossfade returns early only in two cases: when no fade is running and incoming == activeModType_ (:344), or when a fade is running and incoming == incomingModType_ (:347). Any other call during a running fade overwrites incomingModType_ (:350) and resets modCrossfadeAlpha_ to 0 (:351). No branch handles incoming == activeModType_ while a fade runs, and none fast-tracks the fade the way setDelayType does at :410-413.

Its caller is processor_params.cpp:197, which runs on every kModulationTypeId change point. The per-block setModulationType (processor_params.cpp:559, ruinae_effects_chain.h:334-338) does nothing while modCrossfading_ is true, so it does not cover the problem.

A->B->A case: active=Phaser, incoming=Chorus, then startModCrossfade(Phaser) sets incoming=Phaser and alpha=0. processModulationSlot (:1312 and :1314) then calls processModEffect(Phaser) twice per block, once on tempL_/tempR_ and once in place. Both calls go through phaser_.processStereo (:1345), so the single phaser_ instance's LFO and state advance twice per block. When the fade ends, completeModCrossfade (:1363-1364) resets phaser_ because activeModType_ == Phaser, and then sets activeModType_ = Phaser (:1370). The effect that stays active is therefore reset mid-signal. The half-faded Chorus is never reset either.

A->B->C case: B's contribution goes from alpha to 0 in one sample, which is a discontinuity, and B is never reset.

The quoted measurement (13x step versus steady state) is consistent with this. Medium severity fits: the trigger is automation or fast dropdown changes within 30 ms, and the result is an audible click or discontinuity, not instability.

**Note 2.** The defect is confirmed from source, and no guard or documented design decision covers it.

- ruinae_effects_chain.h:343-354: startModCrossfade returns early only for `!modCrossfading_ && incoming == activeModType_` (:344) or `modCrossfading_ && incoming == incomingModType_` (:347). It has no branch for "crossfading and incoming == activeModType_". Otherwise it overwrites incomingModType_ (:350) and resets modCrossfadeAlpha_ to 0 (:351). Unlike setDelayType (:410-417), which fast-tracks a running fade with completeCrossfade() and then rechecks, there is no fast-track and no swap.
- A->B->A: activeModType_ == incomingModType_ == A. processModulationSlot (:1312, :1314) then calls processModEffect on the same instance twice per block, once into tempL_ and once in place (processModEffect :1341-1357 dispatches to the single phaser_/flanger_/chorus_). Its LFO and delay state advance twice. At completion, completeModCrossfade (:1363-1369) resets the effect of activeModType_ (A) and then sets activeModType_ = incomingModType_ (A) (:1370). The effect that stays active is therefore reset.
- A->B->C: alpha goes back to 0, so B's partial contribution disappears in one sample. B is also not reset at that point; it is reset only on completion, and only if it is the active type.
- The path is reachable. processor_params.cpp:193-198 calls startModCrossfade on every kModulationTypeId change. Nothing upstream dedupes a reversal, and nothing tracks a fade in progress. setModulationType (:334-338 via processor_params.cpp:559) is a no-op while crossfading, so it does not rescue this case.
- The fade is 30 ms (:352), about 1323 samples at 44.1 kHz, which spans 2-3 host blocks of 512. Automation or dropdown scrolling across consecutive blocks can therefore re-target a fade while it runs.
- The only covering test is modulation_type_test.cpp:281-296. It checks a single Phaser->Flanger fade and nothing that re-targets mid-fade.
- No code comment documents this behaviour as intentional. The doc comment at :340-342 describes only the no-op case.
- The quoted probe measurement (13x step at the A->B->A switch) is consistent with the source.

I left the severity at medium. The trigger is a user or automation gesture rather than steady-state use, but the result is an audible click plus a reset of the effect that stays active.

**Note 3.** The defect is real and its consequence holds at medium severity.

The code path:
- plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:193-198 calls startModCrossfade on every kModulationTypeId change. Nothing checks whether a fade is already running.
- ruinae_effects_chain.h:343-354 has only two early-outs: no fade running and the target is the active type (:344), or a fade running and the target is the incoming type (:347). Every other case overwrites incomingModType_ (:350) and resets modCrossfadeAlpha_ to 0 (:351). The case where a fade is running and the target equals activeModType_ is not caught.
- processModulationSlot (:1304-1337) then calls processModEffect(activeModType_) on tempL_/tempR_ (:1312) and processModEffect(incomingModType_) in place (:1314). When both are the same type, the same phaser_/flanger_/chorus_ instance (:1341-1357) runs twice per block, so its LFO and delay state advance at double rate.
- completeModCrossfade (:1361-1374) resets the instance for activeModType_ and then assigns activeModType_ = incomingModType_. In the A->B->A case that resets the very effect that stays active, so its sweep restarts from reset at the end of the fade.
- In the A->B->C case, alpha jumps back to 0 at :351, so the half-faded-in B vanishes in one sample. B is never reset, because only the outgoing active type is reset at :1363-1369, so it keeps stale state for its next use.
- setDelayType (:410-413) handles a mid-fade retarget correctly with completeCrossfade(), which shows the modulation slot lacks the same guard.

Impact: the fade is 30 ms (1323 samples at 44.1 kHz, about 2.6 blocks of 512). Any change within that window triggers the bug: automation flips, a host replacing a parameter lane, or quickly stepping through the 4-entry dropdown. The quoted probe measured a peak sample step 13x the natural sine step, against 1.5x in the steady phaser blocks. That is a clear click, and the restart of the active effect is audible too. It needs a fast change of a discrete parameter, so it is not routine, and the result is a click, not a level blow-up or NaN. Medium is right.

Test coverage: plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/processor/modulation_type_test.cpp:285-295 only exercises a single Phaser->Flanger fade, not a retarget.

</details>

### R-060

**Chorus with 2+ voices wraps each voice's modulation in the amplitude domain, jumping the delay tap by up to 20 ms twice per LFO cycle (click)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** effects-chain · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/chorus.h:308-320, 338-349`

**Problem.** For voice v the chorus takes the unipolar LFO value, adds v/voices and wraps with `if (shifted >= 1.0f) shifted -= 1.0f`. When the LFO amplitude crosses 1 - v/voices, modValue jumps from +1 to -1 in one sample. The cubic-read delay position then jumps by 2*sweepRangeSamples (up to 20 ms * depth, i.e. 441 samples at depth 0.5 at 44.1 kHz). The offset should be applied to the LFO PHASE, not to its output amplitude.

**Why it is wrong.** Multi-voice chorus spreads voices by phase-offsetting their LFOs. Each voice's delay must vary continuously. A step in a delay-line read position is a waveform discontinuity, i.e. a click.

**Consequence.** The Chorus modulation type clicks twice per LFO cycle per extra voice at its default 2 voices, for every Ruinae preset using Chorus and any other Chorus consumer.

**Suggested fix.** Give each voice its own LFO phase (LFO per voice with phase offset v/voices, or compute the waveform from phase + offset). Alternatively reflect instead of wrap (triangle fold), at the cost of the phase relationship. Test in dsp_processors_tests: a 440 Hz 0.3-amp sine through Chorus with 2 and 3 voices, depth 0.5, mix 1, where the max per-sample step must be &lt;= 1.5x the single-voice result.

**Evidence.** chorus.h:313-315 `float shifted = unipolarL + voiceOffset; if (shifted >= 1.0f) shifted -= 1.0f; const float modValue = shifted * 2.0f - 1.0f;` :317 `delaySamples = centerDelaySamples + modValue * sweepRangeSamples;` :290 sweepRangeMs = (25-5)*0.5*depth. MEASURED (probe, Chorus standalone, 440 Hz 0.3-amp sine, rate 1 Hz, depth 0.5, mix 1, fb 0): max per-sample step voices=1 0.0194, voices=2 0.2235, voices=3 0.1807 (natural sine step 0.0188).

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I confirmed the defect by reading the source. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/chorus.h:309-315 (left) and :338-344 (right), the code builds `unipolar = lfoValue*0.5+0.5` from ONE shared LFO per channel (lfoL_/lfoR_, :302/:333). For voice v it then does `shifted = unipolar + v/voices; if (shifted >= 1.0f) shifted -= 1.0f; modValue = shifted*2-1`. That is a wrap of the LFO's output AMPLITUDE, not of its phase.

At the default of 2 voices (kDefaultVoices = 2, :79; Ruinae's state default also stores 2, processor_state.cpp:255), voice 1 has offset 0.5. With the default Triangle waveform (:384):
- When unipolar rises through 0.5, shifted jumps from just under 1.0 to 0.0, so modValue goes from +1 to -1 in one sample.
- When it falls back through 0.5, the reverse jump happens.

So each extra voice gets two discontinuities per LFO cycle.

The delay tap is `centerDelaySamples + modValue*sweepRangeSamples` (:317/:346), and sweepRangeMs = (25-5)*0.5*depth (:290, kMin/kMaxDelayMs = 5/25 at :56-57). The tap therefore jumps by 2*sweepRange: 10 ms (441 samples at 44.1 kHz) at depth 0.5, and up to 20 ms at depth 1. It is read with readCubic at :319/:348, and nothing smooths it, so the output steps. That is a click.

Ruinae reaches this code through its effects chain: processor_params.cpp:708 calls chorus.setVoices(chorusParams_.voices). The comment at :308 shows the wrap was deliberate, but it is not a documented exemption, and the result is a delay-read discontinuity.

The quoted measurement agrees: the maximum per-sample step is about 0.22 with 2 voices against 0.019 with 1 voice.

Severity stays medium: the click is audible and reachable at default settings, but the plugin stays stable.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. The source shows the defect directly.

- **The wrap is in the amplitude domain.** In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/chorus.h:309-315, `unipolarL = lfoValueL*0.5f+0.5f` is the output of a single shared LFO (lfoL_, :302). The code then does `shifted = unipolarL + voiceOffset; if (shifted >= 1.0f) shifted -= 1.0f; modValue = shifted*2-1`. The right channel does the same at :338-344.
- **Where it jumps.** With voices=2, voice 1 has offset 0.5. When the unipolar LFO crosses 0.5, `shifted` drops from about 1.0 to about 0.0, so `modValue` steps from +1 to -1 in one sample. That happens twice per LFO cycle, once on the way up and once on the way down.
- **Size of the jump.** The delay read position at :317 is `centerDelaySamples + modValue*sweepRangeSamples`, and `sweepRangeMs = (kMaxDelayMs-kMinDelayMs)*0.5*depth` (:290). So the tap moves by 2*sweepRangeSamples in one sample.
- **It applies to the default waveform too.** The waveform is Triangle by default (:384), and a triangle is continuous only before the wrap.
- **There is no per-voice phase anywhere.** Only lfoL_ and lfoR_ exist (:366-367). setPhaseOffset sets only the stereo spread on lfoR_ (:104, :136, :200).
- **Nothing documents it as intentional.** The comment at :308 says "offset in unipolar [0,1] domain, then wrap", which describes the mechanism. It does not say the jump is a deliberate trade-off.
- **It reaches Ruinae.** The default voice count is kDefaultVoices = 2 (:79). Ruinae's effects chain calls chorus_.processStereo for ModulationType::Chorus (ruinae_effects_chain.h:1350-1351).
- **No test pins it.** Almost every case in dsp/tests/unit/processors/chorus_test.cpp uses setVoices(1) (:264, :317, :351, :382, :457, :482, ...). The cases that use 3-4 voices (:189 parameter clamp, :425, :595, :618, :734) did not catch the jump, and none of them checks for per-sample continuity.

The quoted probe agrees with this. The largest per-sample step was 0.2235 with 2 voices and 0.1807 with 3, against 0.0194 with 1 voice. That is about an 11x jump, which is a click.

I am keeping the severity at medium. It is an audible artefact in a common default setting, but it is not a stability or safety bug.

**Note 3.** The finding holds. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/chorus.h:309-317 (L) and :338-346 (R), each voice computes `shifted = unipolar + v/voices`, wraps it with `if (shifted >= 1.0f) shifted -= 1.0f`, then sets `modValue = shifted*2-1` and `delaySamples = center + modValue*sweepRangeSamples`. When `unipolar` crosses 1 - v/voices, `shifted` jumps from just under 1 to 0, so `modValue` steps from +1 to -1 in one sample. The `readCubic` tap (:319/:348) then moves by 2*sweepRangeSamples. The wrap is crossed in both directions as a bipolar LFO swings up and down, so each voice with v >= 1 jumps twice per LFO cycle.

Size of the jump: sweepRangeMs = (25-5)*0.5*depth (:290, constants at :56-57). At the default depth 0.5 (:62) that is 5 ms, so the jump is 10 ms (441 samples at 44.1 kHz). At depth 1 it is 20 ms. The default is 2 voices (:79). Ruinae passes the voices parameter through unchanged (processor_params.cpp:708), and setState defaults it to 2 (processor_state.cpp:255), so Ruinae's Chorus mode hits this out of the box.

The quoted measurement agrees: the largest per-sample step is 0.2235 with 2 voices and 0.1807 with 3 voices, against 0.0194 with 1 voice (about 11x). The click is scaled by the voice average (voiceScale = 1/voices) and by the mix (default 0.5), but it remains a real waveform discontinuity, about 10x the natural signal step.

Tests do not catch it: dsp/tests/unit/processors/chorus_test.cpp runs nearly every signal test with setVoices(1). The 4-voice cases at :595/:618/:734 make no step or discontinuity assertions in the grep results.

Medium severity fits: the chorus clicks periodically at default settings and is not a crash or a level explosion.

</details>

### R-061

**Switching reverb type while Freeze is on fades the frozen tail into an empty tank: output goes to silence**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** effects-chain · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:684-701, 1125-1171`

**Problem.** Only the active reverb is processed outside a crossfade. The other tank is empty, cleared by prepare/reset or by completeReverbCrossfade's reset of the outgoing type. Freeze mutes the input of both reverbs (they get identical params via setReverbParams :675-676). A type switch while frozen therefore crossfades from the frozen tank into a tank that can never receive input, and completion resets the frozen one. The FR-029 comment (:692-695) claims freeze is 'applied to the incoming reverb', but the call it describes does not exist in the body, and applying freeze to an empty tank cannot preserve the sound anyway.

**Why it is wrong.** A frozen reverb should keep sounding across a type change (FR-029 intent): either defer the switch until unfreeze, or seed the incoming tank by running it unfrozen during the fade.

**Consequence.** A user who freezes a pad and then tries Plate/Hall loses the frozen sound completely and permanently; it is gone after unfreeze too.

**Suggested fix.** While freeze is active, defer the type change, applying it when freeze is released. Or run the incoming reverb with freeze off (fed the outgoing reverb's output) during the 30 ms fade, then freeze it. Test: build a tail, freeze, switch type, and require RMS after 0.5 s >= 0.5x the frozen RMS.

**Evidence.** :697-700 setReverbType body contains no freeze handling despite the :692-695 comment; :1130-1134 both tanks processed only during the fade; :1160-1164 outgoing tank reset at completion. MEASURED (probe, block 2048 so the fade completes, mix 1, size 0.8, 220 Hz input then freeze): frozen-tail RMS 0.30046, after setReverbType(1) RMS 0.000000.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this finding. The code does what it describes, and the only test that covers the case can pass even when the frozen sound is lost.

1. **The comment promises freeze handling that the body does not do.** In ruinae_effects_chain.h:689-701, `setReverbType` only sets `incomingReverbType_`, `reverbCrossfading_`, the alpha and the increment. The FR-029 text at :692-695 is a comment with no code under it.

2. **Both reverbs get the same freeze flag.** `setReverbParams` (:672-676) sends the same params, freeze included, to `reverb_` and `fdnReverb_`. The only caller of the type switch is processor_params.cpp:655, through ruinae_engine.h:693, and nothing on that path defers the switch or clears freeze.

3. **The incoming reverb starts empty.** Outside a crossfade, `processReverbSlot` (:1119-1122) processes only `activeReverbType_`, so the other reverb never receives signal. `completeReverbCrossfade` (:1158-1164) resets the outgoing reverb, so whichever type is inactive holds nothing.

4. **Freeze shuts off input in both reverbs.**
   - The FDN reverb (fdn_reverb.h:398, 429) sets `mono = 0.0f` whenever freeze is on. An empty FDN tank therefore stays exactly silent.
   - The Dattorro reverb (reverb.h:435-438, 507-511) ramps its input gain to 0 and snaps it to exactly 0 under freeze.

   Switching plate to hall (0 to 1) while frozen therefore crossfades into a silent FDN. At the end of the fade (:1145-1151) the frozen plate is reset, so the frozen sound is gone for good. It does not return after unfreeze either, because the plate was cleared.

5. **The existing test does not catch this.** reverb_type_test.cpp:550-630 ("Freeze is applied to incoming reverb before crossfade") checks that the tail sustains only inside `if (rmsAfterCrossfade > 1e-6f)` at :624. When the output goes silent, that check is skipped, so the test passes in exactly the failing case. Its other checks (:594, :603) look only at the 2048-sample block that contains the fade, where the outgoing frozen tail is still audible.

6. **The reported measurement agrees.** The finding's probe went from a frozen RMS of 0.30046 to 0.000000 after `setReverbType(1)`. That matches the source: a frozen FDN with an empty tank and zero input outputs exactly 0.

Severity stays medium. The sound is lost permanently with no crash or NaN, but it needs a specific action: switching type while freeze is on.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source. Nothing in the code, tests or docs makes it intentional or guards against it.

1. setReverbType (plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:689-701) contains no freeze handling. The FR-029 comment at :692-695 describes a setParams call, but the body has none; it only sets incomingReverbType_, reverbCrossfading_, alpha and increment. The only caller is processor_params.cpp:655, which runs right after engine_.setReverbParams(rp) (:653). Nothing upstream seeds the incoming tank or defers the switch while frozen.

2. setReverbParams (:672-676) sends the same params, including freeze, to both reverb_ and fdnReverb_. Freeze cuts each tank's input:
   - reverb.h:434-438 sets inputGainSmoother_ to 0 when freeze_ is on.
   - fdn_reverb.h:273-274 and :429 set mono = 0 when frozen.
   So an incoming tank that was never processed gets no input during the fade.

3. processReverbSlot (:1118-1155) runs the inactive type only while crossfading. completeReverbCrossfade (:1158-1164) then resets the outgoing tank (reverb_.reset() or fdnReverb_.reset()). Once the fade completes, the frozen energy is gone and the new active tank is empty and sealed. Unfreezing later cannot bring the frozen sound back.

4. The test that should pin FR-029 does not. "Freeze is applied to incoming reverb before crossfade" (plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/processor/reverb_type_test.cpp:550-630) asserts the sustain only inside `if (rmsAfterCrossfade > 1e-6f)` (:624-626). The bug produces RMS of about 0, so the check is skipped and the test passes. Its other assertions (crossfadeRms > 1e-6 during the 2048-sample switch block, finiteness, max delta) are all met by the fading-out frozen tank.

5. Neither plugins/ruinae/MANUAL.md nor the prior specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json mentions freeze together with a type switch (the one freeze hit there is an unrelated harmonizer finding). So this is not a documented design decision and not a repeat of a prior finding.

6. The reported measurement (frozen RMS 0.30046, then 0.000000 after setReverbType(1)) matches what this code path does.

I am keeping medium severity. The sound loss is total and permanent, but it needs freeze to be on during a reverb type change, and it produces silence, not a click or a non-finite output.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the defect from source; I did not re-run the probe. The mechanism:
(1) ruinae_effects_chain.h:672-676. setReverbParams sends the same params, freeze flag included, to both reverb_ and fdnReverb_.
(2) Under freeze, both tanks receive no input. dsp/include/krate/dsp/effects/reverb.h:435-438 sets the input-gain target to 0 and :508-510 snaps it to exactly 0. fdn_reverb.h:273-274 and :429 zero the mono input.
(3) Outside a crossfade, processReverbSlot at :1119-1122 runs only the active reverb. The inactive tank is therefore empty: it was cleared at prepare, or by the reset of the outgoing type at :1160-1164.
(4) setReverbType at :689-701 only sets incomingReverbType_ and starts the 30 ms fade (about 1323 samples at 44.1 kHz). The FR-029 comment at :692-695 describes a setParams call that is not in the body. Even if it were, freezing an empty tank leaves it empty.
(5) During the fade, :1130-1141 crossfades the frozen outgoing tank, with equal-power fade-out, into the incoming tank, which has no input and so outputs ~0. completeReverbCrossfade at :1158-1164 then resets the frozen tank.

Result: the frozen tail fades to silence within 30 ms of the type change. It is not recovered on unfreeze, because the old tank was reset. Only new notes, after unfreeze, feed the new type. This matches the quoted measurement (frozen RMS 0.30046, then 0.0 after setReverbType(1)).

The bug survives because the covering test cannot detect it. reverb_type_test.cpp:550-627 ("Freeze is applied to incoming reverb before crossfade") checks only crossfade RMS > 1e-6 at :594, during which the outgoing tank still contributes. Its sustain check at :624-626 runs only when rmsAfterCrossfade > 1e-6, so a silent result skips the assertion.

The trigger is a plain user action: Reverb Freeze on (kReverbFreezeId), then a Reverb Type change (processor_params.cpp:650-655 forwards both). It happens in every host at every block size and sample rate. The consequence is a total loss of the frozen pad, so medium severity stands. It is not a crash, a NaN or a stuck note, so it is no higher than medium. I found no prior F-id to compare against.

</details>

### R-071

**First arp note after an idle gap waits out the step counter frozen at the last key release (measured 6690-sample delay at 2 Hz)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** arpeggiator · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:108-121`

**Problem.** While the held buffer is empty, processBlock returns at :113-121 before the jump-ahead loop, so sampleCounter_ neither advances nor resets. A new key press does not reset it either: noteOn resets selector/lanes only for Retrigger Note (h:342-346), and never sampleCounter_. The first step after the press therefore fires after (currentStepDuration_ - counterAtRelease) samples, which is arbitrary. In Ruinae this applies to free-rate mode and to any tempo-synced use without ppq+kPlaying, where syncToMusicalPosition is skipped (processor.cpp:325).

**Why it is wrong.** An arp clock is either free-running, where the phase advances while idle, or restarted by the first key. A clock frozen at the last release is neither, and makes the first note's latency depend on history.

**Consequence.** Measured (probe, free rate 2 Hz = 22050 samples/step): key released 15360 samples into a step, new key at abs 117760, first NoteOn at abs 124450, a 6690-sample (152 ms) delay. At 0.5 Hz the delay reaches up to 2 s. Playing the arp live in a simple host feels randomly laggy.

**Suggested fix.** When the held buffer goes from empty to non-empty and the transport sync is not driving the counter, set sampleCounter_ = currentStepDuration_ (fire immediately, like firstStepPending_). Alternatively, keep advancing the counter during the empty-buffer early return. Test: release mid-step, idle, press, REQUIRE a NoteOn within the block of the press.

**Evidence.** arpeggiator_core.cpp:113-121 `if (heldNotes_.empty() && sourceMode_ != SourceMode::Sequencer) { if (needsDisableNoteOff_) emitPanicNoteOffs(...); return eventCount; }`, placed before the loop that does `sampleCounter_ += jump` (:224). Probe: 'D release at abs 15360 / D press#2 at abs 117760 / D run2 NoteOn note 62 at abs 124450'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the code and the defect is real.

1. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:113-121: when heldNotes_ is empty (and the source is not Sequencer), processBlock returns before the jump-ahead loop. sampleCounter_ is only advanced at :224 (`sampleCounter_ += jump`), so it stays frozen while no keys are held. The only resets of sampleCounter_ in processBlock are the transport-loop branch (:82), the transport-restart branch (:90-97, which runs only when wasPlaying_ was false) and firstStepPending_ (:102-106). None of these fires on an empty-to-non-empty held-buffer transition.

2. arpeggiator_core.h:314-347 (noteOn) resets only selector_, swingStepCounter_ and the lanes, and only for Retrigger Note (:342-346). It never touches sampleCounter_ or firstStepPending_. noteOff (:354-386) only sets needsDisableNoteOff_. emitPanicNoteOffs (h:1420-1448) clears the note arrays and flags but not sampleCounter_. reset() (h:289-306) does reset it, but in Ruinae it is called only from setActive (processor.cpp:207) and state load (processor_state.cpp:365), not per key press.

3. Ruinae caller, plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:304-330: in a simple host that never reports kPlaying, arpCtx.isPlaying is forced true (:308-310). wasPlaying_ therefore stays true and the restart branch never fires again. syncToMusicalPosition (:325-327) runs only when projectTimeMusicValid && isPlaying, and it returns early when !tempoSync_ (arpeggiator_core.h:1030). So free-rate mode in any host, and tempo-sync in a host without a valid ppq while playing, leave the counter frozen.

4. Effect: on the next press the first step fires after currentStepDuration_ - sampleCounter_ samples (:136). With the quoted values, 22050 - 15360 = 6690, which matches the reported delay from abs 117760 to abs 124450 exactly.

5. No test covers re-pressing after release: a grep of dsp/tests/unit/processors/arpeggiator* for re-press / after-release cases finds only a Latch Hold test (arpeggiator_core_core_test.cpp:1031).

6. Limit on scope: with a DAW playing and tempo-sync on, syncToMusicalPosition realigns the counter every block, so that case is unaffected. The finding's stated scope matches this.

Medium severity fits: no stuck notes or corruption, but free-rate live playing gets a first-note latency that depends on history, up to a full step.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. The source confirms it, and nothing in the code, tests or docs I searched treats it as intended.

1. **Early return.** dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:113-121 returns when `heldNotes_.empty()` (outside Sequencer mode). It does this before the jump-ahead loop, and that loop is the only place that advances `sampleCounter_` (`sampleCounter_ += jump`, :224). So the counter keeps its value from the moment the last key was released.

2. **Nothing resets it on a new press.**
   - `noteOn` (arpeggiator_core.h:314-347) resets only `selector_`, `swingStepCounter_` and the lanes, and only for Retrigger=Note. It never touches `sampleCounter_` or `firstStepPending_`.
   - `noteOff` with Latch Off (h:364-372) only sets `needsDisableNoteOff_`.
   - The resets that do exist need other triggers: `firstStepPending_` / `sampleCounter_ = 0` are set only on a transport restart (:90-97), a transport loop (:67-86) or `reset()` (h:289-306).

3. **Ruinae reaches this path in two common cases.**
   - **Host that never reports kPlaying:** processor.cpp:308-310 forces `arpCtx.isPlaying = true`. `wasPlaying_` therefore stays true and the transport-restart reset at :90 never runs again.
   - **Free rate in a playing DAW:** `syncToMusicalPosition` is called at processor.cpp:325-326, but h:1030 returns early when `!tempoSync_`, so it does not re-align the counter.

   The only case that is safe is tempo sync while the DAW transport plays with a valid ppq, where the counter is re-aligned every block (h:1041-1051).

4. **The measured delay matches.** A free-rate step at 2 Hz is 22050 samples at 44.1 kHz. With the counter frozen at 15360, the next step is 22050 − 15360 = 6690 samples away, which equals the reported first NoteOn at abs 124450 − 117760.

5. **No documentation or test covers it.**
   - I found no comment, spec or manual text describing a counter that holds while idle. The Gradus comment at plugins/gradus/src/processor/processor.cpp:247-252 says the arp "free-runs off held notes", which this frozen clock contradicts.
   - My grep of dsp/tests/unit/processors/arpeggiator_core_core_test.cpp found no test of how long the first note takes after a release-and-press. The Latch Off test at :871 only checks that the arp stops.

**Severity:** medium stands. It cannot leave a note stuck, but in free-rate mode, which the plugin offers for live use, the first note can lag by up to one whole step (2 s at 0.5 Hz).

**Note 3.** The source confirms the claim. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/arpeggiator_core.cpp:113-121, when heldNotes_ is empty (and the arp is not in Sequencer mode), processBlock returns before the jump-ahead loop. The only line that advances the counter is `sampleCounter_ += jump` at :224, so the counter stays frozen at the value it had when the last key was released.

Nothing resets it when a key is pressed again:
- ArpeggiatorCore::noteOn (arpeggiator_core.h:314-347) only calls heldNotes_.noteOn. For Retrigger=Note it also resets selector_, swingStepCounter_ and the lanes (:342-346), but never sampleCounter_ or firstStepPending_.
- The counter is reset only by reset() (h:290-294), the transport-loop branch (.cpp:81-82), the transport-restart branch (.cpp:90-96, which needs a !wasPlaying_ edge) and syncToMusicalPosition (h:1029-1051).
- syncToMusicalPosition returns early unless tempoSync_ is on (h:1030), and Ruinae calls it only when projectTimeMusicValid && blockCtx.isPlaying (processor.cpp:325-326).

So the bug reaches users in two Ruinae cases:
1. Any host, free-rate mode (setTempoSync(false), processor_params.cpp:896-907).
2. Tempo-sync in a simple host that never reports kPlaying. There processor.cpp:308-310 forces arpCtx.isPlaying = true, which means wasPlaying_ never drops and the restart reset never runs, while the sync at :325 is skipped because blockCtx.isPlaying is false.

In these cases the first step after a press fires (currentStepDuration_ - counterAtRelease) samples later. That is anywhere from 0 to one full step and depends on when the last key was released. Free rate is clamped to 0.5-50 Hz (processor_params.cpp:897), so the worst delay is about 2 s at 0.5 Hz and 500 ms at the 2 Hz default range. The quoted probe (6690 samples, 152 ms at 2 Hz) fits this mechanism: 22050 - 15360 = 6690.

Not affected: a DAW with transport running and tempo sync on. There the counter is re-synced to the PPQ grid every block, and grid quantisation of the first note is the intended behaviour.

I found no test asserting an immediate first step after a release-and-repress, so nothing covers this case.

Impact: random first-note latency of up to one step for live free-rate play. No stuck note and no level or click hazard. Medium severity is appropriate.

</details>

### R-081

**Mod-matrix curve dropdown labels 'Logarithmic'/'S-Curve' select DSP SCurve/Stepped**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high → medium · **Dimension:** ui-wiring · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/mod_matrix_params.h:43-47`
- **Also flagged by:** duplication-drift, spec-conformance, portability-quality, gestalt-controller

**Problem.** The curve StringListParameter is registered with Linear, Exponential, Logarithmic, S-Curve, and the grid cycles through kCurveTypeNames with the same four labels. The processor clamps the index to 0-3 and casts it to Krate::DSP::ModCurve, which is {Linear=0, Exponential=1, SCurve=2, Stepped=3}. The DSP has no logarithmic curve.

**Why it is wrong.** The UI label must describe the transfer function the DSP applies. Index 2 is labelled 'Logarithmic' but is a smoothstep, and index 3 is labelled 'S-Curve' but quantises to 4 levels. The preset generator already uses the DSP meaning (kCurveSCurve = 2, kCurveStepped = 3), so factory presets display the wrong curve name too.

**Consequence.** A user who picks 'S-Curve' for a smooth LFO-to-cutoff route gets a 4-step staircase, which zippers audibly. 'Logarithmic' gives a smoothstep instead of a log response. Factory presets that use Stepped show as 'S-Curve' in the grid and in the host.

**Suggested fix.** Rename the labels in mod_matrix_params.h:43-47 and mod_matrix_types.h:113-118 (shared with the grid) to Linear, Exponential, S-Curve, Stepped, and fix the mod_matrix_params.h:26 comment. Add a static_assert or a unit test that ties the label index to ModCurve (e.g. label[2] corresponds to ModCurve::SCurve). Check whether other plugins share kCurveTypeNames before renaming.

**Evidence.** mod_matrix_params.h:46-47 `STR16("Logarithmic"), STR16("S-Curve"),`. mod_matrix_types.h:113-118 kCurveTypeNames {"Linear","Exponential","Logarithmic","S-Curve"}. modulation_types.h:79-84 `Linear = 0, Exponential = 1, SCurve = 2, Stepped = 3`. processor_params.cpp:488,492 `int curveIdx = std::clamp(slot.curve..., 0, 3); auto curve = static_cast<ModCurve>(curveIdx);`. ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:260-261 `kCurveSCurve = 2; kCurveStepped = 3;`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The defect is confirmed from source. The labels are at plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/mod_matrix_params.h:43-48: kModCurveStrings = {"Linear","Exponential","Logarithmic","S-Curve"}, with the matching comment at :26 ("2=Logarithmic, 3=S-Curve"). The shared grid label table is at plugins/shared/src/ui/mod_matrix_types.h:113-118: kCurveTypeNames = {"Linear","Exponential","Logarithmic","S-Curve"}. mod_matrix_grid.h:899, 997 and 1326-1327 use it for the menu, for click-cycling and for display. The processor does the cast at plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:488 (`std::clamp(slot.curve..., 0, 3)`) and :492 (`static_cast<ModCurve>(curveIdx)`), then calls engine_.setGlobalModRoute(..., curve, ...) at :494, which stores it as routing.curve at ruinae_engine.h:458-470. The enum is at dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/modulation_types.h:79-83: Linear=0, Exponential=1, SCurve=2, Stepped=3. The transfer functions are at dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/modulation_curves.h:48-52: SCurve is x*x*(3-2x) (smoothstep) and Stepped is floor(x*4)/3. So index 2, labelled "Logarithmic", applies a smoothstep; index 3, labelled "S-Curve", applies a 4-level staircase; and no logarithmic curve exists. The preset generator uses the DSP meaning (tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:260-261 kCurveSCurve=2, kCurveStepped=3). Its own comments say so: line 774 says "with a Stepped curve" and line 502 says "with an S-curve". So factory presets that use Stepped (e.g. lines 565, 716, 777, 1494, 1681) show "S-Curve", and those that use SCurve show "Logarithmic". Severity downgrade: this is a label/UI mismatch only. The audio path is internally consistent, state round-trips to the same sound, and nothing is a real-time safety, stuck-note or NaN hazard. It misleads users and is worth fixing, but medium fits better than high.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source. The dropdown labels and the DSP enum disagree at indices 2 and 3:
- **Labels:** plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/mod_matrix_params.h:43-48 registers kModCurveStrings = {Linear, Exponential, Logarithmic, S-Curve}, and the slot comment at :26 says the same. The shared grid list plugins/shared/src/ui/mod_matrix_types.h:113-118 (kCurveTypeNames, plus the comment at :80) has the same four labels. mod_matrix_grid.h:892-899 builds the curve menu from it, :997-1004 cycles through it, and :1326-1327 displays it.
- **DSP enum:** dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/modulation_types.h:79-84 defines ModCurve {Linear=0, Exponential=1, SCurve=2, Stepped=3}.
- **Processor:** plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:488-494 clamps the index to 0-3, casts it with static_cast&lt;ModCurve> and passes it to engine_.setGlobalModRoute. Nothing remaps the index between UI and DSP.
- **Controller:** controller_mod_matrix.cpp:233-237 also stores the raw index, round(norm*3).
- **Curve math:** dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/modulation_curves.h:48-52 confirms index 2 is a smoothstep, x*x*(3-2x), and index 3 is floor(x*4)/3, a 4-level staircase. No ModCurve value is logarithmic.
- **Factory presets:** tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:258-261 uses the DSP meaning (kCurveSCurve=2, kCurveStepped=3). Several factory presets use kCurveStepped (lines 565, 716, 777), so the grid and the host show those routes as 'S-Curve'.

Nothing marks this as intentional. MANUAL.md does not mention these curve names, prior findings.json has no such entry, and the comments state the wrong mapping as fact. The only test reference I found is plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/mod_matrix_params_test.cpp:153, whose comment calls index 2 'Logarithmic'. That comment repeats the wrong label, and I found no test that ties labels to ModCurve. Gradus's own 'Logarithmic' velocity-curve list (gradus arpeggiator_params.h:1322) is a separate list and does not apply here.

Severity: I recommend downgrading from high. The audio path is consistent and saved state reloads correctly. Only the label is wrong: the user hears a different curve than the name promises, which is a misleading UI rather than broken audio or corrupted state. Medium fits better.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the defect from source. The labels and the DSP enum disagree at indices 2 and 3:
- plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/mod_matrix_params.h:43-48: kModCurveStrings = {Linear, Exponential, Logarithmic, S-Curve}. These are appended to the StringListParameter at :231-235, so the host shows these names.
- :26: the comment says the same thing (2=Logarithmic, 3=S-Curve).
- :105-108: the curve is denormalized straight to index 0-3.
- plugins/shared/src/ui/mod_matrix_types.h:113-118: kCurveTypeNames has the same four labels. mod_matrix_grid.h:892-899, 997 and 1326-1327 are the only consumers (menu, cycle and cell text), so the grid shows the wrong names too.
- processor_params.cpp:488 and :492 clamp the index to 0-3 and then `static_cast<ModCurve>(curveIdx)`.
- dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/modulation_types.h:79-84 defines {Linear=0, Exponential=1, SCurve=2, Stepped=3}. modulation_curves.h:48-52 implements index 2 as smoothstep x^2(3-2x) and index 3 as floor(4x)/3. The DSP has no logarithmic curve.
- tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:260-261 uses kCurveSCurve=2 and kCurveStepped=3, with kCurveStepped at :565, 716, 777, 1494, 1681, 2201 and 2536. Those factory presets therefore show "S-Curve" for what is actually a 4-level staircase.

The consequence is real: choosing "S-Curve" gives 4 discrete levels, which at the default smoothMs 0 steps the destination, for example the filter cutoff. Choosing "Logarithmic" gives a smoothstep.

I am downgrading the severity. No audio is corrupted, nothing goes non-finite, state round-trips identically, and the sound is deterministic and matches what the presets intended. The defect is a wrong name for a curve that is otherwise selectable and audible, and a user who chooses by ear gets what they hear. That makes it a medium UI-wiring or label bug, not high.

</details>

### R-083

**Grid edits of global-route curve/scale/bypass/smooth call performEdit only; the controller's parameters go stale and the grid reverts on rebuild**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** ui-wiring · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/controller/controller_mod_matrix.cpp:55-61, 80-120`
- **Also flagged by:** gestalt-controller

**Problem.** The grid's ParameterCallback only calls performEdit, under suppressModMatrixSync_. Curve and scale cycling, the bypass toggle and the smooth drag send their parameter only through this callback (mod_matrix_grid.h:591-596, 1001-1007, 1021-1027, 1039-1044). The routeChanged callback that follows calls setParamNormalized for source, dest and amount only. So the controller-side Parameter objects for curve, smooth, scale and bypass never change. Separately, routeChanged runs a full beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit for source, dest and amount on every amount-drag mouse move. That closes the amount gesture that the drag's own beginEditCallback opened, and writes source/dest automation during an amount drag.

**Why it is wrong.** An edit that starts in the controller must update the controller's Parameter (setParamNormalized) before performEdit, as every other callback in this controller does (e.g. controller_adsr.cpp:63-65, verify_view.cpp:89-92). Gestures must not be nested or closed early.
