### R-150

**All five delay types and the FDN Hall reverb render differently depending on host buffer size**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/effects/digital_delay.h:614-641`

**Problem.** With a deterministic note stream, one effect at a time, blocks 32/100/441/2048 differ from block 512 by up to 0.89 (Digital) for every delay type and for FDN Hall. Plate, Phaser, Flanger, Chorus, Harmonizer and the dry engine are bit-identical. One located per-call construct: DigitalDelay::process runs a per-sample loop that only pushes setDelayTimeMs/setFeedbackAmount into the FeedbackNetwork, then calls feedbackNetwork_.process once for the whole block (line 641). Only the last sample's smoothed and LFO-modulated delay time reaches the network, so the delay-time trajectory is stepped per call. The chain is invoked per engine segment (ruinae_engine.h:956). FDNReverb snapshots its coefficients per 16-sample sub-block counted from each call's start (fdn_reverb.h:385-413). The exact divergence point for Tape, PingPong, Granular, Spectral and FDN was not isolated by the probe.

**Why it is wrong.** The engine comment (ruinae_engine.h:819-825) claims every buffer size renders the same audio. Effect parameter trajectories must be sample-based, not call-based, for output to be reproducible across hosts and offline/online renders.

**Consequence.** Bounces differ from real-time playback and between hosts or buffer settings. Diff energy is up to -0.5 dB relative to the signal, so the difference is audible. Delay modulation depth effectively acts per block.

**Suggested fix.** In DigitalDelay (and the same pattern in TapeDelay::process, tape_delay.h:520-535) pass per-sample delay time into the FeedbackNetwork, or process the network sample by sample. Bisect Tape, PingPong, Granular, Spectral and FDN with the probe's renderInv2 harness per delay. Add a block-size-invariance test (bs 32/441/2048 vs 512) per delay type and reverb type.

**Evidence.** probe block-invariance2: 'Digital 0.59-0.89 (-8.1 to -0.7 dB); Tape 0.29-0.56; PingPong 0.29-0.65; Granular 0.29-0.48; Spectral 0.34-0.81 (-0.5 dB at bs32); Hall(FDN) 0.15-0.51 (-5 dB at bs2048). Plate, Phaser, Flanger, Chorus, Harmonizer and the dry engine are bit-identical'; block-invariance:v3 ~1.0. digital_delay.h:616-641 'for (size_t i = 0; i &lt; numSamples; ++i) { ... feedbackNetwork_.setDelayTimeMs(modulatedDelay); ... } feedbackNetwork_.process(left, right, numSamples, ctx);'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The headline holds: output does depend on host block size. The probe that measured it exists (specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:2287-2338, renderInv2 / block-invariance2). But the mechanisms the finding names are only partly right, and the fix plan needs correcting.

1) DigitalDelay (digital_delay.h:614-641). The code does what the finding says. The per-sample loop calls feedbackNetwork_.setDelayTimeMs / setFeedbackAmount, and those only store targetDelayMs_ (feedback_network.h:321-336). FeedbackNetwork::process then calls delaySmoother_.setTarget(targetDelayMs_) once per call (feedback_network.h:225). So only the last sample's smoothed and LFO-modulated time becomes the network's target, which gives a per-call staircase. The engine runs the chain once per engine call (ruinae_engine.h:956), and the processor calls the engine per segment. On the first call, setDelayTimeMs snaps the network to the last value of that call (hasProcessed_==false, lines 330-335), which also depends on block size. That is a real per-call construct. The probe does not exercise the LFO part, though: digitalModDepth defaults to 0 (delay_params.h:33), and renderInv2 does not set it. The probe's ramp is 500 to 300 ms (delay_params.h:23, audit_probes.cpp:2297), and it settles within about 100 ms, before any audio reaches the 300 ms read head. So the measured 0.59-0.89 Digital divergence probably has another source as well. A candidate is the single DynamicsProcessor limiter_, which processes the whole left block and then the whole right block with one envelope state (digital_delay.h:717-718). That makes the gain trajectory depend on block size. I did not bisect this. The cited construct is still a genuine block-size dependence whenever the time is modulated or changing.

2) FDN Hall: the cited mechanism is WRONG. fdn_reverb.h:385-413 only takes snapshots of member values (lfoEpsilon_, filterCoeffs_, feedbackGains_, mix_) that change only in setParamsInternal (fdn_reverb.h:550-632). With constant parameters, a 16-sample sub-block grid produces the same per-sample result at any block size. The real cause is in the effects chain. renderInv2 switches the reverb type from Plate (0) to Hall (1) at t=0. Processor::applyParamsToEngine runs once per host process() (processor.cpp:251) and calls engine_.setReverbType on every block (processor_params.cpp:655 -> ruinae_engine.h:693). RuinaeEffectsChain::setReverbType (ruinae_effects_chain.h:689-701) only returns early when `type == activeReverbType_ && !reverbCrossfading_`. While a crossfade to Hall is running, active is still 0, so every host block resets reverbCrossfadeAlpha_ = 0 and restarts it. The 30 ms crossfade (1440 samples at 48 kHz) can only finish within one host block of at least 1440 samples. That explains why bs2048 differs from bs512. More seriously, at common buffer sizes (64-1024) a live Plate-to-Hall switch never completes: the output keeps cycling between the two reverbs, ramping toward Hall and resetting every block. setDelayType does not have this bug, because it returns early when the requested type is already the incoming one (lines 398-401). The fix plan should target setReverbType, not fdn_reverb.h.

3) Tape, PingPong, Granular, Spectral: renderInv2 switches these from the default Digital type (delay_params.h:22, type{0}). A switch runs a pre-warm, and the crossfade starts at the first chunk boundary after preWarmRemaining_ runs out (ruinae_effects_chain.h:883-891). The start of the transition is therefore quantised to the block, which makes these renders differ by block size. This is a type-switch transient. The probe does not show that steady-state Tape/PingPong/Granular/Spectral processing is block-variant, and the finding's pointer to tape_delay.h:520-535 was not demonstrated.

Verdict: the defect class is real and confirmed from source (the per-call network target in DigitalDelay, the block-quantised delay pre-warm end, and the reverb crossfade that restarts every block). The FDN attribution is wrong, and the probe mostly measures type-switch transients rather than steady-state per-delay processing. Severity stays medium for this finding as written. The setReverbType restart (a live Plate-to-Hall switch never completes at buffer sizes under about 1440 samples at 48 kHz) deserves its own finding at higher severity.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source. Nothing guards against this and nothing documents it as intended.

(1) dsp/include/krate/dsp/effects/digital_delay.h:617-638: the per-sample loop only calls feedbackNetwork_.setDelayTimeMs(modulatedDelay) and setFeedbackAmount(currentFeedback). The network then runs once per call at line 641. FeedbackNetwork::process (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/feedback_network.h:219-236) reads its target with delaySmoother_.setTarget(targetDelayMs_) once at the top of the call. So only the last sample's smoothed and LFO-modulated time is used, and the delay-time target moves in steps at call boundaries. When the time is changing (smoother glide, mod depth > 0, sync tempo), the trajectory depends on the call length.

(2) tape_delay.h:515-536 has the same pattern. Its per-sample loop does push setTapTimeMs, but the feedback is read once per call via feedbackSmoother_.getCurrentValue() (line 531) before tapManager_.process runs on the whole block.

(3) fdn_reverb.h:385-413 snapshots LFO, filter coefficients, mix and width every 16 samples, counted from offset 0 of each call. The sub-block grid therefore restarts at every call boundary and depends on block size.

(4) Callers: ruinae_engine.h:956 runs effectsChain_.processBlock once per engine call over the whole numSamples. ruinae_effects_chain.h:281-291 only splits at maxBlockSize_. Unlike the voices and the mod engine (lines 846-912, which use modGridPhase_), the effects have no fixed grid counted across calls. The engine comment at 819-825 covers only Steps 3-7 (the mod engine and voices), so it does not claim invariance for the FX. Line 923 even says the chain "runs once per buffer". That shows the FX path was never brought onto the grid. It is not a documented acceptance of block-size dependence.

(5) No block-size-invariance test exists for Ruinae or its FX. The grep for BlockSize/invariance finds only Profundum/Seraphis/Vorago/NoiseOrganism and similar.

(6) The probe harness exists and matches the claim: specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:2287-2338 (renderInv2, AuditProbe2 block invariance isolation). It is deterministic: a fixed note stream, one effect per variant, 2 s at 48 kHz, each block size compared against 512. Its params set the delay time to 300 ms at the start, so the time smoother's glide is exactly the case where the stepped target diverges. The default digitalModDepth is 0 (delay_params.h:33), so the LFO path is not the only trigger. The glide from the initial time and any later time or tempo change are enough.

Severity medium stands: offline bounces and real-time playback, and different hosts, render differently. It is not a crash and not a NaN.

**Note 3.** The cited construct is real. In digital_delay.h:614-638 the time, feedback and mod-depth smoothers and the modulation LFO advance once per sample, but each iteration only overwrites the FeedbackNetwork target (setDelayTimeMs at :636, setFeedbackAmount at :637). feedbackNetwork_.process is then called once at :641. In feedback_network.h:225, process() latches delaySmoother_.setTarget(targetDelayMs_) once per call and runs its own smoother per sample (:230). setDelayTimeMs (:321-336) only stores the target, except before the first process, where it snaps. So the delay time the network actually uses is a smoothed staircase whose steps sit at call boundaries. Ruinae calls it per chunk (ruinae_effects_chain.h:1178 inside processChunk :817) and exposes Digital mod depth (:512), so the claim about the mechanism holds.

The finding overstates the impact:
(1) When the delay time is constant and mod depth is 0, the result does not depend on block size once the smoothers settle. DigitalDelay::setTime (:316-320) only sets a smoother target, and prepare/reset snap it (:232, :283, :293). The probe (audit_probes.cpp:2287-2297) sets kDelayTimeId=~300 ms in the first block, so the smoother glides from kDefaultDelayMs while the stepped targets differ by block size. That startup glide is then echoed by the feedback, which is where the large max|diff| of 0.59-0.89 comes from. It is a one-time transient made by the probe, not a steady-state difference.
(2) A diff energy of -0.7 to -8 dB between two renders whose echoes are offset by a fraction of a millisecond is waveform decorrelation. It does not show an audible artifact, because both renders are click-free glides. "Audible difference" is not established.
(3) For Tape, PingPong, Granular and Spectral the divergence was not isolated. A more likely chain-level cause is that the end of pre-warm is quantized to the block: ruinae_effects_chain.h:883-887 tests numSamples >= preWarmRemaining_ and calls startCrossfade() at the end of the chunk. The crossfade from the default Digital type therefore starts up to one block late, depending on block size. That is a different construct from the one cited.

What is left is real: delay-time automation and LFO mod depth are sampled once per process call and then smoothed. At large buffers (2048 = 43 ms) this lowers the effective modulation sample rate to about 23 Hz and changes the modulation depth and shape. It is a block-size-dependent behaviour of a modulation and automation feature, not a constant difference in the audio. I downgrade the severity from medium to low.

</details>

### R-152

**Filter type change mid-note clicks: hard switch to a filter with stale state, no crossfade**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:748-763`

**Problem.** setFilterType changes filterType_, updates the SVF mode and re-applies cutoff and resonance to the newly active filter. It does no crossfade and no state reset or warm-up, so the incoming filter (Ladder, SelfOscillating, ...) starts from whatever state it held the last time it was active. For SelfOscillating, noteOn() was never run for the current note.

**Why it is wrong.** Type switches are automatable and preset-driven, and every other switch the probe tested (oscillator, distortion, mix mode, voice mode, FX types) stays at or below a 1.5 jump ratio. A filter switch needs a short crossfade or a matched-state start.

**Consequence.** An audible click when automating or changing the filter type while notes sound (SVF LP -> Ladder and SVF LP -> SelfOscillating).

**Suggested fix.** Run old and new filters in parallel for 5-10 ms and crossfade, resetting the incoming filter first. Add a test: saw A3 held, step the filter type at a block boundary, jump ratio &lt;= 1.5 for every type pair.

**Evidence.** probe automation:filter type SVF_LP->Ladder / SVF_LP->SelfOscillating: 'jump ratio 3.55 (1 outlier sample) for both; Ladder->Comb ok' (threshold &lt;=1.5). ruinae_voice.h:755-762 'filterType_ = type; updateSvfMode(type); setActiveFilterCutoff(filterCutoffHz_); setActiveFilterResonance(filterResonance_);'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The source and the probe output both confirm it. plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:748-763: when the type changes, setFilterType only sets filterType_, calls updateSvfMode(type) and re-applies cutoff and resonance through setActiveFilterCutoff and setActiveFilterResonance (switch at :1371). It does not crossfade, it does not call resetActiveFilter() (defined at :1313-1343, its only use is a full voice reset), and it does not call snapActiveFilterToTarget() (:1350). The incoming filter therefore starts from whatever state it last held, which is all zeros if it was never active. For SelfOscillating, filterSelfOsc_->noteOn() runs only inside the voice's noteOn (:279-283), so a mid-note switch never triggers it for the held note. The call path has no smoothing anywhere else: processor_params.cpp:317 applyFilterParams -> engine_.setFilterType -> ruinae_engine.h:1085-1086, which loops voice.setFilterType(type) over every voice. The measurement is real. f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/probe-results.txt:74 ('filter type SVF_LP->Ladder ... jump ratio = 3.55 (outlier samples 1) ... bad') and :76 ('SVF_LP->SelfOscillating ... jump ratio = 3.55 (outlier samples 1) ... bad') against threshold &lt;=1.5. Ladder->Comb at :72 measures 0.98 ok, which matches the finding's wording. The probe is specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1296-1342 (runStep: saw A3 held, parameter step at a block boundary, clickAt ±10 ms against 50 ms steady references). Both bad transitions show a single-sample outlier, which fits a hard switch of the output source to a filter whose state does not match the old one. Medium severity fits: the step is audible, but it happens only when the filter type is automated or changed while notes sound.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. The code works as the reviewer describes, and nothing guards it or documents it as intended.

- **No crossfade or warm-up.** ruinae_voice.h:748-763 (setFilterType) sets filterType_ and then calls updateSvfMode, setActiveFilterCutoff and setActiveFilterResonance. There is no crossfade, no reset and no warm-up of the incoming filter.
- **Only one filter runs at a time.** processActiveFilter (ruinae_voice.h:1449-1479) switches on filterType_ and processes only the active filter. On the next sample the output moves from the live SVF state to the Ladder or SelfOscillating state. That state is either still at zero from prepare (it was never active) or left over from the last time that filter ran.
- **Self-oscillating filter never gets its note-on.** filterSelfOsc_->noteOn() is called only inside noteOn() (lines 279-283), and only when filterType_ was already SelfOscillating at note start. Switching to SelfOscillating mid-note never triggers it, as the finding says.
- **No reset elsewhere.** snapActiveFilterToTarget (lines 1350-1368) only acts on the SVF types and runs only at noteOn. resetActiveFilter (lines 1313-1343) is documented as being for a full voice reset or a stolen voice only.

Guards I looked for:

- **Comments.** The class comment (lines 56-60) and the setFilterType comment (lines 744-747) promise only that the switch is allocation-free (SC-004). They say nothing about being click-free, and they do not record the hard switch as a design decision. My search of specs/Ruinae.md, the roadmap, plugins/ruinae and the prior audit files found no ruling that accepts a click on filter-type changes.
- **The existing test does not cover clicks.** "RuinaeVoice: filter type switch no clicks or allocation (AS-4.4)" (plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/ruinae_voice_test.cpp:543-585) is named as a no-clicks test, but it only checks that the peak stays above 0.001 and that there is no NaN or Inf after each switch. It has no discontinuity or jump-ratio assertion, so nothing pins the behaviour.
- **The measurement is real.** I read the probe in specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt: runStep at lines 1296-1330 and the filter-type cases at lines 1339-1342. It holds a saw on A3 at 48 kHz and steps kFilterTypeId at a block boundary. It then measures the jump ratio with clickAt over a ±10 ms window against 50 ms of steady output before it, with "≤1.5 ok" as the threshold. That matches the quoted SVF_LP->Ladder and SVF_LP->SelfOscillating cases.

**Severity: downgrade.**

- The defect is one outlier sample at a 3.55x jump ratio, which is a mild click.
- It only happens when a stepped list parameter (the filter type) changes while a note sounds, which hosts rarely automate.
- Ladder->Comb measured OK.
- It causes no NaN, no stuck note and no level explosion.

That is a real but low-severity click artifact, not medium.

**Note 3.** I could not refute this. The code matches the claim and the measurement is consistent with it.

Code:
- `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:748-763`: `setFilterType` sets `filterType_` (755), calls `updateSvfMode` (758), then `setActiveFilterCutoff` and `setActiveFilterResonance` (761-762). It does not reset, prime or crossfade.
- `processActiveFilter` (1449-1478) runs only the filter for the current `filterType_`. The filter being switched to therefore starts with whatever state it had: all zeros if it has never run since `prepare`, or old state from its last use.
- `snapActiveFilterToTarget` (1350-1367) is called only from `noteOn` (271), and for non-SVF types it does nothing anyway.
- `filterSelfOsc_->noteOn(...)` (279-283) runs only when the type is already SelfOscillating at note-on. After a switch mid-note it is never triggered for the held note, and `noteOff` (296-298) then calls `noteOff` on a filter that never received the note-on.

Callers:
- `processor_params.cpp:317` calls `engine_.setFilterType` from the parameter value.
- `ruinae_engine.h:1085-1087` loops over every voice and calls `voice.setFilterType(type)`.
- Neither level smooths or crossfades. Every sounding voice switches on the same sample.

Measurement (`specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1296-1342`): saw A3 held at 48 kHz, filter type stepped at a block boundary, jump ratio taken over a ±10 ms window against 50 ms steady references.
- SVF_LP→Ladder and SVF_LP→SelfOscillating both measured 3.55 (1 outlier sample). The ok threshold is ≤1.5 and the suspicious threshold is 3.
- The two values are identical. That fits the explanation that in both cases the new filter starts from zero state, so output drops on the first sample from the filtered saw level to near zero. The size of the step is set by the old output, not by the new filter.
- Ladder→Comb measured ok.
- The same probe reads ≤1.5 for the oscillator, distortion and mix-mode switches (1346-1354), so the filter switch is the inconsistent case.

Impact:
- At the switch, every held voice has a one-sample step about as large as the signal itself, 3.5 times the largest per-sample change of a held saw. That is an audible click.
- The SelfOscillating case also leaves that filter running without the note-on it normally gets until the next note-on (279-283). That is a behaviour defect on top of the click.

Severity:
- This happens only when the user or automation changes a discrete filter-type list mid-note. It does not occur on held notes otherwise and it is not a stability or stuck-note risk.
- It is consistently reproducible and audible on every voice, so medium is justified and I am not changing it.

</details>

### R-168

**Mono mode noteId never follows the sounding note: a released legato note's id and per-note tuning stay on voice 0, so the held note's MPE expressions are lost**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** followup:allocator-slot-and-noteid-bookkeeping · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:289-292, 296-312, 1815-1826`

**Problem.** In mono mode, noteOn(note, vel, noteId) unconditionally stamps voices_[0] with the new noteId (:289-292). This includes a note that MonoHandler rejected (out of range, mono_handler.h:150-152), a velocity-0 note (mono_handler.h:155-157), and a non-winning Low/High-priority note. noteOff(note, noteId) handles noteId only in Poly mode (:300). In mono it falls back to noteOff(note) and never touches voice 0's noteId. When dispatchMonoNoteOff returns to a still-held note, it only calls voices_[0].setFrequency(processPortamento()) (:1823-1825). The noteId stays the released note's id, and expressionTuning_/expressionVolume_ stay the released note's values. Only RuinaeVoice::noteOn and reset clear them (ruinae_voice.h:212-214, 249-251), and updateOscFrequencies keeps applying expressionTuning_ (ruinae_voice.h:1601). Sequence: MPE mono, legato on. Hold C3 (id 1), press E3 (id 2), and voice 0 is stamped id 2. Bend E3 +1 st via kTuningTypeID, then release E3. Voice 0 glides back to C3 but plays it +1 st. Further tuning expressions for id 1 are dropped, because findVoiceByNoteId(1) finds nothing (:317-325).

**Why it is wrong.** Per-note expression must address the note that is sounding. When the mono voice changes or returns to a note, the voice's noteId and expression state must switch to that note's id and its last expression values, or at least reset to neutral. A rejected or non-winning note-on must not take over the voice's identity.

**Consequence.** With an MPE controller in Mono mode, releasing the upper note of a legato pair leaves the remaining held note detuned by the departed finger's last pitch glide, at the wrong volume and brightness. The held note no longer responds to its own finger's slide or pressure until it is re-struck.

**Suggested fix.** Track noteId per entry alongside MonoHandler's stack (a 16-entry array in the engine keyed by MIDI note). Stamp voices_[0] only when the winner changes. On a return-to-held-note, set voice 0's noteId to the winner's stored id and reset expression to neutral, or to the last values cached per id. In mono noteOff(note, noteId), clear the id from the side table. Test (mpe_test): mono+legato, noteOn(48,id1), noteOn(52,id2), expression tuning on id2 = +1 st, noteOff(52,id2). Assert that the voice 0 frequency equals C3 within 1 cent, and that a tuning expression on id1 changes the frequency.

**Evidence.** ruinae_engine.h:289-291 `} else if (noteId >= 0 && mode_ != VoiceMode::Poly) { voices_[0].setNoteId(noteId); voices_[0].setMidiNote(...)`; :300 `if (noteId >= 0 && mode_ == VoiceMode::Poly) {`; :1823-1825 `// Returning to a held note  float freq = monoHandler_.processPortamento(); voices_[0].setFrequency(freq);`; ruinae_voice.h:1601 `const float tuningRatio = semitonesToRatio(expressionTuning_);`; ruinae_voice.h:304-309 setFrequency does not touch expression fields.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the whole path and the defect is real.

1. Processor routing: processor_midi.cpp:93 sends an MPE note-on with noteId>=0 to engine_.noteOn(pitch, vel, noteId). :97 sends the note-off to engine_.noteOff(pitch, noteId). :107 sends expressions to engine_.setNoteExpression(noteId, ...).

2. Note-on: ruinae_engine.h:272-292 first calls noteOn(note, vel, legato), which reaches dispatchMonoNoteOn (:250). It then stamps voices_[0] with setNoteId(noteId) and setMidiNote(note) at :289-291 whenever mode_ != Poly. It does this unconditionally, whatever MonoHandler decided. mono_handler.h:178-183 can pick a different winner under Low/High priority, and the new id is stamped anyway.

3. Legato note-on: mono_handler.h:190-191 returns retrigger=false when notes are held and legato is on. ruinae_engine.h:1805-1809 then calls only voices_[0].setFrequency(freq). setFrequency (ruinae_voice.h:304-309) does not touch expressionTuning_, expressionVolume_ or expressionBrightness_. Only RuinaeVoice::noteOn (:249-251) and reset (:214-216) clear them.

4. Note-off: ruinae_engine.h:300 handles noteId only in Poly mode. In mono, :312 falls back to dispatchMonoNoteOff. When MonoHandler returns to a held note (mono_handler.h:251-269, isNoteOn=true), ruinae_engine.h:1822-1825 calls only voices_[0].setFrequency(processPortamento()). The noteId stays the released note's id, and the expression fields keep the released note's values.

5. Expression lookup: findVoiceByNoteId (:317-325) matches voices_[i].noteId(). After the sequence C3(id1), E3(id2), release E3, voice 0 still carries id2. Expressions for id1 are dropped. updateOscFrequencies keeps applying expressionTuning_ (ruinae_voice.h:1601). So C3 sounds with E3's last tuning offset, and only a stray id2 expression could still reach it.

No test in plugins/ruinae/tests/integration/mpe_test.cpp covers mono mode.

Minor overstatements, which do not change the verdict:
- The out-of-range rejection (mono_handler.h:150) is practically unreachable through the processor for normal 0-127 notes.
- The velocity-0 path depends on processor conversion.
- Even without legato, the return-to-held-note path with retrigger=true still calls only setFrequency (engine :1823-1825), so the problem is broader than the legato case.

Medium severity fits: the bug needs MPE input plus Mono mode, but then it audibly detunes a held note.

**Note 2.** I could not refute it. The source confirms each step of the claim, and I found no guard elsewhere, no test pinning the behaviour, and no documentation calling it intentional.

(1) noteOn with a noteId (ruinae_engine.h:272-293) first calls noteOn(note, vel, legato). In mono mode it then sets voices_[0].setNoteId(noteId) and setMidiNote(note) at :289-291 without checking whether MonoHandler accepted the note or picked it as the winner. MonoHandler::noteOn (mono_handler.h:150-152) returns an inactive event for an out-of-range note, and findWinner (:179) may keep the old note under Low/High priority. dispatchMonoNoteOn (:1796-1813) ignores both cases, but the stamp still happens.

(2) noteOff with a noteId (:296-313) only matches by id in Poly mode (:300). In mono it falls through to noteOff(note), which never resets voice 0's noteId.

(3) dispatchMonoNoteOff (:1815-1827), when MonoHandler returns to a held note (mono_handler.h:251-269 returns isNoteOn=true), calls only voices_[0].setFrequency(processPortamento()). It never reads monoEvent.retrigger, never calls noteOn and never updates the noteId. RuinaeVoice::setFrequency (ruinae_voice.h:304-309) changes only noteFrequency_ and calls updateOscFrequencies. expressionTuning_ and expressionVolume_ are reset only in reset() (:214-215) and noteOn() (:249-251). The legato note-on path also uses setFrequency (:1809), so expression values carry across.

(4) The processor routes host noteIds into these overloads (processor_midi.cpp:93, 97), and expressions go to setNoteExpression (:107). That function uses findVoiceByNoteId (ruinae_engine.h:317-325), which matches the stored noteId only, so later expressions for the held note's id find no voice and are dropped.

The reported sequence therefore holds: voice 0 returns to C3 while still applying E3's last tuning, volume and brightness, and C3's id cannot be addressed. A grep of plugins/ruinae for mono MPE / noteId found no test and no documentation (the MANUAL hit is unrelated).

Severity stays medium: the bug only affects MPE input in Mono mode, but there it produces audibly wrong pitch and level.

**Note 3.** The defect is real and I confirmed it from source. ruinae_engine.h:289-291: in any non-Poly mode, the noteId-aware noteOn stamps voices_[0].setNoteId(noteId) unconditionally after delegating. It does not check whether MonoHandler accepted the note or whether it won priority. ruinae_engine.h:300: the noteId-aware noteOff only handles the id in Poly mode, then falls through to noteOff(note), which reaches dispatchMonoNoteOff. dispatchMonoNoteOff (ruinae_engine.h:1815-1826) handles a return to a held note only with voices_[0].setFrequency(monoHandler_.processPortamento()). It never resets noteId_ or the expression fields, and it ignores MonoNoteEvent.retrigger even though mono_handler.h:259-269 returns retrigger=!legato_ there. The legato note-on path (1805-1810) also calls only setFrequency. RuinaeVoice::setFrequency (ruinae_voice.h:304-309) only sets noteFrequency_ and calls updateOscFrequencies(). That function still applies semitonesToRatio(expressionTuning_) (ruinae_voice.h:1601), and expressionVolume_ still scales the amp at :622. Only noteOn/reset clear those fields (:214-215, :249-250). The processor routes noteId-carrying events to engine_.noteOn/noteOff(pitch, vel/noteId) and expressions to engine_.setNoteExpression (processor_midi.cpp:93-107). setNoteExpression -> findVoiceByNoteId (ruinae_engine.h:317-325) matches on voices_[0].noteId(). After E3 (id 2) is released, voice 0 keeps id 2, so expressions sent for id 1 (the held C3) are silently dropped. C3 keeps E3's last tuning offset; the full range is ±120 st (:337), so any pitch slide the departed finger made remains. Volume also stays at E3's last value. Impact: this triggers only in Mono mode with a host or controller that sends noteIds plus per-note expressions (MPE/VST3 note expression: Bitwig, Cubase, MPE controllers) and overlapping notes. That is niche but entirely ordinary for MPE use. The result is an audible, persistent detune of the held note (cents to semitones, whatever the released finger last slid) until it is re-struck. Medium is appropriate. The brightness part of the claim I did not verify (the kBrightness case was not read). The voice-volume and tuning parts are confirmed.
