### R-169

**Out-of-range OSC A/B Type from state is latched in SelectableOscillator::activeType_ and later used unchecked as a slots_ index in prepare(): out-of-bounds read and a virtual call through a garbage pointer**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high → medium · **Dimension:** followup:state-load-unclamped-sweep · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/selectable_oscillator.h:105, 132-147`

**Problem.** loadOscParams stores the OSC type raw (osc_params.h:731-732, `params.type.store(intVal, ...)`), while the parameter handler clamps it to 0..9 (osc_params.h:219-222). applyVoiceAndOscParams casts it straight to OscType (uint8_t underlying, oscillator_types.h:25) (processor_params.cpp:280-281, 289-290). SelectableOscillator::setType assigns `activeType_ = type;` at line 138 *before* its bounds check at 144-147. The check therefore only rejects the slot switch, and the invalid enum value stays in activeType_. On the next prepare(), which runs from Processor::setupProcessing via engine.prepare and voice.prepare (processor.cpp:182, ruinae_engine.h:141, ruinae_voice.h:135-136), line 105 does `active_ = slots_[static_cast<size_t>(activeType_)].get();` with no check, then calls `active_->setFrequency(...)` at line 110.

**Why it is wrong.** slots_ is a std::array of 10 unique_ptrs (line 295), so operator[] with an index of 10-255 is undefined behaviour. Index 10 reads active_, index 11 reads the packed activeType_/phaseMode_/currentFrequency_ bytes, and index 12 reads the sampleRate_ double (lines 298-304). Any of these that is non-null is then used as an OscillatorSlot* and called virtually. A loader that clamps every other index (arp, trance gate) should clamp this one too, and the DSP should not store an enum value it has just rejected.

**Consequence.** Loading a corrupt or hand-edited preset or project with OSC A/B type at or above 11 (as uint8) plays normally until the host calls setupProcessing again: a sample-rate change, buffer-size change, offline-render re-setup, or the deactivate/re-setup that many hosts do on transport or engine restart. At that point every voice dereferences garbage in prepare() and the host crashes. In 16 voices x 2 oscillators the crash is near-certain. With type exactly 10 the old slot stays active and type changes are silently ignored.

**Suggested fix.** (1) loadOscParams: `params.type.store(std::clamp(intVal, 0, kOscTypeCount - 1))`. (2) SelectableOscillator::setType: validate idx before assigning activeType_, and return without changing state when it is out of range. (3) prepare(): bound-check activeType_ and fall back to PolyBLEP. Test: a dsp_systems test that calls setType(static_cast&lt;OscType>(12)) and then prepare(), checking getActiveType() is still valid and processBlock is finite (under ASan). Also a Ruinae processor test: setState with an OSC type of 200, process one block, setupProcessing at 96 kHz, process again, and expect no crash.

**Evidence.** osc_params.h:731-732 `if (!streamer.readInt32(intVal)) return false; params.type.store(intVal, ...)` vs handler 220-221 `std::clamp(..., 0, kOscTypeCount - 1)`; processor_params.cpp:280 `engine_.setOscAType(static_cast<OscType>(oscAParams_.type.load(...)))`; selectable_oscillator.h:138 `activeType_ = type;` then 144-147 `if (idx >= kNumOscTypes || !slots_[idx]) return;`; line 105 `active_ = slots_[static_cast<size_t>(activeType_)].get();` then 110 `active_->setFrequency(currentFrequency_);`; members 295-304 (slots_[10], active_, activeType_, phaseMode_, currentFrequency_, sampleRate_).

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the full path in the source and could not refute the finding.
(1) Load: plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/osc_params.h:731-732 stores the raw int32 with `params.type.store(intVal, ...)` and no clamp. The automation handler at 220-222 does clamp to 0..kOscTypeCount-1. loadOscAParams and loadOscBParams (osc_a_params.h:39, osc_b_params.h:39) forward to it. Processor::setState calls them straight into the live atomics (processor_state.cpp:156-157), and so does applyPresetSnapshot (322-323). Nothing in processor_state.cpp clamps the value afterwards: a grep for clamp, type.store and kOscTypeCount returns nothing.
(2) Use: processor_params.cpp:280-281 and 289-290 cast the stored value straight to OscType, which has a uint8_t underlying type (oscillator_types.h:25). RuinaeEngine::setOscAType (ruinae_engine.h:1009-1011) passes it to every voice, and RuinaeVoice::setOscAType (ruinae_voice.h:638-640) passes it to SelectableOscillator::setType.
(3) Latch: selectable_oscillator.h:138 assigns `activeType_ = type;` before the `prepared_` early return (140) and before the bounds check `idx >= kNumOscTypes` (144-147). An out-of-range enum therefore stays in activeType_ even though the slot switch is rejected.
(4) Out-of-bounds read: Processor::setupProcessing calls engine_.prepare (processor.cpp:182). That calls voice.prepare (ruinae_engine.h:141), which calls oscA_.prepare and oscB_.prepare (ruinae_voice.h:135-136). SelectableOscillator::prepare line 105 then does `active_ = slots_[static_cast<size_t>(activeType_)].get();` with no bounds check. slots_ is `std::array<unique_ptr<OscillatorSlot>, kNumOscTypes>` (line 295), so an index of 10 or more is undefined behaviour. The value read is whatever member follows the array (active_ at 298, then activeType_, phaseMode_, currentFrequency_ and sampleRate_ at 300-303). Lines 109-110 then call active_->setFrequency virtually if that pointer is non-null.
(5) A second route the finding does not mention: if setState runs before the first setupProcessing and a process() call applies the params while prepared_ is false, setType latches the bad value and returns at line 141. The first prepare then indexes out of bounds directly.
The trigger needs a corrupt or hand-edited state, since a normal getState writes only clamped values. The crash and undefined behaviour are real and reachable from host-supplied data, so I am keeping the severity as reported.

**Note 2.** I confirmed every link of the claimed path in the source. No guard elsewhere breaks it.
- plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/osc_params.h:731-732 stores the OSC type raw (`params.type.store(intVal, ...)`). The normalized handler at osc_params.h:220-221 clamps to 0..kOscTypeCount-1, but the loader does not.
- processor_state.cpp:156-157 (setState) and :322-323 (preset snapshot path) call loadOscA/BParams straight into oscAParams_/oscBParams_. No processor-side clamp exists; a grep for clamp in src/processor finds none on osc type.
- processor_params.cpp:280-281 and 289-290 do `engine_.setOscAType(static_cast<OscType>(oscAParams_.type.load()))`. OscType is `enum class : uint8_t` with values 0..9 plus NumTypes=10 (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/oscillator_types.h:25-37), so the int is truncated to a uint8.
- ruinae_engine.h:1009-1015 and ruinae_voice.h:638-645 forward it with no check.
- selectable_oscillator.h:138 assigns `activeType_ = type;` before the bounds check at :144-147. That check only skips the slot switch, so the invalid value stays latched.
- On the next setupProcessing (processor.cpp:182, engine_.prepare), RuinaeVoice::prepare calls oscA_/oscB_.prepare (ruinae_voice.h:135-136). selectable_oscillator.h:105 then does `slots_[static_cast<size_t>(activeType_)]` with no bounds check. slots_ is a std::array of kNumOscTypes=10 (:295), so any index of 10 or more is out of bounds. Line 110 then calls the garbage pointer virtually.
- No test covers an out-of-range type. selectable_oscillator_test.cpp has only the NumTypes==10 static assert.
- This is not a repeat of a prior F-id. The only prior-audit mention of loadOscParams (implementation-plan.md:590) is the osc_params.h dedup refactor, not a clamp.
- I found no design note marking this as intentional.

I recommend downgrading the severity. The defect is real UB and a likely crash, but a real host only hands back state that getState wrote, and that state is always in range. It needs a corrupt, hand-edited or fuzzed preset or project, followed by a re-setup. That makes it a robustness and hardening bug rather than a crash in normal use.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the mechanism from source.
(1) The load is unclamped. plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/osc_params.h:731-732 reads an int32 and stores it in params.type with no clamp. The parameter handler at 219-222 clamps to 0..kOscTypeCount-1. processor_state.cpp:151-157 checks only the stream version (1..kCurrentStateVersion) and then calls loadOscAParams/loadOscBParams. No later sanitise step exists: there is no clamp or sanitise in processor_state.cpp.
(2) The bad value reaches the oscillator on every block. process() calls applyParamsToEngine() at processor.cpp:251. That calls applyVoiceAndOscParams, which does a raw static_cast&lt;OscType>(type) at processor_params.cpp:280-281 and 289-290. OscType is a uint8_t enum (oscillator_types.h:25). The value then goes through ruinae_engine.h:1009-1014 and ruinae_voice.h:638-645 to SelectableOscillator::setType.
(3) The bad type is latched before the check. selectable_oscillator.h:138 assigns activeType_ = type before the bounds check at 144-147, so the rejected value stays stored. The early return at 134 means it is never re-examined.
(4) The out-of-range index is used on the next setupProcessing. processor.cpp:182 calls engine_.prepare, then voice prepare (ruinae_voice.h:135-136), then SelectableOscillator::prepare. Line 105 indexes slots_ (std::array of 10, line 295) with activeType_ unchecked, and line 110 makes a virtual call through the result. Member layout is at 295-305. Index 10 aliases active_, which is still a valid slot, so it does not crash but later type changes are ignored. Index 11 reads activeType_/phaseMode_/currentFrequency_ as a pointer and index 12 reads sampleRate_; both are non-null garbage, so the call crashes. Higher indices read maxBlockSize_ and the members that follow, or other RuinaeVoice memory: undefined behaviour.

Impact and severity: the claimed crash path is real, but the trigger is narrow. Normal saves and factory presets only write 0..9 (osc_params.h:678 writes the handler-clamped atomic). States from a newer plugin version are rejected by the version check at processor_state.cpp:151, so forward compatibility cannot trigger it. Only a corrupt or hand-crafted project or preset (any value 11..255 as uint8, including negative int32s such as -1 -> 255) leads to the crash. Even then it needs a later setupProcessing (a sample-rate or block-size change, or an offline-render re-setup). It is a real out-of-bounds read and host crash, but only from malformed input. I downgrade it from high to medium.

</details>

### R-176

**Changing Pitch Shift Mode mid-stream hard-resets all four voice shifters with no fade, leaves the shared STFT stale, and scoops the pitch from unison**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** followup:harmonizer-wiring-and-shared-engine · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/harmonizer_engine.h:616-623 (with ruinae_effects_chain.h:766-768, processor_params.cpp:727, pitch_shift_processor.h:1235-1245, 444-456, stft.h:166-169, 210-247)`

**Problem.** applyHarmonizerParams calls setHarmonizerPitchShiftMode every block. The equality guard keeps an unchanged value idempotent. On a real change, HarmonizerEngine::setPitchShiftMode calls pitchShifter.reset() on all four voices immediately: no crossfade, no wet fade-out or fade-in, and no new applyVoiceFadeIn, so fadeInGain stays 1. It does not reset sharedStft_ or sharedPitchDetector_. PitchShiftProcessor::reset() also resets its internal semitoneSmoother to 0 and then sets the target, so the shift glides up from 0 semitones.

**Why it is wrong.** A user-facing mode switch on a running effect must be click-free and must not replay old audio. The chain uses crossfades for delay, reverb and modulation type changes, but this one is a bare reset. sharedStft_ is only fed while the mode is PhaseVocoder. After a PV -> other -> PV round trip, its ring still holds samplesAvailable_ = fftSize - hop = 3072 samples from the moment PV was last left, which can be any time earlier.

**Consequence.** Switching Simple, Granular or PitchSync while notes sound: the wet harmony drops instantly from full level to silence (click). The reset SimplePitchShifter reads zeros at delay1_ = maxDelay (50 ms window), then hits the zero/signal edge in its buffer (a second click). Every harmony voice scoops from unison to its interval over about 10 ms. Switching to PhaseVocoder: the harmony goes silent for the 5120-sample (116 ms) PV latency, then returns at full gain. Its first frames contain up to 3072 samples (about 70 ms) of audio from the last time PV was used, a ghost of old material.

**Suggested fix.** In setPitchShiftMode: reset sharedStft_ / sharedAnalysisSpectrum_ / sharedPitchDetector_ when entering their mode, snap the PitchShiftProcessor semitone smoother to its target after reset(), and re-arm a per-voice fade-in (as applyVoiceFadeIn does). Better: have the chain crossfade the harmonizer wet out over 10 ms, switch, and fade back in. Test: render a sustained sine through the effects chain with the harmonizer On (interval +7). Switch the mode mid-render. Assert that the maximum |y[n]-y[n-1]| stays within the steady-state bound, and that the post-switch PV output is uncorrelated with a distinct earlier input segment.

**Evidence.** harmonizer_engine.h:616-623: `if (mode == pitchShiftMode_) return; pitchShiftMode_ = mode; for (auto& voice : voices_) { voice.pitchShifter.setMode(mode); voice.pitchShifter.reset(); }` (no sharedStft_.reset()). pitch_shift_processor.h:1242-1245: `semitoneSmoother.reset(); semitoneSmoother.setTarget(pImpl_->semitones);` (reset() zeroes current_, smoother.h:273-276). PV latency: pitch_shift_processor.h:941-944 `return kFFTSize + kHopSize;` = 4096+1024. stft.h:247 `samplesAvailable_ -= hopSize_;` (residual kept, only stft.h:166-169 reset() clears it). processor_params.cpp:727 re-applies the mode every block.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the claim through the source, and the defect is real.

1. Call path. processor_params.cpp:727 re-applies the mode on every block: `engine_.setHarmonizerPitchShiftMode(harmonizerParams_.pitchShiftMode.load(...))`. That goes through ruinae_engine.h:717 to ruinae_effects_chain.h:766-768, a bare `harmonizer_.setPitchShiftMode(static_cast<PitchMode>(std::clamp(mode,0,3)))`. The chain applies no crossfade or fade state to a mode change. The harmonizer fade machinery at lines 740-753 only runs for enable and disable.

2. harmonizer_engine.h:616-623. On a real change it does `pitchShiftMode_ = mode; for (auto& voice : voices_) { voice.pitchShifter.setMode(mode); voice.pitchShifter.reset(); }`. It does not touch fadeInGain or fadeInIncrement. Compare applyVoiceFadeIn at 705-714 and the setNumVoices fade at 582-596. It also does not reset sharedStft_, sharedAnalysisSpectrum_ or sharedPitchDetector_; only reset() at 186-191 clears those. Because fadeInGain stays 1, the per-voice accumulation loops at 351, 441 and 523 output the freshly reset shifter at full level immediately. The wet signal drops abruptly to the new shifter's start-up output.

3. Stale STFT. sharedStft_.pushSamples is only called inside the `pitchShiftMode_ == PitchMode::PhaseVocoder` branch (276). stft.h:247 `samplesAvailable_ -= hopSize_` leaves a residual of up to fftSize-1 samples, and only stft.h:166-169 reset() clears it. After PV -> other -> PV, analyze() at stft.h:226 reads `(writeIndex_ + bufSize - samplesAvailable_)`, so the first frames after re-entry splice old samples onto new ones. That is ghost audio from the last time PV was active.

4. Scoop. pitch_shift_processor.h:1242-1243 `semitoneSmoother.reset(); semitoneSmoother.setTarget(semitones)`. smoother.h:273-276 shows reset() sets current_ to 0. process() (1259-1274) and the shared-pitch path (1402-1414) then glide from 0 semitones to the target over the 10 ms smoother (1227-1228). This applies to Simple, Granular and PitchSync.

5. SimplePitchShifter::reset at pitch_shift_processor.h:444-456 zeroes the buffer and sets delay1_ = maxDelay_, so the shifter restarts from an empty buffer.

Minor inaccuracies, which do not change the defect:
- The PV path (harmonizer_engine.h:287-288) uses getSemitones() directly, so there is no scoop when switching into PV.
- Because the stale residual is roughly fftSize-hop, the first PV frame arrives after only about hop new samples, not after the full 5120-sample silence the finding states. That makes the ghost appear sooner; it does not remove it.

I found no harmonizer engine test that switches modes mid-stream and checks for discontinuities. Every setPitchShiftMode call in harmonizer_engine_test.cpp is setup before processing.

Severity medium is appropriate: a user-facing dropdown change while notes sound causes an audible click, pitch scoop and ghost audio.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. I read the code and it confirms each part of the claim, and nothing upstream guards it.

1. **Hard reset with no fade.** `harmonizer_engine.h:616-623` `setPitchShiftMode` returns early when the mode is unchanged. On a real change it calls `voice.pitchShifter.setMode(mode)` and then `voice.pitchShifter.reset()` on all four voices. It does not set `fadeInGain` or `fadeInIncrement`, and it does not crossfade.
   - Compare `setNumVoices` (`:582-595`), which re-arms a 100 ms fade-in, and `applyVoiceFadeIn` (`:705-714`), which the chain calls only on enable (`ruinae_effects_chain.h:1002-1005`).
   - The chain wrapper `ruinae_effects_chain.h:766-768` only clamps the value and forwards it.
   - `processor_params.cpp:727` re-applies the mode on every block. A host or UI change of this dropdown therefore reaches the reset directly while audio is running.

2. **Shared state left stale.** `sharedStft_.reset()`, `sharedAnalysisSpectrum_.reset()` and `sharedPitchDetector_.reset()` appear only in `HarmonizerEngine::reset()` (`:186-191`), not in `setPitchShiftMode`.
   - `sharedStft_.pushSamples` runs only when the mode is PhaseVocoder (`:236`, `:276`).
   - `stft.h:247` (`samplesAvailable_ -= hopSize_`) keeps between `fftSize - hop` and `fftSize - 1` samples as residue. Only `stft.h:166-170` `reset()` clears it.
   - `analyze` reads from `writeIndex_ - samplesAvailable_` (`stft.h:226`). So the first analysis frame after a PV, other mode, PV round trip mixes at least 3072 old samples with 1024 new ones: audio from whenever PV was last left.

3. **Pitch scoop from unison.** `PitchShiftProcessor::reset()` (`pitch_shift_processor.h:1242-1245`) calls `semitoneSmoother.reset()`, which sets `current_` to 0 (`smoother.h:273-276`), and then sets the target. That gives a glide of about 10 ms (`kSmoothTimeMs`, `:1227`) up from 0 semitones.
   - In the non-PV paths the engine feeds `setSemitones(smoothedPitch)` into `process` and `processWithSharedPitch` (`harmonizer_engine.h:407`, `:425`), and those apply the reset smoother, so the scoop happens there.
   - The PV shared path reads `getSemitones()` directly (`:287-288`), so the scoop does not apply when switching to PhaseVocoder. That part of the claim is correctly limited to Simple, Granular and PitchSync.

4. **Not documented as intentional, and the test misses it.** A comment above the artifact test (`harmonizer_engine_test.cpp:4773-4774`) itself says this reset "causes a discontinuity". The test "pitch shift mode change is click-free" (`:4775-4839`) is vacuous:
   - It measures deltas only inside `postL` (the loop starts at i=1), so it never compares the last sample before the switch with the first sample after it.
   - It switches Simple to PV, and the PV output is silent for longer than the 4-block (1024-sample) window it checks. So `maxDelta` is about 0 and the hard drop from full wet level to silence is never measured.
   - T031 (`:3905`) covers PV to Simple only for correctness, not clicks.

No setActive or prepare path, no clamp and no chain-level crossfade sits between the mode parameter and this reset. Medium severity fits: the click needs a user mode change while notes sound, but it is reliable when that happens, and the old-audio ghost is real but bounded to one frame of about 70 ms.

**Note 3.** I could not refute this finding. Every link in the claim matches the source.

(1) The mode is re-applied every block. processor_params.cpp:727 calls engine_.setHarmonizerPitchShiftMode(...) inside applyHarmonizerParams. ruinae_effects_chain.h:766-768 forwards it unchanged, with only a clamp to 0..3, to harmonizer_.setPitchShiftMode. No crossfade state or fade is armed. The harmonizer's only crossfade is the enable/disable fade at ruinae_effects_chain.h:738-753 and 998-1055. The chain re-arms applyVoiceFadeIn only through harmonizerNeedsPrime_, at 741 and 1002-1004, and that happens on enable only.

(2) On a real change, harmonizer_engine.h:616-623 calls setMode(mode) and then pitchShifter.reset() on all four voices. It does not touch fadeInGain/fadeInIncrement, sharedStft_, sharedAnalysisSpectrum_ or sharedPitchDetector_. Those are cleared only in the full reset() at 186-191. The voice fade-in is re-armed only in setNumVoices (582-596) and applyVoiceFadeIn (705-714). So fadeGain stays 1 at 351/441/523, and the old shifter's output is replaced in one sample by a freshly zeroed shifter's output. That is a step discontinuity on the order of the wet harmony amplitude, scaled by the wet level, 1/sqrt(N) and level.

(3) The pitch scoop is confirmed. pitch_shift_processor.h:1242-1243 calls semitoneSmoother.reset() and then setTarget(semitones). smoother.h:273-276 reset() sets current_ = 0. The smoother is configured at 10 ms (1227-1228), and process() advances it per sub-block from that zero (1259-1277). So in Simple and Granular modes each voice glides from 0 semitones to its interval over about 10 ms after the switch.

(4) The stale STFT is confirmed. The PV path is the only one that feeds sharedStft_ (harmonizer_engine.h:276-280). stft.h:247 leaves samplesAvailable_ in [fftSize-hop, fftSize-1] (3072 to 4095) after each analyze loop. Only stft.h:166-169 reset() clears it, and setPitchShiftMode never calls it. After a PV -> other -> PV round trip, the first analysis frame becomes ready after only 1024 new samples (canAnalyze, stft.h:213). Up to about 3/4 of that frame, read at stft.h:226, is audio from whenever PV was last active, so a ghost of old input is resynthesized at full gain. The detail that "PV goes silent for 5120 samples" is slightly off: because of the stale residual, output resumes after about one hop, and what resumes is the ghost material. This does not weaken the finding.

(5) Coverage: there is no switch-click test. Grep shows that harmonizer_engine_test.cpp and ruinae_effects_chain_test.cpp only set the mode before processing, or in a loop over fresh engines (1804, 2555). None of them switches mid-stream.

Impact: the trigger is a user or automation change of the Pitch Shift Mode dropdown while the harmonizer is enabled and notes sound. The result is an audible click from a step equal to the wet harmony amplitude, a roughly 10 ms upward chirp per harmony voice in Simple and Granular modes, and, on returning to PV, about 70-93 ms of stale audio resynthesized at full gain. The chain crossfades delay, reverb and modulation type switches, so this is inconsistent with the chain's own standard. The trigger is a discrete, infrequent control, so medium is appropriate; no change.

</details>

### R-177

**Pre-reverb soft limiter is tied to harmonizerEnabled_: it limits the whole dry mix (even with Soft Limit off), and its removal at the end of the fade-out is a block-boundary level jump**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** followup:harmonizer-wiring-and-shared-engine · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:1062-1072 (with 1049-1054; ruinae_engine.h:956-982)`

**Problem.** While harmonizerEnabled_ is true, Sigmoid::softLimit (threshold 0.85) is applied to the full left/right signal before the reverb. That signal includes the dry synth, the delay and the harmonizer's mono dry. It runs before the master gain and regardless of the user's global Soft Limit setting (softLimitEnabled_, ruinae_engine.h:979, processor_params.cpp:275). harmonizerEnabled_ is cleared inside the fade-out loop, and the limiter check runs after the loop. So the final fade block (which still contains harmonizer output at alpha > 0) is passed unlimited, and from then on the transfer curve is linear. The nonlinearity switches off abruptly at a block boundary.

**Why it is wrong.** A protection stage must not change the dry sound because an unrelated effect is enabled, must respect the user's Soft Limit switch, and must not toggle on and off as a hard step. Voices are summed without 1/sqrt(N) compensation (ruinae_engine.h:958-963), so peaks above 0.85 are normal with several voices. The comment says it is 'transparent pass-through otherwise', but with the harmonizer on it is not transparent to the dry signal either.

**Consequence.** Turning the Harmonizer on (even with Wet at -60 dB) audibly squashes a hot patch. A 1.5-peak chord is limited to about 0.98 before the master gain, so lowering Master no longer restores the dynamics, and Soft Limit = Off is silently overridden. When the harmonizer is turned off, sustained material jumps up at the end of the 10 ms fade: a 2.0 peak goes from about 0.99 to 2.0 (+6 dB) in one sample, and the reverb input (and its tail) gets louder the same way.

**Suggested fix.** Apply the protection to the harmonizer's wet contribution only, or scale it by the fade (y = mix(x, softLimit(x), harmonizerFadeAlpha_)). Alternatively drop it and rely on the engine's output limiter plus the reverb's own input handling, and honour softLimitEnabled_. Test: feed a 1.5-amplitude sine through the chain with harmonizer On, Wet -60 dB, Dry 0 dB, and compare against harmonizer Off. Assert an RMS difference below 0.1 dB, and assert no sample-to-sample step at the end of the fade-out.

**Evidence.** ruinae_effects_chain.h:1067-1071: `if (harmonizerEnabled_) { for (...) { left[i] = Sigmoid::softLimit(left[i]); right[i] = Sigmoid::softLimit(right[i]); } }` placed after the FadingOut loop that sets `harmonizerEnabled_ = false;` (:1053). core/sigmoid.h:293-301: linear below 0.85, tanh above. ruinae_engine.h:956 chain runs before master gain (:965-973) and before the user-switchable output limiter `if (softLimitEnabled_)` (:979).

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The source confirms each part of the claim.

1. **Limiter scope and gating.** In plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:1067-1072, when `harmonizerEnabled_` is true, `Sigmoid::softLimit` is applied to the whole `left`/`right` buffer. That buffer is the full chain signal after the mod slot and the delay, plus the harmonizer output, which is built from the mono sum of that signal at :1009-1012. Nothing else gates it, so it also changes the dry synth.

2. **Not a pure pass-through.** In dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/sigmoid.h:293-302, `softLimit` is linear only up to |x| = 0.85. Above that it returns `threshold + headroom*fastTanh(...)`. A 1.5 peak gives about 0.85 + 0.15*tanh(4.33), roughly 0.98, which matches the finding.

3. **It ignores the user's Soft Limit switch.** It runs inside `effectsChain_.processBlock` (ruinae_engine.h:956). That is before the master gain (:965-973) and separate from the engine's `if (softLimitEnabled_)` limiter (:979-982). So Soft Limit = Off does not turn it off, and the Master knob cannot undo the compression that already happened.

4. **The off switch is a block-boundary step.**
   - `setHarmonizerEnabled(false)` (:747-752) leaves `harmonizerEnabled_` true and starts the FadingOut state.
   - The fade loop sets `harmonizerEnabled_ = false` when alpha reaches 0 (:1050-1053).
   - The limiter check at :1067 runs after that loop. So the final fade block, whose earlier samples still carry harmonizer output, passes unlimited, while the block before it was limited.
   - The transfer curve therefore jumps from compressed to linear at a block boundary. A sustained 2.0 peak goes from about 0.99 to 2.0.
   - The reverse happens on enable: :742 sets `harmonizerEnabled_ = true` at once while alpha starts at 0, so the limiter switches fully on in the first fade-in block.

5. **The code comment is wrong.** The comment at :1062-1066 says the limiter keeps "transparent pass-through otherwise", but with the harmonizer on it changes the dry signal too, so the finding's point holds.

I found no other code path that compensates for or bypasses this. Medium severity fits: the effect is audible and changes the sound, but only when the Harmonizer is on.

**Note 2.** The code matches the claim. ruinae_effects_chain.h:1067-1072 runs Sigmoid::softLimit (core/sigmoid.h:293-302: linear up to 0.85, then 0.85 + 0.15*fastTanh) on the full left/right signal whenever harmonizerEnabled_ is true. In the FadingOut branch (:1045-1055), harmonizerEnabled_ is set to false inside the per-sample crossfade loop (:1053). The limiter check at :1067 runs after that loop, so the whole final fade block passes unlimited, including its earlier samples where alpha > 0. The block before it was limited. The same thing happens in reverse at fade-in: the setter (:739-743) sets harmonizerEnabled_=true, and the limiter then applies at full strength from the first sample of the FadingIn block. For any sustained material above 0.85 at this point (before master gain: ruinae_engine.h:956 runs the chain, :965-973 master gain, :979 the user-switchable output limiter), the limiter switches on or off as a step at a block boundary. Real hosts can reach this through the Harmonizer enable toggle, automation or a preset switch.

Part of the finding is documented, intentional design. CHANGELOG.md:247 ("inter-stage soft limiting between harmonizer and reverb prevents overdriving the reverb feedback network"), docs/ruinae_signal_flow.dot:318 and :526 (Harmonizer -> Soft Limit -> Reverb, "when harmonizer active") and the code comment at :1060-1066 all describe it. These cover the limiter acting on the whole mix while the harmonizer is on and being independent of the master Soft Limit switch (which controls only the output stage at :979). Those two points are not defects.

I found no test that pins the fade-boundary behaviour. That leaves a real defect: the limiter's transfer curve switches as a hard step, not with harmonizerFadeAlpha_. It is audible only on hot signals (above 0.85 before master gain), and the output soft limiter (on unless the user turns it off) partly masks it. The finding's 'squashes dry / ignores Soft Limit' consequences are by design, so severity is downgraded.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. ruinae_effects_chain.h:1067-1072 applies `Sigmoid::softLimit` to the full L/R bus whenever `harmonizerEnabled_` is true. Upstream that bus carries the dry voice sum and the delay output, and the harmonizer slot (998-1056) writes its own output, dry included, back into left/right. The limiter does not depend on the user's Soft Limit switch: `softLimitEnabled_` gates only the output stage at ruinae_engine.h:979-982, and that switch is a user parameter (global_params.h:30/63, default on). The chain runs at engine.h:956, before master gain (965-973). `harmonizerEnabled_` is cleared inside the fade-out loop (effects_chain.h:1053), and the limiter check comes after that loop. So the last fade block, which still holds harmonizer output at alpha > 0, passes unlimited, and every later block is linear. The nonlinearity therefore switches off at a block boundary, as the finding claims.

Transfer curve (core/sigmoid.h:293-301) and its numbers: softLimit(1.5) gives 0.85 + 0.15*tanh(4.33), about 0.9997, so the finding's "about 0.98" is slightly low but the right order. softLimit(2.0) is about 1.0. With Soft Limit Off, or with master gain below 1, a sustained 2.0 peak steps from about 1.0 to 2.0 (+6 dB) at the end of the fade, and the reverb input steps up the same way.

Quantified by setting: with the defaults (Soft Limit on, master 1.0) the output limiter follows anyway. There a 1.5 peak reads about 0.964 with the pre-reverb limiter and about 0.9997 without it, a peak difference of only about 0.3 dB, so the default-setting impact is small. The factory presets, however, often run master gain far below unity (tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp: masterGain 0.0415, 0.108, 0.17, 0.239, 0.304, 0.36, 0.516 ...), which means the pre-master sum is gain-staged hot. Many presets also set harmonizerEnabled = 1 (lines 2047, 2276, 2586, 2721, 3073, ...). In exactly those patches the pre-master limiter squashes the dry sound by several dB, and toggling the harmonizer produces the claimed step. The impact is real for shipped content, so medium severity holds.

</details>

### R-181

**Mono Priority dropdown labels are swapped against MonoMode: 'High' plays Low-note priority and 'Low' plays High-note priority**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** followup:param-pack-default-and-mapping-drift · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/mono_mode_params.h:48-51`

**Problem.** registerMonoModeParams builds the Mono Priority StringListParameter as {"Last", "High", "Low"}. handleMonoModeParamChange stores the list index unchanged (line 28-30), and Processor::applyAuxModSourceParams casts it straight to the DSP enum: engine_.setMonoPriority(static_cast&lt;MonoMode>(monoModeParams_.priority)) (processor_params.cpp:777-778). The enum is LastNote=0, LowNote=1, HighNote=2 (dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/mono_handler.h:53-57).

**Why it is wrong.** The label at index i must name the enum value at index i. Ruinae's own table, kMonoModeStrings in dropdown_mappings.h:142-145, is {"Last Note", "Low Note", "High Note"}, and MANUAL.md:261 also says 'Last, Low, or High'. The registered list is the only one in the wrong order, and it is the one the COptionMenu shows (editor.uidesc:4031-4039 has no menu-names, so the entries come from the parameter) and the one the host shows.

**Consequence.** A user who picks 'High' in mono mode gets low-note priority, and 'Low' gets high-note priority. Presets keep the enum value, so they play correctly but show the wrong label. Host automation lanes show the swapped names too.

**Suggested fix.** Register the list in enum order, {"Last", "Low", "High"}, or reuse kMonoModeStrings. Add a controller test that compares each StringListParameter entry for kMonoPriorityId with the MonoMode enumerator at that index; checkParam at controller_params_test.cpp:151 only checks the title. Add a processor test that sets kMonoPriorityId to normalized 0.5 (index 1), holds C3 and C4 in mono, and asserts that the lower note sounds.

**Evidence.** mono_mode_params.h:48-51 `createDropdownParameter(STR16("Mono Priority"), kMonoPriorityId, {STR16("Last"), STR16("High"), STR16("Low")})`; mono_handler.h:54-56 `LastNote = 0, LowNote = 1, HighNote = 2`; dropdown_mappings.h:142-145 `"Last Note", "Low Note", "High Note"`; MANUAL.md:261 'Last, Low, or High'; processor_params.cpp:777-778 `engine_.setMonoPriority(static_cast<MonoMode>(monoModeParams_.priority.load(...)))`

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The defect is real, and I confirmed each step from the source.

- **The registered labels.** At plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/mono_mode_params.h:48-51, kMonoPriorityId is registered as {"Last", "High", "Low"}. The comment at line 17 and plugin_ids.h:669 ("Last/High/Low") repeat the same wrong order.
- **The index is stored unchanged.** handleMonoModeParamChange (mono_mode_params.h:27-30) rounds the normalized value to index 0-2 and stores it as is.
- **The index is cast straight to the enum.** processor_params.cpp:777-778 does `engine_.setMonoPriority(static_cast<MonoMode>(monoModeParams_.priority.load(...)))`. ruinae_engine.h:1579-1581 passes that to monoHandler_.setMode.
- **The enum order.** mono_handler.h:54-56 defines LastNote=0, LowNote=1, HighNote=2. findWinner (mono_handler.h:463-481) picks the lowest note for LowNote and the highest for HighNote.
- **The result.** The menu entry "High" (index 1) gives LowNote, and "Low" (index 2) gives HighNote.

**Nothing relabels it.** The COptionMenu at editor.uidesc:4031-4039 has no menu-names attribute, so it shows the StringListParameter entries. formatMonoModeParam (mono_mode_params.h:62-78) only handles portamento time and returns kResultFalse for priority, so the host also sees the swapped list names.

**Every other source uses enum order.** kMonoModeStrings at dropdown_mappings.h:142-145 is {Last Note, Low Note, High Note}, and MANUAL.md:261 says "Last, Low, or High". The preset generator writes priority=2 for "High-note priority" (tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:2467, 5204, 5376) and priority=1 for "Low-note priority" (2649, 5508). Presets therefore play the intended priority but show the wrong label, as the finding says.

**No test catches it.** controller_params_test.cpp:151 only checks the title, and the ruinae_engine_test.cpp:561-563 case only checks that the call does not crash.

I kept the severity at medium. It is a user-visible inversion of behaviour against the label, but it causes no crash, no audio-safety problem and no state corruption.

**Note 2.** The defect is real. I could not find any guard or design note that explains it.

1. The registered labels are in the wrong order. plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/mono_mode_params.h:48-51 registers Mono Priority with createDropdownParameter and the list {"Last","High","Low"}. The helper at plugins/shared/src/ui/parameter_helpers.h:33-47 builds a StringListParameter and calls appendString on each entry in the order given, so list index 1 is "High" and index 2 is "Low".

2. The processor uses that list index as the enum value. handleMonoModeParamChange (mono_mode_params.h:27-30) stores round(value*2) unchanged. processor_params.cpp:777-778 then passes it through static_cast&lt;MonoMode>, and ruinae_engine.h:1579-1580 forwards it to monoHandler_.setMode. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/mono_handler.h:54-56 the enum is LastNote=0, LowNote=1, HighNote=2. So picking "High" (index 1) sets LowNote, and picking "Low" (index 2) sets HighNote.

3. Every other source uses the enum order:
   - dropdown_mappings.h:142-146 kMonoModeStrings = {"Last Note","Low Note","High Note"}. This table is defined but never used for registration; grep finds no other use.
   - The preset generator (tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:2467 `priority = 2; // High-note priority`, :2649 `priority = 1; // Low-note priority`, :5508) writes enum values. Those presets therefore play correctly but display the swapped label.
   - The only stale source is the comment at mono_mode_params.h:17 ("0-2: Last/High/Low"), which matches the wrong registration. plugin_ids.h:669 says "Last/High/Low", which fits either order.

4. Nothing overrides the menu entries. The COptionMenu at editor.uidesc:4031-4039 has no menu-names attribute, so it shows the parameter's own strings.

5. No test pins the mapping. controller_params_test.cpp:151 checks only the title. ruinae_engine_test.cpp:561-563 calls setMonoPriority(LowNote) directly and asserts only that it does not crash.

I found no clamp, remap or documented design decision that makes this intentional. Medium severity is appropriate: the user hears the opposite mode from the one selected, but nothing crashes and saved state keeps the enum value.

**Note 3.** The defect is real, and its consequence matches the claim.
- plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/mono_mode_params.h:48-51 registers Mono Priority as {"Last","High","Low"}. The struct comment at :17 and plugin_ids.h:669 ("Last/High/Low") repeat that order.
- handleMonoModeParamChange (:28-30) stores round(value*2) unchanged. processor_params.cpp:777-778 casts it straight to the enum: `static_cast<MonoMode>(monoModeParams_.priority...)`.
- dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/mono_handler.h:54-56 defines LastNote=0, LowNote=1, HighNote=2. findWinner (:467-481) returns the lowest held note for index 1 and the highest for index 2.
- The COptionMenu at editor.uidesc:4031-4039 has no menu-names, so its entries come from the StringListParameter in the wrong order.
- Ruinae's own kMonoModeStrings (dropdown_mappings.h:142-145, "Last Note","Low Note","High Note") follows enum order but is never used for this parameter. Grep finds it only at its definition.
- The preset generator writes enum indices (tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:2467 `priority = 2; // High-note priority`, :2649 `= 1; // Low-note`, :5204, :5376, :5508). So factory presets play as designed but the UI and host lane show the swapped name: a High-priority lead reads "Low".

Impact: whenever two or more keys are held in mono mode, choosing "High" in the UI or in host automation gives low-note priority and "Low" gives high-note priority. The wrong note sounds, a whole interval away, every time. No host or sample-rate setting avoids it, and Last (index 0) is unaffected.

Test coverage: controller_params_test.cpp:151 checks only the title, and ruinae_engine_test.cpp:561 calls engine.setMonoPriority(MonoMode::LowNote) directly, bypassing the parameter list. Nothing tests the label-to-enum mapping.

Severity: medium is right. This is wrong user-facing behaviour of a documented control, but not a crash, stuck note or level hazard.

</details>

### R-182

**Mixer 'Spectral Shift' knob is registered, drawn, saved and loaded but never reaches the engine, and its defaults disagree (0.5 vs 0.0)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** followup:param-pack-default-and-mapping-drift · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:305-309`

**Problem.** applyVoiceAndOscParams pushes mixer mode, position and tilt (setMixMode, setMixPosition, setMixTilt) but nothing for mixerParams_.shift. A grep for '.shift', 'MixShift' and kMixerShiftId across plugins/ruinae finds only mixer_params.h (handle/register/format/save/load/controller-load), the uidesc tag and one state round-trip test. The engine and voice have no shift setter, while SpectralMorphFilter has setSpectralShift(semitones), clamped to [-24, +24] (spectral_morph_filter.h:84-85, 429-432). The defaults also differ: the atomic is shift{0.0f} (mixer_params.h:25), the registered default is 0.5 (mixer_params.h:68-69), and the uidesc knob default-value is 0.5 (editor.uidesc:3835).

**Why it is wrong.** Every registered, visible and automatable parameter must change the sound it is labelled for. The knob is labelled 'Shift' under the Spectral Morph pad (editor.uidesc:3833-3839) and is formatted as 0-100 %, but it has no audio path. The 0.5 default suggests a bipolar control (centre = 0 st), while the stored default 0.0 would be the -24 st end of the DSP range if the knob were wired with a linear map.

**Consequence.** Turning Spectral Shift does nothing in Spectral Morph mode. Presets save and recall a value with no effect, and automating it is silent. The host shows 50 % on a fresh instance while getState saves 0.0.

**Suggested fix.** Either wire it, by adding RuinaeVoice/RuinaeEngine::setMixShift forwarding to spectralMorph_->setSpectralShift((shift*2-1)*24) and calling it in applyVoiceAndOscParams with the atomic default changed to 0.5, or remove the knob and mark the ID deprecated. Add an engine test in SpectralMorph mode that renders shift 0.25 and shift 0.75 and asserts that the spectral centroids differ.

**Evidence.** processor_params.cpp:305-309 (mixer block: setMixMode/setMixPosition/setMixTilt only); mixer_params.h:25 `std::atomic<float> shift{0.0f}`; mixer_params.h:68-69 `addParameter(STR16("Spectral Shift"), STR16("%"), 0, 0.5, ..., kMixerShiftId)`; editor.uidesc:3835 `control-tag="MixerShift" default-value="0.5"`; spectral_morph_filter.h:429 `void setSpectralShift(float semitones)`; Grep 'MixShift|kMixerShiftId|.shift' in plugins/ruinae finds no processor or engine use

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this finding. The source confirms it.
- In processor_params.cpp:305-309 the mixer block calls only engine_.setMixMode, setMixPosition and setMixTilt. Nothing reads mixerParams_.shift.
- I grepped plugins/ruinae for MixerShift, kMixerShiftId, .shift, MixShift and SpectralShift. Every hit is in one of these places:
  - plugin_ids.h:220 (the ID)
  - mixer_params.h:48-52 (handle), 68-69 (register), 91-96 (format), 104 (save), 116 (load) and 133 (load into the controller)
  - editor.uidesc:264 and 3835
  - state_roundtrip_test.cpp:191
- No file in the processor, the engine or applyPresetSnapshot uses the value.
- I grepped plugins/ruinae/src/engine for Shift. It found only setFormantShift (ruinae_voice.h:1396) and the harmonizer's setPitchShiftMode. There is no mix-shift setter in RuinaeVoice or RuinaeEngine. SpectralMorphFilter::setSpectralShift does exist, at spectral_morph_filter.h:429, but Ruinae never calls it.
- The defaults disagree as described. The atomic is `shift{0.0f}` (mixer_params.h:25), while addParameter registers a default of 0.5 (mixer_params.h:68). A fresh instance therefore shows 50% but saves 0.0. The value does not reach the audio, so this mismatch only affects what is displayed and stored.

The knob is registered, automatable, shown in the UI and saved, but it has no effect on the sound. I am keeping the severity at medium: it is a dead control, not a click, crash or audio fault.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the finding from source and could not refute it.
- processor_params.cpp:305-309 handles the mixer with only setMixMode, setMixPosition and setMixTilt. Nothing reads mixerParams_.shift.
- A grep for MixerShift|kMixerShiftId|.shift|MixShift|SpectralShift across plugins/ruinae finds only plugin_ids.h:220, mixer_params.h (handle at :48-51, register at :68-69, format at :91-96, save at :104, load at :116, controller-load at :133), the editor.uidesc tags at :264 and :3835, and state_roundtrip_test.cpp:191.
- A repo-wide grep for setSpectralShift finds callers only in dsp/tests and the DSP header itself (spectral_morph_filter.h:429). Neither the Ruinae engine nor the voice ever calls it.
- The defaults disagree as described: the atomic is `shift{0.0f}` (mixer_params.h:25), the registered default is 0.5 (mixer_params.h:68), and the uidesc ArcKnob default-value is "0.5" (editor.uidesc:3834-3836), labelled "Shift" at :3837-3839.
- It is not intentional. plugins/ruinae/MANUAL.md:223 documents Shift as working ("Spectral frequency shift — shifts all frequencies up or down by a fixed amount ... Creates inharmonic, metallic textures"), and MANUAL.md:204 shows the shift knob in the Spectral Morph container. I found no code comment, spec (specs/Ruinae.md, ruinae-roadmap, ruinae-audit/*) or deprecation marker that calls it reserved or unimplemented.
- The only test, state_roundtrip_test.cpp:191, checks that the value survives a state round-trip. It does not check the audio, so it pins the save/load bytes rather than covering the gap.
- The defect is a dead, automatable, documented control. Medium severity is appropriate.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the finding from source. In processor_params.cpp:306-309 the mixer block calls only engine_.setMixMode, setMixPosition and setMixTilt. processor.cpp:519-525 reads mixerParams_.position and .tilt for the modulated morph and tilt, but not shift. A grep of plugins/ruinae for MixerShift|kMixerShiftId|.shift|MixShift|setSpectralShift finds only these places: plugin_ids.h:220 (the ID), mixer_params.h:25/48-51/68-69/91-96/104/116/133 (atomic, handle, register, format, save, load, controller-load), editor.uidesc:264 and :3835 (the tag and a knob with default-value="0.5"), and state_roundtrip_test.cpp:191. The engine and voice have no shift setter: ruinae_engine.h:1067-1080 has setMixMode/Position/Tilt only, and ruinae_voice.h:718-734 has the same three. The DSP side exists but is never called: spectral_morph_filter.h:429 setSpectralShift(semitones) is applied at :543-544/:565-566, and spectralShift_ defaults to 0 (:796). So in Spectral Morph mode the knob, its automation and its preset value have no audible effect. The default mismatch is real too: the atomic is shift{0.0f} (mixer_params.h:25) while the registered default is 0.5 (mixer_params.h:68). On a fresh instance the controller shows 50 %, and after setComponentState it shows 0 %, because loadMixerParamsToController (:132-133) pushes the saved 0.0. Impact: this is a dead, user-visible and automatable control. It causes no audio corruption, no click and no NaN; the only cost is a misleading UI and automation. A labelled knob that does nothing fits medium for ui-wiring, so I made no severity change.

</details>

### R-183

**Chaos mod 'Depth' knob is registered, drawn, saved and loaded but never applied to the modulation output**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** followup:param-pack-default-and-mapping-drift · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:463-472`

**Problem.** applyModSourceParams forwards the chaos rate, model, sync and note value (setChaosSpeed, setChaosModel, setChaosTempoSync, setChaosNoteValue) but never chaosModParams_.depth. A grep for chaosModParams_.depth and setChaos* under plugins/ruinae/src finds no reader outside the controller display: the controller only pushes kChaosModDepthId into chaosModDisplay_->setDepth (controller_view_sync.cpp:775, controller_verify_view.cpp:750). The ModulationEngine's ChaosModSource has no depth parameter in Ruinae's path.

**Why it is wrong.** handleChaosModParamChange stores the depth (chaos_mod_params.h:32-33), and it is registered as an automatable 'Chaos Depth' % parameter (chaos_mod_params.h:53-54) with a visible knob (editor.uidesc:2167). The same defect was reported for LFO 1/2 Depth, but that report did not cover the Chaos source.

**Consequence.** The Chaos source always outputs at full scale. The Depth knob moves the drawn waveform in the mod-source display but changes nothing audible. Its default of 0 % suggests the source is off while it fully modulates every route that uses Chaos.

**Suggested fix.** Scale the Chaos source output by depth in the engine, through a ModulationEngine source-gain hook or by multiplying the chaos value before routing. Otherwise remove the knob. Add a mod_source_pipeline test that routes Chaos to the global filter cutoff and asserts that depth 0 gives zero offset and depth 1 gives a non-zero offset.

**Evidence.** processor_params.cpp:463-472 (chaos block, no depth); chaos_mod_params.h:19 `std::atomic<float> depth{0.0f}`; chaos_mod_params.h:32-33 handler stores depth; Grep `chaosModParams_\.depth` → no hits; controller_view_sync.cpp:775 `chaosModDisplay_->setDepth(...paramNorm(kChaosModDepthId))` (display only); editor.uidesc:2167 `control-tag="ChaosDepth"`

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Confirmed from source. processor_params.cpp:463-472, the Chaos block in applyModSourceParams, calls setChaosSpeed, setChaosModel, setChaosTempoSync and setChaosNoteValue. It never reads chaosModParams_.depth. A grep for chaosModParams_ under plugins/ruinae/src finds only:
- the handler call (processor_params.cpp:179)
- save and load (processor_state.cpp:42/167/333)
- the four reads at 464-470, none of which is depth.

chaos_mod_params.h stores depth at lines 19 and 32-33. It registers 'Chaos Depth' as an automatable % parameter at 53-54, formats it at 75-79, and saves and loads it at 89/98/111.

The engine has no depth setter. ruinae_engine.h:514-518 forwards only Speed, Model, TempoSync and NoteValue to globalModEngine_. In modulation_engine.h the chaos setters at 500-507 have no depth, and getRawSourceValue returns chaos_.getCurrentValue() unscaled for ModSource::Chaos (697-698). chaos_mod_source.h has no depth member; a grep for [Dd]epth finds nothing.

kChaosModDepthId is read elsewhere only in the controller (controller_view_sync.cpp:353 and 775, controller_verify_view.cpp:750), where it drives the display. No test under plugins/ruinae/tests mentions kChaosModDepthId.

So the Depth knob has no audible effect and the Chaos source always routes at full scale. Each mod-matrix route still has its own amount control, so the result is a dead control, not runaway modulation; medium severity stands. The prior specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json has no depth finding, so this is not a repeat of an F-id.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source. The Chaos Depth knob is stored, saved, loaded and drawn, but no audio-path code reads it.

1. **The forwarding block skips depth.** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:463-472` forwards the chaos rate, model, tempo sync and note value to the engine. It never forwards depth.
2. **There is no setter to forward it to.**
   - The engine's only chaos setters are `setChaosSpeed`, `setChaosModel`, `setChaosTempoSync` and `setChaosNoteValue` (`plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:514-518`). There is no `setChaosDepth`.
   - The only depth setter in `dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/modulation_engine.h` is `setRunglerDepth` (lines 550 and 557). It has no chaos depth or source-gain setter.
3. **Nothing on the audio side reads the stored value.**

   - A grep of `plugins/ruinae/src` finds no reader of `chaosModParams_.depth`. The only other users of `kChaosModDepthId` are in the controller: `controller_view_sync.cpp:353` and `:775` (`chaosModDisplay_->setDepth`, which only drives the display) and `controller_verify_view.cpp:750`.
4. **The knob is live in the editor.** `plugins/ruinae/resources/editor.uidesc:2166-2171` shows an `ArcKnob` with `control-tag="ChaosDepth"` and a "Depth" label.

**Context lens (is it intentional?):**
- `specs/_archive2_/045-plugin-shell/spec.md:351` says "LFO/Chaos depth are routed through the mod matrix and have no direct engine setter — this is by design and will be addressed in Phase 8 (mod matrix)." That note is in an archived spec and promises a later fix. The mod matrix today has amount, curve, scale, smooth and bypass per slot (`processor_params.cpp:480-494`), and no stage reads the chaos depth.
- The current user docs describe the knob as working: `plugins/ruinae/MANUAL.md:515` lists Chaos "Depth | Output intensity". So no current document records a dead knob as a design decision.
- Nothing in `specs/ruinae-audit` mentions chaos depth, so this is not a repeat of a prior F-id.
- I found no code upstream or elsewhere that applies the depth.

**Corrections to the finding's details:**
- The LFO packs no longer have a depth field: `lfo1_params.h` has no "depth" match. The aside about an LFO Depth report therefore does not describe current code. This does not affect the Chaos defect.
- "Always outputs at full scale" is accurate. Chaos still reaches its targets through the mod-matrix slot amount, so the harm is an automatable knob, shown in the editor and documented in the manual, that does nothing. The audio path is not unbounded, so medium severity stands.

**Note 3.** The defect is real. Severity stays at medium.

What the code does with Depth:
- processor_params.cpp:463-472: the Chaos Mod block calls only setChaosSpeed, setChaosModel, setChaosTempoSync and setChaosNoteValue. Nothing reads chaosModParams_.depth.
- A grep for `chaosModParams_` across plugins/ruinae/src finds only:
  - the handler call (processor_params.cpp:179)
  - the rate, type, sync and noteValue reads (processor_params.cpp:464-470)
  - save and load (processor_state.cpp:42, 167, 333)
- A grep for `Params_\.depth` in src/processor finds depth reads for flanger, chorus, phaser, trance gate and rungler (rungler at processor_params.cpp:760), but none for chaos.

The engine has nowhere to send it:
- ruinae_engine.h:514-518 exposes only Speed, Model, TempoSync and NoteValue for chaos.
- modulation_engine.h:500-507 has setChaosModel, Speed, Coupling, TempoSync and NoteValue. There is no depth or gain setter. Ruinae does not call setChaosCoupling either.

The parameter is still fully live everywhere else:

- chaos_mod_params.h:53-54 registers it as an automatable "Chaos Depth" in %, default 0.0.
- chaos_mod_params.h:89 saves it and :98 loads it.

The display scales by Depth but the audio does not:
- The controller forwards Depth only to the display (controller_view_sync.cpp:353-354 and 775).
- chaos_mod_display.h:246 multiplies the drawn output by depth_ (`... * depth_`).
- At the default Depth of 0 %, the display shows a flat line. The ModulationEngine's chaos source still feeds its full-scale value to every mod-matrix route that selects Chaos.

Impact: a misleading, dead automatable control. Any route that selects Chaos is attenuated only by the slot's amount and scale. The Depth knob has no audible effect at any setting, and its default visually suggests the source is off.

Why medium is right:
- It does not create a stuck note, NaN, or level explosion. The chaos output is bounded and the matrix amount still controls how much it modulates.
- It is a user-facing parameter that is registered, saved and automatable but does nothing.

Prior audit: I found no matching chaos-depth entry in specs/ruinae-audit, so this does not repeat an F-id.

### R-189

**Ruinae declares 'no process-context data needed' (IProcessContextRequirements = 0) while its tempo sync, arp and transport logic depend on tempo, PPQ, time signature and play state**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** high → medium · **Dimension:** followup:host-contract-tail-buses-au · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:48-65 (initialize), 245-279, 300-327, 535-537`

**Problem.** Processor inherits Steinberg::Vst::AudioEffect, which implements IProcessContextRequirements and returns processContextRequirements.flags (vstaudioeffect.cpp:182-185). That member is default-constructed to 0 (processcontextrequirements.h:32, flags{0}), and Ruinae never sets it: initialize() (processor.cpp:48-65) only adds buses, and a grep for processContextRequirements across plugins/ finds no assignment in any plugin. The factory registers the class with SDK version 'VST 3.8.1' (entry.cpp:59 kVstVersionString; vsttypes.h:27), so a 3.7+ host takes the 0 at face value. process() nevertheless reads kTempoValid/tempo (processor.cpp:245-248, 261-263), kTimeSigValid (264-267), kPlaying (268, 535-537) and kProjectTimeMusicValid/projectTimeMusic (269-275, 315-327).

**Why it is wrong.** ivstaudioprocessor.h:417-436 marks IProcessContextRequirements as [mandatory] since 3.7: 'it is now required to implement this interface and return the desired bit mask of flags which your audio effect needs. If you do not implement this interface, you may not get any information at all of the process function!' The host queries it once between initialize and setActive. Ruinae needs at least kNeedTempo | kNeedTimeSignature | kNeedProjectTimeMusic | kNeedTransportState and declares none. The SDK validator does not catch this: ProcessContextRequirementsTest (testsuite/processing/processcontextrequirements.cpp:103-135) prints ' - None' and returns true, so pluginval and validator stay green.

**Consequence.** A host that honours the flags (the interface exists so Steinberg-SDK-3.7+ hosts can strip unrequested fields; reading the code did not show which shipping hosts strip them) gives Ruinae no tempo, PPQ or play state. Then: blockCtx.tempoBPM stays at the BlockContext default of 120, so LFO, delay, trance-gate and arp sync ignore the project tempo. projectTimeMusicValid is never set, so arp grid-lock, transport-loop detection and the trance-gate PPQ sync are dead. kPlaying is never seen, so hostSupportsTransport_ stays false and the arp free-runs through transport stops. Hosts that pass the full context regardless are not affected. The same gap exists in every Krate plugin.

**Suggested fix.** In Processor::initialize() (or the constructor) set processContextRequirements.needTempo().needTimeSignature().needProjectTimeMusic().needTransportState(), adding needContinousTimeSamples / needBarPositionMusic only if a consumer reads them. Add a test in plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/processor_bus_test.cpp (or a new processor_context_test.cpp) that queries IProcessContextRequirements through FUnknownPtr on an initialized Processor and REQUIREs each of the four bits. Apply the same check to the other instrument plugins, which the grep showed have the same gap.

**Evidence.** vstaudioeffect.h:33,86-87,99: 'class AudioEffect : ... public IProcessContextRequirements', 'uint32 PLUGIN_API getProcessContextRequirements ()', 'ProcessContextRequirements processContextRequirements;'. vstaudioeffect.cpp:182-185: 'return processContextRequirements.flags;'. processcontextrequirements.h:32: 'ProcessContextRequirements (uint32 inFlags = 0) : flags (inFlags) {}'. Grep 'processContextRequirements|ProcessContextRequirements' over plugins/**/*.{h,cpp}: no matches. ivstaudioprocessor.h:422-426: '[mandatory] ... If you do not implement this interface, you may not get any information at all of the process function!'. processor.cpp:246 'kTempoValid', :264 'kTimeSigValid', :268 'kPlaying', :269 'kProjectTimeMusicValid'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I checked the claim against the code and it holds. Processor::initialize (plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:48-79) calls AudioEffect::initialize, adds the sidechain, event in/out and audio out buses and pre-allocates the skip messages. It never touches processContextRequirements. A grep for 'processContextRequirements|ProcessContextRequirements|needTempo|kNeedTempo' over plugins/ finds nothing, so neither Ruinae nor any other plugin sets the flags.

In the SDK, AudioEffect::getProcessContextRequirements returns processContextRequirements.flags (extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.cpp:182-184). That member defaults to 0 (utility/processcontextrequirements.h:32 and :141 'uint32 flags {0}'). ivstaudioprocessor.h:419-429 marks IProcessContextRequirements as [mandatory] since 3.7: 'it is now required to implement this interface and return the desired bit mask ... If you do not implement this interface, you may not get any information at all'.

process() does depend on these fields:
- kTempoValid at processor.cpp:245-247 and 261-262
- kTimeSigValid at 264-266
- kPlaying at 268, which feeds hostSupportsTransport_ at 300-310
- kProjectTimeMusicValid at 269-275, which drives transport-loop detection and arp grid-lock at 315-327

So the plugin tells the host it needs no context while depending on tempo, time signature, transport state and project music time. That breaks the mandatory 3.7 contract.

I recommend a severity downgrade, for two reasons:
1. The harm is hypothetical. The finding itself says it found no shipping host that strips unrequested fields, and with a host that sends the full context nothing goes wrong.
2. The flags have no effect inside the SDK's own code. In public.sdk/source, only vstaudioeffect, vstsinglecomponenteffect, the testsuite and hosting/pluginterfacesupport (which registers the interface) reference getProcessContextRequirements / ProcessContextRequirements. No SDK wrapper code reads the flags, so the AU build path cannot lose context through them.

The fix is cheap and correct: in initialize(), set processContextRequirements.needTempo().needTimeSignature().needProjectTimeMusic().needTransportState(). Medium severity, not high.

**Note 2.** The defect is real and I found nothing that covers it. Processor::Processor() (processor.cpp:40-42) only calls setControllerClass, and Processor::initialize() (processor.cpp:48-65) only calls AudioEffect::initialize and adds buses. A Grep for `processContextRequirements|ProcessContextRequirements|kNeedTempo|needTempo` across f:/projects/iterum/plugins returns no matches. The SDK's AudioEffect returns `processContextRequirements.flags` (vstaudioeffect.cpp:184), and that member is declared at vstaudioeffect.h:99. The plugin never sets it, so the plugin reports 0. ivstaudioprocessor.h:419-429 marks IProcessContextRequirements as `[mandatory]` since 3.7.0 and says: "If you do not implement this interface, you may not get any information at all of the process function!" The SDK's own sample does set the flag (syncdelayprocessor.cpp:39, `processContextRequirements.needTempo ();`), so this is the expected pattern and not something the SDK covers by default. process() does read the fields the claim lists: kTempoValid/tempo at processor.cpp:245-248 and 261-263, kTimeSigValid at 264-267, kPlaying at 268, and kProjectTimeMusicValid/projectTimeMusic at 269-275. It uses them for arp transport tracking (300-302), loop detection (315-321) and grid sync (325-327). A Grep over the repo's *.md/*.h/*.cpp/*.json found no plugin code, spec or comment that documents this as a design decision. Every match is inside extern/vst3sdk. Severity: I downgraded it from high. The finding itself says it could not name a shipping host that strips the context. Mainstream hosts in practice fill the full ProcessContext no matter what the flags say, so the harm is conditional on a host that honours the flags. It is a real spec non-conformance with a one-line fix, not a confirmed sync failure in a real host.

**Note 3.** The defect is real in source. processor.cpp:48-65 (initialize) calls AudioEffect::initialize and adds the four buses. Lines 67-157 only pre-allocate messages. Nothing anywhere sets processContextRequirements: a grep for processContextRequirements|ProcessContextRequirements|needTempo over plugins/ returns no matches. The SDK's AudioEffect (vstaudioeffect.h:33, :87, :93 DEF_INTERFACE, :99 member) exposes IProcessContextRequirements and returns the member's flags. That member is default-constructed to 0 (utility/processcontextrequirements.h:32). So Ruinae actively tells the host it needs no context, which is worse than not implementing the interface at all. Yet process() reads the host context: kTempoValid/tempo at processor.cpp:245-248 and 261-263, kTimeSigValid at 264-267, kPlaying at 268, and kProjectTimeMusicValid/projectTimeMusic at 269-275. The arp then uses isPlaying and projectTimeMusic for hostSupportsTransport_ (300-302), loop detection (315-321) and grid sync (325-327). The validator's ProcessContextRequirementsTest (processcontextrequirements.cpp:103-135) only lists the flags and passes, so pluginval and the validator stay green.

Impact is overstated, so I recommend a downgrade. The finding itself says it could not name a single shipping host that strips unrequested ProcessContext fields. The mainstream VST3 hosts fill the whole ProcessContext regardless of the mask, and the failure only appears in a host that honours a 0 mask. Where that does happen, the code degrades in a bounded way rather than corrupting anything or running unsafely:
- tempoBPM falls back to the BlockContext default of 120, so synced LFO, delay, gate and arp rates run at 120 BPM instead of the project tempo.
- hostSupportsTransport_ stays false, so the arp is forced to free-run (processor.cpp:308-310) instead of stopping. Notes still get their note-offs, so there are no stuck notes.
- PPQ grid-lock and loop detection are skipped because they are guarded by projectTimeMusicValid at 315 and 325.

There are no NaNs, no crash and no stuck notes. The consequence is wrong tempo sync in a hypothetical strict host. This is a real spec-conformance gap that is cheap to fix by setting needTempo, needTimeSignature, needProjectTimeMusic and needTransportState in initialize. It is not high severity without a concrete host that triggers it: low-to-medium.

</details>

### R-190

**getTailSamples() is not overridden: Ruinae reports kNoTail although reverb Freeze and delay feedback up to 1.2 give an infinite tail and release reaches 10 s**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** followup:host-contract-tail-buses-au · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.h:140-150`

**Problem.** The Processor overrides setupProcessing, setActive, process and setBusArrangements, but not getTailSamples (processor.h:140-150; grep over plugins/ruinae/src finds no getTailSamples). The SDK default applies: 'uint32 PLUGIN_API getTailSamples () SMTG_OVERRIDE { return kNoTail; }' (vstaudioeffect.h:84). Ruinae can still produce sound after the last note: reverb Freeze (reverb_params.h:20,56), delay feedback stored as value*1.2 clamped to [0,1.2] (delay_params.h:108-111; a separate finding covers that this self-sustains), amp release up to 10 000 ms (env_params.h x^3*10000), and plate/FDN decay.

**Why it is wrong.** ivstaudioprocessor.h:349-357: 'Gets tail size in samples ... This information could be used by host for offline processing, process optimization and downmix (avoiding signal cut (clicks)). It should return kNoTail when no tail, x * sampleRate when x Sec tail, kInfiniteTail when infinite tail.' The sibling plugins follow this: Iterum returns kInfiniteTail (iterum processor.h:90), and Vorago returns kInfiniteTail when freeze is on and release + RT60 otherwise (vorago processor.cpp:700-722).

**Consequence.** A VST3 host that uses the tail to stop calling process(), to end an offline render or freeze, or to schedule a downmix is told that Ruinae has no tail. That host can cut reverb, delay and long release tails, or drop a frozen reverb. AU hosts get no tail either way: AUWrapper::GetTailTime (auwrapper.mm:2112-2118) divides getTailSamples() by the sample rate, but the wrapper never overrides SupportsTail (grep found no match), so the property is not published. The hazard is latent today because process() never writes output silenceFlags (already reported), so silence-based suspension cannot trigger. Fixing that silenceFlags finding without this one would expose it.

**Suggested fix.** Add 'Steinberg::uint32 PLUGIN_API getTailSamples() override' that returns kInfiniteTail when reverb freeze is on, or when the delay is enabled with feedback >= 1.0. Otherwise return llround((ampRelease + reverb decay estimate + delay time * log(1e-3)/log(feedback)) * processSetup.sampleRate). Read the existing pack atomics, and model it on Vorago's tail_estimate.h. Tests: getTailSamples() == kInfiniteTail with Freeze on and with feedback 1.2; a finite value >= release time with defaults. Land it together with the silenceFlags fix.

**Evidence.** processor.h:140-150 lists setupProcessing/setActive/process/setBusArrangements only. vstaudioeffect.h:84 '{ return kNoTail; }'. reverb_params.h:20 'std::atomic&lt;bool> freeze{false};'. delay_params.h:110 'std::clamp(static_cast&lt;float>(value * 1.2), 0.0f, 1.2f)'. iterum processor.h:90 'getTailSamples() override { return Steinberg::Vst::kInfiniteTail; }'. vorago processor.cpp:702-703 'if (spaceParams_.freeze.load(kRelaxed) != 0) { return kInfiniteTail; }'. auwrapper.mm:2116 'tailTimeInSeconds = audioProcessor->getTailSamples () / getSampleRate ();'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this finding. The missing override is real.
- plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.h:140-150 overrides only setupProcessing, setActive, process and setBusArrangements in the IAudioProcessor section. A grep for getTailSamples|kInfiniteTail|kNoTail over plugins/ruinae finds nothing in src or tests.
- The SDK default therefore applies: extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.h:84 `uint32 PLUGIN_API getTailSamples () SMTG_OVERRIDE { return kNoTail; }`.

The sources of an infinite or long tail are real:
- reverb_params.h:20 holds the atomic `freeze{false}`, set at :56.
- delay_params.h:110 stores feedback as `std::clamp(value*1.2, 0, 1.2)`, and the comment at :24 reads "0-1.2".
- env_params.h:31 maps envelope times to `v*v*v*10000` ms, which is up to 10 s.

The sibling comparisons hold:
- iterum processor.h:90 returns kInfiniteTail.
- vorago processor.cpp:700 and disrumpo processor.cpp:1038 override getTailSamples.
- profundum processor.cpp:574 does too.

Seraphis also keeps the default, but processor.cpp:1773-1779 states the reason: its tail reporting is a deferred Phase 10 item, and it clears silenceFlags on purpose. Ruinae has no comparable rationale or comment.

As the finding itself says, the impact is mostly latent while process() never asserts silence. Hosts that use the tail for offline render or freeze can still cut freeze and feedback tails, so I left medium as stated.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source. plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.h:140-150 overrides only setupProcessing, setActive, process and setBusArrangements, plus initialize/terminate, getState/setState and notify (133-165). getTailSamples is not among them. A grep for getTailSamples|kInfiniteTail|kNoTail|TailTime over plugins/ruinae finds no match, so the SDK default AudioEffect::getTailSamples applies and returns kNoTail. The tail sources the finding names are real. delay_params.h:108-111 stores feedback as clamp(value*1.2, 0, 1.2), the finding cites reverb freeze and a release of up to 10 s, and the plate and FDN reverbs decay over time.

Nothing documents this as a design decision. Searching specs/ for "tail samples / kNoTail / infinite tail" finds hits only for Disrumpo, Iterum-freeze and Profundum, none for Ruinae. specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json mentions "tail" only in reverb crossfade and enable-toggle findings (lines 44, 76, 92), so this is new and does not repeat an F-id. The only in-repo rationale for staying on the SDK default is in Seraphis (seraphis processor.cpp:1773-1779), and it is plugin-specific and phase-deferred. That Seraphis code also clears silenceFlags so a host cannot cut its tail, and Ruinae has no equivalent: a grep for silenceFlags over plugins/ruinae/src finds no match.

The sibling plugins cited by the finding do implement it: iterum processor.h:90 returns kInfiniteTail, and vorago processor.cpp:700, profundum processor.cpp:574 and disrumpo processor.cpp:1038 override it. Disrumpo's identical gap was CONFIRMED as D-108 at medium in specs/disrumpo-audit. The finding's own note that suspension is latent while process() writes no silenceFlags is accurate and already reflected in its framing. Offline-render and freeze tail sizing in hosts that read getTailSamples is still affected, so medium stands.

**Note 3.** The defect is real, but the stated consequence is speculative today, so I recommend downgrading it from medium to low.

What I confirmed in the code:
- plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.h:124-157 declares overrides for initialize, terminate, setupProcessing, setActive, process, setBusArrangements, getState and setState. getTailSamples is not among them.
- A grep for getTailSamples, kInfiniteTail and kNoTail over plugins/ruinae finds no match. Ruinae therefore gets the SDK default from extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.h:84, `{ return kNoTail; }`.
- Ruinae can sound long after the last note:
  - Amp release reaches 10 s (env_params.h:31, `v*v*v*10000`, clamped to 10000 ms).
  - Reverb freeze exists (reverb_params.h:20 and :56).
- The sibling plugins do override it: Iterum processor.h:90 (always kInfiniteTail), Vorago processor.cpp:700-703, Disrumpo processor.cpp:1038 and Profundum processor.cpp:574.
- The SDK does consume the value: basewrapper.cpp:477 sets `_noTail(true)` when the tail is kNoTail, and auwrapper.mm:2116 divides getTailSamples() by the sample rate.
- So Ruinae breaks the IAudioProcessor contract ("kInfiniteTail when infinite tail"), and it is the only one of these synths that does not override.

Why this should be downgraded:
- A grep for silenceFlags over plugins/ruinae/src finds nothing, so process() never marks its output as silent. The finding itself says the hazard is latent for that reason.
- A VST3 host keeps calling process() for an active instrument instance, and note events wake it. No host behaviour shown here cuts Ruinae's audio today. The cut-tail scenarios (offline render length, freeze, suspending after silent input) depend on host policies, and the finding cites none it confirmed.
- The AU half carries even less weight. The finding itself says the tail property is never published (SupportsTail is not overridden), so getTailSamples() does not change anything there.
- Seraphis processor.cpp:1773-1778 also leaves getTailSamples() at the default as a recorded decision.
- The remaining value is consistency with the host contract, plus making sure a future silenceFlags fix lands together with this one.

Verdict: a real conformance gap, low severity.

</details>

### R-194

**The F002/F003 regression tests drive the switch in the reverse of the real order and count only display pointers, which hides R-129 and R-131**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium · **Dimension:** followup:asan-editor-lifecycle-probe · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/controller/mod_source_view_teardown_test.cpp:150-162`

**Problem.** The ModSourceViewMode test calls controller.setParamNormalized(kModSourceViewModeTag, ...) BEFORE modSourceSwitch->setCurrentViewIndex(i). The hook therefore nulls pointers before the new template exists, the reverse of the real attached-editor order (vst3editor.cpp:174-180, 350 and uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:273-282, where the switch happens inside the base call). It asserts only modSourceViewPointerCount() &lt;= 3, and that function counts the six displays and three sidechain labels (controller.cpp:636-648), not the ten rate/note-value groups. The MainTab test (169-197) calls notifyTabChangedForTest directly and never builds the incoming tab.

**Why it is wrong.** A lifecycle regression test must reproduce the host's event order and observe every cached pointer, or both the dangling and the over-nulling defects pass green.

**Consequence.** The suite is green while the probe measures 11 heap-use-after-free reports (R-079, R-129, R-080/R-130) and fully nulled incoming tabs (R-131).

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite these tests to (a) apply the base parameter change, perform the switch, then call Controller::setParamNormalized, matching the real order; (b) check every cached pointer against the live frame tree plus a viewWillDelete tracker (the probe's DeleteTracker/inventory), so a pointer that is neither null nor live fails; (c) assert that the visible views follow a parameter change after the switch. Run them in the ASan CI job.

**Evidence.** mod_source_view_teardown_test.cpp:154-157 (setParamNormalized, then setCurrentViewIndex) and :161 CHECK(modSourceViewPointerCount() &lt;= 3). controller.cpp:636-648 (the count excludes the groups). The probe's real-order walk of the same switch shows lfo1RateGroup_ etc. FREED and ASan heap-use-after-free at controller_view_sync.cpp:276/280/343/388/392, while this test passes.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the test against the code and VSTGUI, and the finding holds.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the finding from source. I did not run the ASan probe, so the "11 reports" figure is unverified, but the code paths behind it are real.
