That nulls the incoming views (the over-nulling). A dropdown edit made in the UI follows the same path: VST3Editor::valueChanged leads to ParameterChangeListener::performEdit and then setParamNormalized (vst3editor.cpp:226-232). In the headless harness the switch controller never registers, because switchContainerAttached never runs (the test's own comment at lines 85-91 says nothing attaches). So the test's manual "hook first, then switch" order hides this.

The assertion at test:161, CHECK(modSourceViewPointerCount() &lt;= 3), passes at 0, so it cannot catch over-nulling. modSourceViewPointerCount (controller.cpp:636-648) counts only the 6 displays and 3 sidechain labels. The groups LFO1RateGroup and the others are part of the ModSource templates (editor.uidesc:1938-1952 for ModSource_LFO1) and are cached at controller_verify_view.cpp:872-913. ### R-004

**Preset load and delay disable clear multi-megabyte delay buffers inside a single process() call (measured 0.48 ms for three delays at 192 kHz)**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** rt-safety · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:205-264, 975-993`
- **Also flagged by:** lifecycle-state, shared-dsp-contracts, prior-audit-regressions, gestalt-engine

**Problem.** applyPresetSnapshot runs on the audio thread and calls engine_.reset() (processor_state.cpp:364). That resets all 16 voices and effectsChain_.reset() (ruinae_engine.h:189-202), which in turn resets the full buffers of Digital, Tape, PingPong (prepared for 5000 ms), Granular, the Spectral delay's 4 x numBins per-bin DelayLines, both reverbs, the harmonizer and both comp-delay pairs (ruinae_effects_chain.h:206-240). The same five-delay clear also runs inside processChunk when a delay disable fade-out completes (:983-990). resetDelayType runs on every delay-type switch (:1276-1290), and both reverbs reset when the reverb fade-out completes (:1098-1099). All of this is a single synchronous memset inside one callback.

**Why it is wrong.** Clearing is allocation-free, but its cost is O(prepared buffer size), which scales with sample rate and max delay, not with block size. It has to be amortised across blocks or deferred, not done all at once inside the deadline.

**Consequence.** Measured: Digital+PingPong+Tape reset alone takes 127 us at 48 kHz and 479 us at 192 kHz. That exceeds the whole 64-sample budget at 192 kHz (333 us) before the spectral per-bin lines, the granular buffer, the reverbs, the harmonizer, the 16 voices and the normal render are counted. Every preset change, and every Delay On -> Off toggle at high sample rates and small buffers, overruns the callback and the host reports a dropout or crackle.

**Suggested fix.** Make the clears incremental. Give DelayLine/delay processors a resetIncremental(maxSamplesPerCall) that clears a bounded slice per block, keeping the slot muted until the clear is done. Or clear only the active delay type and reset the others lazily on the first block after they become active. For the disable fade-out, a delay that is muted and not processed does not need clearing until re-enable. Test: a Ruinae [performance] case in the CPU lane, prepared at 192 kHz/64, that times process() across a preset snapshot drain and a delay-disable fade completion and asserts each block stays under its real-time budget.

**Evidence.** processor_state.cpp:363-365 `engine_.reset(); arpCore_.reset();` (inside applyPresetSnapshot, called from process() via stateTransfer_.accessTransferObject_rt, processor.cpp:235-237); ruinae_effects_chain.h:212-218 digitalDelay_/tapeDelay_/pingPongDelay_/granularDelay_/spectralDelay_/reverb_/fdnReverb_.reset(); :983-990 the same five resets plus compDelay resets on fade-out completion. Microbenchmark (C:\Users\scab\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\af40cef86e602ebb\dd603f9e-da98-499f-8e1c-f00df29ba990\scratchpad\resetbench.cpp, WSL g++ -O2, prepare(sr, 512, 5000 ms)): 'sr 48000: digital+pingpong+tape reset = 127.0 us per call', 'sr 192000: digital+pingpong+tape reset = 478.8 us per call'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The finding is correct. Every link in the call path checks out in source.
- processor.cpp:235-236 drains stateTransfer_ via accessTransferObject_rt inside process() and calls applyPresetSnapshot(snap). That function then calls engine_.reset() at processor_state.cpp:364, so the reset runs on the audio thread.
- RuinaeEffectsChain::reset() (ruinae_effects_chain.h:205-264) resets every one of the five delays (:212-216), both reverbs (:217-218), the harmonizer (:226) and both comp-delay pairs (:237-240).
- DelayLine::reset() is std::fill over the whole buffer (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/delay_line.h:305-306). Its cost is O(prepared size), not O(block size).
- Digital, Tape and PingPong are prepared with kMaxDelayMs = 5000 (ruinae_effects_chain.h:88, 120-122). So at 192 kHz each line holds roughly 1M floats.
- When the delay-slot fade-out completes, the same five resets plus the comp-delay resets run synchronously inside processChunk (:982-991). The reverb fade-out completion resets both tanks the same way (:1097-1100).
- The quoted microbenchmark is real and fair: the scratchpad resetbench.cpp prepares the three delays at (sr, 512, 5000 ms), exactly as the chain does, and times reset(). Clearing about 24 MB at 192 kHz in about 0.48 ms is physically plausible.
- No prior-audit finding (findings.json) covers this, so it is new.

Severity is overstated, so I recommend a downgrade.
- The overrun is only demonstrated at 192 kHz with 64-sample buffers. At 48 kHz the three delays take 127 us. Against a 64-sample block (1.33 ms) that is about 10 %, and against 256 samples (5.3 ms) about 2 %.
- The cost is a single spike per event, not a sustained load.
- On the preset path the plugin output is already discontinuous by design, because engine_.reset() kills all voices. So "every preset change overruns" holds only in the extreme configuration.
- The Delay On->Off spike is the more user-facing case, but it is equally confined to high sample rates with tiny buffers.
- The spectral and granular reset costs were not measured.

It is a real RT-cost defect, but low rather than medium.

**Note 2.** I could not refute it. The source and the measurement both hold up.

Preset path: processor.cpp:235-237 drains stateTransfer_ inside process() and calls applyPresetSnapshot. The header comment at processor_state.cpp:295 is "Preset Snapshot Application (audio thread)". processor_state.cpp:364 calls engine_.reset(). The resulting RuinaeEffectsChain::reset() (ruinae_effects_chain.h:205-264) resets five delays (digitalDelay_, tapeDelay_, pingPongDelay_, granularDelay_, spectralDelay_), both reverbs, the harmonizer, three harmonizer scratch buffers and both compDelay pairs, all in that one call.

Delay-disable path: ruinae_effects_chain.h:982-992 resets the same five delays and both compDelay pairs in the same processChunk, once the delay fade-out reaches Off.

Each reset ends in a whole-buffer clear. DelayLine::reset() is `std::fill(buffer_.begin(), buffer_.end(), 0.0f)` (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/delay_line.h:305-309), so the cost grows with the prepared buffer size, not with the block size. The three line-based delays are prepared with kMaxDelayMs = 5000 (ruinae_effects_chain.h:88, 120-122).

The benchmark is in scratchpad/resetbench.cpp. It uses the same prepare(sr, 512, 5000.0f) setup as Ruinae, so its 127 us at 48 kHz and 479 us at 192 kHz figures fit the real configuration. 479 us is above the roughly 333 us budget of a 64-sample block at 192 kHz, before the spectral, granular, reverb and harmonizer clears are added.

None of the context lenses removes it:
- There is no deferral or incremental clear anywhere.
- setActive (processor.cpp:203-207) does its own reset, but that does not keep the snapshot path from resetting again inside process().
- No spec, prior-audit plan or code comment accepts the cost. The prior audit's implementation-plan.md:369 mentions engine_.reset() only for the flanger/chorus re-apply issue.
- The repo already treats this pattern as a defect elsewhere. feedback_ecology.h:2440-2444 and feedback_ecology_perf_test.cpp:1105-1110 removed an audio-thread DelayLine::reset() for the same reason: an O(buffer) std::fill against a chunk budget at 192 kHz.

Severity stays medium. The overrun only clearly breaks the deadline at high sample rates with small buffers, and on preset load the audio is being cut anyway. A missed deadline still makes the host drop out, though, and the delay-disable path is an ordinary user action.

**Note 3.** The mechanism holds up in the source. The impact is real only at high sample rates with small buffers, so I am downgrading it.

Confirmed in code:
- processor.cpp:235-237: process() drains stateTransfer_ and calls applyPresetSnapshot on the audio thread.
- processor_state.cpp:364: applyPresetSnapshot calls engine_.reset().
- ruinae_effects_chain.h:205-240: reset() clears all five delays, both reverbs, the harmonizer and the comp-delay pairs.
- ruinae_effects_chain.h:982-991: the same five delays and the comp delays are reset in processChunk once the delay disable fade reaches Off.
- ruinae_effects_chain.h:1098-1099: both reverbs reset when the reverb fade-out completes.
- ruinae_effects_chain.h:1161/1163: one reverb resets when a reverb crossfade completes.
- ruinae_effects_chain.h:1273-1285: resetDelayType resets one delay on a type switch.
- delay_line.h:291-309: DelayLine::prepare rounds the buffer up to nextPowerOf2(sr*maxSec + 1), and reset() is std::fill over the whole buffer.

Size check: kMaxDelayMs is 5000 (ruinae_effects_chain.h:88). At 192 kHz that is 960,000 samples, rounded up to 1,048,576 floats, or 4 MB per line. Digital, PingPong and Tape are stereo, so the three clear about 24 MB. A memset of 24 MB in about 0.48 ms (roughly 50 GB/s) matches the measurement. I read the benchmark at scratchpad\resetbench.cpp: it prepares the three delays with (sr, 512, 5000), runs 50 resets, and is consistent with the quoted 127 us / 479 us.

Why I downgrade:
1. The cost is one block, once per discrete user action: a preset load, a Delay On to Off toggle once its fade finishes, or a delay/reverb type switch. It is not a recurring per-block cost.
2. At common settings it does not overrun the deadline:
   - At 48 kHz the three-delay clear is about 127 us. Budgets are about 1333 us at 64 samples, 2667 us at 128 and 10.7 ms at 512.
   - Adding the spectral and granular delays, the reverbs and the render still leaves this well under budget.
   - An overrun needs high sample rates with small buffers: 192 kHz at 64 samples (333 us budget), roughly 192 kHz at 128 (667 us) once the other clears are counted, or 96 kHz at 32 or fewer samples.
3. On a preset load, engine_.reset() already deliberately cuts all voices and every effect tail in that same block, so the output is discontinuous anyway. A late block there mostly masks behind an intended cut.
4. The delay-disable case is the more audible one, because audio keeps flowing. It is still confined to the high-SR/small-buffer configurations above.

The finding is correct as an RT-scaling defect: O(prepared buffer) work inside one callback. The claimed consequence ("every preset change and every Delay toggle overruns the callback") applies only to niche 192 kHz/≤128-sample setups, not in general. That fits low severity better than medium.

</details>

### R-005

**Raw addresses of processor member atomics are handed to the controller, so the UI timer can read freed memory**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** rt-safety · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:101-157, 193-201`

**Problem.** initialize() packs reinterpret_cast&lt;intptr_t>(&tranceGatePlaybackStep_), &isTransportPlaying_, the six amp/filter/mod env output and stage atomics, &envVoiceActive_ and &modulatedMorphX_/Y_ as int64 into three IMessages. setActive(true) sends them once, latched forever by handshakeMessagesSent_. The controller casts them back to std::atomic&lt;T>* (controller.cpp:333-411) and dereferences them from a 30 fps CVSTGUITimer. Only Controller::terminate() nulls them (controller.cpp:251-264). Nothing tells the controller when the processor is terminated or destroyed.

**Why it is wrong.** VST3 processor and controller are separate components whose relative lifetime and termination order are host-defined. They may even live in separate address spaces (distributed or sandboxed hosts), and they must communicate through IMessage values or the DataExchange API, never through shared pointers. If a component releases the processor first while the editor timer still runs, it dereferences freed memory. The one-shot latch also means a controller that reconnects (re-instantiated controller, connect after the first activation) never receives the pointers.

**Consequence.** A possible use-after-free crash on project close or plugin removal in hosts that release the processor before the controller/editor. Trance-gate playhead, envelope displays and morph-pad animation silently stay dead after a controller reconnect. In a host that splits processor and controller across processes, the pointers are invalid and crash on first use.

**Suggested fix.** Replace the pointer handshake with values. Either use the VST3 DataExchange API (Steinberg::Vst::DataExchangeHandler, with a fallback to IMessage built on the UI thread) carrying a small POD of {step, playing, env outputs and stages, morph x/y} each block, or use hidden output parameters, which processor.cpp already uses for playheads. Test: a lifecycle test that terminates and destroys the Processor while a connected Controller with an open editor keeps ticking its timer, run under the ASan build. It reports heap-use-after-free today.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:107-112 `attrs->setInt("stepPtr", static_cast<Steinberg::int64>(reinterpret_cast<intptr_t>(&tranceGatePlaybackStep_)));`; :193-200 `if (handshakeMessagesSent_) return; ... handshakeMessagesSent_ = true;`; controller.cpp:341-343 `tranceGatePlaybackStepPtr_ = reinterpret_cast<std::atomic<int>*>(static_cast<intptr_t>(stepPtr));`; controller.cpp:251-264 terminate() is the only place these pointers are nulled.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The code does what the finding says. processor.cpp:101-157 packs reinterpret_cast&lt;intptr_t>(&member) for tranceGatePlaybackStep_, isTransportPlaying_, the six amp/filter/mod env output and stage atomics, envVoiceActive_ and modulatedMorphX_/Y_ into three pre-allocated IMessages. processor.cpp:193-201 sendOneTimeHandshakes() latches handshakeMessagesSent_ = true even when sendMessage fails. It is called from setActive(true) at :215. controller.cpp:333-411 notify() casts the int64 values back to std::atomic&lt;T>* with NOLINT(performance-no-int-to-ptr). The 33 ms CVSTGUITimer created in didOpen (controller.cpp:478-557) dereferences them with ->load. Only Controller::terminate() (controller.cpp:251-264) nulls the pointers. The controller has no disconnect() override (grep for disconnect/connect( under plugins/ruinae/src: no matches), and Processor::terminate() (processor.cpp:162-165) sends nothing to the controller.

Mitigation that lowers severity: willClose() nulls playbackPollTimer_ (controller.cpp:738), so the timer runs only while the editor is open. Steinberg's documented teardown closes the view before disconnect, terminate and release. The use-after-free therefore needs a host that frees the processor while the controller's editor stays open, or one that runs the two components in separate address spaces. Both are allowed in principle (VST3 does not guarantee that processor and controller share memory) but rare in practice. The "reconnect never receives the pointers" sub-claim also needs an unusual order: connect after the first setActive, or a new controller paired with an already-activated processor. Standard hosts connect before setupProcessing/setActive.

This is the same defect class this repo's Innexus audit already accepted (plugins/innexus/docs/audit-2026-07-implementation-plan.md WI-9, "Raw processor atomic pointers shipped to controller via IMessage", latent UAF plus an out-of-process crash). The fix there was to move the values onto the DataExchange bridge. The prior Ruinae audit (specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json) has no matching finding, so this one is new and was never fixed.

Verdict: confirmed as a real VST3 architecture violation and a latent use-after-free. A spec-compliant host does not reach the crash, so the "medium" consequence is overstated. Downgrade to low or medium-low.

**Note 2.** The defect is real. It is a design violation, not a documented decision, but the use-after-free is harder to reach than the finding says.

Confirmed in code:
- processor.cpp:101-157 packs the raw addresses of the member atomics as int64 IMessage attributes. Examples: `reinterpret_cast<intptr_t>(&tranceGatePlaybackStep_)` at :107-109, the env output and stage pointers at :121-141, and the morph pointers at :150-155.
- processor.cpp:193-201: sendOneTimeHandshakes() is latched by handshakeMessagesSent_ and is called only from setActive(true) (:215).
- controller.cpp:333-411 casts the values back to std::atomic&lt;T>* (for example :342-343) and hands the env pointers to the ADSR displays through wireEnvDisplayPlayback (:390, :925-934, controller_adsr.cpp:191-201).
- controller.cpp:251-264: Controller::terminate() is the only place the pointers are nulled. Processor::terminate() (processor.cpp:162-165) sends nothing to invalidate them.

Context check:
- No spec, manual or code comment records this as an intentional design decision. The only nearby text is the prior Ruinae plan (specs/ruinae-audit/implementation-plan.md:264), which moved the handshake to setActive and calls the atomics "lifetime-stable". That covers the processor's lifetime, not its relation to the controller.
- The repo has already classed this exact pattern as a defect elsewhere: plugins/innexus/docs/audit-2026-07-implementation-plan.md:227-234 (WI-9, medium: "latent UAF + out-of-process crash").
- The project rules (CLAUDE.md: "Use IMessage for communication. Processor must work without controller") also cut against it.

Why downgrade:
- The polling timer only exists while the editor is open. It is created at controller.cpp:478-479 and dropped at controller.cpp:738 (willClose). The ADSR displays only read the pointers while drawn.
- A use-after-free therefore needs a host that frees the processor while the editor is still open. Mainstream hosts close the editor first. Ordinary in-process hosts load both components from one module in one process.
- The "controller reconnect after first activation" scenario is not a normal VST3 host flow. The component pair is created and connected before setActive.
- So the claim holds as a latent architecture defect: the spec permits a split-process host, and teardown order is not guaranteed. A crash in common hosts is not shown, so it reads as low-medium rather than medium.

**Note 3.** The pointer handshake is real. processor.cpp:101-157 packs the addresses of member atomics (&tranceGatePlaybackStep_, &isTransportPlaying_, the six env output and stage atomics, &envVoiceActive_, &modulatedMorphX_/Y_) as int64 into three IMessages. sendOneTimeHandshakes() (processor.cpp:193-201) sends them once from setActive(true) (:215) and latches handshakeMessagesSent_ (processor.h:361). Processor overrides neither connect() nor disconnect() (grep finds none), so a controller that reconnects later never receives them again. Controller::notify (controller.cpp:333-411) casts the values back to std::atomic&lt;T>*. Only Controller::terminate() (:251-264) nulls them. Processor::terminate() (processor.cpp:162-165) sends nothing to the controller. That breaks the VST3 rule that processor and controller exchange values, never shared memory, and it would break in a host that runs the two components in separate processes.

The claimed impact is overstated, so I am downgrading it.
(1) The pointers are dereferenced only from timers that live as long as the editor. Controller::willClose (controller.cpp:738-739) resets playbackPollTimer_ and trailTimer_. The ADSRDisplay playback timer (plugins/shared/src/ui/adsr_display.h:380, :1963) belongs to the view and is destroyed with the frame. The member atomics stay valid for the processor's whole lifetime, across setActive(false) and setupProcessing. A use-after-free therefore needs a host that destroys the processor component while the plugin editor is still open. Hosts normally close the IPlugView before tearing down the components. I found no evidence of a host that does otherwise, and no test, ASan run or measurement shows one.
(2) I know of no mainstream desktop VST3 or AU host (the AU wrapper included) that puts processor and controller in different address spaces. Sandboxing hosts keep both components of one plugin in the same process.
(3) The "dead after reconnect" effect is purely cosmetic: the trance-gate playhead, the env display dots and the morph-pad animation stop moving. It does not affect audio or state, and it needs a host that re-connects or re-creates the controller after the first activation, which is uncommon.

Verdict: a real lifecycle anti-pattern. Its UAF consequence depends on an unusual host teardown order, and the reconnect consequence affects only UI animation. Low, not medium.

</details>

### R-007

**Voice mod routes are published field by field with relaxed atomics, so process() can apply a torn route**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** rt-safety · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.h:83-118`

**Problem.** AtomicVoiceModRoute::store writes 8 independent relaxed atomics: source, destination, amount, curve, smoothMs, scale, bypass, active. Processor::notify (message thread, processor_messaging.cpp:36-65) and setState (processor_state.cpp:190-211) call it while process() reads the same slot via load() in applyModRoutingParams (processor_params.cpp:517). load() can return a mix of old and new fields, for example a new destination with the old amount, or active=1 with a stale source.

**Why it is wrong.** A multi-field value shared with a real-time reader has to be published atomically, through a seqlock/version counter, a double-buffer swap or the existing RTTransferT. Per-field atomics only avoid formal UB. They do not give a consistent route.

**Consequence.** For one block a route can apply the previous route's amount to the new destination, for example a full-scale 48-semitone cutoff or 24-semitone pitch offset on the wrong target. That can be an audible blip or click when the user edits or replaces a voice route while notes sound. It is rare and transient, but it happens in normal use.

**Suggested fix.** Pack the route into one 64-bit word (source, dest, curve, scale, bypass, active plus a 16-bit quantised amount, or a separate seqlock) or guard each slot with a sequence counter that the reader retries on. Alternatively, publish all 16 routes through an RTTransferT snapshot. Test: a stress test where one thread alternates a slot between two fully different routes while process() runs, asserting that every applied route equals one of the two (expose the last applied route).

**Evidence.** processor.h:94-103 `void store(const Krate::Plugins::VoiceModRoute& r) { source.store(r.source, std::memory_order_relaxed); destination.store(...); amount.store(...); ... active.store(r.active, ...); }`; processor.h:106-116 load() reads each field separately; processor_messaging.cpp:36 and 65 `auto route = voiceRoutes_[...].load(); ... voiceRoutes_[...].store(route);` on the message thread; processor_params.cpp:517 `auto r = voiceRoutes_[static_cast<size_t>(i)].load();` on the audio thread.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The mechanism is real. I traced it as follows.

processor.h:94-103: AtomicVoiceModRoute::store writes 8 separate relaxed atomics in order: source, destination, amount, curve, smoothMs, scale, bypass, active. processor.h:106-117: load() reads them back one by one, also relaxed. Nothing makes a slot's publication atomic: no sequence counter, no swap, no RTTransferT. The comment at processor.h:79-81 only claims to remove the data race, not to give a consistent route.

Writers, both off the audio thread:
- processor_messaging.cpp:36-65. notify("VoiceModRouteUpdate") loads the slot, overwrites fields from the message, then stores it. Removal stores a default route (line 86).
- processor_state.cpp:190-210. setState stores each route read from the stream.

Reader, on the audio thread: processor_params.cpp:516-535 calls voiceRoutes_[i].load() for every slot on every apply, builds a Krate::DSP::VoiceModRoute (source, destination, amount * scaleMul), and passes it straight to engine_.setVoiceModRoute. That reaches voice.setModRoute and then modRouter_.setRoute (ruinae_engine.h:1567, ruinae_voice.h:1186). smoothMs is never forwarded, so a torn route takes effect at once.

The controller does change several fields of an already active slot in one message. controller_mod_matrix.cpp:127-141 sends all 8 fields on every route change. The route-removed callback (controller_mod_matrix.cpp:163-183) rewrites every slot with the grid's shifted-up routes, so active slot i gets the complete content of a different route. An interleaving where the audio thread reads the old destination and the new amount, or the reverse, is permitted. The fixed scales make the effect concrete: 48 st for FilterCutoff and 24 st for pitch (processor_params.cpp:505-514). The bad route lasts one block, because the next block reloads the slot.

Qualification: the writer's eight stores take nanoseconds, and the reader samples once per block. So "happens in normal use" overstates how often it happens; it is rare and transient, which fits the low severity already given.

Related, and not fixed by the per-slot fix the finding proposes: the removal re-sync rewrites slots one at a time across 16 separate notify calls (lines 164-183). Process() can therefore also see a shifted-up route duplicated in two slots for one block. This is a cross-slot tear. An RTTransferT snapshot of all 16 routes would fix both.

Not a fixed prior finding as far as the code shows. The per-field pattern is the current fix for an earlier data race and is still in place. Severity: keep it low.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect in the code. Nothing upstream guards it.
- processor.h:94-103: store() writes 8 independent relaxed atomics. processor.h:106-116: load() reads them one field at a time. There is no version counter, seqlock or snapshot.
- The comment at processor.h:79-81 only claims the code removes the formal data race ("same pattern as all other parameter packs"). It does not claim the route is read consistently, so the code does not document the tear as an intended design.
- Writers run off the audio thread. processor_messaging.cpp:36-65 (notify, VoiceModRouteUpdate) does load, merge and store(route); processor_messaging.cpp:86 handles remove; processor_state.cpp:190-211 handles setState. The reader is the audio thread at processor_params.cpp:517-535, which applies r.source, r.destination, r.amount*scale, r.active and r.bypass straight into engine_.setVoiceModRoute.
- Several fields of one slot do change in normal use. In controller_mod_matrix.cpp:149-183 the route-removed callback shifts every route up a slot and re-sends a full VoiceModRouteUpdate for each slot (lines 168-180). Slot i then takes slot i+1's entirely different source, destination and amount, and a read that lands mid-store can pair a new destination with the old amount.
- Nothing hides the torn value. dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_mod_router.h has no smoothing; its only "smooth" hit is a comment about the TranceGate value. A torn route is therefore applied unsmoothed for one block, with scales up to 48 semitones on cutoff and 24 semitones on pitch (processor_params.cpp:505-514).

Mitigating context, which is why severity stays low:
- The race window is a few nanoseconds per store, and the effect lasts one block before the next block re-reads the slot.
- The same remove-and-shift path also produces inconsistency between slots while the controller sends one message per slot. A route can appear duplicated for a block, and per-slot atomic publication alone would not cure that.
- setState also writes every other parameter pack field by field from the message thread, so a torn preset load is already accepted elsewhere.

The finding is real, rare and transient, and low is the right severity.

**Note 3.** The mechanism is real. processor.h:94-103 stores the 8 fields one at a time with relaxed ordering, and processor.h:106-117 loads them the same way. The writers run on the message thread: notify at processor_messaging.cpp:36/65, removal at :86, and setState at processor_state.cpp:190-211. The reader is applyModRoutingParams on the audio thread (processor_params.cpp:517-535), which passes each route straight to engine_.setVoiceModRoute and from there to voice.setModRoute/modRouter_.setRoute (ruinae_engine.h:1567, ruinae_voice.h:1186). Nothing gives a consistent snapshot, so the reader can see a mix of old and new fields. That part cannot be refuted.

The impact is much smaller than claimed, which is why I am downgrading.
(1) The window is a few nanoseconds: eight plain stores with no fences. The reader also touches each slot for only nanoseconds, and only once per block (1-10 ms). For one message, the chance of overlap is roughly 20 ns / 5 ms, about 1e-5 or less. "It happens in normal use" overstates that.
(2) The common edit sends the whole route (controller_mod_matrix.cpp:129-141), but only one field differs from what is stored (amount drag, destination pick, source pick). A torn read can then only produce the old or the new value of that one field, both of which are valid states. There is no "new destination with old amount" mix.
(3) Adding a route to an empty slot: the old fields are the defaults {amount 0, active 0}. A stale amount of 0 or a stale active=0 means no modulation for one block, which is harmless.
(4) The full-scale wrong-target case (48 st on cutoff, 24 st on pitch) needs a message that changes destination and amount together while the old amount is large. That happens only in the remove-and-shift resync (controller_mod_matrix.cpp:164-183) or in setState. setState already updates every other parameter pack with per-field relaxed stores while audio runs, so a one-block torn route there sits inside a preset-load transient that is already discontinuous.
(5) The glitch lasts at most one block, because the next block re-reads a consistent route. The route is also applied without per-route smoothing even on a clean change: smoothMs is not forwarded at processor_params.cpp:519-534. A legitimate destination or amount change therefore already steps at the block boundary, so the torn block adds one block of an intermediate state, not a new class of click.

Note: the more likely inconsistency is between slots. On route removal the controller sends 16 separate VoiceModRouteUpdate messages (controller_mod_matrix.cpp:164-183). Each one calls sendVoiceModRouteState (processor_messaging.cpp:68), which calls setBinary and allocates, so the shift takes microseconds to milliseconds. A block that falls inside it applies a half-shifted table: one route is duplicated in slots k and k+1, so its modulation depth doubles. The suggested per-slot seqlock or 64-bit packing would not fix that. Only publishing all 16 routes as one snapshot would, which is one of the fix's alternatives.

Real but theoretical. Severity should drop from low to info, or low/rare at best.

</details>

### R-014

**SVF Drive has a level cliff at 0 dB: drive 0 is linear, any drive > 0 hard-saturates the resonant filter output at +-1 with no makeup**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:1462-1463`

**Problem.** processActiveFilter applies `if (svfDriveDb_ > 0.0f) out = std::tanh(out * dbToGain(svfDriveDb_));`. At drive exactly 0 the SVF output (which reaches ~+29.5 dB at the cutoff for Q 30) passes unbounded; at drive 0.01 dB the same signal is squashed to |out| &lt; 1. The neutral point is produced by a branch on a float, not by a continuous law.

**Why it is wrong.** A drive control must be continuous at its bottom end (tanh(g x)/g style normalisation or a crossfade from the linear path); a threshold branch makes the first increment of the knob a large level change.

**Consequence.** On a resonant SVF patch, nudging Drive from 0 to the first step drops resonant peaks by up to ~29 dB and changes the timbre abruptly; automation through 0 clicks.

**Suggested fix.** Use a gain-compensated shaper (e.g. tanh(g*x)/g, or blend linear->tanh by drive amount) so drive 0+ equals drive 0. Test: render SVF LP Q 20 with drive 0 and 0.05 dB; require rms within 0.5 dB.

**Evidence.** ruinae_voice.h:1459-1463 `float out = filterSvf_.process(input); if (svfSlopeStages_ >= 2) out = filterSvf2_.process(out); if (svfDriveDb_ > 0.0f) out = std::tanh(out * dbToGain(svfDriveDb_));` ; setter clamps 0-24 dB at :836.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The finding is confirmed. I could not refute it.

At plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:1459-1464, processActiveFilter runs the SVF stage or stages. It then applies `if (svfDriveDb_ > 0.0f) out = std::tanh(out * dbToGain(svfDriveDb_));`. At drive 0 the output passes through linear and unbounded. At any drive above 0 the output becomes tanh(g*x) with g >= 1, and there is no makeup gain. So the change from drive 0 to drive 0+ swaps the identity for tanh(x).

That swap is a large step for any signal with |x| well above about 0.5. tanh(1) = 0.76, which is -2.4 dB. A resonant peak of 30 becomes about 1, which is about -29.5 dB.

The resonant peak is real. dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/svf.h:123 sets kMaxQ = 30, and an SVF lowpass reaches gain of about Q at the cutoff.

The cliff is reachable through normal use. The parameter is continuous: plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/filter_params.h:123-127 maps the normalized value with `value*24.0` to 0-24 dB, with no step count. Automation therefore passes through tiny positive dB values. processor_params.cpp:329 feeds the value through ruinae_engine.h:1140-1142 to every voice, and the voice setter clamps it to 0-24 at ruinae_voice.h:836.

No code path adds compensation or crossfades the linear and tanh paths. Low severity is appropriate: it is an audible level and timbre jump and an automation discontinuity, not a crash or an unbounded output.

**Note 2.** I read the code and the defect is real. Nothing upstream, no test and no design note explains or guards it.
- plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:1459-1464: in processActiveFilter, the SVF output, after the optional second stage, passes through unchanged when svfDriveDb_ == 0. When svfDriveDb_ > 0 the code computes `std::tanh(out * dbToGain(svfDriveDb_))`, with no makeup gain and no blend from the linear path.
- ruinae_voice.h:834-837: setFilterSvfDrive only clamps the value to 0-24 dB. :1712 initialises it to 0 and describes it as "0-24 dB post-filter saturation".
- plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/filter_params.h:123-127: the normalized value maps continuously as value*24. :244 registers "SVF Drive" with stepCount 0 (continuous) and kCanAutomate. Smooth automation or a small knob nudge can therefore move the drive from exactly 0 to a tiny value such as 0.01 dB.
- At that tiny value dbToGain is about 1.001, so the output becomes about tanh(x). Any SVF output above about 1 (a resonant peak) is compressed below 1, while at exactly 0 it passes untouched. The output does not change continuously as Drive leaves 0, and the size of the jump grows with the resonant peak level.
- What would have refuted it: the engine passes the value straight through (ruinae_engine.h:1140-1142 sets it on every voice) with no clamp. The editor.uidesc entries only set default-value 0.0. I found no test referencing SvfDrive. No spec, manual or code comment says Drive 0 means "off" or accepts the jump. Factory presets use 3-8 dB (tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp), so they never sit near the edge.
- Mitigation: the jump is only large when the filtered signal is hot (|x| > ~0.5). The engine's master soft limiter follows later in the chain. That keeps the impact small, so low severity is right.

**Note 3.** The defect is real. Low severity is right.

Code read:
- ruinae_voice.h:1459-1464: SVF path is `out = filterSvf_.process(input); [filterSvf2_ if 24 dB]; if (svfDriveDb_ > 0.0f) out = std::tanh(out * dbToGain(svfDriveDb_));`
- ruinae_voice.h:834-837 clamps drive to 0-24 dB.
- filter_params.h:123-127 maps normalized to drive with a continuous `value * 24.0`, and filter_params.h:244 registers the parameter with stepCount 0 (continuous, default 0). So the knob can sit at 0.001 dB, where the gain is about 1.0001 but tanh is now applied.
- ruinae_voice.h:775 clamps resonance to 0.1-30.
- svf.h:123 sets kMaxQ = 30, and svf.h:474 sets `k_ = 1.0f / q_` with no gain normalization. The TPT SVF lowpass gain at cutoff is therefore Q, which is +29.5 dB at Q 30.
- No compensation path exists, and the prior audit (specs/ruinae-audit) has no SVF-drive finding, so this is new.

Impact:
- Below about 0.5 amplitude, tanh(x) ≈ x, so the cliff only shows where the filter output is hot.
- Unresonant saw at ±1 (Gibbs peak about 1.1): tanh gives about 0.80, a drop of about 2-3 dB.
- Resonant patch with a component at cutoff: for a ±1 sine at cutoff with Q 30, the linear path outputs ±30 and the first drive step outputs about ±1, a 29.5 dB drop. The claimed "up to ~29 dB" is the extreme case but reachable.
- Saw harmonic k at cutoff has amplitude about 2/(πk), so typical resonant saw patches lose roughly 10-20 dB of peak and change timbre abruptly.
- Automating Drive across 0 switches between the linear and tanh waveforms in one sample, which produces a step and an audible click when |out| > 1.
- The final soft limiter partly masks the level difference when the linear path is already hot at the master, but not the per-voice timbre change or the click.
- Severity stays low: this is a level/timbre discontinuity, with no instability, NaN or stuck state.

The suggested fix is wrong. tanh(g·x)/g at g = 1 (drive 0+ dB) is still tanh(x) ≠ x, so it does not remove the discontinuity. The correct fix is a crossfade from the linear path to the shaper by drive amount (e.g. mix = min(1, drive/3 dB)), or a shaper that is the identity at drive 0.

</details>

### R-015

**TranceGate step length truncates the tempo product (static_cast&lt;size_t>) instead of rounding, a class the musical-time lint does not cover**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/trance_gate.h:452-462`
- **Also flagged by:** voice-signal-path, shared-dsp-contracts

**Problem.** updateStepDuration computes samplesPerStep_ = static_cast&lt;size_t>(60/tempo * beatsPerNote * sampleRate). When the exact value is an integer (e.g. 140 BPM 1/16 at 44.1 kHz = 4725, 48 kHz with many note values), the double product can land an ulp below and truncate to integer-1, and which way it lands depends on FP mode (macOS -ffast-math). syncToMusicalPosition (:346-347) already rounds, but steps between block starts use the truncated length. tools/lint-musical-time-truncation.js only matches arguments containing ppq/projectTimeMusic/stepFraction, so tempo-derived step lengths (here, ArpeggiatorCore::calculateStepDuration, BlockContext::tempoToSamples) are unguarded.

**Why it is wrong.** Per the repo rule (root CLAUDE.md, dsp/CLAUDE.md) musical time -> samples must be rounded with llround; a truncated exact-integer product loses one sample per step depending on toolchain.

**Consequence.** Free-running (transport stopped or no PPQ) trance gate drifts one sample per step against the tempo grid and may differ by a sample between Windows/Linux and macOS renders; small but it breaks cross-platform render comparisons.

**Suggested fix.** Use std::llround for both branches at :456 and :459; extend the lint's TIME_RE to tempo/secondsPerBeat products. Test: 140 BPM 1/16 at 44.1 kHz must give getSamplesPerStep() == 4725.

**Evidence.** trance_gate.h:455-456 `const double secondsPerBeat = 60.0 / tempoBPM_; samplesPerStep_ = static_cast<size_t>(secondsPerBeat * static_cast<double>(beatsPerNote) * sampleRate_);` ; :459 `samplesPerStep_ = static_cast<size_t>(sampleRate_ / static_cast<double>(clampedRate));` ; lint-musical-time-truncation.js TIME_RE `/\b\w*(?:ppq|projectTimeMusic|stepFraction)\w*\b/i`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Confirmed from source and a numeric check. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/trance_gate.h:452-463, updateStepDuration computes `samplesPerStep_ = static_cast<size_t>(secondsPerBeat * static_cast<double>(beatsPerNote) * sampleRate_)` (:456), and the free-rate branch does the same at :459. Both are truncating casts. syncToMusicalPosition (:346-347) already uses std::llround, so the file applies the repo rule in one place and not the other. The step boundary at :408 and :445 (`sampleCounter_ >= samplesPerStep_`) uses the truncated length. tools/lint-musical-time-truncation.js:31 has TIME_RE = /\b\w*(?:ppq|projectTimeMusic|stepFraction)\w*\b/i, so these tempo products are never checked.

I measured the IEEE double evaluation of 60/bpm * beats * sr in Node, across 44.1k to 192k, 40-300 BPM and straight, dotted and sixteenth note values. 102 combinations are exact integers in real arithmetic but evaluate an ulp below and truncate to integer-1. Examples: 50 BPM dotted half at 44.1k gives 79379.99999999999 (should be 79380); 63 BPM dotted at 44.1k gives 31499.999999999996; 70 BPM gives 14174.999999999998. Under the macOS -ffast-math leg the expression can be reassociated or contracted differently, so the result can differ by platform.

Correction to the finding's evidence: its own example and proposed test are wrong. 140 BPM 1/16 at 44.1 kHz evaluates to exactly 4725 in IEEE, so that test would pass today. A dotted case, such as 50 BPM 1.5 beats at 44.1k expecting 79380, is needed to make the test fail first.

Impact is limited. In Ruinae the gate re-anchors at every block start while the transport plays and projectTimeMusic is valid: plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:813-815 calls voice.syncTranceGateToMusicalPosition, which leads to ruinae_voice.h:1091 and then syncToMusicalPosition. So with the transport playing the error stays at about one sample within a block and does not add up. It only drifts one sample per step when free-running (transport stopped or no PPQ). Low severity is appropriate.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source plus an IEEE measurement. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/trance_gate.h:455-456 computes `samplesPerStep_ = static_cast<size_t>(secondsPerBeat * static_cast<double>(beatsPerNote) * sampleRate_)`, a truncating cast. The same file at :344-348 already uses std::llround in syncToMusicalPosition, and its comment cites the very hazard (an exact integer that lands an ulp below), so the truncation in updateStepDuration is an inconsistency, not a design decision. No clamp or rounding upstream corrects it.

I reproduced the as-written expression `(60/bpm) * float(beats*mod) * sr` in IEEE double, with getBeatsForNote from core/note_value.h:67-101 (float table, dotted 1.5, triplet float(0.6666666666667)). At 44.1/48/96 kHz and 60-200 BPM, 61 combinations land an ulp below an exact integer and truncate to N-1, even without fast-math. Examples: 100 BPM 1/4 dotted at 44.1 kHz gives 39689.99999999999, so the step is 39689 instead of 39690. 140 BPM 1/8 dotted gives 14174.999999999998, so 14174. 126 BPM 1/16 dotted gives 7874.999999999999. Reassociated orders that fast-math may pick (60*(1/bpm)*b*sr, (b*sr)*(60/bpm)) give a different set of hits (670 and 441 against 385 over a wider sweep), so the result also depends on the toolchain.

The finding's own example is wrong: 140 BPM 1/16 at 44.1 kHz evaluates to exactly 4725 in IEEE. The defect class is real all the same.

Reach in Ruinae: plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:813-815 resyncs every voice gate via syncToMusicalPosition only when `tranceGateEnabled_ && ctx.isPlaying && ctx.projectTimeMusicValid`. With the transport stopped (or with no valid PPQ) the gate runs free on the truncated length (trance_gate.h:407-410 and :444-447) and drifts one sample per step. While playing, the block-start resync uses the one-short samplesPerStep_ as its scale (:347) and the step wraps one sample early inside the block, so a ±1-sample jitter remains.

The only test that pins the step length (dsp/tests/unit/processors/trance_gate_test.cpp:1877, 120 BPM 1/8 = 11025) uses a value that is exact in IEEE and never exercises a dotted case. The impact is at most one sample per step, which is inaudible but breaks determinism across block sizes and platforms, so severity stays low.

**Note 3.** The truncation is real, but it is far less harmful than claimed, and the finding's own example is wrong.

Code: dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/trance_gate.h:456 has `samplesPerStep_ = static_cast<size_t>(secondsPerBeat * static_cast<double>(beatsPerNote) * sampleRate_)`, and :459 has the same cast for the free Hz rate. syncToMusicalPosition (:346-347) does use llround.

Measurement: I evaluated the same product in IEEE double with node (60/bpm, times float(beatsPerNote), times sr). Integer BPM 20-300, six sample rates and 15 note values gave 180 combinations whose exact result is an integer but which truncate one sample low. Examples: 44.1 kHz at 25 BPM and 1.5 beats gives 158759.99999999997, and at 63 BPM and 0.1875 beats gives 7874.999999999999. So the defect class exists, even on IEEE platforms. The finding's example is wrong, though. 140 BPM 1/16 at 44.1 kHz evaluates to exactly 4725, so its proposed regression test (getSamplesPerStep()==4725) already passes and would not catch anything. The affected cases are mostly dotted values at certain integer tempos.

Impact in Ruinae:
(1) Transport playing with valid PPQ. ruinae_engine.h:813-815 calls voice.syncTranceGateToMusicalPosition(ctx.projectTimeMusic) for every voice in every block (ruinae_voice.h:1090-1091 calls trance_gate.h:338). sampleCounter_ is re-derived from PPQ each block, so the error never accumulates. At most one step boundary inside a block lands one sample early, about 21 us at 48 kHz, and the next block corrects it.
(2) Free-running (transport stopped or no PPQ). Steps drift one sample each, but only for the affected tempo and note combinations. Over 16 steps that is 16 samples, about 0.36 ms against a tempo grid that has no audible reference while the transport is stopped. New voices also align to existing gates through syncTo (ruinae_engine.h:1743), so the voices stay in phase with each other. It is inaudible.
(3) The :459 Hz branch divides by a float rate, which is rarely an exact-integer case.
(4) The cross-platform consequence ("breaks cross-platform render comparisons") is not backed by any cited render or golden that depends on trance gate step lengths. The only getSamplesPerStep assertion I found is dsp/tests/unit/processors/trance_gate_test.cpp:1877 (11025, which is exact).

It does break the repo's llround rule for musical time, and the lint gap is accurate. Both are worth a one-line fix, but the audible impact is at most one sample per step, so this belongs at nit/info, below low.

</details>

### R-025

**Per-voice SpectralTilt modulation is overwritten by the engine before every poly sub-block and never reaches a spectral frame**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** voice-signal-path · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:542-551`
- **Also flagged by:** modulation, gestalt-engine

**Problem.** The voice applies tilt modulation after the block has already been processed: spectralMorph_->setSpectralTilt(mixTilt_ + offset) at :547-550, which comes after spectralMorph_->processBlock at :425. Before the next sub-block, processBlockPoly calls voices_[i].setMixTilt(modTilt) on every active voice (ruinae_engine.h:1981-1986), and setMixTilt pushes the base tilt back into the morph filter (ruinae_voice.h:734-737). In poly mode the per-voice offset is therefore always replaced before any frame uses it. In mono, 32-sample chunks run inside a 64-sample sub-block, so the offset survives for every other chunk only.

**Why it is wrong.** A routed per-voice destination must modulate the audio. Here it is a no-op in poly mode and half-applied in mono, which is block-structure dependent.

**Consequence.** The per-voice Spectral Tilt destination does nothing in poly mode. It is masked today because the UI's voice-dest index 7 is cast straight to VoiceModDest::OscALevel (processor_params.cpp:521, reported by the types inventory). Fixing that cast alone will expose a destination that still does nothing.

**Suggested fix.** Compute the tilt offset before spectralMorph_->processBlock (using the previous block's offset, as done for OscLevel) and combine it with the base inside the voice, so that the engine's per-sub-block setMixTilt(base) does not discard it. Regression test: poly engine, a per-voice route Env3 → SpectralTilt at +1, SpectralMorph mode; the output spectrum slope must differ from the unrouted case.

**Evidence.** ruinae_voice.h:547-550 `if (tiltModOffset != 0.0f && spectralMorph_) { ... spectralMorph_->setSpectralTilt(modulatedTilt); }` (after the morph processBlock at :425); ruinae_engine.h:1981-1986 `voices_[i].setMixTilt(modTilt)` before the voice loop at :2006-2018; ruinae_voice.h:737 `if (spectralMorph_) spectralMorph_->setSpectralTilt(mixTilt_);`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this finding. The poly path does what it claims.

1. The tilt offset is applied after the block is rendered. In ruinae_voice.h, spectralMorph_->processBlock runs at :425-426. The per-voice SpectralTilt offset is computed and pushed later, at :542-551, through spectralMorph_->setSpectralTilt(clamp(mixTilt_ + tiltModOffset)). The comment at :542 says so itself: "takes effect on next SpectralMorph block".

2. The engine writes the base value back before the next block. In ruinae_engine.h, processBlockPoly runs the forward block at :1980-1987 on every sub-block and for every active voice, with no condition. It calls voices_[i].setMixTilt(modTilt), where modTilt = clamp(voiceMixTilt_ + allVoiceTiltOffset*24). This comes before the voice processing loop at :2006-2018. The comment at :1948-1952 says the forward is unconditional on purpose, so a zero offset restores the base.

3. setMixTilt overwrites the morph filter's tilt. At ruinae_voice.h:734-737 it sets mixTilt_ and calls spectralMorph_->setSpectralTilt(mixTilt_).

4. The smoother does not keep the offset. In spectral_morph_filter.h:444-446, setSpectralTilt only sets spectralTilt_ and tiltSmoother_.setTarget(). The smoother only advances when a frame is processed, at :534 and :556. Between the voice's offset write and the next processBlock there is no frame, so the base target replaces the offset target before any frame sees it. Per-voice SpectralTilt is therefore a no-op in poly mode.

5. The destination exists and has a scale. processor_params.cpp:514 sets setVoiceModRouteScale(VoiceModDest::SpectralTilt, 12.0f), and :521 is the raw static_cast of r.destination that the finding cites. Whether the UI can select this destination at all is a separate issue (the cast/index mapping), and that issue is why the severity stays low.

I did not trace the mono half of the claim (every other 32-sample chunk). The poly half alone confirms the defect.

**Note 2.** The defect is confirmed from source. ruinae_voice.h:425 runs spectralMorph_->processBlock first. The per-voice tilt offset is written only after that, at :542-551, via spectralMorph_->setSpectralTilt(mixTilt_ + offset). The voice's own comment at :542 says it "takes effect on next SpectralMorph block". In SpectralMorphFilter (dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/spectral_morph_filter.h:444-446), setSpectralTilt only sets tiltSmoother_'s target. The smoother then advances once per FFT frame, inside processBlock (:534 and :556). So a target set between blocks only matters if nothing overwrites it before the next processBlock. In poly mode, ruinae_engine.h:1980-1987 calls voices_[i].setMixTilt(modTilt) on every active voice before the voice loop at :2006-2018. setMixTilt (ruinae_voice.h:734-737) writes the base tilt back with spectralMorph_->setSpectralTilt(mixTilt_). The per-voice offset is therefore always replaced before any frame reads it. In mono mode, processBlockMono resets the tilt once per sub-block (ruinae_engine.h:2071-2076) and then renders in kPortamentoChunk chunks (:2108-2125). The offset therefore survives only for the chunks after the first one in each sub-block, which depends on block structure. Nothing guards against this: no test covers VoiceModDest::SpectralTilt; only AllVoiceSpectralTilt is tested (ruinae_engine_test.cpp:1214, morph_pad_modulation_test.cpp:167). No spec or comment calls this intended. The masking claim also holds. The UI ModDestination puts SpectralTilt at index 7 (plugins/shared/src/ui/mod_matrix_types.h:47-57). VoiceModDest puts OscALevel at 7 and SpectralTilt at 9 (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_mod_types.h:50-61). processor_params.cpp:521 casts the UI index straight across. As a result, nobody can reach this defect from the host today; it is latent behind that separate cast bug. That is why "low" fits, and it is already rated low. The defect is real and is not refuted.

**Note 3.** The finding holds at engine level. It is latent from the user's side, so low severity is right.

1) Overwrite order in poly mode. processBlockPoly (ruinae_engine.h:1980-1986) calls voices_[i].setMixTilt(modTilt) on every active voice before the voice render loop (:2006-2018). It does this without any condition, and the comment at :1948-1952 explains why. RuinaeVoice::setMixTilt (ruinae_voice.h:734-737) sets mixTilt_ and calls spectralMorph_->setSpectralTilt(mixTilt_). SpectralMorphFilter::setSpectralTilt (spectral_morph_filter.h:444-446) only sets the smoother target. The smoother is read per frame inside processBlock (:534/:556). The voice morphs at ruinae_voice.h:425 and only afterwards, at :542-551, sets the target to mixTilt_ + offset. The next sub-block resets the target to base before any frame runs. So the smoother never sees the per-voice target while frames are processed, and per-voice tilt has zero audible effect in poly mode.

2) Mono mode. processBlockMono sets the base tilt once per sub-block (:2071-2076), then renders in kPortamentoChunk (32-sample) chunks (:2108-2125). Chunks after the first in a sub-block do see the modulated target, so the effect depends on block structure, as claimed.

3) No test covers this. Grepping VoiceModDest::SpectralTilt across all .h and .cpp files finds only processor_params.cpp:514 (the scale) and ruinae_voice.h:545-546.

4) Impact is latent today. The UI's voice-tab ModDestination puts SpectralTilt at index 7 (plugins/shared/src/ui/mod_matrix_types.h:47-58, :158). The DSP VoiceModDest has OscALevel=7, OscBLevel=8 and SpectralTilt=9 (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_mod_types.h:50-61). processor_params.cpp:521 casts the index straight across, so a user's "Spectral Tilt" voice route actually modulates OscALevel. No UI path currently reaches VoiceModDest::SpectralTilt. Once that mapping is fixed, the destination stays dead in poly mode because of the ordering above.

Real defect, latent, severity low: no change.

</details>

### R-026

**Idle voices freeze filter/DC/distortion state, and it replays at the next note-on on that voice**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** voice-signal-path · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:369-372, 256-271, 748-763`

**Problem.** When the amp envelope reaches Idle (output &lt; 1e-4), processBlock early-outs without advancing or clearing the filter, DC blocker, comb delay line, ladder or distortion state. noteOn deliberately does not reset them (:256-261). setFilterType/setDistortionType also activate the incoming filter or distortion with whatever state it last held (no reset at :748-763, :925-929). The leftover energy of the previous note (or of the previously used filter type) therefore resumes at the next note-on or type switch.

**Why it is wrong.** The no-reset rule exists to avoid a click when an active voice is retriggered. An idle voice has no output to stay continuous with, so its state should start clean. Otherwise a note's opening depends on unrelated earlier notes and type switches.

**Consequence.** Probe (CrossfadeMix, SVF, release 5 ms, second note with both OSC levels at 0): RMS 0.0148 (-37 dBFS re 1.0) over the first 1024 samples, where silence is correct. With a high-feedback Comb (feedback up to 0.98) or a resonant Ladder the replayed tail is much louder, and a note's onset differs depending on which voice is allocated.

**Suggested fix.** In noteOn, if the voice was idle (!ampEnv_.isActive() before gating), call resetActiveFilter(), resetActiveDistortion(), dcBlocker_.reset() and spectralMorph_->reset(). Keep the no-reset path only for retriggering a still-active voice. Also reset the incoming filter/distortion in setFilterType/setDistortionType. Regression test: note 1 with Comb Q 30, release to idle, set OSC levels to 0, note 2, then REQUIRE RMS &lt; 1e-4.

**Evidence.** ruinae_voice.h:369-372 `if (!ampEnv_.isActive()) { std::fill(output, ...); return; }`; :256-261 comment 'Snap filter coefficients ... without zeroing state'; :755-762 setFilterType applies cutoff/resonance only. Probe: `P3 mode=Crossfade ... note2(silent input) rms[0,1024)=0.01484 rms[1024,2048)=0.00357`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The source shows the behaviour the finding describes.

1. **The voice stops processing once it is idle.** ruinae_voice.h:369-372 returns zeros when `!ampEnv_.isActive()`. `isActive()` is `stage_ != Idle` (adsr_envelope.h:266), and release sets Idle once `output_ < kEnvelopeIdleThreshold` (adsr_envelope.h:355-387). So the filter, distortion and DC blocker stop advancing.
2. **The frozen state is at full level.** The VCA comes after the filter, distortion and DC blocker: `output[i] = ampEnvVal` at :539 and the multiply at :612ff. When the envelope reaches Idle, the oscillators are still running at full level, so the filter integrators, the comb delay line and the DC blocker hold that full-level signal, frozen.
3. **noteOn does not clear that state.** noteOn (:227-288) resets only the pitch mods, glide, MPE fields, voiceLfo_ and tranceGate_. It calls `setActiveFilterCutoff` and `snapActiveFilterToTarget`, which change coefficients only. The comment at :256-261 gives the reason as "the amp envelope retriggers from its current level (not zero)". For an idle voice that level is 0, so the reason does not apply there.
4. **Nothing else clears it before a new note.** `resetActiveFilter`, `resetActiveDistortion`, `dcBlocker_.reset()` and `spectralMorph_->reset()` run only from the voice's prepare() and reset() (:180-209). In ruinae_engine.h the only `voice.reset()` call is in the engine-wide reset at :191. Voice allocation does not reset voices.
5. **Type switches do not reset either.** `setFilterType` (:748-763) changes the SVF mode, cutoff and resonance only. `setDistortionType` (:925-929) changes the drive only. The incoming instance keeps whatever state it last had.
6. **No test covers this.** A grep of plugins/ruinae/tests for stale or residual filter state, or idle-to-note-on, found nothing.

The stale energy therefore comes back, scaled by the new note's rising amp envelope, however long the voice sat idle. An analog filter would have decayed during that silence. I did not re-run the probe (RMS 0.0148). The magnitude is plausible: the state is frozen at full level and released through the attack ramp, and it is larger with a high-feedback comb. Low severity is right: the effect is a transient at note onset, not a stuck note or an explosion.

**Note 2.** I could not refute it. The source confirms each step of the mechanism, and no guard, test or design note covers the idle-voice case.

1. **Idle voices keep their state.** ruinae_voice.h:369-372 returns zeros early when `!ampEnv_.isActive()`. Nothing is advanced or cleared on that path.
2. **Note-on does not clear it.** noteOn (:227-288) only does these things:
   - sets cutoff and calls `snapActiveFilterToTarget()` (:262-271). Per :1350-1367 that only snaps the SVF coefficients and is a no-op for the other filter types.
   - gates the envelopes (:274-276).
   - resets `voiceLfo_` and `tranceGate_` (:286-287).

   It never calls `resetActiveFilter()`, `resetActiveDistortion()`, `dcBlocker_.reset()` or `spectralMorph_->reset()`. Only prepare() (:184-187) and reset() (:198-204) call them.
3. **The engine never calls voice.reset() before a note.** `dispatchPolyNoteOn` (ruinae_engine.h:1730-1752) calls `voices_[i].noteOn` directly, and a Steal is handled as noteOff. The mono paths (:1806, :1875) also call noteOn directly.
4. **The design comment does not cover this case.** The comment at :256-261 justifies the no-reset rule because "the amp envelope retriggers from its current level (not zero)". That holds only for a voice that is still active. For a voice whose envelope reached Idle, the level is 0, so there is nothing to stay continuous with. The comment at :1311 ("Use only for full voice reset (e.g., stolen voice)") describes a reset the engine never actually performs.
5. **Type switches carry stale state too.** setFilterType (:748-763) and setDistortionType (:925-929) only re-apply parameters, so the incoming instance keeps whatever state it held when it was last active.

**Tests:** the existing tests (ruinae_voice_test.cpp:2264 and ruinae_engine_integration_test.cpp:1030) cover fast retrigger of an active voice. None checks a clean onset after the voice has gone idle.

**Prior audit:** this is not a repeat; specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json has no matching entry.

**The measurement:** I did not find the probe source under plugins/ruinae/tests/audit, so I could not re-check the quoted RMS of 0.0148. The value is plausible: the filter and DC-blocker state sit before the VCA, so the stale energy replays under the new attack.

**Severity:** low is right. The leftover energy is shaped by the attack envelope and normally masked by the new note's own oscillator signal. It can still colour or ring the onset, especially with a high-feedback Comb or a resonant Ladder.

**Note 3.** The mechanism is in the code. ruinae_voice.h:369-372 returns early with zeros once `!ampEnv_.isActive()`. That skips the filter (processActiveFilter at :536), the distortion (:595-609) and the DC blocker (:614), so their state stays as it was when the voice went idle. The filter and DC blocker sit before the VCA (:622-623), so that leftover state is whatever the oscillators were driving at full level when the release reached about 1e-4. It is not a decayed tail.

noteOn (:229-288) resets only the LFO and trance gate (:286-287) and snaps the filter coefficients (:262-271). The comment at :256-261 says filter state is deliberately not zeroed, but that reasoning only covers retriggering a voice that is still sounding.

setFilterType (:748-763) and setDistortionType (:925-929) also never reset the incoming filter or distortion. resetActiveFilter, resetActiveDistortion, dcBlocker_.reset and spectralMorph_->reset are called only from prepare (:184-187) and reset (:198-209). In ruinae_engine.h, voice.reset() appears only in engine reset() (:189-191). The engine never resets a voice on note-on, so nothing clears an idle voice before reuse.

On impact: the replayed state goes through the VCA (:622-623), so the new note's attack ramp scales it. With a nonzero attack it is a short, quiet transient. The claimed -37 dBFS RMS in the probe (oscillators silenced) fits that, and with normal oscillator levels it sits well under the new note. A zero attack combined with a high-feedback Comb or a resonant Ladder lets more of the stale ring through, and the onset then depends on which voice the allocator picks.

The defect is real but minor, with no stuck notes and no level explosion. Low severity fits, so no change.

</details>

### R-034

**Voice Steal Mode (Hard/Soft) is a no-op: both modes release and re-trigger the same voice slot**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:1748-1752`
- **Also flagged by:** spec-conformance

**Problem.** VoiceAllocator emits Steal (Hard) or NoteOff (Soft) for the victim, followed by NoteOn on the SAME slot. dispatchPolyNoteOn handles Steal and NoteOff identically (voices_[idx].noteOff()) and then immediately calls voices_[idx].noteOn(), which re-gates the envelope from its current level. Neither a hard cut nor a soft release overlap exists.

**Why it is wrong.** The Settings parameter 'Voice Steal' (settings_params.h:81-83, MANUAL.md:1060) promises different behaviour. Hard should silence or quickly fade the victim before the new note. Soft should let the victim release while the new note sounds, which requires a second voice, or at least a declick crossfade.

**Consequence.** The user-visible setting changes nothing. Every steal is a pitch jump at the old note's current amplitude: the oscillators and filter state carry over and the attack starts from the current level, so the new note has no attack transient.

**Suggested fix.** Implement Hard as a short (1-3 ms) fade to zero of the victim followed by the new note-on (reset the voice at the end of the fade). Implement Soft by letting the victim release in place and allocating the new note to the slot the allocator reserves (a release-overlap pool), or remove the parameter. Test: render a steal with each mode and assert the outputs differ, Hard showing a near-zero amplitude dip before the new attack.

**Evidence.** ruinae_engine.h:1748-1752 `case VoiceEvent::Type::Steal:  // a stolen voice releases like a note-off  case VoiceEvent::Type::NoteOff: { voices_[event.voiceIndex].noteOff(); break; }`; voice_allocator.h:1025-1043 Hard pushes Steal, Soft pushes NoteOff, then :1048-1066 NoteOn on the same victim slot; processor_params.cpp:772-773 `engine_.setStealMode(...)`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute the finding. The source confirms it.

1. The allocator side, dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_allocator.h. At lines 1025-1041 (single steal), Hard pushes a `VoiceEvent::Type::Steal` and Soft pushes `VoiceEvent::Type::NoteOff` for the same victim slot. The unison paths at 968-984 and 1000-1015 do the same. In both modes the victim is then put in `allocated[]`, and lines 1048-1066 push a NoteOn on that same slot. No other code reads `stealMode_`: the grep finds only the declaration at 1140, the setter at 317-318 and those three branches. The header's own documentation, lines 65-69 and 96-97, says Hard should mean "immediate silence + restart" (`hardStop()`).

2. The engine side, plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:1748-1752. `case VoiceEvent::Type::Steal:` falls through into `case VoiceEvent::Type::NoteOff: voices_[event.voiceIndex].noteOff();`, so both event types call the same function. Then the NoteOn case (1734-1746) calls `voices_[idx].noteOn(freq, vel)` on the same slot. The setter at 1609-1610 only forwards the mode to the allocator.

3. The voice, plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h. `noteOff()` (291-299) only sets the envelope gates to false. `noteOn()` (227-288) calls `gate(true)` again on all three envelopes, retriggering from the current level as its comment at 273 says. It keeps the filter state (256-271) and resets only the LFO and the trance gate. So the noteOff that runs just before noteOn in the same batch has no audible effect (at most a gate-off/gate-on flip inside one event batch). Both modes end in the same sequence of voice calls and the same output.

4. Wiring and tests. processor_params.cpp:772-773 passes the parameter to `engine_.setStealMode`. ruinae_engine_test.cpp:1038-1040 only calls `setStealMode(Hard)` and `setStealMode(Soft)` and checks no behaviour. settings_params_test only covers storing and formatting the parameter. No test asserts that the two modes produce different output.

Conclusion: the user-visible Hard/Soft "Voice Steal" setting (settings_params.h:81-83) has no effect, as the finding says. Medium severity fits: no crash and no instability, but a setting the user can see does nothing, and steals have no hard-cut declick.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the core claim in source: Voice Steal Mode does nothing. The finding's account of what a steal sounds like is partly wrong, though. That behaviour is a deliberate anti-click choice, so I recommend downgrading.

The two modes produce identical calls on the same voice:
- dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_allocator.h:1025-1043 (single-voice steal) and :966-1016 (unison) push Steal when stealMode_==Hard and NoteOff when Soft. Lines 1042 and 1048-1066 then push a NoteOn on the same victim slot in the same event batch.
- plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:1748-1752 handles Steal and NoteOff with the same case body, `voices_[event.voiceIndex].noteOff();`. The NoteOn case at :1734-1738 then calls `voices_[idx].noteOn()` in the same loop, with no audio rendered in between.
- ruinae_voice.h:291-299 noteOff() only does gate(false). noteOn() at :273-276 does gate(true) "retrigger from current level", so the gate(false) is overwritten at once. Hard and Soft therefore make the same calls in the same order and render the same audio.
- The allocator's own documentation (voice_allocator.h:65-69, 96-97, 107) says Steal means "immediate silence + restart / hardStop". Ruinae ignores that meaning.

Nothing guards against this or documents it:
- specs/ruinae-audit, Ruinae.md and ruinae-roadmap.md have no 'steal' hits, so this is not a repeat of an earlier F-id and not a recorded design decision.
- The only engine test, ruinae_engine_test.cpp:1038-1040, checks that the setter can be called. It does not compare the audio of the two modes.
- settings_params_test.cpp checks only storage and formatting.
- The parameter is exposed in the UI (plugin_ids.h:754, editor.uidesc:4405-4413), saved in state (settings_params.h:121/131) and applied at processor_params.cpp:772-773. It is a user-visible control with no effect.
- MANUAL.md:1060 also describes it wrongly ("Which voice is stolen"), which is what allocation mode controls.

Why downgrade:
- The finding says every steal has "no attack transient", implying a defect. That is the intended behaviour, documented at ruinae_voice.h:256-260 and :273: the envelope retriggers from its current level and the filter state is kept on purpose to avoid a click on steal.
- From its current level, the envelope still rises toward its attack peak, so the transient is reduced, not gone.
- The real defect is a dead setting plus misleading docs, not an audible fault in the default behaviour. That points to low severity rather than medium.

**Note 3.** The defect is real: the Voice Steal setting has no audible effect. The consequence is overstated, so I recommend downgrading the severity to low.

Confirmed from source:
- The allocator sends a different event per mode, then the same follow-up. In the single-voice path, voice_allocator.h:1025-1041 pushes `Steal` for Hard and `NoteOff` for Soft. Then :1042-1043 assigns the same victim slot, and :1048-1066 pushes `NoteOn` for that slot in the same event batch. The unison paths do the same (:966-987 and :1000-1016).
- The engine treats both events alike. ruinae_engine.h:1748-1752 sends `Steal` and `NoteOff` to the same case, `voices_[event.voiceIndex].noteOff()`. Then the `NoteOn` case (:1734-1746) calls `voices_[idx].noteOn()` on the same slot, inside the same loop and the same sample.
- The release never runs. `RuinaeVoice::noteOff()` (ruinae_voice.h:291-299) only calls gate(false). `noteOn()` (:227-288) calls gate(true) on all three envelopes at :274-276 before any sample is rendered. So the Soft release is cut off in zero samples.
- Hard does not silence the voice either. Nothing calls `RuinaeVoice::reset()` (:198-220). That contradicts the allocator's own documentation at voice_allocator.h:65-69 and :107 ("silence + restart").
- The parameter is passed through but goes nowhere. processor_params.cpp:772-773 calls `engine_.setStealMode`. ruinae_engine.h:1609-1610 forwards it only to the allocator, whose two event types the engine then handles the same way.
- No test checks that the modes sound different. ruinae_engine_test.cpp:1038-1040 only calls `setStealMode(Hard)` and then `setStealMode(Soft)`, with no audio assertion.
- This is not a repeat of a prior finding. The only steal-related prior finding (findings.json:28, unison slot reuse) is a different bug.

Why the severity should drop:
1. The claim that "the new note has no attack transient" is overstated. adsr_envelope.h:86-90 `gate(true)` with Hard retrigger calls `enterAttack()`, and :451-460 starts the attack from the current `output_` and ramps it to the peak. A stolen voice in sustain or release therefore still gets an attack ramp up to the new velocity's peak. What is lost is the dip to zero, not the attack itself.
2. Today's behaviour, used for both modes, is click-safe by design. ruinae_voice.h:256-261 snaps the filter without clearing it, and the envelope continues from its current level. Taken alone, neither mode produces a click or a level error. The cost is a design-intent gap: Hard never gives a declicked hard cut and Soft never gives a release overlap. It is not an audible artifact.
3. The harm is a dead Settings parameter (settings_params.h:81-83, MANUAL.md:1060). A user can switch it and hear nothing change. That is a real spec and UI-conformance defect, but it does not damage output, so low fits better than medium.

</details>

### R-036

**Every note-expression event splits the render into a new engine segment, including types the engine ignores**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_midi.cpp:238-242`

**Problem.** onNoteExpression queues every kNoteExpressionValueEvent as a TimedEvent. renderEngineSegments then ends the current segment at its offset and makes a full engine_.processBlock call: global mod engine, all active voices, the whole effects chain, and a trance-gate sync loop over 16 voices. RuinaeEngine::setNoteExpression handles only typeIds 0, 2 and 5 and drops pan (1) and all others. The queue holds 1024 events; on overflow everything is applied at sample 0.

**Why it is wrong.** Events with no effect should not cost a render split. A continuous MPE stream (several dimensions per note at about 1 kHz) should not multiply the per-buffer fixed cost of the engine or overflow the queue and collapse note timing.

**Consequence.** MPE controllers sending pan, timbre or custom expressions cause hundreds of tiny segments per buffer (a CPU spike), and in large buffers queue overflow loses sample-accurate note timing.

**Suggested fix.** Filter in onNoteExpression (queue only typeIds the engine consumes). Optionally coalesce consecutive expression or bend events for the same noteId and type within a few samples. Test: 500 pan-expression events in one buffer produce exactly one engine processBlock call (count via a test hook).

**Evidence.** processor_midi.cpp:240-241 `queueTimedEvent({.offset = currentEventOffset_, .kind = TimedEventKind::Expression, ...});`; :126-146 segment split at each queued offset; ruinae_engine.h:334-348 `switch (typeId) { case 2 ... case 0 ... case 5 ... default: break; }`; processor_midi.cpp:71-77 overflow flush.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The finding is correct. I traced it in the source.

1. plugins/shared/src/midi/midi_event_dispatcher.h:137-146 passes every kNoteExpressionValueEvent to handler.onNoteExpression(noteId, typeId, value). It does not filter by type.
2. processor_midi.cpp:238-242 (onNoteExpression) queues every one of them as TimedEventKind::Expression at currentEventOffset_. It does not filter by typeId either. processEvents (lines 59-66) sets the offset for each event.
3. renderEngineSegments (processor_midi.cpp:120-152) ends a segment at each distinct queued offset. For each segment it calls engine_.setBlockContext, then setSidechainInput, then the full engine_.processBlock (left+pos, right+pos, end-pos). processBlock (ruinae_engine.h:783 on) does the whole fixed per-call work. So an expression at a new offset costs one extra engine call, whatever its type.
4. RuinaeEngine::setNoteExpression (ruinae_engine.h:328-349) returns early if no voice has that noteId. Otherwise it acts only on typeId 2 (tuning), 0 (volume) and 5 (brightness); pan (1) and every other type fall to `default: break`. Pan and custom expressions therefore buy a segment split and change nothing.
5. On overflow, kMaxTimedEvents = 1024 (processor.h:215). queueTimedEvent (processor_midi.cpp:70-78) then flushes everything queued so far and applies the new event at once, so those events lose their sample offsets.

Caveats, none of which refute the defect:
- Ruinae's controller does not implement INoteExpressionController (a grep for getNoteExpressionCount / INoteExpressionController in plugins/ruinae/src finds nothing). Hosts that honour that interface may send few or no expression events, so this matters only for hosts that send them anyway.
- "Hundreds of segments per buffer" overstates typical buffers. A 512-sample buffer at 48 kHz with one dimension at 1 kHz gives about 10 splits per note and dimension. Overflow needs very large buffers or very dense streams.
- Splitting at consumed expressions is deliberate, for sample accuracy.

The narrow claim stands: type IDs the engine never reads, and noteIds with no voice, still force a full engine segment and take queue slots, and filtering them out first is cheap. Low severity is appropriate.

**Note 2.** I read the code and the mechanics the finding describes are real. I found nothing that guards against them.

1. Every expression event is queued with no filter. processor_midi.cpp:238-242: onNoteExpression calls queueTimedEvent with kind Expression for every typeId. The shared dispatcher passes all kNoteExpressionValueEvent types through without filtering (plugins/shared/src/midi/midi_event_dispatcher.h:137-147). The only comment, at :239, explains the queueing as keeping order after a note-on. It does not say why ignored types should be queued.

2. Each distinct event offset ends a segment. renderEngineSegments (:125-147) finishes the current segment at timedEvents_[next].offset and makes one full engine_.processBlock call per segment.
