### R-125

**Factory-preset audio test never releases the note and ignores clipping, DC and NaN**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/factory_preset_audio_test.cpp:114-222, 252-316`

**Problem.** renderPresetLevels sends one note-on and never a note-off, so no preset is checked for running down to silence (voices that never go idle, feedback delay or granular or phaser self-oscillation, reverb freeze, self-oscillating filter). The peak is accumulated with std::max(peak, std::abs(l)), and std::max(peak, NaN) returns peak, so NaN is invisible (the engine flush hides it anyway). There is no upper bound: a preset driving the soft limiter into constant saturation, or carrying DC, passes. Only 'audible' (> -60 dBFS) and 'not 20 dB under the median' are asserted.

**Why it is wrong.** Rendering every factory preset is the cheapest way to catch level explosions, self-oscillation with no note held, and stuck tails, all of which are on the synthesizer hazard list. The rendering already exists; only the assertions are missing.

**Consequence.** A preset that rings forever after release, sits at the limiter ceiling, or carries large DC ships unnoticed.

**Suggested fix.** Extend renderPresetLevels to send a note-off at 3 s and render 10 s more. Add assertions (CHECK per preset): (a) RMS of the last 1 s &lt; -80 dBFS, except presets flagged as intentionally infinite (freeze or latch) in a small allow-list; (b) peak &lt; 0.99 and the fraction of samples above 0.85 (limiter knee) &lt; 1%; (c) |mean| over the sustained window &lt; 0.01; (d) count non-finite samples with detail::isFinite on a pre-flush tap, or at least on the output. Tag the extended render [long] if it exceeds the per-push budget.

**Evidence.** factory_preset_audio_test.cpp:158 'inEvents.addNoteOn(60, 0.8f, 0);' with no note-off anywhere; :194-195 'peak = std::max(peak, std::abs(l));'; :264 'REQUIRE(levels.peak > kAudibleThreshold);' is the only per-preset assertion.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I read the whole of plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/factory_preset_audio_test.cpp, and every factual claim in the finding holds.
- TestEventList (lines 51-76) only has an addNoteOn helper. renderPresetLevels sends `inEvents.addNoteOn(60, 0.8f, 0)` at :158, clears the event list after every block (:205), and never sends a note-off. A preset is therefore never checked for decaying to silence after release.
- The peak is accumulated at :194-195 with `peak = std::max(peak, std::abs(l/r))`. std::max(a, b) returns `(a < b) ? b : a`, so when b is NaN, `peak < NaN` is false and peak comes back unchanged. A NaN sample is invisible to this test.
- No test asserts an upper bound, DC or finiteness. The only per-preset assertions are `REQUIRE(levels.loaded)` and `REQUIRE(levels.peak > kAudibleThreshold)` at :263-264, plus the bank-relative floor `CHECK(db > medianDb - 20)` at :314. The struct also computes sustainedRms (:218-220), but nothing asserts on it.

I looked for coverage elsewhere. Six other test files load .vstpreset files. The four integration files are per-preset tests:
- euclidean_bells_level_test.cpp:241 and cathedral_organ_envelope_test.cpp:249/270 send note-offs, each for one preset.
- chaos_wind_audio_test.cpp:90 checks NaN for one preset, using std::isnan.
- abyssal_level_test.cpp is about the level of one preset.

The other two test files (preset_browser_test.cpp and ruinae_byte_identical_post_lane10_test.cpp) also refer to presets, but neither renders audio after a note-off. Nothing runs the whole factory bank through note-off and checks that it decays, or checks clipping, DC or NaN across all presets. The gap is real.

I am downgrading severity because this is a missing assertion, not a defect in shipping code. The finding names no preset that actually rings forever, clips or carries DC; that consequence is hypothetical. The finding itself also notes that the engine flushes NaN/Inf before the output, so the NaN part only matters for a pre-flush tap. A coverage gap with no demonstrated failing preset fits low better than medium.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the finding from source. plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/factory_preset_audio_test.cpp:63-72 has only an addNoteOn helper. The test sends one note-on at :158, then clears inEvents every block (:205). No note-off is ever sent, so no preset is rendered past release. The peak is accumulated at :194-195 with std::max(peak, std::abs(l)). std::max(a, b) returns (a &lt; b) ? b : a, and peak &lt; NaN is false, so a NaN sample is dropped without a trace. The only assertions are REQUIRE(levels.loaded) and REQUIRE(levels.peak > kAudibleThreshold) at :263-264, plus the [long] median-outlier floor CHECK(db > medianDb - 20) at :314. There is no upper bound, no DC check and no tail-to-silence check. sustainedRms is computed at :218 but no test asserts it.

I looked for another test that covers this and found none. The only other test that enumerates the factory presets is ruinae_byte_identical_post_lane10_test.cpp:501 (recursive_directory_iterator). Per the architecture facts it pins arp MIDI bytes, not audio tails. preset_switch_safety_test.cpp (:161, :396) checks finite output during preset switching, not a release run per factory preset. The file header (:4-11) limits this test to audibility on purpose. That explains why the assertions are missing, but it does not close the gap. No spec or roadmap rule says factory presets are exempt from tail or level checks.

Two points weaken the finding. First, the engine already flushes NaN/Inf to zero before output, so on the output tap the NaN half of the claim matters little; catching it would need a pre-flush tap, as the suggested fix notes. Second, this is a missing test, not a shipping defect: no preset is shown to ring forever, clip or carry DC. I therefore downgrade it from medium to low.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/factory_preset_audio_test.cpp:158 sends `inEvents.addNoteOn(60, 0.8f, 0);`. The event list has no addNoteOff helper (:63-73), and inEvents is only cleared after the first block (:205), so the note is held for the whole 6 s render (:45, :160-161) and never released. Peak is accumulated with `std::max(peak, std::abs(l))` at :194-195, which ignores a NaN in the second argument. Even so, NaN cannot reach the output: ruinae_engine.h:984-990 flushes NaN/Inf to zero after the soft limiter (:979-981). So the NaN half of the claim only matters on a pre-flush tap, and the finding admits this. sustainedRms is computed (:197-201, :218-220) but never asserted. The only per-preset checks are `REQUIRE(levels.loaded)` and `REQUIRE(levels.peak > kAudibleThreshold)` at :263-264. The loudness-outlier case (:314) is a lower bound only, and it is tagged [long] at :270, so per-push CI never runs it. No other test renders factory-preset audio. The only other preset enumerator is ruinae_byte_identical_post_lane10_test.cpp:492, which covers arp presets and MIDI bytes, not audio tails, DC or limiter saturation. So the coverage gap is real. On impact: this is a test gap, not a demonstrated defect. The finding names no factory preset that rings after release, runs at the limiter ceiling or carries DC, and none was measured. The output can never be NaN because of the engine flush, and Sigmoid::softLimit bounds the level. The consequence is a missing safety net with no observed failure, so it is downgraded from medium to low.

</details>

### R-126

**Sidechain input path is never exercised by any test**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/tests/integration/mod_source_pipeline_test.cpp:(whole suite: every ProcessData uses numInputs = 0)`

**Problem.** Grepping plugins/ruinae/tests for numInputs set to 1 or more finds no match. Every processor test passes numInputs = 0, so the sidechain extraction branch (stereo, mono duplicated, null channel pointers) at processor.cpp:471-489, the per-segment sidechain pointer offset in renderEngineSegments, and the kSidechainActiveId change-only output (:491-504) are untested. EnvFollower, PitchFollower and Transient are only ever tested against self-analysis of previousOutput.

**Why it is wrong.** The sidechain is a declared bus and the main input for three mod sources. Mono duplication, segment pointer arithmetic (ptr+pos) and the switch away from transient-from-velocity when a sidechain is present are logic that can break silently.

**Consequence.** A sidechain regression (wrong channel, off-by-segment pointer, transient detection never re-enabled) would ship.

**Suggested fix.** Add Processor_Sidechain_StereoDrivesEnvFollower: route EnvFollower→GlobalFilterCutoff, feed a 1 kHz burst on input bus 0, and REQUIRE that the output spectral centroid rises during the burst. Add Processor_Sidechain_MonoBusDuplicated (numChannels=1). Add Processor_Sidechain_SegmentOffsetsAligned (note events splitting the block). Add Processor_SidechainActiveParam_WrittenOnFirstBlockAndOnChange.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:475-488 'if (data.numInputs > 0 && data.inputs) { ... else if (scBus.numChannels == 1 ...) { sidechainR = scBus.channelBuffers32[0];  // mono → both channels'; grep of tests for 'numInputs = [1-9]' returns no matches.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I confirmed the gap from source. processor.cpp:471-489 takes the sidechain from data.inputs[0]. A stereo bus uses channels 0 and 1, and a mono bus copies channelBuffers32[0] to both sides (:486). Lines :491-504 write kSidechainActiveId to outputParameterChanges only when the value changes (lastSidechainActive_). Line :509 passes sidechainL/R into renderEngineSegments. In plugins/ruinae/tests, every ProcessData sets numInputs = 0 and inputs = nullptr. That includes mod_source_pipeline_test.cpp:160-161, processor_audio_test.cpp:123-124/161-162/208-209/294-295/408-409, midi_events_test.cpp:88-89, mpe_test.cpp:123-124, drain_preset_transfer.h:22 and every other process test the grep found. No test assigns a non-null data.inputs or numInputs >= 1. processor_bus_test.cpp:42-45 only checks that setBusArrangements accepts a stereo sidechain bus; it never runs process() with one. controller_params_test.cpp:422-427 only checks where the kSidechainActiveId value sits in the ID range. So the processor-level extraction (stereo, mono duplication, null-channel fallback), the per-segment sidechain pointer offset and the change-only kSidechainActiveId output are untested. One part of the finding is overstated. ruinae_engine_integration_test.cpp:1925-1968 calls engine.setSidechainInput(silence, silence) and checks that the Transient source follows a connected sidechain instead of note-ons. The engine-level switch away from transient-from-velocity is therefore covered, though only with a silent sidechain and without going through the processor. Because that engine-level coverage exists and this is a test gap rather than a live defect, I recommend downgrading the severity.

**Note 2.** The processor-level gap is real. processor.cpp:475-489 is the only place the sidechain bus is read: stereo takes channels 0 and 1, and mono at :483-487 uses channel 0 for both sides. processor.cpp:492-504 writes kSidechainActiveId only when the value changes. processor_midi.cpp:144-145 offsets the sidechain pointers by the segment position (`sidechainL + pos`). A grep of plugins/ruinae for `numInputs\s*=\s*[1-9]` or `inputs\s*=\s*&` finds nothing. Every processor test sets `numInputs = 0` and `inputs = nullptr` (for example mod_source_pipeline_test.cpp:160-161, processor_audio_test.cpp:123-124 and drain_preset_transfer.h:22). The only tests that mention kSidechainActiveId are controller_params_test.cpp:422-427, which checks the ID range, and processor_bus_test.cpp:42-45, which tests setBusArrangements and not process(). So the extraction branch, the mono duplication, the segment offset and the active-flag output are never run by any test.

Part of the finding is wrong. The engine's switch between Transient-from-velocity and Transient-from-sidechain is covered: ruinae_engine_integration_test.cpp:1925-1970 calls engine.setSidechainInput directly and asserts both behaviours ("Transient source listens to a connected sidechain, not to note-ons": maxOffset &lt; 0.01). The claim that the mod sources are "only ever tested against self-analysis", and the consequence "transient detection never re-enabled", are therefore partly covered at engine level. What is left is untested processor glue of about 30 lines. I am downgrading from medium to low because the risky behaviour at engine level has tests and only the thin bus-extraction and pointer-offset layer is unexercised.

**Note 3.** The core claim holds. A grep of plugins/ruinae/tests for numInputs finds only `data.numInputs = 0` (for example drain_preset_transfer.h:22, mod_source_pipeline_test.cpp:160, processor_audio_test.cpp:123/161/208/294/408 and about 40 more sites). No processor-level test passes an input bus to process(). That leaves three pieces of processor code unexercised:
- the bus extraction at processor.cpp:475-489 (stereo, mono duplicated to both channels, null channel pointers);
- the kSidechainActiveId change-only output at processor.cpp:492-504;
- the per-segment pointer offset in renderEngineSegments at processor_midi.cpp:144-145 (`sidechainL ? sidechainL + pos : nullptr`).

The finding overstates the gap in two places:
(1) The sidechain is covered at the engine level. ruinae_engine_integration_test.cpp:1925-1970 calls `engine.setSidechainInput(...)` and asserts that the Transient source listens to a connected sidechain and not to note-ons. So the regression "transient detection never re-enabled / switch away from transient-from-velocity" is already guarded downstream of the processor.
(2) processor_bus_test.cpp:42-49 checks that a stereo sidechain bus arrangement is accepted.

On impact, I read the untested processor code and it is correct today. The stereo and mono branches null-check correctly, the segment offset `+ pos` matches `left + pos` at processor_midi.cpp:146, and the active flag is written only on change. There is no present defect, no audible consequence and no host or setting that produces wrong output now. The risk is limited to a future regression in about 20 lines of simple pointer plumbing. That is a genuine but low-severity test gap, not a medium one.

</details>

### R-127

**Wall-clock arp CPU test bypasses the timing exclusion and [!mayfail] masks every CPU bar; arp normalisations use /20 for a 30-entry list**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/arp_performance_test.cpp:164-251, 257-312; ruinae_voice_test.cpp:1550-1604`

**Problem.** 'Arp CPU overhead is less than 0.5%' is tagged '[arp performance][!mayfail]'. 'arp performance' is one tag, not [performance], so the gate filter ~[performance] does not exclude it. It runs 20,000 timed blocks inside the 30-wide shard pool, and [!mayfail] stops its CHECK from ever failing. tools/lint-wallclock-tags.js reports 'clean' because the asserted name 'overheadPct' does not match its TIMEISH pattern. SC-003 (voice test :1550) carries [!mayfail] after its bar was raised from 8% to 10% (comment :1552), and CLAUDE.md forbids relaxing a budget. Both tests normalise kArpNoteValueId as idx/20.0 (:221, :271; also state_roundtrip_test.cpp:696). The handler uses kNoteValueDropdownCount-1 = 29 (arpeggiator_params.h:249), so 7/20 gives index 10 (1/8, not 1/16) and 4/20 gives index 6 (1/16T, not 1/32). The 'worst-case' stress test therefore runs at less than half the stated rate, and it asserts nothing (SUCCEED, :311).

**Why it is wrong.** Timing tests must be tagged so they run alone in the CPU lane and can fail there. A test that cannot fail measures nothing. Wrong normalisation means the stress scenario does not test the claimed worst case (1/32 at 200 BPM, ratchet 4).

**Consequence.** Arp CPU regressions and SC-003 regressions can never turn a run red. Gate shards are loaded with a pointless 20k-block benchmark, and the event-cap overflow path (kMaxEvents = 128) the stress test was meant to reach is never reached.

**Suggested fix.** Retag both arp perf cases [performance] (the stress case [long] if slow), remove [!mayfail] from both CPU cases, and restore the SC-003 bar to 8%, run in the isolated CPU lane. Normalise note values as idx/29.0 (or use Parameters::kNoteValueDropdownCount-1). Make the stress test assert balanced NoteOn/NoteOff on outputEvents and no event-cap saturation. Extend lint-wallclock-tags.js to follow derived names through any assignment from a clock-seeded value, not only TIMEISH names.

**Evidence.** arp_performance_test.cpp:165 '"[arp performance][!mayfail]"'; :221 'params.addChange(Ruinae::kArpNoteValueId, 7.0 / 20.0);  // 1/16 (index 7)'; arpeggiator_params.h:249 'value * (Parameters::kNoteValueDropdownCount - 1) + 0.5'; `node tools/lint-wallclock-tags.js` → 'lint-wallclock-tags: clean'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I checked each claim against the source and could not refute any of them.

(1) In arp_performance_test.cpp:165 the tag is "[arp performance][!mayfail]". Catch2 reads "[arp performance]" as one tag named "arp performance", so the gate filter ~[performance] (ruinae CLAUDE.md, root CLAUDE.md) does not exclude it. It times 2 x N = 20,000 blocks (N=10000 at :176, loops at :206 and :233), and [!mayfail] makes the CHECK at :250 non-fatal.

(2) The stress case at :257-259 is tagged only [arp performance] and ends with SUCCEED at :311. It asserts nothing.

(3) The note-value normalisation is wrong. The Ruinae handler at arpeggiator_params.h:249 computes clamp(int(value*(kNoteValueDropdownCount-1)+0.5)), and kNoteValueDropdownCount is 30 (dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/note_value.h:124).
- 7/20 = 0.35: 0.35 x 29 + 0.5 = 10.65, which truncates to index 10, 1/8 (note_value.h:152), not 1/16 (index 7).
- 4/20 = 0.2: 0.2 x 29 + 0.5 = 6.3, which truncates to index 6, 1/16T (note_value.h:147), not 1/32 (index 4).
- 1/16T is 0.167 beats against 0.125 beats for 1/32, so the stress test runs at 0.75x the stated step rate.
- The same /20 appears at state_roundtrip_test.cpp:696.

(4) ruinae_voice_test.cpp:1550-1555 carries [performance][!mayfail]. The comment at :1552 says the threshold was "relaxed from 8% to 10%", and :1603 is REQUIRE(cpuPercent &lt; 10.0). The test is excluded from gates, but in the CPU lane [!mayfail] still masks a failure.

(5) I ran `node tools/lint-wallclock-tags.js` and it printed "lint-wallclock-tags: clean", which matches the quoted evidence.

One overstatement in the finding: the stress rate drops to 0.75x, not "less than half" (that wording only holds for the first test, where 1/8 is half the 1/16 rate). The defect is the same either way.

Severity stays low: these are test-only gaps and no shipped audio behaviour is affected.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source and from one run of the lint.

1) Tagging. arp_performance_test.cpp:165 is `"[arp performance][!mayfail]"` and :259 and :322 are `"[arp performance]"`. Catch2 reads the bracketed text as one tag named "arp performance". The documented gate filter `~[performance]~[perf]~[benchmark]~[!benchmark]` (root CLAUDE.md, plugins/ruinae/CLAUDE.md) therefore does not exclude these cases. The file is compiled into ruinae_tests (plugins/ruinae/tests/CMakeLists.txt:88), and ci.yml:490 runs ruinae_tests in the shard jobs. The overhead case times two loops of N=10000 blocks (:176, :205-210, :232-237), so 20,000 timed blocks run inside the shard pool. Its only bar, `CHECK(overheadPct < 0.5)` at :250, is under [!mayfail], so the case never turns a run red. The comment at :171-174 says this is deliberate, so it is a known choice, not an oversight. It still conflicts with the root CLAUDE.md policy that timing tests run in the isolated CPU lane and that budgets are never relaxed. The archived spec (specs/_archive2_/082-presets-polish/spec.md:356, :374) records the original bar as 0.1%, so the budget was relaxed from 0.1% to 0.5%.

2) SC-003. ruinae_voice_test.cpp:1551 carries [!mayfail]. The comment at :1552 and the assertion at :1602-1603 say the bar was raised from 8% to 10%. That case does carry [performance], so the gate does exclude it. The [!mayfail] part of the claim still holds.

3) Lint. I ran `node tools/lint-wallclock-tags.js` and it printed "lint-wallclock-tags: clean".

4) Normalisation. dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/note_value.h:124 sets kNoteValueDropdownCount = 30. The handler at arpeggiator_params.h:249 computes `value*(30-1)+0.5`.
- 7/20 = 0.35 gives 0.35*29 + 0.5 = 10.65, so index 10, which is 1/8 (note_value.h:152), not the 1/16 that :221 intends.
- 4/20 = 0.2 gives 0.2*29 + 0.5 = 6.3, so index 6, which is 1/16T (note_value.h:147), not 1/32.
- state_roundtrip_test.cpp:696 uses the same stale 7.0/20.0.
plugins/ruinae/CHANGELOG.md:214 records that the count was changed from 21 to 30 and the tests were fixed, but these sites were missed.

5) Assertion. The stress test ends with an unconditional SUCCEED at :311.

Corrections to the finding. The stress case runs at 0.75x the stated rate (1/16T is 0.167 beats against 0.125 beats for 1/32), not "less than half". Only the overhead case runs at half rate (1/8 instead of 1/16). I did not check whether 1/32 at 200 BPM would actually reach kMaxEvents = 128. These points do not change the verdict: it is a test-quality problem, not a product defect, so low severity is right.

**Note 3.** The finding is confirmed. Every factual claim checks out against the source and against one lint run. The impact is limited to tests, so 'low' is the right severity.

1) Tagging: plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/arp_performance_test.cpp:164-165 tags the 0.5% case "[arp performance][!mayfail]". In Catch2 that is one tag, "arp performance", so the documented gate filter '~[performance]~[perf]~[benchmark]~[!benchmark]' does not exclude it. The case times 2x10,000 blocks (:176, :205-237) and checks `CHECK(overheadPct < 0.5)` (:250). Because of [!mayfail], a failure never turns the run red. The stress case at :257-259 is tagged "[arp performance]" only.

2) Lint: I ran `node tools/lint-wallclock-tags.js` and it printed "lint-wallclock-tags: clean". The TIMEISH regex at tools/lint-wallclock-tags.js:39 does not match `overheadPct`, and line 70 needs the name to match TIMEISH, so the derived name is never flagged.

3) SC-003: ruinae_voice_test.cpp:1550-1555 carries [!mayfail], and its comment says the bar was "relaxed from 8% to 10%" (`REQUIRE(cpuPercent < 10.0)` at :1603). That case does carry [performance], so the gate already excludes it. The real defect there is the relaxed bar plus [!mayfail], which means it can never fail in the CPU lane either.

4) Normalisation: arpeggiator_params.h:249 denormalises as `value*(kNoteValueDropdownCount-1)+0.5`, and dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/note_value.h:124 sets kNoteValueDropdownCount = 30, so the multiplier is 29.
- 7/20 = 0.35, and 0.35*29 + 0.5 = 10.65, which gives index 10 = 1/8 (note_value.h:152), not 1/16 (index 7, :148).
- 4/20 = 0.2, and 0.2*29 + 0.5 = 6.3, which gives index 6 = 1/16T (:147), not 1/32 (index 4, :144).

So the 'worst case 1/32' stress test runs at 0.1667 beats per step instead of 0.125, which is 75% of the stated rate. That is slower than intended, though not under half the rate as the finding says. The stress test then only calls SUCCEED (:311).

Additional confirmation: state_roundtrip_test.cpp:696 sets 7.0/20.0, commented as "noteValue = 7 (1/16)". That lands on index 10, which is kNoteValueDefaultIndex (note_value.h:127). The 'non-default' round-trip therefore never exercises a non-default note value.

Impact: no audio or user-facing effect. Arp CPU overhead and SC-003 regressions cannot turn any lane red, and the stress scenario under-exercises the event path. The finding's one overstatement is the rate: 1/16T is 75% of the 1/32 rate, not 'less than half'. Low severity stands.

</details>

### R-137

**Host tempo dropout gives the engine 120 BPM while delay/S&H/Random/arp-rate use the last valid tempo**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** gestalt-processor · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.cpp:245-248, 254-279`

**Problem.** tempoBPM_ is updated only when kTempoValid is set and otherwise keeps its last value. blockCtx is a fresh BlockContext with tempoBPM defaulting to 120 (block_context.h:69). When kTempoValid is absent, engine_.setTempo(blockCtx.tempoBPM) pushes 120 BPM to the LFOs, trance gates, phaser, flanger, chorus and chain delay tempo, and the arp receives arpCtx.tempoBPM = 120. In the same block, applyDelayParams, the S&H/Random sync and the arp rate-mod conversion use tempoBPM_. transportPositionSamples is also derived from projectTimeMusic at 120 BPM.

**Why it is wrong.** One block must use one tempo. Either both paths hold the last valid tempo or both use the default.

**Consequence.** In hosts that omit kTempoValid on some blocks (offline bounce, start of playback, some plugin hosts), tempo-synced LFOs, the trance gate and the arp jump to 120 BPM while synced delay time and S&H/Random rates stay at the project tempo. The result is audible desync and rate jumps.

**Suggested fix.** Seed blockCtx.tempoBPM from tempoBPM_ (the cached last valid tempo) when kTempoValid is missing, and use a single tempo source for applyParamsToEngine and setTempo. Test: alternate blocks with and without kTempoValid at 90 BPM and assert the trance gate step length stays at the 90 BPM value.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:245-247 `if (... kTempoValid) { tempoBPM_ = data.processContext->tempo; }`; :254 `Krate::DSP::BlockContext blockCtx;` and :261-262 only overwrites tempoBPM when kTempoValid; :279 `engine_.setTempo(blockCtx.tempoBPM);`; processor_params.cpp:572-573 `dropdownToDelayMs(..., tempoBPM_)`, :793, :809, :888-889.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The finding is confirmed from source. I traced the call path to check it.

Two tempo values exist for the same block:
- processor.cpp:245-248 updates the cached member `tempoBPM_` (processor.h:267, initial value 120.0) only when kTempoValid is set. Otherwise it keeps the last valid host tempo.
- processor.cpp:254 builds a fresh `Krate::DSP::BlockContext blockCtx`. Its `tempoBPM` defaults to 120.0 (dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/block_context.h:69). Lines 261-262 overwrite it only when kTempoValid is set. Lines 273-274 compute transportPositionSamples with `ppqToSamples(..., blockCtx.tempoBPM, ...)`.
- processor.cpp:278-279 passes blockCtx to `engine_.setBlockContext` and `engine_.setTempo(blockCtx.tempoBPM)`. setTempo (ruinae_engine.h:1635-1645) forwards that tempo to `blockContext_.tempoBPM`, the effects-chain delay tempo, the phaser, flanger and chorus, and every voice's trance gate.
- processor.cpp:304 copies the same value into the arp: `arpCtx = blockCtx`, which goes to `arpCore_.processBlock(arpCtx, ...)` at :330.

The other paths in the same block read the cached tempo instead. applyParamsToEngine (called at :251) uses `tempoBPM_` in:
- the synced delay time (processor_params.cpp:572-573)
- the synced S&H rate (:793)
- the synced Random rate (:809)
- the arp rate-mod duration (:888-889)

Result: if a host sends kTempoValid on some blocks and not others, a block without the flag gives the engine, trance gate, modulation FX, block-context LFOs and arp 120 BPM. In that same block the delay time, S&H/Random rates and arp rate-mod use the last valid host tempo. The described inconsistency is real.

Recommended severity: downgrade. The defect only appears with a host that sets kTempoValid and later drops it. A host that never sets the flag gets a consistent 120 BPM on both paths, and mainstream DAWs set the flag on every block. The code path is reachable but uncommon, so low fits better than medium.

**Note 2.** I confirmed the defect from source. processor.cpp:245-248 caches `tempoBPM_` only when kTempoValid is set, so it holds the last valid tempo (processor.h:267, initialised to 120.0). processor.cpp:254 builds a fresh `Krate::DSP::BlockContext blockCtx`, whose `tempoBPM` defaults to 120.0 (dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/block_context.h:69). Lines 261-263 overwrite it only when kTempoValid is set. Lines 278-279 then call `engine_.setBlockContext(blockCtx)` and `engine_.setTempo(blockCtx.tempoBPM)`. ruinae_engine.h:1635-1645 shows setTempo forwarding that value to the chain delay tempo, the phaser, the flanger, the chorus and every voice's trance gate. The arp gets `arpCtx = blockCtx` (processor.cpp:304, 330), and transportPositionSamples comes from `ppqToSamples(..., blockCtx.tempoBPM, ...)` (processor.cpp:273-274).

In the same block, applyParamsToEngine (called at processor.cpp:251) uses the cached `tempoBPM_`: the delay note-value time (processor_params.cpp:572-573), the synced S&H rate (:793), the synced Random rate (:809) and the arp rate-mod duration (:888-889). So when processContext is non-null without kTempoValid, or is null after an earlier valid tempo, one block runs two tempos: 120 for the engine, gates, modulation FX and arp, and the last host tempo for the delay time, S&H, Random and arp rate mod.

I found nothing that marks this as intentional. No code comment explains it, and no test pins it: tempo_sync_test.cpp:43 only checks that a null ProcessContext does not crash, and :113 always sets kTempoValid. No upstream code reconciles the two values.

I recommend a downgrade because the defect is hard to reach. The two paths only disagree when a host sends kTempoValid on some blocks and drops it, or sends a null processContext, on others. A host that never sets kTempoValid leaves both at 120, so they agree. Mainstream DAWs set kTempoValid on every block. The intermittent case is limited to a few hosts and edge moments, such as some offline or bounce paths, and it only affects tempo-synced features while the dropout lasts.

**Note 3.** The code inconsistency is real. processor.cpp:245-248 updates tempoBPM_ only when kTempoValid is set and otherwise keeps the last valid value (processor.h:267, initial value 120.0). processor.cpp:254 builds a fresh BlockContext whose tempoBPM defaults to 120.0 (block_context.h:69), and :261-263 overwrite it only when kTempoValid is set. :278-279 then pass that value to engine_.setBlockContext and engine_.setTempo. ruinae_engine.h:1635-1644 forwards it to effectsChain_.setDelayTempo, the phaser, flanger and chorus tempo, and every voice's trance gate. arpCtx copies blockCtx (processor.cpp:304), and ppqToSamples uses blockCtx.tempoBPM (:273-274). In the same block, applyParamsToEngine (processor.cpp:251) uses tempoBPM_ for the delay ms and the S&H/Random sync (processor_params.cpp:573, 793, 809, 889). So when a block arrives without kTempoValid after earlier valid blocks, one block mixes two tempos.

The impact is smaller than claimed. (1) A host that NEVER sets kTempoValid causes no mismatch, because tempoBPM_ also stays at 120. (2) A null processContext gives the same split, but the mainstream VST3 DAWs (Cubase, Live, Reaper, Bitwig, Studio One, FL) set kTempoValid on every processing block, so the trigger is a host that drops the flag intermittently. The finding names no such host. "Offline bounce, start of playback" is unsupported. (3) setTempo and setBlockContext are re-sent every block, so one block without the flag causes a one-block rate excursion (LFO, trance-gate or arp phase advances at 120 instead of the project tempo for N samples). That is a small phase offset, not a sustained desync. A sustained desync needs a host that keeps omitting the flag after it once supplied it, which is an unusual host bug. (4) When the arp has projectTimeMusicValid and is playing, syncToMusicalPosition (processor.cpp:325-326) re-locks its grid every block, which limits arp drift further.

The finding is valid as a consistency bug with a cheap fix: seed blockCtx.tempoBPM from tempoBPM_. Because the trigger depends on the host and is rare, and the effect is transient, low severity fits better than medium.

</details>

### R-139

**Processor header and members are stale: 'No audio input bus', unused mixBufferL_/R_ and four dead flags**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** gestalt-processor · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor.h:16-19, 324-326, 349-350, 386, 397`

**Problem.** The class comment says 'No audio input bus', but initialize() adds a stereo Sidechain aux input (processor.cpp:58-62). mixBufferL_ and mixBufferR_ are resized in setupProcessing and zero-filled in setActive, but nothing reads or writes them otherwise. currentBlockSamples_, wasTransportPlaying_, envDisplayMessageSent_ and morphPadModMessageSent_ are declared and never used, left over from the handshake move (F042) and earlier designs. maxBlockSize_ is stored, but process() never checks numSamples against it; RuinaeEngine silently truncates oversized blocks.

**Why it is wrong.** Dead members and wrong comments mislead maintainers about the threading and bus design. Dead '...MessageSent_' flags suggest per-message guards that no longer exist.

**Consequence.** This is a maintenance trap. A reader trusting the header would remove the sidechain handling or assume the handshake guards are per message. The unused vectors cost two allocations per setupProcessing.

**Suggested fix.** Fix the header comment, delete the unused members and their resize/fill, and either assert or chunk when data.numSamples > maxBlockSize_.

**Evidence.** processor.h:17 '// - No audio input bus'; grep under plugins/ruinae/src/processor: mixBufferL_ only at processor.cpp:178,208 and processor.h:349; currentBlockSamples_, wasTransportPlaying_, envDisplayMessageSent_ and morphPadModMessageSent_ appear only at their declarations (processor.h:324,326,386,397).

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I confirmed the dead-code and stale-comment parts of the finding from source. The clause about oversized blocks is weak but does not change the verdict.

1. **Stale comment.** processor.h:17 says "// - No audio input bus". processor.cpp:58 calls addAudioInput(...), which adds the stereo sidechain bus. The comment is wrong.

2. **Unused mixBufferL_/R_.** In the processor, these vectors appear only at processor.h:349-350, the resize at processor.cpp:178-179 and the std::fill at processor.cpp:208-209. Nothing else reads or writes them. Every other match is the engine's own members of the same name (ruinae_engine.h:168-169, 799-995 and 2160-2161), which the engine uses for the voice sum. The processor's copies duplicate the engine's buffers and are dead.

3. **Four unused flags.**
   - currentBlockSamples_: only processor.h:324.
   - envDisplayMessageSent_: only processor.h:386.
   - morphPadModMessageSent_: only processor.h:397.
   - wasTransportPlaying_: under plugins/ruinae it appears at processor.h:326 and in the controller (controller.h:527 and controller.cpp:503/515/743). The controller copy is a different class's member. The processor's copy is never used.

   None of the four is referenced in any processor TU or test. All are private, so no test subclass can reach them. handshakeMessagesSent_ (processor.h:361) is now the only handshake guard, so the per-message "...MessageSent_" flags are misleading leftovers.

4. **Oversized blocks.** maxBlockSize_ is stored at processor.cpp:175. process() never compares data.numSamples against it; processor.cpp:257 only computes blockCtx.blockSize. RuinaeEngine::processBlock clamps at ruinae_engine.h:796 (numSamples = std::min(numSamples, voiceScratchBuffer_.size())), so the samples past the clamp are silently never written. This clause is weak: VST3 hosts must not exceed maxSamplesPerBlock, so in practice this is defensive hardening, not a reachable bug.

Low severity / anti-pattern is the right classification, so there is no severity change.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. Every part of it checks out against the source.
- The header comment is wrong. processor.h:17 says "No audio input bus", but processor.cpp:58-59 adds a "Sidechain" aux input with addAudioInput. The process path also reads sidechainL/R (processor.cpp:494-509, lastSidechainActive_).
- mixBufferL_/R_ in Processor are dead. A grep of plugins/ruinae finds them only at processor.h:349-350, processor.cpp:178-179 (resize) and processor.cpp:208-209 (fill). Every other hit belongs to the separate RuinaeEngine members in ruinae_engine.h:2160-2161, which are used.
- Four flags are only ever declared. currentBlockSamples_ (processor.h:324), wasTransportPlaying_ (processor.h:326), envDisplayMessageSent_ (processor.h:386) and morphPadModMessageSent_ (processor.h:397) have no other hits in src or tests. The wasTransportPlaying_ hits at controller.cpp:503/515/743 are the Controller's own member (controller.h:527), not the Processor's. The handshake guard that does exist is handshakeMessagesSent_ (processor.h:361), which confirms the per-message flags are leftovers.
- The block-size claim holds. maxBlockSize_ is set at processor.cpp:175 and used only to prepare the engine and arp. process() never compares data.numSamples with it (processor.cpp:437-509). RuinaeEngine::processBlock clamps with numSamples = std::min(numSamples, voiceScratchBuffer_.size()) at ruinae_engine.h:796. An oversized block would therefore leave the rest of the output silent, because processor.cpp:463-464 zero-fills the whole output first.
- Nothing documents these members as intentional or covers them with a test.
Low severity is right. The VST3 contract binds hosts to maxSamplesPerBlock, so the truncation path is unreachable in a conforming host. The rest is dead code plus a misleading comment, a maintenance issue rather than a functional bug.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. processor.h:17 says "// - No audio input bus", but processor.cpp:58-62 adds a stereo kAux "Sidechain" input. The comment is copied verbatim into tests/unit/processor_bus_test.cpp:5. A Grep over plugins/ruinae finds Processor::mixBufferL_ and mixBufferR_ only at processor.h:349-350, the resize at processor.cpp:178-179 and the fill at processor.cpp:208-209. The engine uses its own RuinaeEngine::mixBufferL_ and mixBufferR_ (ruinae_engine.h:168, 2160). currentBlockSamples_ (processor.h:324), wasTransportPlaying_ (processor.h:326), envDisplayMessageSent_ (processor.h:386) and morphPadModMessageSent_ (processor.h:397) occur only at their declarations. The only other wasTransportPlaying_ is the controller's own member (controller.h:527), a different class. The one-shot guard is now handshakeMessagesSent_ (processor.h:361, processor.cpp:193-201), so the per-message flags are leftovers. maxBlockSize_ is stored at processor.cpp:175, and the engine clamps at ruinae_engine.h:796 (numSamples = std::min(numSamples, voiceScratchBuffer_.size())). Impact check: the claimed consequence is maintenance only, and it holds at that level. There is no audible or real-time effect. The two vector resizes run in setupProcessing on a non-audio thread, and the fill in setActive is a negligible memset, so they cost nothing that matters. The oversize-block truncation needs a host that breaks the VST3 contract (numSamples > maxSamplesPerBlock), so in practice that part is a robustness note, not a reachable defect. Severity "low" is correct for dead members and a stale comment, so no change.

</details>

### R-144

**Arp lane playheads are polled only while the host reports kPlaying, but the processor free-runs the arp in hosts without transport**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** gestalt-controller · **Source:** static (verify round static)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/controller/controller.cpp:545-556, 501-516`

**Problem.** The poll timer updates lane playheads only when the processor's isTransportPlaying_ atomic is true. The processor stores the raw kPlaying bit in that atomic (processor.cpp:535-537). The arp itself runs with isPlaying forced true while the host has never reported kPlaying (processor.cpp:300-310). On transport stop, the timer clears trails and overlays but never calls setPlayheadStep(-1). clearOverlays clears only the trail (arp_lane_editor.h:305-308), and polling stops, so the last step stays highlighted.

**Why it is wrong.** The UI should show the arp's real running state. The processor already distinguishes 'host has no transport' from 'stopped' with hostSupportsTransport_. The controller does not have that information, so the two disagree.

**Consequence.** In transport-less hosts, standalone wrappers and simple hosts, the arp plays but no lane shows a playhead or trail. After a DAW stop, a stale playhead remains on screen.

**Suggested fix.** Gate polling on the playhead parameter value instead of transport, since the processor writes the 1.0 sentinel when the arp is off. Alternatively, export the processor's effective arp-running state. On stop, call lane->setPlayheadStep(-1) for all 8 lanes.

**Evidence.** controller.cpp:545-547 `bool transportPlaying = isTransportPlayingPtr_ && isTransportPlayingPtr_->load(...); if (transportPlaying) { pollLanePlayhead(...` ; processor.cpp:308-310 `if (!hostSupportsTransport_) { arpCtx.isPlaying = true; }`; processor.cpp:535-537 `isTransportPlaying_.store(playing ...)` from raw kPlaying.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute the finding. Both halves hold when traced through the code.

1. Hosts without transport: processor.cpp:535-537 stores the raw kPlaying bit in isTransportPlaying_ (`playing = processContext && (state & kPlaying) != 0`). The arp, however, forces arpCtx.isPlaying = true whenever hostSupportsTransport_ is false (processor.cpp:298-310). That flag latches only after kPlaying has been seen (processor.cpp:300-302). It also writes real step positions to kArpVelocityPlayheadId / kArpGatePlayheadId on every arp-running block (processor.cpp:393-415). On the controller side, every pollLanePlayhead call sits behind `if (transportPlaying)` (controller.cpp:545-556), and transportPlaying is that same raw kPlaying atomic. So in a host that never sets kPlaying, the arp plays but no lane ever gets setPlayheadStep or setTrailSteps. No other path in the Ruinae controller sets the lane playhead: a grep for setPlaybackStep / setPlayheadStep / isTransportPlayingPtr_ finds only controller.cpp:484-489 (the trance gate) and 501-556.

2. Stale playhead after a DAW stop: on the playing-to-stopped edge, controller.cpp:501-516 clears laneTrailStates_, resets lastPolledSteps_ to -1 and calls clearOverlays() on all 8 lanes. clearOverlays only does trailState_.clear(); setDirty() (arp_lane_editor.h:305-308, and the same in arp_modifier_lane.h:228-231, arp_condition_lane.h:263-266 and enum_popup_arp_lane.h:216-219). It never resets playbackStep_ / playheadStep_. After that, polling is gated off, so setPlayheadStep(-1) is never called. The overlay draw does not check StepPatternEditor::isPlaying_: drawBarPlaybackOverlay (arp_lane_editor.h:837-839) draws whenever 0 &lt;= getPlaybackStep() &lt; numSteps. So the last step stays highlighted. Unlike the trance gate, the controller never calls setPlaying(false) on the arp lanes. Even if it did, the arp lane overlays ignore isPlaying_.

Related fact found while tracing: the processor writes only the velocity and gate playhead parameters (processor.cpp:393-433). The pitch, ratchet, modifier, condition, chord and inversion playhead IDs (plugin_ids.h:1107-1110, 1190-1191) are polled but never written. So even while the transport plays, only two of the eight lanes animate. This is a separate defect, but it limits the 'all 8 lanes' wording of the consequence. The processor's 1.0 sentinel is also written only for velocity and gate, so the suggested fix (gate polling on the playhead parameter value) would work only for those two lanes.

Severity: the defect is UI-only. No audio, state or real-time-safety impact. It is a missing or stale visual indicator, so I am downgrading from medium to low.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source. (1) controller.cpp:545-556 calls pollLanePlayhead for the 8 lanes only when isTransportPlayingPtr_->load() is true. (2) processor.cpp:535-537 stores the raw ProcessContext::kPlaying bit into isTransportPlaying_, and that bit is false when processContext is null or kPlaying is never set. (3) processor.cpp:298-310: when the host never reports kPlaying (hostSupportsTransport_ false, reset in setActive at :188), arpCtx.isPlaying is forced true, so the arp runs, dispatches notes (:330-378) and writes the playhead output params (:393-415). The controller ignores those params because transportPlaying is false, so in a host without transport no lane playhead or trail is ever drawn. (4) On a stop edge (controller.cpp:501-516), the controller clears laneTrailStates_, sets lastPolledSteps_ to -1 and calls clearOverlays() on each lane. Every clearOverlays only clears trailState_ (arp_lane_editor.h:305-308, arp_condition_lane.h:263-266, arp_modifier_lane.h:228-231, enum_popup_arp_lane.h:216-219). Polling stops on the same tick, so setPlayheadStep is never called again and the last step stays highlighted. Nothing else drives the lanes: setPlayheadParamId only stores the ID (arp_lane_editor.h:225, enum_popup_arp_lane.h:138 etc.), and the only reader of the playhead params is the poll at controller.cpp:523. I found no spec, comment or test that makes either behaviour intentional. The 081 comment at :500 says only that trails are cleared on stop, and arp_integration_test.cpp:883 tests the processor's no-transport arp path, not the UI. The effect is UI-only, with no audio or stuck-note consequence, but it is a visible feature failure in transport-less hosts such as standalone wrappers and simple hosts like the user's Plugin Buddy, so medium stands. Side note: the processor writes only the velocity and gate playhead params (processor.cpp:393-433). Pitch, ratchet, modifier, condition, chord and inversion are never written, so those six lanes would show no playhead even under transport. That is a separate issue that is likely worth checking.

**Note 3.** The defect is real, but it only affects what the editor shows, so I am downgrading it from medium to low.

What the code shows:
- Polling depends on the raw transport bit. controller.cpp:545-556 calls pollLanePlayhead for the 8 lanes only when isTransportPlayingPtr_ is true. That atomic is processor.cpp:535-537, which stores the raw ProcessContext kPlaying bit.
- The arp ignores that bit in hosts without transport. processor.cpp:300-310 sets hostSupportsTransport_ only after the host has reported kPlaying at least once. Until then it forces arpCtx.isPlaying = true, so the arp runs and plays notes.
- The processor still writes the playheads. processor.cpp:393-415 writes kArpVelocityPlayheadId and kArpGatePlayheadId on every block while the arp runs. In a host that never sets kPlaying the controller never reads them, so no lane shows a playhead or a trail.
- The stop branch never resets the playhead. On a playing-to-stopped edge, controller.cpp:501-516 clears laneTrailStates_, sets lastPolledSteps_ to -1 and calls clearOverlays() on each lane. clearOverlays clears only trailState_ (arp_lane_editor.h:305-308, enum_popup_arp_lane.h:216-219, arp_modifier_lane.h:228-231, arp_condition_lane.h:263-266). Nothing calls setPlayheadStep(-1).
- The stale highlight is drawn. After the stop, polling ends (line 547), so playbackStep_ keeps the last step. drawBarPlaybackOverlay (arp_lane_editor.h:837-853) checks only that the step is in range, not isPlaying_. StepPatternEditor's own check at step_pattern_editor.h:1013 does not apply, because setPlaying is called only on the trance-gate editor (controller.cpp:488), never on an arp lane. The modifier and condition lanes also draw playheadStep_ whenever it is >= 0 (arp_modifier_lane.h:613, arp_condition_lane.h:672). So after a DAW stop the last step stays white on the velocity and gate lanes.

Why the severity is lower:
- Nothing reaches the audio. There are no stuck notes and no change to the sound or the saved state.
- The first symptom needs a host that never sets kPlaying. Mainstream DAWs set it, so the trigger is limited to simple hosts and standalone wrappers.
- The impact is narrower than claimed. processor.cpp:393-415 writes only the velocity and gate playheads. The pitch, ratchet, modifier, condition, chord and inversion playheads (plugin_ids.h:1107-1110, 1190-1191) are never written, so those six lanes show no live playhead even in a DAW while it plays. The stale highlight after a stop can therefore appear only on the velocity and gate lanes, not on 8.
- That missing write for six lanes is a separate and larger UI gap than this finding.

</details>

### R-149

**Formant oscillator clamps the fundamental at 2000 Hz: every note above B6 plays at 2 kHz**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/formant_oscillator.h:194, 272-273`

**Problem.** kMaxFundamental = 2000 Hz, and setFundamental clamps to [20, 2000].

**Why it is wrong.** A note-tracked oscillator must follow the keyboard across the instrument's range, or at least the playable range of factory patches. C7 (2093 Hz) and above collapse to one pitch.

**Consequence.** C7 is 78.7 cents flat. Every higher note plays the same 2 kHz pitch, so melodies or arps in the top octave, and pitch-mod or bend above it, flatten out.

**Suggested fix.** Raise the cap toward Nyquist/2 or the FOF grain limit (with an anti-alias fade), or document it and fade the oscillator out above the cap instead of pinning the pitch. Add a test: osc-pitch for notes 93-108 within 5 cents.

**Evidence.** probe osc:Formant:C7 / osc-pitch:Formant: 'A6 0.00, B6 0.00, C7 -78.70 (2000 Hz instead of 2093)'. formant_oscillator.h:194 'static constexpr float kMaxFundamental = 2000.0f;'; :273 'fundamental_ = std::clamp(hz, kMinFundamental, kMaxFundamental);'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Confirmed from source. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/formant_oscillator.h:195 `static constexpr float kMaxFundamental = 2000.0f;` and :272-277 `setFundamental` does `fundamental_ = std::clamp(hz, kMinFundamental, kMaxFundamental)` and then drives `fundamentalPhase_` at the clamped value. The doc comment at :271 says "clamped to [20, 2000]", so the clamp was deliberate in the DSP component's own spec. Ruinae's plugin architecture does not document it as a limit, though.

Call path: RuinaeVoice::updateOscFrequencies (plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:1599-1611) computes freqA/freqB = noteFrequency_ * expression tuning * semitonesToRatio(tune + fine + pitch mod) and passes the result to oscA_/oscB_.setFrequency with no clamp of its own. In OscillatorAdapter::setFrequency (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/oscillator_adapters.h:157-175), FormantOscillator is in "Group B" and calls osc_.setFundamental(hz) directly. Nothing in between raises or works around the 2 kHz cap.

Any frequency at or above 2000 Hz therefore plays at exactly 2000 Hz. That covers MIDI 96 (C7, 2093 Hz) and higher, and also lower notes pushed up by osc tune, pitch mod, bend or MPE tuning. C7 comes out 1200*log2(2000/2093.0) = -78.7 cents, which matches the quoted probe figure. The finding's claimed behaviour and arithmetic are correct.

Medium severity fits: Formant is a user-selectable keyboard-tracked oscillator type, and the top octave collapses to a single pitch.

**Note 2.** The clamp exists exactly as claimed: dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/formant_oscillator.h:195 `kMaxFundamental = 2000.0f`, and :272-277 setFundamental clamps `fundamental_ = std::clamp(hz, kMinFundamental, kMaxFundamental)` before driving fundamentalPhase_. Ruinae reaches it on every note: dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/oscillator_adapters.h:168-171 routes the voice pitch for FormantOscillator straight to `osc_.setFundamental(hz)`, with no fade or cutoff above the cap. So in a real host any note at or above C7 (MIDI 96, 2093 Hz) plays at 2000 Hz, and the same happens to pitch bend or modulation that pushes the frequency past the cap. I found no Ruinae-level guard against this.

Context check (could it be intentional?): at the primitive level the cap is deliberate. Archived spec specs/_archive2_/027-formant-oscillator/spec.md:252-254 (FR-012) says "Range: 20Hz to 2000Hz (covers human voice and musical range)", :325 repeats the range, and dsp/tests/unit/processors/formant_oscillator_test.cpp:584-595 ("FR-012: setFundamental() clamps to [20, 2000] Hz range") pins it. That spec was written for a stand-alone vowel oscillator, though. Its own edge-case note (:172) expects valid output with "formant character reduced" above 2 kHz, not a frozen pitch. I searched specs/Ruinae.md, specs/ruinae-roadmap.md, plugins/ruinae/MANUAL.md, the archived 041 and 068 Ruinae specs, OSC-ROADMAP and selectable_oscillator.h, and none of them records that Ruinae's Formant oscillator stops tracking pitch above B6. The cap is an intended limit of the DSP primitive, not a documented decision for the plugin, so Ruinae's keyboard-tracked use exposes it as a real pitch error.

Severity: I recommend lowering it to low. The cap is a stated design range of the primitive, backed by a test. It only affects the top octave and a half of a vowel/FOF oscillator, where the formant character is already mostly gone. The fix is either a fade-out above the cap in the adapter or a higher cap together with a check of the grain-pool limits (kGrainsPerFormant = 8 with 20 ms grains), which is not a one-line change.

**Note 3.** The defect is real. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/formant_oscillator.h:195 sets `kMaxFundamental = 2000.0f`, and :272-277 has `setFundamental` clamp the value to [20, 2000] and drive `fundamentalPhase_` (the FOF pulse rate, which is the pitch) from the clamped value. Ruinae reaches it through the selectable oscillator: dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/selectable_oscillator.h:280-281 creates `OscillatorAdapter<FormantOscillator>`, and in dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/oscillator_adapters.h:168-171 the adapter's setFrequency hands the note's Hz directly to `osc_.setFundamental(hz)`, with no compensation anywhere. So every target pitch above 2000 Hz plays at 2000 Hz. The quoted number checks out: C7 = 2093.0 Hz, and 1200*log2(2000/2093.0) = -78.7 cents. B6 (1975.5 Hz) is below the cap and plays correctly.

Impact, quantified: only target pitches of 2000 Hz and up are affected. At zero tune offset that is MIDI 96-108, the top 13 keys of an 88-key range. Osc tune, pitch bend or pitch modulation lower that threshold, and each of those keys plays the same 2 kHz pitch. Factory presets use Formant oscA/oscB (tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:457/461, 1162/1166, 1820, 2237, 3699/3703, 4430/4432). A grep of tuneSemitones assignments finds none in those Formant blocks that transposes up, so no factory Formant patch goes above the cap except by playing in the top octave or bending up there. At a fundamental near 2 kHz a vowel oscillator is also musically marginal: the pulse rate is above F1 and close to F2 for most vowels, so it is already a thin buzz. The pitch error is real and audible (78.7 cents and up, notes collapsing to one pitch), but it only appears at the extreme top of the keyboard, for one of ten oscillator types. Severity should go from medium to low.

</details>

### R-151

**Modulation sub-block grid is not block-size invariant: buffers shorter than 64 samples evaluate modulation every 32 samples**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:819-825, 846-850, 909`

**Problem.** The loop cuts len = min(kModSubBlock - modGridPhase_, numSamples - start) and calls globalModEngine_.process for every partial piece. When a buffer (or segment) boundary falls inside the 64-sample grid, the modulation engine is evaluated, and its end-of-sub-block offsets are sampled, at the partial boundary too. A 32-sample host therefore updates offsets every 32 samples instead of every 64.

**Why it is wrong.** The comment states 'every buffer size cuts the same sub-blocks and renders the same audio'. The grid phase is kept, but offsets are still re-evaluated at each partial cut, so the hold pattern changes with buffer size.

**Consequence.** LFO-to-cutoff routes render differently at small buffer sizes (max diff 0.136). Output is not reproducible between a 32-sample live buffer and an offline bounce.

**Suggested fix.** Accumulate partial pieces and evaluate the mod engine only when the 64-grid completes (carry the held offset across calls), or advance the sources sample-accurately and sample them only at grid boundaries. Add a test: LFO1 -> global and all-voice cutoff, bs 32 vs 512, max diff &lt;= 1e-5.

**Evidence.** probe block-invariance:v2: 'bs32 0.1360935 (30023, -17.3 dBFS)'; bs64 and bs2048 0.0000000. ruinae_engine.h:847 'const size_t len = std::min(kModSubBlock - modGridPhase_, numSamples - start);'; :823-825 'The grid is counted across buffers (modGridPhase_), so every buffer size cuts the same sub-blocks and renders the same audio.'

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The source confirms it. In plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:847 the piece length is `len = std::min(kModSubBlock - modGridPhase_, numSamples - start)` (kModSubBlock = 64, :2167). Every piece then calls `globalModEngine_.process(subCtx, ..., len)` (:852), reads every offset with getModulationOffset (:855-876), and passes those offsets to processBlockPoly/Mono for that piece (:897-907). modGridPhase_ only keeps where the 64-sample cells start (:909). It does not delay evaluation until a cell is complete.

ModulationEngine::process (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/modulation_engine.h:226-288) steps the LFOs per sample. It then takes lfo1LastValue_, the value at the LAST sample of the call (:231, :275-279), and calls evaluateRoutings. getModulationOffset (:298-302) returns that stored value.

So with a 32-sample host buffer, the first 32 samples of each 64-sample cell are rendered with the LFO value at sample 32. With a 512 or 2048 buffer, the same samples get the value at sample 64. The offsets differ, the cutoff differs and so the audio differs. This matches the probe (bs32 diff 0.136; bs64 and bs2048 diff 0). The comment at :823-825 ("every buffer size cuts the same sub-blocks and renders the same audio") holds only when the buffer size is a multiple of 64. Processor-side segment splits at note events also cut cells short, for the same reason.

The covering test cannot catch this. plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/ruinae_engine_test.cpp:1678-1701 compares only render(64) with render(2048), both multiples of the grid, so a sub-64 or non-multiple buffer size is never tested. Severity "low" is appropriate: the output is still smooth, but it is not reproducible across buffer sizes.

**Note 2.** Confirmed from source. plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:846-852 cuts `len = min(kModSubBlock - modGridPhase_, numSamples - start)` and calls `globalModEngine_.process(subCtx, ..., len)` on every piece, including a partial one where a buffer ends inside a grid cell. It then reads the offsets immediately (:855-876) and uses them for that piece's voices (:897-907) and for the global filter/master gain sub-block (:882-894). modGridPhase_ (:909) only keeps the grid aligned; it does not hold a value across the cut. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/modulation_engine.h:226-288, process() advances the LFOs per sample but publishes only the last value (lfo1LastValue_ -> lfo1CurrentOutput_) and runs evaluateRoutings once per call. The offset is therefore the end-of-call value. With 32-sample buffers, samples 0-31 of each 64-cell get the LFO value at sample 32. With buffers of 64 or more, all 64 samples get the value at sample 64. The output differs, and the same happens with any buffer size that is not a multiple of 64 (e.g. 100, 441, variable-size hosts). The comment at :823-825 ("every buffer size cuts the same sub-blocks and renders the same audio") does not hold for these sizes. The only test, plugins/ruinae/tests/unit/ruinae_engine_test.cpp:1647-1703, compares 64 against 2048, both multiples of 64, so it cannot catch this. No clamp, reset or documented design decision covers it. The reported probe numbers (bs32 differs, bs64 and bs2048 identical) match this mechanism. Severity stays low: smaller buffers give finer, not coarser, modulation, so nothing clicks. The harm is non-reproducibility between live buffer sizes and an offline bounce, plus a code comment that overstates the guarantee.

**Note 3.** The defect is real. Low severity fits: the output does differ between block sizes at the sample level, but the change is unlikely to be audible.

Source (plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h):
- The comment at :819-825 says "every buffer size cuts the same sub-blocks and renders the same audio".
- :847 cuts `len = std::min(kModSubBlock - modGridPhase_, numSamples - start)`, with kModSubBlock = 64 (:2167).
- :852 calls `globalModEngine_.process(subCtx, ..., len)` for every piece, including partial ones.
- :855-876 read the offsets right after that call.
- :885-894 store them per sub-block (global cutoff, resonance, master gain).
- :898-906 pass the all-voice offsets to processBlockPoly/Mono for that piece.
- :909 only carries the grid phase forward.

So with a 32-sample buffer, every 64-cell is split into two 32-sample pieces. Each piece re-runs the mod engine and samples its offsets at sample 32 and again at sample 64. A buffer of 64 or a multiple of 64 samples it once, at sample 64.

The mod engine is not invariant to the split. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/modulation_engine.h:226-246 the LFOs advance per sample, which on its own would be split-invariant. But :275-279 take the LFO output as `lfo1LastValue_`, the value at the end of the piece, and :288 `evaluateRoutings(numSamples)` derives the offsets from that. The first 32 samples of a cell therefore use the LFO value at sample 32 at a 32-sample buffer and the value at sample 64 at a 64-sample buffer. The sources processed once per call (Random, Chaos, S&H, PitchFollower, :252-264) are also stepped per call.

The same happens at any buffer size that is not a multiple of 64, for example 100 or 441. The probe's v2 result matches the code exactly: specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1263-1282 compares bs 32, 64 and 2048 against bs 512. Only bs 32 differs (0.136); bs 64 and bs 2048 are bit-exact, as predicted.

Impact:
- The difference is a shift of up to 32 samples (0.67 ms at 48 kHz) in when a stepped modulation value is held. At small buffers the staircase is finer and arguably smoother, never coarser.
- The 0.136 peak sample difference is phase divergence in the filtered waveform, not an added artifact or click.
- Consequence: a 32-sample live buffer, or a host with variable or non-power-of-two buffers, does not reproduce an offline bounce sample for sample.
- The code comment's invariance claim is false, and no test covers this.
- Nothing becomes unstable or non-finite, and the perceptual change is probably below audibility.

Low severity stands.

</details>

### R-153

**Switching the delay to Spectral discards the echoes of notes played during the pre-warm window**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:419-428, 842-891, 956-960, 1260-1266`

**Problem.** setDelayType starts a pre-warm of max(time, 20 ms) + targetLatencySamples_ (6144) samples (line 468-470). During pre-warm the incoming delay is fed the input but its output is discarded (lines 858-860), while the outgoing delay's wet output goes into the compensation delay. When the crossfade completes, completeCrossfade resets the outgoing delay (line 1262). With Spectral active, the normal path only writes to the compensation delays (warmBothCompDelays, line 960) and never reads them, so the outgoing echoes still inside the 6144-sample comp line are never heard either. The 25 ms blip in the probe was emitted by the Spectral delay during pre-warm (discarded) and by Digital into the comp line (never read).

**Why it is wrong.** A delay-type change, including the one triggered by loading a Spectral preset (reset() keeps activeDelayType_, so the next applyDelayParams starts a switch), must not drop signal. The first output of the held-note probe lands exactly at the end of pre-warm (0.181 / 0.384 / 1.131 s for 50 / 250 / 1000 ms, i.e. time + 128 ms).

**Consequence.** After switching to Spectral (or loading a Spectral-delay preset), notes played in the first 'delay time + 128 ms' produce no echo at feedback 0, or start only at the second repeat. That reads as a broken delay right after a preset change.

**Suggested fix.** When the incoming type is Spectral, drain the outgoing comp line (read it) until it empties, or do not discard the incoming delay's output during pre-warm; start the crossfade immediately and let the incoming path's own latency fill. Add a test: delay Digital -> Spectral switch at t=0, blip at 0.1 s, fb 0, mix 1; an echo is present.

**Evidence.** probe fx-spectral-delay:fb0: '-240 in every window (exactly zero output for 3 s)'; fb0.25 'first sound in the 0.5-0.75 s window'; fx-spectral-delay-held: 'first output 0.384 s for 250 ms, 0.181 s for 50 ms, 1.131 s for 1000 ms'. Probe code audit_probes.cpp:2349-2356 sets kDelayTypeId 1.0 (Spectral) at block 0 with the note at 4800. ruinae_effects_chain.h:470 'return static_cast&lt;size_t>(preWarmMs * sampleRate_ / 1000.0) + targetLatencySamples_;'; :858-860 '// Incoming delay processes same input (output discarded, fills buffer)'; :960 'warmBothCompDelays(left, right, numSamples);'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the mechanism in plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h and it is real.

1. setDelayType (392-429) resets the incoming type (425) and starts a pre-warm of preWarmTotalSamples() = max(time, 20 ms)·sr/1000 + targetLatencySamples_ (468-471). targetLatencySamples_ is the spectral delay latency plus the harmonizer's PhaseVocoder latency (150).
2. During pre-warm (842-891), with Digital active and not Spectral, the active output goes through applyCompensation (869). That function writes to both comp pairs and reads compDelay[a] at targetLatencySamples_ (1209-1222), so Digital's echoes are heard about 128 ms late. The incoming Spectral is processed into crossfadeOut* and that output is thrown away (858-860).
3. In the crossfade (892-949), outIsSpectral is false and inIsSpectral is true. Only the outgoing path is compensated (916-918). The incoming Spectral output is used directly, and the crossfade lasts kCrossfadeDurationMs = 30 ms (85, 1255).
4. completeCrossfade (1260-1270) resets the outgoing delay (1262) and makes Spectral active. From then on the normal path only calls warmBothCompDelays (960), which writes to the comp lines and never reads them (1240-1249). So the Digital output still in the comp line (the last targetLatencySamples_, about 128 ms) is never played.

Result: Digital output made in roughly [P-128 ms, P], where P is the end of the pre-warm, never reaches the output. Spectral output made before P was discarded during the pre-warm. For a note played after the switch, its first echo lands at n + time (+ about 21 ms of spectral latency). That echo is lost from both paths when n is in about [switch, switch + 107..128 ms]. That matches the probe: switch at block 0, note at 0.1 s (audit_probes setup as quoted), with silence at fb 0 and the first sound only at the second repeat with fb 0.25. reset() (205-263) clears the pre-warm and crossfade state but leaves activeDelayType_ alone (it is only assigned at 1265 and in its initializer at 1410). So a later setDelayType(Spectral) after a reset does start a switch, as the finding says.

Why downgrade: the consequence is overstated. The finding says notes played in the first "delay time + 128 ms" lose their echo. By the timing above, the affected window is fixed at about 0.1-0.13 s after the switch (plus the 30 ms crossfade edge), whatever the delay time. Notes played before the switch keep their Digital echoes through the comp line, and notes played later than about 128 ms after the switch get Spectral echoes after P. The delay-time-dependent "first output at time + 128 ms" in the held-note probe only reflects the note sitting inside that fixed window.

Cutting the outgoing tail at completeCrossfade is the intended behaviour for every type switch. The extra loss here is only the approximately 128 ms comp-line gap when the incoming type is Spectral. It happens on a transient type switch or preset load. For a preset load it only hits notes played within about 0.1 s of the load. So low severity, not medium.

**Note 2.** I could not refute the defect, but the finding overstates the consequence.

What I confirmed in plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h:
- setDelayType (:419-428) starts a pre-warm of max(D, 20 ms) + targetLatencySamples_ (:468-470). targetLatencySamples_ is the spectral FFT size (spectral_delay.h:604-606, 1024) plus the PhaseVocoder harmonizer latency (:150), 6144 in total.
- During pre-warm (:842-891) the incoming Spectral delay's output is thrown away (:858-860). The outgoing Digital output goes through applyCompensation (:869, :1209-1222), which writes both comp lines and reads 6144 samples back.
- startCrossfade (:1252) runs for 30 ms (kCrossfadeDurationMs, :85). During it the outgoing Digital path is read through applyCompensationSingle (:916). The incoming Spectral output is used directly (:910, :920, nothing is compensated).
- completeCrossfade (:1260-1270) resets the outgoing delay and swaps activeCompIdx_. With Spectral active, the normal path (:956-961) only calls warmBothCompDelays (:1240-1249), which writes and never reads. Whatever Digital echo is still inside the 6144-sample comp line when the crossfade ends is never output.
- For a switch between two non-spectral types, applyCompensation keeps running on the blended signal (:947-948), so the line drains. Only a switch into Spectral drops it.
- No code comment documents this loss, and no test covers it. The only test I found that switches to Spectral is ruinae_effects_chain_test.cpp:678-681, and it checks only that the switch completes.
- So the defect is real and reachable: the user selects Spectral, or loads a preset with a Spectral delay while the current type differs.

Where the finding is wrong, which is why I downgrade it:
- Take an input at time t after the switch (L = 6144, X = 30 ms crossfade, D ≥ 20 ms).
- The Digital echo comes out at t + D + L, so it is heard (fading out) only if t &lt; X.
- The Spectral echo comes out at t + D + 1024 and survives only if that is at or after the pre-warm end, D + L. That means t ≥ L - 1024, about 107 ms at 48 kHz.
- So only input in roughly [30 ms, 107 ms] after the switch loses its echo. That is a window of about 77 ms at 48 kHz (shorter at higher rates, since L is in samples), and it does not depend on D.
- The finding's claim that notes played in the first 'delay time + 128 ms' get no echo is overstated.
- The held-note probe matches this narrower reading. Its first output at D + 128 ms is the end of pre-warm. That output is the Spectral echo of input from about 0.107 s, so only the first ~7 ms of the note (which started at 0.1 s) are missing; the note's echo is not lost wholesale.
- The fb0 blip probe (audit_probes.cpp:2340-2366) puts its 20 ms blip at 0.1 s with the switch at block 0, which is inside the window. It is the worst case of a fresh-instance first-block transient.

In practice the loss is a sub-reaction-time gap of about 77 ms of input, once per switch into Spectral. It is not a broken delay after every preset change, so low severity fits better than medium.

**Note 3.** The mechanism is real. The claimed consequence is overstated: only notes played in a window of about 77 ms lose their echo, not every note in the first "delay time + 128 ms".

Code path for a Digital -> Spectral switch at time S:
- setDelayType (ruinae_effects_chain.h:424-428) starts a pre-warm of max(time, 20 ms) + targetLatencySamples_ (:468-470).
- targetLatencySamples_ = spectralDelay_.getLatencySamples() + harmonizer PhaseVocoder latency (:150). getLatencySamples() returns fftSize_ (spectral_delay.h:604-606), default 1024 (:90). The finding uses 6144 samples, about 128 ms at 48 kHz.
- During pre-warm, the incoming Spectral delay runs and its output is discarded (:858-860). The active Digital output goes through applyCompensation (:868-869 -> :1209-1221), so it is heard about 128 ms late.
- The crossfade lasts 30 ms (kCrossfadeDurationMs, :85; startCrossfade :1252-1257). With Spectral incoming, outgoing Digital still reads its own comp line (:915-919). Spectral is not compensated (:920).
- completeCrossfade (:1260-1270) resets Digital and swaps the comp index. After that, normal Spectral processing only calls warmBothCompDelays (:960 -> :1240-1249), which never reads.
- So Digital echo content still inside the comp line when the crossfade ends is never output, and Spectral output produced before pre-warm ends is thrown away.

Timing of an input at time t (at 48 kHz, with time >= 20 ms):
- Pre-warm ends at PE = S + time + 128 ms.
- The Digital echo reaches the output at t + time + 128 ms. It is audible only before the crossfade ends at PE + 30 ms, so only for t &lt; S + 30 ms.
- The Spectral echo appears at t + time + 21 ms (1024 samples). It is discarded when t &lt; S + 128 - 21 = S + 107 ms.
- Result at feedback 0: inputs in about [S + 30 ms, S + 107 ms] get no echo. That window is about 77 ms, does not depend on delay time, and part of each edge is only faded.
- The probe's blip at 0.1 s (4800 samples) falls inside this window. That explains the measured silence at feedback 0, and why the first sound at feedback 0.25 is the second repeat (0.1 + 0.5 + 0.021 = 0.62 s).

The held-note evidence does not show a large loss. The natural onset of the Spectral echo for a note held from 0.1 s is 0.1 + time + 0.021 s (0.371 s for 250 ms). The probe measured 0.384 s, only about 13 ms late. So "notes played in the first delay time + 128 ms produce no echo" is wrong. Notes played in the first 30 ms keep their Digital echo, and notes played after about 107 ms keep their Spectral echo.

Triggers: switching the type away from a non-Spectral delay (in practice Digital/Tape/PingPong/Granular -> Spectral) while notes are being played, or the first process after loading a Spectral preset when the active type differs. Notes are rarely played within 30-107 ms of a type change or preset load. The result is a dropped echo, not a click, noise or a stuck state.

Verdict: real, but narrow and transient. Downgrade from medium to low.

</details>

### R-156

**Comb filter at maximum resonance has +22 dB gain with no level compensation**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:1667-1671`

**Problem.** updateCombFeedback maps Q linearly to feedback up to 0.98 (peak gain about 1/(1-0.98) = 34 dB at the comb teeth) and applies no output compensation.

**Why it is wrong.** Other filter types top out around +14-17 dBFS at Q 30 in the same sweep. The comb's resonance knob should not push a single voice to +22 dBFS, which relies on the soft limiter and multiplies across 16 voices.

**Consequence.** Raising comb resonance makes the patch about 8 dB louder than any other filter at the same setting, and drives the limiter hard. Six click frames during the sweep (worst ratio 5.7).

**Suggested fix.** Scale the comb output by (1 - feedback) or a measured makeup curve. Add a test: comb res 1.0 sweep peak &lt;= +6 dBFS with the limiter off.

**Evidence.** probe filter:Comb:res1.0: '+22.08 / +22.22 dBFS at 48k (+22.07 / +22.19 at 192k); 6 click frames, worst ratio 5.7 at 48k'. ruinae_voice.h:1668-1670 'const float normalizedQ = std::clamp((q - 0.1f) / 29.9f, 0.0f, 1.0f); const float feedback = normalizedQ * 0.98f; comb.setFeedback(feedback);'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The finding holds on both counts: the code does what it says, and the measurement exists. I recommend downgrading it, because some supporting claims are overstated.

Code (confirmed): plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:1667-1671 maps Q in [0.1, 30] linearly to a feedback of 0..0.98: `normalizedQ = clamp((q-0.1)/29.9, 0, 1); feedback = normalizedQ*0.98f; comb.setFeedback(feedback)`. Two call sites feed it: setActiveFilterResonance (:1435-1436) and prepare (:1253). The modulated path also reaches it through the per-sample resonance clamp to [0.1, 30] at :530-533. processActiveFilter (:1470-1471) returns `filterComb_->process(input)` unscaled, and the caller (:536) writes it straight into mixBuffer_. Nothing compensates the level after it. FeedbackComb::process (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/comb_filter.h:326-362) computes `y = x + g*LP(y[n-D])` and applies no normalization. Its gain at a tooth is 1/(1-g) = 50, about 34 dB, when damping is 0. Damping defaults to 0.0f (plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/filter_params.h:33), so the full peak gain is the default behaviour.

Measurement (confirmed): f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/probe-results.txt:303-309 has Comb res1.0 sweep peaks of +22.08 dBFS at 48k and +22.07 at 192k, parked peaks of +22.22 and +22.19, and 6 click frames with worst ratio 5.7 at 48k. The probe (specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:695-734) plays a triangle at A2, vel 0.8, with the soft limiter off. The parked reading makes sense: at cutoff 20 kHz the delay is 1000/20000 ms, about 2.4 samples. The DC tooth then gives about +28 dB at the 110 Hz fundamental (1/|1-0.98e^{-jwD}| ≈ 25), so a fully open comb at max resonance acts as a large bass boost.

Overstatements, which are the reasons to downgrade:
(1) The finding says the comb is about 8 dB louder than any other filter. The same sweep measured SVF_LP at +16.94 and SVF_HP at +16.31 (probe-results.txt:549, :489), and EnvelopeFilter at +15.54 (:339). The gap is about 5 dB.
(2) No filter type is level-compensated: SVF and EnvelopeFilter also reach +15-17 dBFS uncompensated at max Q. So the comb is the loudest case of a policy that applies to every filter type, not a mistake in one.
(3) The soft limiter is on in normal use, so the result is louder output and harder limiting, not runaway or non-finite output (NaN/Inf count 0, :300 and :305).
(4) The 6 click frames are not shown to come from the gain. They are more plausibly zipper noise from the comb delay jumping once per 64-sample block during the probe's sweep. At 192k there are 0 click frames (:301), so they are not a resonance-gain artefact.

The core claim stands: comb resonance 1.0 adds about 22 dBFS of uncompensated peak level, the loudest of all filter types. It is a level and gain-staging issue, not a correctness or safety defect.
