**Note 2.** The mechanism the finding describes is in the code. ruinae_voice.h:1667-1671 (updateCombFeedback) maps Q [0.1,30] linearly to feedback normalizedQ*0.98. setResonance calls it at :1436. processActiveFilter returns filterComb_->process(input) at :1470-1471 with no makeup or compensation scaling. In the shared primitive, comb_filter.h:353 computes output = input + feedback_*damped, the plain IIR comb, so with damping 0 the peak gain at the teeth is 1/(1-0.98) = 50, about +34 dB. setFeedback clamps only to kMaxCombCoeff 0.9999 (comb_filter.h:35, :272), so nothing downstream limits it. I found no code comment, MANUAL.md text, Ruinae.md text or test that documents or pins comb level as an intended design choice. A grep for comb gain/level/compensation in those files and in plugins/ruinae/tests found nothing.

Reasons to downgrade:
(1) The soft limiter is ON by default (global_params.h:30, softLimit{true}). The probe turns it off explicitly (audit_probes.cpp:702), so the +22 dBFS number is a limiter-off worst case, not what a default patch outputs.
(2) The finding itself says the other resonant types also reach +14-17 dBFS at Q 30 in the same sweep. The SVF path at :1459-1464 is just as uncompensated (Q 30 gives roughly +29.5 dB peak gain). The comb is therefore a level-matching outlier of about 5-8 dB within a family where every resonant filter is uncompensated, not a unique runaway or a stability defect. FeedbackComb is stable for g&lt;1.
(3) I could not check the quoted numbers (+22.08 dBFS, 6 click frames). specs/ruinae-audit/probes/ contains only audit_probes.cpp and no results file. The probe code (audit_probes.cpp:695-737) does match the stated setup: triangle A2, vel 0.8, limiter off, cutoff swept per 64-sample block.
The click frames during the sweep are more plausibly caused by updateCombDelay (:1661-1665) jumping the delay per block than by the gain itself, and that would be a separate issue.

Verdict: the missing compensation is real, but it is a gain-staging and level-matching issue that the default-on limiter mitigates. It is better rated low than medium.

**Note 3.** The code matches the claim. plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:1667-1671 maps Q linearly to feedback with `normalizedQ * 0.98f`. FeedbackComb::setFeedback (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/comb_filter.h:271-273) only clamps to +/-0.9999. The comb output is returned unscaled at ruinae_voice.h:1470-1471 (`return filterComb_ ? filterComb_->process(input) : input;`), and process() at comb_filter.h:353 computes y = x + g*LP(y[n-D]) with no makeup. The only thing that reduces peak gain is damping (setFilterCombDamping, ruinae_voice.h:815-818). Its zero-damping DC/tooth gain is 1/(1-0.98) = 50, about +34 dB.

I checked the measurement in f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/probe-results.txt. The probe setup is in specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:695-734 (triangle A2 at vel 0.8, soft limit OFF, cutoff swept 0 to 1 and then parked). At 48k, res 1.0, it reads:
- Comb: sweep peak +22.08 dBFS, parked +22.22 dBFS, 6 click frames (worst ratio 5.7).
- Other filters at the same setting: SVF_LP sweep +16.94 / parked -5.81, SVF_HP +16.31 / -68.22, EnvelopeFilter +15.54 / -5.81, Ladder -1.93 / -1.84. The SVF types at unity sit at -5.82.
- Comb at res 0.0 sits at -5.82, the same dry level.

The +28 dB parked figure matches the math. With cutoff parked at 20 kHz the delay is about 2.4 samples, so the 110 Hz fundamental sits next to the k=0 tooth: |1 - 0.98 e^{-j0.0346}| = 0.039, a gain of about 25x (+28 dB).

The consequence is real, and the finding understates it. Against the loudest other filter's sweep transient (SVF_LP +16.9) the comb is about 5 dB louder, not 8. In steady state at high cutoff, though, it is about 28 dB above dry and above every other filter type. Even res 0.5 adds about 6 dB (-0.01 vs -5.82 dBFS parked).

I keep severity at medium. The soft limiter is on by default (basePatch sets kSoftLimitId 1.0, and only the probe turns it off), so the output stays bounded and finite. The result is heavy limiter saturation and a large level jump on a user-chosen high-resonance setting, not NaN or clipping past full scale. I found no test or CHANGELOG entry that pins this level as intended.

</details>

### R-158

**Additive oscillator has a -42 dBc inharmonic floor because partials are rounded to the nearest FFT bin**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/additive_oscillator.h:527-529`

**Problem.** Each partial is placed at bin = round(freq * fftSize / sampleRate) of a 1024-point IFFT frame (about 47 Hz bins at 48k). Off-bin partials leak and are corrected only by per-hop phase advance.

**Why it is wrong.** Bin rounding without proper sinusoid synthesis (window-kernel placement or phase-correct per-bin synthesis) gives spectral leakage and inharmonic products. Other tonal types measure at or below -50 dBc.

**Consequence.** An audible noise and inharmonic floor about -42 dBc on every Additive note at A1, A4 and C7.

**Suggested fix.** Synthesize each partial with its window main-lobe kernel at the fractional bin (standard IFFT additive), or use a larger FFT. Add a test: worst non-harmonic &lt;= -60 dBc at A1/A4/C7.

**Evidence.** probe osc:Additive: 'worst non-harmonic dBc -41.9 / -41.2 / -42.1' (threshold &lt;=-50). additive_oscillator.h:528-529 'float binFloat = freq * static_cast&lt;float>(fftSize_) / static_cast&lt;float>(sampleRate_); auto bin = static_cast&lt;size_t>(std::round(binFloat));'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this finding, and the source supports it. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/additive_oscillator.h:528-529 puts each partial into a single bin, `bin = round(freq*fftSize/sampleRate)`, with one complex value A·e^{jφ} (lines 541-547). It never places a window kernel at the fractional bin.

Ruinae uses a 1024-point FFT. oscillator_adapters.h:133 calls `osc_.prepare(sampleRate, 1024)` for AdditiveOscillator, and selectable_oscillator.h:272 instantiates it. Hop size is N/4 = 256 (line 145), with a Hann window and overlap-add (lines 585-591).

Inside each frame, the IFFT therefore produces a sinusoid at the bin centre frequency, not the true one. Only the start phase follows the true frequency: advancePhases (lines 563-567) adds f_true·hop/fs per hop.

Worked example, A4 at 48 kHz: binFloat = 440·1024/48000 = 9.39, which rounds to bin 9 = 421.9 Hz, an 18 Hz error (0.39 bin). Two overlapping frames at the same output sample then differ in phase by 2π·Δf·hop/fs ≈ 0.6 rad. Overlap-adding four such frames at different phases modulates the signal at the hop rate (fs/256 = 187.5 Hz). That creates sidebands that are not harmonics of 440 Hz, which is the inharmonic floor the finding describes.

Pitches near a bin centre suffer less, but A1, A4 and C7 all land well off-centre. The measured -42 dBc is consistent with this mechanism.

Nothing upstream corrects it. The adapter only sets the fundamental, partial count, tilt and inharmonicity. The probe source exists at specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:617, but I did not re-run it.

Severity stays low. The flaw is a design limitation of this FFT-additive oscillator rather than a crash or a stuck note.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. Both the code mechanism and the measurement check out.

Code: dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/additive_oscillator.h:528-529 computes `binFloat = freq*fftSize_/sampleRate_` and rounds it to an integer bin. Lines 546-547 then put the whole partial (amplitude and accumulated phase) into that single bin. Each IFFT frame therefore holds a sinusoid at the bin-centre frequency, which can be up to half a bin away from the real partial frequency. advancePhases() (lines 552-573) moves each partial's phase forward by the real frequency times the hop, so every frame starts at the corrected phase. The Hann overlap-add at 75% overlap (lines 585-591, hop = fftSize/4 per line 145) blends those mistuned frames. The result is amplitude and phase modulation at the hop rate, which shows up as non-harmonic sidebands.

Reachability: Ruinae always prepares this oscillator with a 1024-point FFT (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/oscillator_adapters.h:131-133). At 48 kHz that gives 46.9 Hz bins, so at A1 (55 Hz) the fundamental alone lands well off its bin. That is the normal path for every Additive note.

Measurement: the probe log exists at f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/probe-results.txt:797, 804 and 811, and in the gate shard log f:/tmp/gate/20261116-100221/ruinae_tests-4.log. It reads "worst non-harmonic component dBc = -41.9 / -41.2 / -42.1" at A1, A4 and C7. The probe code is specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:653-660. Pitch error is 0.00 cents, so the alias analysis is centred on the right fundamental.

Nothing guards it or documents it:
- No code comment calls bin rounding an accepted limitation. The FR-019 comment only says that partials landing in the same bin are summed.
- The spec it cites (specs/025-additive-oscillator) no longer exists.
- The unit tests in dsp/tests/unit/processors/additive_oscillator_test.cpp:403-427 measure only the levels at harmonic frequencies (H2/H3 &lt; -60 dB). They use the default 2048-point FFT at 44.1 kHz and never measure inharmonic sidebands, so nothing pins or excludes this behaviour.

Severity stays low. The probe's verdict was "suspicious", not "bad", and the total non-harmonic energy reads -43.9 to -44.2 dB, which passes the probe's own &lt;=-40 threshold.

**Note 3.** The defect is real, and low severity fits.

**The code does what the finding says.** In additive_oscillator.h:528-529, each partial goes to `bin = round(freq*fftSize/sr)`. Lines 541-547 put one complex value into that single bin. Lines 582-590 run the IFFT, apply the Hann window and overlap-add at `hopSize_ = fftSize/4` (line 145). Lines 563-567 advance the phase by the true frequency once per hop. Ruinae always prepares this oscillator with a 1024-point FFT (oscillator_adapters.h:132-133: `osc_.prepare(sampleRate, 1024)`). So inside each frame, every partial plays at its rounded bin frequency, which is up to 0.5 bin (23.4 Hz at 48 kHz) off. Each frame restarts at the true phase.

**The mechanism is slightly different from what the finding says.** The finding calls it "leakage". It is actually a modulation that repeats once per hop. Each output sample is the sum of 4 overlapping frames, and each frame has drifted a different amount since it started. The result is a periodic AM/PM at fs/H = 187.5 Hz. It puts sidebands at ±187.5 Hz (and multiples) around every partial that is off its bin. It also lowers the partial's own level by up to 1.4 dB, depending on how far off the bin it is.

**I checked the size with an analytical model.** I computed the periodic complex gain Σ_k w(u+kH)·e^{-j2πd(u+kH)/N} for N=1024, H=256 and a Hann window, using a node script in my scratchpad (olasb.js). Worst sideband relative to the partial:
- d = 0.1 bin: -55.0 dBc
- d = 0.25 bin: -46.4 dBc
- d = 0.4 bin: -42.2 dBc
- d = 0.5 bin: -40.4 dBc

This matches the reported numbers:
- A4 = 440 Hz falls at bin 9.387 (d ≈ 0.39), and the model predicts about -42 dBc. The probe reads -41.2.
- The default partials all have equal amplitude, so a higher partial near d = 0.5 produces sidebands about 40-42 dB below the fundamental. That explains A1 at -41.9 and C7 at -42.1.

**The quoted measurement is consistent with the probe code.** I read the probe in specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:
- `aliasAnalysis` (lines 448-479) masks a ±6-bin guard around each harmonic in a 65536-point spectrum and reports the worst unmasked bin against the fundamental peak.
- `runOscProbe` (lines 653-660) applies the -50 dBc threshold.

**No test covers this.** dsp/tests/unit/processors/additive_oscillator_test.cpp only checks levels at harmonic positions (H2/H3, tilt, and Nyquist at lines 419-499, 608-701 and 1271). Nothing measures the floor between harmonics, so the floor is not pinned anywhere.

**Why low severity is right.** The artifacts are about 40-42 dB below the fundamental. They sit at fixed ±187.5 Hz offsets, so they are not harmonically related to the note. They are audible as slight roughness or beating on an exposed Additive tone, and the in-voice filter and other partials partly mask them. Nothing becomes unstable, no NaN appears, and level does not explode. This matches "low"; it is neither higher nor lower.

**One correction to the suggested fix.** "Use a larger FFT" alone does not remove the floor. The sideband level depends on the fractional-bin offset d, which stays between 0 and 0.5 at any FFT size, and on the window/hop overlap. A larger FFT only moves the sidebands closer to the partial. The fix that works is to place the window's main-lobe kernel at the fractional bin, or to synthesize each partial in the time domain.

</details>

### R-159

**Formant (FOF) oscillator has period jitter and inharmonic sidebands, because grains trigger only on integer-sample phase wraps**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/formant_oscillator.h:420-422`

**Problem.** triggerGrains() fires when fundamentalPhase_.advance() wraps, i.e. at the integer sample after the wrap, without a sub-sample onset offset. The FOF period is quantised to whole samples and jitters by up to one sample per period.

**Why it is wrong.** Sub-sample grain onset (fractional delay or phase-offset start) is needed for a clean harmonic spectrum. Jitter creates sidebands around a weak fundamental.

**Consequence.** Non-harmonic content of +3.0 dBc at A1 and -20.7 dBc at A4: rough, noisy formant tones.

**Suggested fix.** Start each grain with its fractional phase offset (wrap remainder / increment) applied to the grain envelope and carrier. Add a test: worst non-harmonic &lt;= -40 dBc at A2-A5.

**Evidence.** probe osc:Formant:A1/A4: 'A1 +3.0 dBc (-28 dB energy); A4 -20.7 dBc (-22.8 dB)'. formant_oscillator.h:420-422 '// Advance fundamental phase and trigger grains on wrap / if (fundamentalPhase_.advance()) { triggerGrains(); }'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The code does what the finding says.

- dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/formant_oscillator.h:420-423: `process()` calls `triggerGrains()` only when `fundamentalPhase_.advance()` returns true.
- dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/phase_utils.h:160-167: `PhaseAccumulator::advance()` does `phase += increment; if (phase >= 1.0) { phase -= 1.0; return true; }`. The remainder left after the wrap (the sub-sample position of the true onset) is never passed out or used.
- formant_oscillator.h:469-482 and 507-532: `triggerGrains()` -> `initializeGrain()` resets every grain the same way: `grain.phase = 0.0f`, `envelope = 0`, `sampleCounter = 0`. No fractional offset goes into the envelope (attack at :542-547 is indexed by the integer `sampleCounter`) or into the carrier (:555 `sin(kTwoPi * grain.phase)`).
- So each grain starts on an integer sample, and the gap between onsets is floor or ceil of fs/f0. At A4 / 48 kHz, fs/f0 = 109.0909 = 1200/11. The gaps follow a 109/110 pattern that repeats every 11 periods, so the output repeats every 25 ms (40 Hz). That puts spectral lines at multiples of 40 Hz that are not multiples of 440 Hz, which is real inharmonic content.
- The phase accumulator is double precision, so the pitch averages out correctly. The probe agrees: it measures cents separately, and the finding is about jitter only.

The probe measurement is valid:
- specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:402-414 uses a 4-term Blackman-Harris window over a 65536-point FFT.
- :448-479 marks ±6 bins (about ±4.4 Hz) around each harmonic as harmonic. The main lobe is ±4 bins, so window leakage cannot explain the result.

One caveat on the headline number:
- `worstDbc` (:476) is measured against the fundamental's peak. A FOF fundamental is weak because the formants sit far above A1, so "+3.0 dBc at A1" overstates how bad it sounds.
- The energy ratio (`totalDb`, -28 dB at A1 and -22.8 dB at A4) is the better measure of severity.
- The ratio should get worse as pitch rises: 1 sample of jitter is a larger share of a shorter period, and the phase error 2*pi*f_formant/fs is fixed. The measured trend matches (A4 worse than A1 by energy).

Severity stays low: the defect is real, but it is a tone-quality flaw, not a stability or real-time-safety problem.

**Note 2.** The defect is real, and nothing guards it or documents it as intentional. I checked the code against the claim:

- formant_oscillator.h:420-423: `if (fundamentalPhase_.advance()) { triggerGrains(); }`.
- phase_utils.h:160-167: `PhaseAccumulator::advance()` does `phase -= 1.0` and returns only a bool. The wrap remainder, which is the sub-sample onset, never reaches the caller.
- formant_oscillator.h:507-531 (`initializeGrain`): each grain starts with `phase = 0.0f`, `envelope = 0`, `sampleCounter = 0`. No fractional offset is applied to the carrier or to the attack envelope (lines 542-547).
- Result: grain onsets land on whole samples. At A4 (440 Hz, 44.1 kHz) the period is 100.227 samples, so onsets fall 100 or 101 samples apart. At A1 the period is 801.82 samples, and the onset pattern repeats about every 11 periods. That puts discrete lines at roughly f0/11 spacing, which are not harmonics of f0.
- Magnitude check (my own estimate, not a run): rounding to the nearest sample gives an rms timing error of about 0.29 sample. At F1/F2 (600 and 1040 Hz) that is about 0.03-0.05 rad of carrier phase, roughly -28 to -32 dB of non-harmonic energy. This agrees with the quoted A1 figure of -28 dB energy. The +3 dBc reading at A1 is plausible because the 55 Hz fundamental carries little energy when the formants sit at 600 Hz and above.
- At A4 the period is about 100 samples and a grain lasts 882 samples (20 ms at line 191), so about 8.8 grains overlap. The pool holds only 8 (line 189), so `findOldestGrain` (lines 485-504) cuts grains off early. That is probably a second contributor to the -22.8 dB at A4. The jitter mechanism stays valid.

Context lens:
- The class header (lines 1-22) and the Ruinae path through selectable_oscillator.h:281 and oscillator_adapters.h:170 (which only calls `setFundamental`) contain no comment or design note accepting this quantisation.
- No upstream compensation exists, such as oversampling or fractional onset handling in the adapter.
- formant_oscillator_test.cpp checks only where the dominant peak or a formant-region peak lands (lines 278-307, 350-407, 633-656). No test pins the non-harmonic floor, so nothing protects against or documents this behaviour.

Reachability: OscType::Formant is user-selectable in Ruinae, so this is reachable in a real host. Low severity fits: the effect is roughness and inharmonic content, not instability or unsafe output.

**Note 3.** I could not refute this finding. Both the code and the measurement support it.

**Code**
- `dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/formant_oscillator.h:420-423`: `process()` calls `triggerGrains()` only when `fundamentalPhase_.advance()` reports a wrap, so each grain starts on the integer sample after the wrap.
- `initializeGrain` (:507-532) always starts the grain at `grain.phase = 0.0f`, `envelope = 0`, `sampleCounter = 0`. It applies no fractional offset from the wrap remainder, and nothing else in the file does either (read :1-642).
- The result is that onsets fall on whole samples. When the period is not a whole number of samples, the spacing alternates between floor and ceil of the period. The pulse train then repeats only over a longer cycle (A4 at 48 kHz: 109.09 samples, so the pattern repeats every 11 periods), which puts sidebands at multiples of f0/11 between the harmonics.
- Ruinae reaches this code unchanged. `oscillator_adapters.h:169-171` forwards the note pitch to `setFundamental`, and `:374-385` calls `osc_.processBlock` and then applies a flat 2.7x gain.

**Measurement**
- `f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/probe-results.txt` has the quoted numbers:
  - :830/:833 A1: energy -28.0 dB, worst component +3.0 dBc
  - :837/:840 A4: energy -22.8 dB, worst component -20.7 dBc
- The C7 case acts as a control for the cause. It reads -89.2 dB energy and -93.7 dBc (:844/:847) because `kMaxFundamental` = 2000 Hz (:195) clamps 2093 Hz to 2000 Hz. At 48 kHz that is exactly 24 samples per period, so there is no onset jitter and the sidebands disappear.
- The method is sound: a Blackman-Harris window, ±6-bin harmonic guards and pitch fitted per note (`audit_probes.cpp:402-479`, :655-658). PolyBLEP, Wavetable and PD read -53 to -99 dB under the same setup, which rules out a probe artefact.

**Impact and caveat**
- The "+3.0 dBc" figure overstates the problem. `aliasAnalysis` measures against the h=1 bin (:461, :476), and FOF puts very little energy at the 55 Hz fundamental, far below F1 at 600 Hz.
- The meaningful numbers are the energy ratios: about 4-7 % of the amplitude is inharmonic, a roughness that is audible on every note whose period is not a whole number of samples.

**Coverage**
- `formant_oscillator_test.cpp` only checks that peaks land near harmonics (:278-307, :350-407, :633-656). No test bounds non-harmonic content.

**Severity**
- Low fits. It is a timbre defect in one of 10 oscillator types, with no crash, NaN or stuck-note risk.

</details>

### R-161

**Spectral delay RNG is seeded from the object address, so presets using it render non-deterministically**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/effects/spectral_delay.h:235-238`

**Problem.** prepare() seeds rng_ with reinterpret_cast&lt;uintptr_t>(this) ^ sampleRate. The phase-randomisation and decorrelation sequence therefore differs on every instantiation and every run.

**Why it is wrong.** Rendering the same preset twice should give the same audio (offline bounces, freeze, A/B, render tests). A fixed or state-derived seed keeps per-instance variety without run-to-run randomness.

**Consequence.** Textures/Spectral_Wash differs by 0.145 peak between two fresh loads, and round-trip checks have to fall back to an RMS tolerance (0.98 dB).

**Suggested fix.** Seed from a constant, optionally mixed with a per-channel or per-engine index. Add a test: two fresh processors loading Spectral_Wash render bit-identically.

**Evidence.** probe preset:Textures/Spectral_Wash: 'NON-deterministic (two fresh loads differ by 0.1451), RMS compared ... round-trip RMS diff dB = 0.98'. spectral_delay.h:237-238 'rng_.seed(static_cast&lt;uint32_t>(reinterpret_cast&lt;uintptr_t>(this) ^ static_cast&lt;uintptr_t>(sampleRate)));'. tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:6902 '"Spectral Wash" - ... spectral delay'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The source shows the claimed behaviour.
- The seed: dsp/include/krate/dsp/effects/spectral_delay.h:235-238 seeds rng_ (Xorshift32, declared at :1027) from `reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(this) ^ sampleRate`. The comment says this is meant to give each instance its own sequence, but the side effect is that the sequence depends on heap address and ASLR.
- Where the seed is used: prepare() fills stereoPhaseL_/R_ from it at :246-251. reset() draws fresh phases from the same continuing stream at :296-299. processFrame adds a random walk to every bin, every frame, at :832-835.
- The phases reach the output: :989-992 applies stereoPhase * stereoWidth whenever stereoWidth > 0.001.
- Ruinae never sets a deterministic seed. A grep of plugins/ruinae/src finds no seedRng call. ruinae_effects_chain.h only calls spectralDelay_.prepare (:124), reset (:216, :987, :1290) and the setters (:616-637). seedRng (:312) exists only as a test hook.
- The preset uses the effect with width on: tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:6937-6941 sets Spectral_Wash to delay type 4 (Spectral), mix 0.35, spectralWidth 0.9. That is well above 0.001, so the random phases are audible.
- The measurement method is sound: specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1928-1966 builds two fresh Rigs, loads the same bytes, takes the max sample difference, and flags anything above 1e-7 as NON-deterministic.
- Other random sources do not explain the difference. In dsp/include/krate/dsp, spectral_delay.h:237 is the only RNG seeded from `this`. Other RNGs use fixed or derived seeds (unison_engine kPhaseSeed, timevar_comb_bank 12345+i*7919, pattern_freeze 12345). That supports attributing the 0.145 peak difference to the spectral delay, though I did not trace every Ruinae random source (the Random mod source, the SpectralFreeze osc).

Refinement to the suggested fix: a constant seed in prepare() is not enough. reset() keeps drawing from the running stream (:296-299), so the same instance would still render differently after a reset or a delay-type switch (ruinae_effects_chain.h:987, :1290). The fix should also reseed rng_ at the top of reset().

Severity stays low. This is a reproducibility problem, not a crash, NaN or real-time violation, and the round-trip level difference was 0.98 dB.

**Note 2.** The finding holds up. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/effects/spectral_delay.h:235-238, prepare() seeds rng_ with reinterpret_cast&lt;uintptr_t>(this) ^ sampleRate, and that RNG then fills stereoPhaseL_/R_ (lines 246-251). processSpectralFrame also takes a fresh RNG step for every bin on every frame (834-835), and the stereo width uses that phase walk. A grep finds no other `reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(this)` seed anywhere in dsp/include/krate/dsp. The only deterministic way in is seedRng() (308-319), and its own comment says it "should only be called in tests". Ruinae never calls it: in plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_effects_chain.h, spectralDelay_ is only prepared (124), reset (216, 987, 1290) and given parameters (455-637). Nothing guards against this upstream and nothing pins it.

The probe supports the attribution. In specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1926-1966, two fresh Rigs load the same bytes and are compared sample by sample, so selfDiff 0.145 is a real run-to-run difference. tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:6902-6941 configures Spectral_Wash with delay type 4 (Spectral) and spectralWidth 0.9. The preset's other random source is the Random mod source, and processors/random_source.h:51/59/164 seeds that with a fixed kSeed, so it is deterministic. The spectral delay's address seed is therefore the plausible cause.

There is a mitigating context. The comment at 235-236 calls the per-instance seed intentional ("ensures different instances produce different random sequences"), and reset() at 294-299 deliberately re-randomises each time ("each reset produces new random starting phases"). That covers per-instance variety. Neither comment argues for render-to-render non-reproducibility, which hurts offline bounce, freeze and A/B, and no spec decision I found accepts it.

The suggested fix is incomplete. A constant seed in prepare() is not enough, because reset() keeps drawing from the same RNG stream: a reset that follows setActive or a delay-type switch (ruinae_effects_chain.h:987/1290) would still give different phases from one render to the next. reset() also has to re-seed. The severity of low stays the same: this is effect texture, not a correctness or safety failure.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. dsp/include/krate/dsp/effects/spectral_delay.h:235-238 seeds `rng_` with `reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(this) ^ sampleRate`. Because of ASLR and heap placement, the address changes on every instantiation and every process run. The RNG drives two things:
- the initial stereo phase offsets in ±π/2 (lines 246-251)
- a per-frame random walk on every bin in processSpectralFrame (lines 832-847)

reset() (lines 296-299) also re-draws the phases from the running RNG state, so even one instance renders differently after each reset.

Ruinae uses this class directly: ruinae_effects_chain.h:1407 `SpectralDelay spectralDelay_;`. A grep of plugins/ruinae/src finds no seedRng call. The deterministic test hook, seedRng at lines 312-319, is documented as tests-only.

The finding blames this seed for the measured 0.145 peak difference, and I checked the other candidates:
- This is the only `uintptr_t>(this)` seed under dsp/include.
- The Random mod source that Spectral_Wash uses has a fixed seed: random_source.h:51/59 `rng_.seed(kSeed)`.
- The DSP headers contain no random_device, time-based or rand() seeding.

The probe (specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1928-1966) builds two fresh Rigs from the same bytes and compares their peak sample difference. The preset sets `delay.type = 4 // Spectral` (tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp:6936-6939). So the measured non-determinism comes from this seed.

Impact: the effect is real. Offline bounces, A/B tests and render tests of presets that use the Spectral delay cannot be reproduced exactly, and the round-trip RMS differs by about 1 dB. The difference is only in phase decorrelation and texture, though. It does not cause instability, a NaN, a level explosion or a stuck state. The comment at lines 235-236 also shows the per-instance variety was intended; run-to-run randomness is a side effect of it. Low severity is appropriate, so no adjustment.

</details>

### R-162

**Release 0 ms cuts the voice in about 3 samples (envelope minimum 0.1 ms), with no declick ramp**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/env_params.h:27-31`

**Problem.** Env times map x^3*10000 ms, so normalized 0 = 0 ms, which ADSREnvelope clamps to kMinEnvelopeTimeMs = 0.1 ms (envelope_utils.h:51, adsr_envelope.h:134). A sustained sine is cut in about 5 samples at 48k.

**Why it is wrong.** Most synths enforce a minimum declick (about 1-3 ms) on note-off, even at release 0, so a held tone does not end on a step.

**Consequence.** A click at note-off whenever release is at its minimum (jump ratio 2.80).

**Suggested fix.** Raise the effective minimum release (or add a fixed 1-2 ms declick fade in the VCA) for the amp envelope. Add a test: release 0, note-off jump ratio &lt;= 1.5.

**Evidence.** probe lifecycle:note-off-edge (release 0 ms): 'jump ratio 2.80 (4 outlier samples); the tail ends in 0.06 ms'. env_params.h:31 'return std::clamp(v * v * v * 10000.0f, 0.0f, 10000.0f);'. envelope_utils.h:51 'inline constexpr float kMinEnvelopeTimeMs = 0.1f;'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The finding holds. I traced the path from the parameter to the output.

1. Mapping: plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/env_params.h:29-31 `envTimeFromNormalized` returns `clamp(v*v*v*10000, 0, 10000)`, so a normalized release of 0 gives 0 ms.

2. Delivery: plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:101 calls `engine_.set##Prefix##Release(ld((pack).releaseMs))`. That reaches ruinae_engine.h:1399-1402 `setAmpRelease`, which only rejects NaN/Inf and has no minimum, and then calls each voice's `getAmpEnvelope().setRelease(ms)`.

3. Envelope: dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/adsr_envelope.h:132-135 `setRelease` clamps to `kMinEnvelopeTimeMs`, which is 0.1 ms (envelope_utils.h:51). At 48 kHz that is 4.8 samples. Both release paths end within a few samples:
   - Table path (:498): `logPhaseInc_ = 1/max(1, 0.1e-3*48000)`, about 0.21, so the release lasts about 5 samples.
   - One-pole path (:384-388): it drops below `kEnvelopeIdleThreshold` even sooner.
   - Either way the stage becomes Idle, which matches the measured "tail ends in 0.06 ms", about 3 samples.

4. VCA: plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:464 multiplies the voice output by `ampEnv_.process()` per sample. `noteOff()` (:291-299) only gates the envelopes off, and once the envelope is Idle, :369-372 zero-fills the block. I found no declick or minimum-release fade anywhere on the voice note-off path.

5. Measurement: the quoted figure comes from specs/ruinae-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:899-927 ("AuditProbe voice edges attack0 release0"). It sets `kAmpEnvReleaseId` to 0.0 on a sine A4 at 48 kHz and measures the note-off jump ratio. The result, 2.80, falls in that probe's "suspicious" band (above 1.5, at most 3).

The mechanism is confirmed. The one argument against it is a design reading: a user who dials release to 0 ms may expect a hard stop. Nothing in the code or comments documents that as intended, though, and the attack side carries the same 0.1 ms floor. Low severity is the right level, so no adjustment.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this. The source confirms it, and nothing upstream or downstream guards it.

(1) Mapping. plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/env_params.h:29-31 maps envTimeFromNormalized(v) to clamp(v^3*10000, 0, 10000), so normalized 0 gives 0 ms. The parameter is registered from 0 (env_params.h:209), and plugin_ids.h:358 documents kAmpEnvReleaseId as "0-10000ms".

(2) Envelope floor. ADSREnvelope::setRelease (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/adsr_envelope.h:132-135) clamps to kMinEnvelopeTimeMs = 0.1f (envelope_utils.h:51). calcEnvCoefficients (envelope_utils.h:96-99) then uses rate = max(0.1e-3*fs, 1), which is 4.8 samples at 48 kHz. With the exponential ratio kDefaultTargetRatioDR = 1e-4 the one-pole drops almost at once. processRelease (adsr_envelope.h:350-391) zeroes the output and goes Idle once output &lt; kEnvelopeIdleThreshold = 1e-4. The table and log paths also take max(1, 0.1ms*fs) samples (adsr_envelope.h:498, 506). The ramp therefore lasts a handful of samples, matching the probe's "tail ends in 0.06 ms".

(3) No declick downstream. RuinaeVoice::noteOff (plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h:291-299) only gates the envelopes. The VCA at ruinae_voice.h:621-623 is output = sample * ampEnvVal * expressionVolume_, with no extra smoothing or fade. isActive() is simply ampEnv_.isActive() (ruinae_voice.h:335-337), and processBlock returns silence once the envelope is Idle (ruinae_voice.h:369-372). No minimum release or declick exists for the amp path anywhere in plugins/ruinae: a grep for declick or minimum release found none. Other modules do enforce floors, e.g. TranceGate kMinReleaseMs = 1 ms (trance_gate.h:101) and filter env release 1-5000 ms (filter_params.h:43). Only the amp env goes down to 0.

(4) Documentation. MANUAL.md:459 lists Release as "0-10,000 ms | Time from note-off to silence". Neither the manual, a code comment nor a test documents a cut at release 0 as intentional. No test pins note-off click-freedom at minimum release. ruinae_engine_integration_test.cpp:1049 uses 10 ms.

The behaviour is reachable in any host by turning Release fully down. An argument for "intentional" is that a near-instant release is what the user dialled in, and some synths do click there. That supports keeping the severity low, not refuting the finding. Minor inaccuracy: the title says "about 3 samples" while the body says about 5 at 48k; the code gives a ~4.8-sample time constant.

**Note 3.** The mechanism is real, but the claimed consequence only shows up at an extreme setting the user picks deliberately.

Confirmed:
- env_params.h:29-31 maps normalized 0 to 0 ms with `v*v*v*10000`.
- ADSREnvelope::setRelease (adsr_envelope.h:132-135) clamps that to kMinEnvelopeTimeMs = 0.1 ms (envelope_utils.h:51).
- In table mode, enterRelease (adsr_envelope.h:493-498) sets `logPhaseInc_ = 1/max(1, 0.1e-3*fs)`, about 1/4.8 at 48 kHz. processRelease (adsr_envelope.h:350-365) therefore reaches `logPhase_ >= 1` and goes Idle in about 5 samples. The non-table one-pole path is just as short.
- Nothing in the voice adds a declick. RuinaeVoice multiplies by ampEnv_.process() (ruinae_voice.h:464), and once the envelope is idle the next block is zero-filled (ruinae_voice.h:369-371).
- The probe's jump ratio of 2.80 is consistent with this.

Why the impact is smaller than claimed:
- It only happens when amp release is at the very bottom of the knob. Normalized 0.0215 gives 0.1 ms, and normalized 0.05 gives 1.25 ms (x^3 law).
- No factory preset gets near it. Every `ampEnv.releaseMs` assignment in tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp is 50 ms or more (grep found no assignment under 10 ms).
- A literal "0 ms release" is a gate-style setting the user asks for on purpose, and many synths click there too. So this is a design or polish choice, not a defect in a default or shipped sound.
- The voice does get a short fade of about 5 samples, not a pure step.

Keep it as a polish item, one notch below "low".

</details>

### R-163

**uidesc-inventory --check fails on the Ruinae editor: 38 overlaps, 26 out-of-bounds**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/resources/editor.uidesc:-`
- **Also flagged by:** measured, measured, measured, measured

**Problem.** The uidesc inventory check exits 1 for plugins/ruinae/resources/editor.uidesc. Many of the flagged pairs are deliberate (labels under knobs, stacked mod-type groups, the off-screen settings drawer), but several are real clipping or overlap (see the per-template findings).

**Why it is wrong.** A clean check, or an allow-list for deliberate stacking, is needed so real layout defects are not lost in the noise.

**Consequence.** Real clipped or overlapping controls ship unnoticed, and the check cannot be used as a gate.

**Suggested fix.** Fix the real defects listed below, then add the deliberate stacks and overlays to an allow-list so --check exits 0.

**Evidence.** lint: 'uidesc-inventory --check: UIDESC DEFECTS {"overlap":38,"out-of-bounds":26}, exit 1' (f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/lint-uidesc.log).

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. The quoted measurement is real. f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/lint-uidesc.log ends with `UIDESC DEFECTS {"overlap":38,"out-of-bounds":26}`. tools/uidesc-inventory.js:313 exits 1 when `--check` finds any defect.

Ruinae has no allow-list. The tool supports one (`--allow <json>`, applyAllowList at tools/uidesc-inventory.js:179-192), but only Disrumpo has a file (plugins/disrumpo/tests/uidesc_overlaps_allowed.json) and a CMake test in plugins/disrumpo/tests/CMakeLists.txt. Searching the repo for uidesc-inventory found nothing for Ruinae, so its deliberate stacks (labels under knobs, the off-screen settings drawer at x=1400 width 220) are reported together with the real defects. The check therefore cannot be used as a gate.

At least two flagged items are real layout defects in the source:
1. editor.uidesc:4016 declares MonoGroup as a CViewContainer at origin 8,36 with size 120x18. Inside it, editor.uidesc:4046-4047 places the MonoPortaMode COptionMenu at origin 94,0 with size 43x18. Its right edge is at 137 against a 120 px parent, so 17 px of the dropdown is clipped.
2. editor.uidesc:3494-3495 puts the ArpMode COptionMenu at 136,14 with size 80x18 (spanning x 136-216). editor.uidesc:3499-3501 puts the "Octaves" label at 204,16, so the two overlap by 12 px.

The log also lists the Tab_Seq "Rate" label hanging off its parent's left edge ("-6,28 size 40,10 in parent 48,38"). I did not open that one in the source.

The finding is accurate. Low severity fits: these are cosmetic and tooling problems with no effect on audio or state.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. Both the measurement and part of the substance hold up.

1. **The quoted lint output is real.** f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/lint-uidesc.log ends with `UIDESC DEFECTS {"overlap":38,"out-of-bounds":26}`.

2. **There is no allow-list for Ruinae.** tools/uidesc-inventory.js:20-25 and :179-192 already support `--allow <json>`, and Disrumpo uses one (plugins/disrumpo/tests/uidesc_overlaps_allowed.json, wired into a ctest). Ruinae has no such file under plugins/ruinae/tests and no uidesc test in its CMake. So nothing records the deliberate stacks as intentional, and no spec, manual or code comment does either.

3. **Some of the flagged items are real clipping, not deliberate stacking:**

Its child COptionMenu MonoPortaMode (:4046-4054) has origin 94,0 and size 43,18, so it spans x 94..137. The container clips 17 of its 43 px whenever Voice Mode = Mono. The controller only toggles visibility here (controller_verify_view.cpp:1012-1016) and never resizes the group, so nothing at runtime corrects this.

The same layout repeats for voices 2-4, which accounts for 16 of the out-of-bounds hits. controller_verify_view.cpp:863 only stores the row pointer.
   - **Arp Pattern menu.** At editor.uidesc:3495-3502, the ArpMode menu spans x 136..216 and the "Octaves" label starts at x=204, so the two overlap by 12 px.

4. **Many other hits are deliberate,** as the finding itself says: labels under knobs, the stacked Phaser/Flanger/Chorus groups, and the off-screen settings drawer at x=1400.

The finding's core claim stands: `--check` cannot pass, there is no allow-list, and real clipping is buried in the noise.

On the consequence: "cannot be used as a gate" is accurate. The tool is not a CI gate for Ruinae today; only workflows call it. The real user-visible defect (the clipped portamento-mode menu) is cosmetic.

Severity stays low.

**Note 3.** The measurement is real. In f:/tmp/ruinae-audit/lint-uidesc.log, line 130 reads `UIDESC DEFECTS {"overlap":38,"out-of-bounds":26}`, and lines 66-129 list each flagged pair. Most of them are deliberate, as the finding admits. So the stated consequence holds: --check exits 1, and the real defects sit among roughly 60 deliberate flags. ### R-164

**Tab_Fx: the 16 Harmonizer voice knobs sit at y=-2 in their 34-px row and are clipped by 2 px; several labels lie outside their parents**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured (verify round measured)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/resources/editor.uidesc:3051-3070`

**Problem.** Inside CViewContainer 'HarmonizerVoice1' (origin 8,104, size 320,34), the ArcKnobs HarmonizerVoice1Level/Pan (and Delay/Detune, voices 1-4) are at origin (122,-2) / (158,-2) with size 22,22, so their top 2 px fall outside the container. The lint also flags CTextLabel Cutoff (178,36) and Reso (234,36), 40x10 in a 1384x44 parent, CTextLabel Rate at -6,28 (x3) in 80x40 parents, and Time at -6,30 in a 110x42 parent.

**Why it is wrong.** VSTGUI clips children to the container rect, so the arcs' top edge and the out-of-bounds label text are cut off.

**Consequence.** Visibly clipped knob arcs and truncated labels in the FX tab.

**Suggested fix.** Move the knobs to y>=0 (or grow the row), and move the labels inside their parents.

**Evidence.** lint: 'out-of-bounds: HarmonizerVoice1-4 Level/Pan/Delay/Detune ArcKnobs (16 views) at y=-2 size 22,22 in parent 320,34'. editor.uidesc: '&lt;view class="CViewContainer" origin="8, 104" size="320, 34" custom-view-name="HarmonizerVoice1"' ... '&lt;view class="ArcKnob" origin="122, -2" size="22, 22" control-tag="HarmonizerVoice1Level"'.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** The layout facts are correct, but the finding overstates how visible the clipping is.

Confirmed from source: editor.uidesc:3052 declares CViewContainer HarmonizerVoice1 at origin 8,104, size 320,34. Lines 3062, 3065, 3068 and 3071 place the ArcKnobs Level, Pan, Delay and Detune at x 122/158/194/230, y=-2, size 22x22. Voices 2-4 repeat this at 3091+, 3131+ and 3170+, which gives the 16 knobs. Line 2520 is the 1384x44 Global Filter strip; its Cutoff and Reso labels at 2535 and 2541 sit at y=36 with height 10, so they reach 46 and overflow by 2 px. Lines 2602/2609 put a Rate label at -6,28 inside an 80x40 PhaserRateGroup, and the same pattern repeats at 2711, 2795 and 3599. Lines 2908/2915 put the Time label at -6,30 in a 110x42 DelayTimeGroup. VSTGUI clips each child to its container's rect, so whatever is drawn outside the parent is lost.

The finding is wrong about how much drawn content falls outside. In plugins/shared/src/ui/arc_knob.h, getArcRadius (267-271) is min(w,h)/2 - indicatorLength_/2, with indicatorLength_ = 4.0 (541). For a 22-px knob that gives radius 9, centred 11 px from the knob's top edge. With arcLineWidth_ = 1.0 (542), the top of the arc stroke covers knob-local y 1.5..2.5. In the parent (knob top at y=-2) that is -0.5..+0.5. The tick drawn by drawIndicator (376-390) is 2 px wide with a round cap. At value 0.5 it points straight up and reaches knob-local y=1, which is parent y=-1. That is the default for Pan and Detune (3066, 3072). So the top 2 px of the knob view lose only a half-pixel anti-aliased edge of the 1-px arc, plus 1 px of the tick's round cap when the knob sits near centre. The arcs are not cut off by 2 px.

The Rate and Time labels are 40 px wide, start at x=-6 and centre their text (text-alignment="center"). A 4-letter word in the small font is about 20 px wide and lands near x 4..24, inside the parent. Only the empty left padding is out of bounds, so no text is truncated there. Cutoff and Reso lose the bottom 2 px of a 10-px label box. Those words have no descenders, so the visible effect is marginal at most.

Verdict: the out-of-bounds positions exist and a little drawn content is clipped (half a pixel of arc edge, 1 px of the tick at default Pan and Detune, the bottom of the Cutoff and Reso label boxes). This is cosmetic, and the claimed consequences ("2 px of arcs cut off", "truncated labels") are overstated. Not refuted; severity downgraded.

**Note 2.** The geometry is real and nothing marks it as intentional, but the visible effect is much smaller than the finding says. In plugins/ruinae/resources/editor.uidesc:3052-3073, the CViewContainer HarmonizerVoice1 (320x34) holds four 22x22 ArcKnobs at y=-2 (3062, 3065, 3068, 3071). No allow list or comment explains this: there is no uidesc allow file under plugins/ruinae/tests, and the --allow option in tools/uidesc-inventory.js only covers overlaps anyway. So the out-of-bounds lint hit is a genuine defect, not a design decision.

However, ArcKnob does not draw to the edge of its view (plugins/shared/src/ui/arc_knob.h). getArcRadius (267-271) is dim/2 - indicatorLength_/2 = 11 - 2 = 9, with indicatorLength_ = 4 and arcLineWidth_ = 1 (541-542). The knob centre is at container y = -2 + 11 = 9, so the top of the arc sits at y=0. Only half a pixel of the 1-px guide stroke falls outside the container. The indicator (376-391) runs from the arc radius inward with a 2-px round cap, so about 1 px of the cap is clipped when it points straight up. That happens at the default 0.5 of Pan and Detune. The real loss is about 0.5-1 px of anti-aliased stroke, not the "top 2 px" of the knob.

The label claims are mostly not visible. The Rate labels (2609, 2711, 2795, 3599) and the Time label (2915) sit at x=-6 with width 40 and centred text, so the short words are drawn around x=14 and no ink falls at x&lt;0. Nothing is truncated there. The Cutoff and Reso labels (2535, 2541) at y=36 with height 10 in a 44-px parent lose their bottom 2 px of rect. With a NormalFontSmaller (about 10 px) baseline near y≈8.5, at most a sub-pixel sliver of glyph without descenders is cut.

Verdict: a valid but cosmetic layout-hygiene finding. Moving the knobs to y>=0 (or growing the row) is still the right fix. The stated consequence, "visibly clipped knob arcs and truncated labels", is overstated, so the severity should drop to info or trivial.

**Note 3.** The geometry is real, but the visible consequence is much smaller than claimed.

Knobs (editor.uidesc:3052-3073): the HarmonizerVoice1 container is 320x34 at (8,104). Its Level/Pan/Delay/Detune ArcKnobs are 22x22 at (122|158|194|230, -2), so the view rects do stick 2 px above the container. Whether the knob drawing is cut depends on what ArcKnob paints in those 2 px. In plugins/shared/src/ui/arc_knob.h, getArcRect/getArcRadius (256-271) give arcRadius = min(w,h)/2 - indicatorLength_/2 = 11 - 2 = 9, because indicatorLength_ defaults to 4.0 (arc_knob.h:541). The guide/value arc stroke is 1.0 px (arcLineWidth_, :542). Its top edge therefore sits at view y = 1.5, which is container y = -0.5: only half a pixel of the arc stroke is clipped. The pointer is drawn with a 2 px round-cap line out to arcRadius (arc_knob.h:382-390), so its tip reaches view y = 1, container y = -1. About 1 px of the pointer is lost, and only when it points near 12 o'clock. That happens at the 0.5 defaults of Pan and Detune (uidesc:3066, 3072). The mod arc is drawn inside the main arc (:351). Net effect: at most 0.5-1 logical px of stroke is cut, and only at the topmost point. The claimed 2 px of knob is not lost.

Labels:
- Cutoff/Reso (uidesc:2535, 2541): 40x10 at y=36 in the 1384x44 strip (2520), so the bottom 2 px of the label box are clipped. The glyphs are 'Cutoff'/'Reso' with no descenders, vertically centred in 10 px. At most the bottom edge of the glyphs is shaved, if anything.
- Rate (2609, and the same pattern at 2711, 2795, 3599) and Time (2915): these are only x = -6 overflows of a 40-px-wide, text-alignment="center" box. Centred 4-letter text about 18-20 px wide covers roughly x = 4..24 of the box, which is parent x = -2..18 at worst. In practice the glyphs fall inside the parent, so no text is truncated. The y extent fits (28+10 = 38 &lt;= 40; 30+10 = 40 &lt;= 42).

The 'truncated labels' consequence therefore does not occur for Rate/Time and is marginal for Cutoff/Reso. The 'visibly clipped knob arcs' amount to a sub-pixel to 1-px loss at the top of four knobs per row. The finding is real as layout/lint hygiene: the views are out of bounds, and moving them inside is correct. Its impact is below the stated low severity.

</details>
