### R-167

**A noteId note-on whose velocity rounds to 0 stamps its noteId onto the newest sounding voice; its note-off then releases that held note and leaks the allocator slot**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** followup:allocator-slot-and-noteid-bookkeeping · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:272-293, 296-308`

**Problem.** Processor::onNoteOn(pitch, velocity, noteId) converts the float velocity with static_cast&lt;uint8_t>(velocity * 127.0f + 0.5f) (processor_midi.cpp:203). The shared dispatcher only turns velocity &lt;= 0.0f into a note-off (midi_event_dispatcher.h:110), so any velocity in (0, 0.0039) arrives at the engine as noteOn(pitch, 0, noteId). The base noteOn calls allocator_.noteOn(note, 0), which treats velocity 0 as a note-off (voice_allocator.h:231-233) and allocates nothing. RuinaeEngine::noteOn(note, vel, noteId) does not know that. It stamps the voice with the highest noteOnTimestamps_ (ruinae_engine.h:279-288) with the new noteId and midiNote. That voice belongs to an earlier note that is still sounding. Event sequence in poly mode: (1) hold C4 with noteId 1, which goes to voice V. (2) A soft E4 arrives with velocity 0.003 and noteId 2. The allocator does nothing, and V is restamped noteId=2, midiNote=64. (3) The host's noteOff(E4, id 2) finds V through noteId 2, because V is active (:301-303). It calls V.noteOff(), so C4 starts its release while the key is still held, and then setNoteId(-1). It calls allocator_.noteOff(64), but no slot holds 64, so C4's slot stays Active while its voice decays to Idle. processBlockPoly calls voiceFinished(i) when V goes idle (:2032-2035), but voiceFinished ignores the Active slot (voice_allocator.h:293). (4) When the user releases C4, the lookup by noteId 1 fails, because that id was overwritten. The engine falls back to noteOff(60), which moves the slot to Releasing, and V.noteOff() is a no-op on an Idle envelope (adsr_envelope.h:105). V can never again pass from active to inactive, so the slot stays Releasing until a steal reclaims it. Further side effects: the velocity-0 note-on also retriggers the global LFOs through globalModEngine_.noteOn() (:242), and allocator noteOff(E4) would release a held E4 played under another noteId. Note: a sustain-0 envelope does NOT open this leak. processDecay ends in Sustain (adsr_envelope.h:342-345), and Sustain never goes Idle (243-247). The noteId mismatch path above is the reachable route to 'voice Idle while the slot is Active'.

**Why it is wrong.** The noteId stamp must go on the voice that the allocator's NoteOn event actually assigned in this call, and only if one was assigned. A positive VST3 velocity is a note-on per the VST3 contract, so it must map to MIDI velocity >= 1, never to 0. noteOff-by-noteId must free the allocator slot of the voice it releases (its index), not slots matching the event pitch.

**Consequence.** With high-resolution velocity (MIDI 2.0 / 14-bit MPE controllers, or generated notes) a very soft note: (a) silently drops itself, (b) moves the previous note's MPE identity, so the held note's per-note pitch bend, pressure and brightness stop applying, (c) when the soft note is released it cuts the held note early (an audible early release), (d) leaks an allocator slot stuck in Active and then Releasing. That inflates getActiveVoiceCount and removes a slot from findIdleVoice until a steal reclaims it. Steal preference for Releasing slots (voice_allocator.h:630-637) can then pick a genuinely ringing release tail over the silent leaked slot in Oldest mode.

**Suggested fix.** In processor_midi.cpp:160/203 map velocity as std::clamp(static_cast&lt;int>(std::lround(velocity * 127.0f)), 1, 127) whenever velocity > 0. This also removes the UB float->uint8 conversion for velocity > ~2.0. In RuinaeEngine, have dispatchPolyNoteOn/dispatchMonoNoteOn return the voice index that received the NoteOn (or -1), and stamp only that index. In noteOff(note, noteId), release the allocator slot by voice index (add VoiceAllocator::releaseVoice(index) or call noteOff(allocator_.getVoiceNote(i))). Tests: engine-level, noteOn(60,100,1); noteOn(64,0,2); noteOff(64,2) -> voice of 60 must still be past attack and not in Release; then noteOff(60,1), render until silent, and assert allocator getActiveVoiceCount()==0. Processor-level, the same thing with velocity 0.003f.

**Evidence.** processor_midi.cpp:203 `auto midiVelocity = static_cast<uint8_t>(velocity * 127.0f + 0.5f);`; midi_event_dispatcher.h:110 `if (event.noteOn.velocity <= 0.0f)`; voice_allocator.h:231-233 `if (velocity == 0) { return noteOff(note); }`; ruinae_engine.h:277-288 `if (noteId >= 0 && mode_ == VoiceMode::Poly) { ... if (noteOnTimestamps_[i] > maxTs) ... voices_[newest].setNoteId(noteId); voices_[newest].setMidiNote(...)`; :302-306 `if (voices_[i].noteId() == noteId && voices_[i].isActive()) { voices_[i].noteOff(); voices_[i].setNoteId(-1); (void)allocator_.noteOff(note);`; voice_allocator.h:293 `if (state != VoiceState::Releasing) return;`; ruinae_engine.h:2033 `if (wasActive[i] && !voices_[i].isActive())`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the full path in the source, and the finding holds. (1) processor_midi.cpp:201-215: onNoteOn(pitch, velocity, noteId) computes `static_cast<uint8_t>(velocity * 127.0f + 0.5f)`, so any velocity in (0, ~0.00394) gives 0, and queueTimedEvent passes it on with the noteId. (2) midi_event_dispatcher.h:110 only turns `velocity <= 0.0f` into a note-off, so a tiny positive velocity reaches onNoteOn. (3) applyTimedEvent (processor_midi.cpp:93) calls engine_.noteOn(pitch, 0, noteId). (4) ruinae_engine.h:272-293: the noteId overload calls the base noteOn. That retriggers globalModEngine_.noteOn() (:242) and then reaches dispatchPolyNoteOn (:1720-1755), which calls allocator_.noteOn(note, 0). voice_allocator.h:231-233 turns that into noteOff(note), which returns no NoteOn event, so noteOnTimestamps_ is not updated. The overload then stamps noteId and midiNote unconditionally onto the voice with the highest existing timestamp (:279-288), which is the held earlier note. (5) noteOff(note, noteId) at :296-308 finds that voice by the stolen noteId, calls voices_[i].noteOff(), which releases the still-held note, and then calls allocator_.noteOff(note) with the soft note's pitch. No slot holds that pitch, so the held note's slot stays Active. (6) When the voice decays, processBlockPoly :2032-2035 calls allocator_.voiceFinished(i), which returns early because the state is not Releasing (voice_allocator.h:293). The slot stays Active with the voice Idle. (7) The later noteOff(60, id1) misses the noteId lookup and falls back to noteOff(60), so the slot goes to Releasing. Because wasActive[i] is false from then on (:1941, :2033), voiceFinished is never called again for that slot. Nothing else in the engine reconciles the allocator with the voice states: the only resets are at :145/194/1848-1895 (prepare, reset, mode switch). The slot stays out of the idle pool until a steal or a same-note retrigger reclaims it. No test covers velocity-0 or sub-1/127 noteId note-ons (searching plugins/ruinae/tests found none). I recommend lowering the severity. The trigger needs a host velocity below 0.5/127. A normal MIDI 1.0 velocity of 1 is 1/127 = 0.00787, which rounds to 1, so only high-resolution or generated velocities, sent with noteId >= 0, reach this path. The consequences (early release of a held note, a leaked slot) are real but rarely reached.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this. Every step of the chain is in the source.

1. **Velocity becomes 0 with no guard.**
   - Velocity 0.003 maps to MIDI 0 at plugins/ruinae/src/processor/processor_midi.cpp:203 (`static_cast<uint8_t>(velocity * 127.0f + 0.5f)`, which truncates 0.88 to 0).
   - The dispatcher only turns `velocity <= 0.0f` into a note-off (plugins/shared/src/midi/midi_event_dispatcher.h:110), so this note stays a note-on.
   - It is queued as a NoteOn with its noteId (processor_midi.cpp:214-215). applyTimedEvent then calls `engine_.noteOn(pitch, 0, noteId)` (:93).
   - No other clamp exists in processor/*.cpp. A grep for velocity found only these sites and the arp paths.

2. **The note-on allocates nothing.**
   - RuinaeEngine::noteOn(note, vel, noteId) (ruinae_engine.h:272-274) calls the base noteOn. That calls `globalModEngine_.noteOn()` unconditionally (:242), so the LFOs do retrigger, then dispatchPolyNoteOn (:248).
   - dispatchPolyNoteOn calls `allocator_.noteOn(note, 0)` (:1730). voice_allocator.h:231-233 turns that into `noteOff(note)`. No slot holds E4, so it returns an empty span (voice_allocator.h:262-279).
   - Without a NoteOn event, noteOnTimestamps_ is not updated (:1739).

3. **The wrong voice gets the new noteId.**
   - The stamp loop at ruinae_engine.h:279-288 still picks the voice with the highest timestamp, which is the held C4 voice V. It writes noteId 2 and midiNote 64 onto V.

4. **The soft note's note-off releases C4 and leaks the slot.**
   - noteOff(64, 2) matches V by noteId 2 while V is active (:302). It calls V.noteOff(), so the held C4 starts its release.
   - It then calls `allocator_.noteOff(64)` (:306). No slot holds 64, so C4's slot stays Active.
   - When V goes idle, step 16 calls `allocator_.voiceFinished(i)` (:2032-2034). voiceFinished returns early because the slot is not Releasing (voice_allocator.h:293).

5. **The slot stays stuck after C4 is released.**
   - The later noteOff(60, 1) misses the noteId lookup, because id 1 was overwritten. It falls back to noteOff(60), which moves the slot to Releasing (voice_allocator.h:265-268).
   - V is already idle, so wasActive is never true again and voiceFinished never runs for that slot. Only a steal reclaims it.

I found no code comment, guard or design note that makes this intentional.

**Severity: downgrade.**
- The trigger needs a positive VST3 velocity below 0.5/127 (about 0.0039).
- No MIDI 1.0 source can produce that: the smallest non-zero MIDI 1.0 velocity is 1/127, which rounds to 1.
- Only high-resolution velocity (MIDI 2.0 or 16-bit sources) or note events generated by software reach it, and the note also needs a noteId >= 0 and poly mode.
- The leak recovers through voice stealing. It does not leave a note sounding (the leaked voice is silent), and it cannot make NaN or level problems.
- It is a real but rare edge case, better rated low than medium.

The suggested fix is still right. Clamp a positive velocity to 1-127, stamp only the voice index that the allocator's NoteOn event returned, and free the allocator slot by voice index.

**Note 3.** The mechanism holds in source. The impact is real but narrow, so I recommend low severity.

Trigger path:
- processor_midi.cpp:203 converts with `static_cast<uint8_t>(velocity * 127.0f + 0.5f)`. Any VST3 velocity below 0.5/127 (about 0.00394) becomes 0.
- midi_event_dispatcher.h:110 diverts only `velocity <= 0.0f` to note-off. A tiny positive velocity reaches onNoteOn(pitch, vel, noteId), and applyTimedEvent then calls engine_.noteOn(pitch, 0, noteId) (processor_midi.cpp:93).

Engine path:
- RuinaeEngine::noteOn(note, vel, noteId) (ruinae_engine.h:272-293) calls noteOn(note, 0, false). That fires globalModEngine_.noteOn() (:242) and then dispatchPolyNoteOn (:1720).
- dispatchPolyNoteOn calls allocator_.noteOn(note, 0). That returns noteOff(note) (voice_allocator.h:231-233), so no NoteOn event and no timestamp update (:1739).
- The stamping loop (:279-288) then picks the voice with the largest noteOnTimestamps_ and overwrites its noteId and midiNote. That voice belongs to the previous, still-held note.
- noteOff(note, noteId) (:296-308) finds that voice through the stolen noteId and calls voices_[i].noteOff(), so the held note starts its release early. It then calls allocator_.noteOff(64), which matches no slot.
- The C4 slot stays Active. Its voice decays to Idle, and voiceFinished(i) (:2033-2034) is a no-op on an Active slot (voice_allocator.h:293).
- The later noteOff(60, id1) misses the lookup because the noteId was set to -1 at :304. The fallback noteOff(60) moves the slot to Releasing. The voice is already idle, so the wasActive -> inactive transition never comes again, and the slot stays Releasing until a steal reclaims it.
- Nothing else in the engine resyncs allocator state, short of the allocator_.reset() calls at 145/194/1850/1887/1895.

Why the impact is lower than claimed:
1. Every MIDI 1.0 source is immune. The smallest nonzero MIDI 1.0 velocity is 1/127 = 0.00787, which maps to 1. Only sub-0.4% float velocities trigger it: MIDI 2.0 16-bit velocity below about 257/65535, or a host piano-roll velocity set below 0.4%.
2. The leak is bounded and self-healing. findStealVictimSingle prefers Releasing slots (voice_allocator.h:631-633), so the silent leaked slot is the likely victim on the next full-polyphony note. Before that, the engine only loses one of 16 idle slots, and getActiveVoiceCount reads one too high.
3. The audible part is real: the held note releases early when the near-silent soft note is released, and the held note's MPE identity moves. That needs the narrow trigger above.

The source does confirm the incorrect noteId stamping when the allocator assigns nothing. With so few hosts and inputs able to trigger it, low is the right severity, not medium.

</details>

### R-170

**NaN LFO Rate/Symmetry or Macro value from state reaches the global modulation engine, which never sanitizes offsets: the global filter's SVF integrators go NaN and the plugin stays silent until the next reset**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** followup:state-load-unclamped-sweep · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/modulation_engine.h:466-470, 761-821`

**Problem.** loadLFOParams and loadLFOExtendedParams store rateHz and symmetry raw (lfo_params.h:253, 278), and loadMacroParams stores the four macro values raw (macro_params.h:75-78). The DSP setters clamp only with std::clamp, which passes NaN through: LFO::setFrequency (lfo.h:213-218), LFO::setSymmetry (lfo.h:297-299) and ModulationEngine::setMacroValue (modulation_engine.h:466-470). A NaN rate makes the phase increment NaN (phase_utils.h:47-55), and PhaseAccumulator::advance (phase_utils.h:160-167) then keeps the phase NaN for good. evaluateRoutings clamps the source and the per-destination sum with std::clamp only (modulation_engine.h:776, 789-790, 805-816) and has no NaN/Inf sanitization, unlike VoiceModRouter (voice_mod_router.h:189-195). In the engine, the global filter cutoff and resonance are computed with std::clamp (ruinae_engine.h:885-890), which also passes NaN, and are pushed into the SVF (939-942). SVF::setCutoff's clampCutoff passes NaN (svf.h:690-694).

**Why it is wrong.** A NaN coefficient turns the TPT integrators ic1eq_ and ic2eq_ into NaN (svf.h:371-377). The only recovery path in the SVF is a NaN *input* (svf.h:360-363), and the voice sum is finite. Once the modulation offset is finite again, the integrators stay NaN, every output sample is NaN, and the engine flushes it to 0 (ruinae_engine.h:985-990). A MasterVolume route makes sub.masterGain NaN (892-894) and gives the same silence. The global-mod path needs the same isFinite sanitization the per-voice router already has.

**Consequence.** A preset whose state contains a NaN LFO rate, LFO symmetry or macro value, routed to Global Filter Cutoff or Resonance (with the global filter on) or to Master Volume, makes the whole plugin silent. It stays silent after the user moves the knob back, because the LFO phase and SVF state remain NaN until setActive or a preset reload resets the engine. The same NaN reaches the arp destinations, where `static_cast<int>(std::round(3.0f * octaveOffset))` at processor_params.cpp:924 is undefined behaviour and the arp core receives NaN rate and gate values.

**Suggested fix.** (1) Sanitize at load: use a shared finite-or-default clamp helper (detail::isFinite then clamp) in loadLFOParams, loadLFOExtendedParams and loadMacroParams. (2) Defence in depth in ModulationEngine::evaluateRoutings: map a non-finite sourceValue, contribution or summed offset to 0 (as VoiceModRouter does), and guard LFO::setFrequency and setSymmetry and setMacroValue against NaN. Test: a dsp_ieee_tests case where ModulationEngine has setLFO1Rate(NaN) and a route LFO1 -> dest, checking getModulationOffset is finite. Also a Ruinae processor test: setState with LFO1 rate = NaN routed to the global cutoff, render, restore a finite rate, render again, and expect non-zero output.

**Evidence.** lfo_params.h:253 `params.rateHz.store(fv, ...)`, 278 `params.symmetry.store(fv, ...)`; macro_params.h:75 `params.values[0].store(fv, ...)`; lfo.h:214 `frequency_ = std::clamp(hz, kMinFrequency, kMaxFrequency);`; modulation_engine.h:468 `macros_[index].value = std::clamp(value, 0.0f, 1.0f);`, 776 `sourceValue = std::clamp(sourceValue, -1.0f, 1.0f);` (no isNaN anywhere in the file); ruinae_engine.h:885-887 `sub.globalCutoffHz = std::clamp(globalFilterCutoffHz_ * semitonesToRatio(cutoffOffset * kFilterModSemitones), 20.0f, 20000.0f);`; svf.h:692-694 `if (hz < kMinCutoff) ... if (hz > maxFreq) ... return hz;`; svf.h:360-363 reset only on NaN input.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the full path and confirmed the defect in IEEE arithmetic.

1. Load stores raw values. `loadLFOParams` stores rateHz without any check (plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/lfo_params.h:253). `loadLFOExtendedParams` does the same for symmetry (lfo_params.h:278), and `loadMacroParams` for values[0..3] (macro_params.h:75-78). `Processor::setState` calls these on the message thread with no sanitization (processor_state.cpp:165, 262, 266). Only the normalized handle path clamps (lfo_params.h:112/133, macro_params.h:22-35).

2. The values are applied every block. `applyModSourceParams` calls `engine_.setGlobalLFO1Rate` and `setGlobalLFO1Symmetry` with the stored atomics (processor_params.cpp:430, 443), and macros go through `engine_.setMacroValue` (processor_params.cpp:753-754). These reach `ModulationEngine::setLFO1Rate` -> `LFO::setFrequency` (modulation_engine.h:417, lfo.h:213-218) and `setMacroValue` (modulation_engine.h:466-470). Both use `std::clamp`, which returns v when both comparisons fail, so NaN passes through.

3. The LFO goes NaN and stays NaN. `calculatePhaseIncrement` returns NaN/sr (phase_utils.h:47-55). `PhaseAccumulator::advance` leaves the phase NaN for good, because `NaN >= 1.0` is false (phase_utils.h:160-167). `wrapPhase` returns NaN (both while loops are false, phase_utils.h:74-82). `readWavetable` masks the index, so it does not read out of bounds, but `frac` is NaN and the output is NaN (lfo.h:450-457). `process()` has no finiteness guard (lfo.h:111-170). A finite rate set later does not clear the NaN phase; only `reset` or a retrigger (lfo.h:269) does.

4. The modulation engine does not sanitize. In `evaluateRoutings` (modulation_engine.h:776), `std::clamp(NaN, -1, 1)` gives NaN. `applyBipolarModulation` -> `applyModCurve` clamps with `std::clamp` again (modulation_curves.h:39, 71-81), so the NaN goes on to the accumulated offsets (805-806) and the final clamp (814-815). The file contains no `isNaN` or `isFinite`. `getMacroOutput` passes NaN the same way (720-731).

5. The engine and the SVF keep it. `sub.globalCutoffHz`, `globalResonance` and `masterGain` are each produced by a `std::clamp` that passes NaN (ruinae_engine.h:885-894). They are pushed into the `SVF globalFilterL_/R_` (ruinae_engine.h:939-942, 2143). `SVF::clampCutoff` passes NaN (svf.h:690-694), and `updateCoefficients` produces NaN `a1_`/`a2_`/`a3_` (svf.h:469-486). The integrators then go NaN (svf.h:371-377). `flushDenormal(NaN)` returns NaN (db_utils.h:264-265). The only reset in the SVF is on a NaN *input* (svf.h:360-363). The engine's final flush zeroes every sample (ruinae_engine.h:985-990), so the output is silent. The SVF state stays NaN until `engine.reset()` (ruinae_engine.h:198-200).

The causal chain holds as claimed. I am downgrading the severity because the trigger is a NaN float inside a saved state blob, and no normal UI or host path writes one: the normalized handlers clamp and the rate mapping is finite. The finding is a hardening of corrupt-state handling, not a defect reachable from ordinary use.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this finding. Every step of the chain checks out against the source.

**Load path stores the values raw**
- lfo_params.h:253 stores rateHz with no check, and lfo_params.h:278 does the same for symmetry.
- macro_params.h:75-78 stores the four macro values with no check.
- processor_state.cpp:165-166 and 262-266 call these loaders, and nothing sanitizes the values afterwards. No load function under plugins/ruinae/src/parameters calls isFinite or isNaN.
- processor_params.cpp:430, 443, 447, 460 and 753-754 pass the values straight to the engine. ruinae_engine.h:486, 501 and 521-522 forward them to globalModEngine_ unchanged.

**The DSP setters let NaN through**
- std::clamp lets NaN through: lfo.h:214 (setFrequency), lfo.h:298 (setSymmetry), modulation_engine.h:468 (setMacroValue).
- lfo.h:520-522 together with phase_utils.h:47-55 give a NaN increment.
- PhaseAccumulator::advance (phase_utils.h:160-167) does `phase += increment` and only wraps when `phase >= 1.0`, so a NaN phase never recovers. A later valid setFrequency only fixes the increment.

**evaluateRoutings does not sanitize**
evaluateRoutings (modulation_engine.h:775-816) uses std::clamp only and never checks for NaN.

**The engine and SVF keep the NaN**
- ruinae_engine.h:885-894 clamps the NaN with std::clamp and passes it on into globalCutoffHz, globalResonance and masterGain. Lines 939-942 push those into the SVF.
- svf.h:690-694 (clampCutoff) uses comparisons only.
- svf.h:371-377 then makes ic1eq_ and ic2eq_ NaN. The only reset is on a NaN *input* (svf.h:360-363).
- The output is flushed to 0 at ruinae_engine.h:985-990, so the plugin stays silent.

**Arp path**
processor_params.cpp:924 casts `std::round(3.0f*octaveOffset)` to int. With a NaN offset that cast is undefined behaviour.

**Not intentional and not guarded elsewhere**
The engine's documented design is to ignore NaN at its setter boundary. ruinae_engine_test.cpp tests this: line 403 (setStereoSpread), 728 (setMasterGain), 948 (setPitchBend) and 1022 (setGlobalFilterCutoff, FR-016). The global LFO rate, LFO symmetry and macro forwards have no such guard, so they are inconsistent with that intent. They are not a deliberate exception.

**Why I downgraded the severity**
The trigger only exists in a corrupted or hand-crafted state blob or .vstpreset. The parameter-change paths cannot produce NaN: lfo_params.h:112 uses lfoRateFromNormalized, and lfo_params.h:133 clamps a host-normalized value. So a host replaying state this plugin saved itself never contains NaN. The defect is real, but it is defence-in-depth against untrusted preset files. It does not happen in normal use, so low is a better severity than medium.

**Note 3.** The code chain holds as described. Severity should drop because nothing Ruinae writes itself can put a NaN into the state.

How the NaN gets in and spreads:
- Load path: setState (processor_state.cpp:165-166, 262-263, 266) calls loadLFO1/2Params, loadLFO*ExtendedParams and loadMacroParams. These store the raw readFloat result with no finiteness check: lfo_params.h:253 (rateHz), lfo_params.h:278 (symmetry), macro_params.h:75-78 (macro values). Nothing after that sanitizes the values.
- Engine setters: processor_params.cpp:430/443/447/460/753 push the values into the engine. LFO::setFrequency (lfo.h:214) and setSymmetry (lfo.h:298) use only std::clamp. So does ModulationEngine::setMacroValue (modulation_engine.h:468). std::clamp lets NaN through, because both comparisons are false.
- Routing: evaluateRoutings (modulation_engine.h:776, 789-790, 805-816) has no isNaN or isFinite check anywhere in the file (grep found none).
- Global filter: ruinae_engine.h:885-894 computes cutoff, resonance and master gain with std::clamp, so a NaN offset gives a NaN value. Lines 939-942 pass it to SVF::setCutoff and setResonance. clampCutoff (svf.h:690-694) returns a NaN unchanged. process() (svf.h:360-377) resets only on a NaN input. A NaN coefficient therefore makes ic1eq_ and ic2eq_ NaN, and they stay NaN after the coefficients become finite again, since the input from the voice sum is finite.
- Output: the end-of-block flush (ruinae_engine.h:985-990) turns the NaN into 0, so the plugin is silent rather than outputting NaN. A NaN LFO rate also leaves the phase accumulator NaN even after the rate is fixed, so that source stays NaN until reset.
- Arp: the std::round to int cast at processor_params.cpp:924 does receive NaN on the arp-octave route.

Impact, and why I downgrade:
- Every value written by getState comes from atomics filled by handle*ParamChange, which maps from the normalized value. The 168 factory presets are generated by tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp.
- So the trigger needs one of two things: a malformed or corrupted .vstpreset or host state blob, or a host that sends a NaN normalized parameter value.
- When it does trigger, the effect is real and lasting: complete silence that moving the knob does not fix, until setActive or a preset reload resets the engine. That makes it a valid robustness defect (missing sanitization on input from outside the plugin).
- Because no normal session can produce the trigger, medium is too high. Low fits better.

</details>

### R-171

**NaN Reverb Size, Damping or Width from state poisons the FDN (Hall) reverb tank permanently: the whole plugin output goes silent**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** followup:state-load-unclamped-sweep · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/effects/fdn_reverb.h:553-608, 336-343`

**Problem.** loadReverbParams stores size, damping, width, preDelay and modRate raw (reverb_params.h:176-184), while the handler clamps every one of them (reverb_params.h:30-65). applyReverbParams passes them every block (processor_params.cpp:643-653), and RuinaeEffectsChain::setReverbParams forwards them to both reverbs (ruinae_effects_chain.h:672-676). FDNReverb::setParamsInternal clamps with std::clamp only, which passes NaN: `roomSize = std::clamp(params.roomSize, 0, 1)` leads to `fbGain = 0.78f + 0.17f*roomSize*roomSize` = NaN, which is written into every feedbackGains_ entry (566-568). A NaN damping makes t60nyq and gNyq NaN, and the coefficient clamp at 597-599 passes NaN into filterCoeffs_. Unlike the Dattorro Reverb, which routes every parameter through OnePoleSmoother::setTarget (reverb.h:438-458, where NaN becomes 0, smoother.h:168-173), the FDN writes coefficients directly with no smoothing.

**Why it is wrong.** `processed[i] * feedbackGains_[i] + preDelayed` (336-338) writes NaN into all eight delay lines. The NaN guard covers only the input sample (264-265, 421-422), so the tank keeps recirculating NaN after the parameter is finite again. The wet NaN plus dry is NaN, so the engine's final flush (ruinae_engine.h:985-990) zeroes the entire output, not just the reverb.

**Consequence.** A preset with a NaN reverb size or damping and the Hall type selected (or a crossfade into Hall) makes Ruinae completely silent. Correcting the knob does not help, because the tank stays NaN until engine reset (setActive or preset reload). The Plate type is immune, so the bug appears only with Hall.

**Suggested fix.** Clamp with finite checks in loadReverbParams, using the same ranges as handleReverbParamChange. In FDNReverb::setParamsInternal, ignore non-finite fields: `if (!detail::isFinite(params.roomSize)) keep previous`. Test: a dsp_ieee_tests case where FDNReverb gets setParams{roomSize=NaN}, process, then setParams{roomSize=0.5}, process, and the output is finite and non-zero. Also a Ruinae test that loads state with reverb size NaN and type 1 and checks the output is not all-zero after the size is restored.

**Evidence.** reverb_params.h:176 `params.size.store(fv, ...)`, 177 damping, 178 width (handler 31-41 clamps 0..1); fdn_reverb.h:553 `float roomSize = std::clamp(params.roomSize, 0.0f, 1.0f);` 558 `float fbGain = 0.78f + 0.17f * roomSize * roomSize;` 566-568 `feedbackGain = fbGain;`; 337 `processed[i] = processed[i] * feedbackGains_[i] + preDelayed;` 342 `delayBufWrite(i, processed[i]);`; 421 input-only guard; reverb.h:446-458 all via smoother setTarget (NaN resets to 0).

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced the path in source and it holds for size and damping.

1. Load path. reverb_params.h:176-184: loadReverbParams stores every float raw, with no clamp and no finiteness check. The handler at :30-65 clamps every field. setState calls it at processor_state.cpp:171, and the preset-snapshot path calls it at :337. Neither path sanitises afterwards: a grep for isFinite, isNaN or sanitize in plugins/ruinae/src/processor finds nothing.

2. Forwarding. processor_params.cpp:643-653 copies size, damping, width and the other fields into a ReverbParams and calls engine_.setReverbParams. That reaches ruinae_engine.h:692 and then ruinae_effects_chain.h:672-676, which calls fdnReverb_.setParams(wetOnly). setParams at fdn_reverb.h:251 calls setParamsInternal.

3. NaN through std::clamp. fdn_reverb.h:553-554 clamps with std::clamp, which compares (v&lt;lo, hi&lt;v); both are false for NaN, so NaN comes back. Then:
- :558 makes fbGain NaN, and :566-568 copies it into every feedbackGains_ entry.
- For damping, t60nyq at :579 and gNyq at :586 are NaN, and ratio at :596 is NaN. The clamps at :597 and :599 let NaN through, so filterCoeffs_ becomes NaN.

4. Recirculation. processBlock (the path the chain uses, effects_chain.h:1109) snapshots feedbackGains_ and filterCoeffs_ at :404-408. It applies them at :456-462 and :491, then writes into the delay lines at :495-496. The only NaN guard is on the input sample, at :421-422. filterStates_, dcBlock state and the delay buffers keep the NaN after the parameter is finite again. Nothing clears them except reset() (:218). reset() runs from the chain only when the reverb slot fades out (effects_chain.h:1097-1099), on crossfade completion for the outgoing type (:1160-1164), and on prepare or reset.

5. Whole output. The wet NaN plus dry gives NaN at effects_chain.h:1091-1092. The engine's flush at ruinae_engine.h:985-990 zeroes each NaN sample. Every sample is NaN, so the output is silent.

Corrections to the finding:
- Width does NOT poison the tank. width_ only scales the output at fdn_reverb.h:525-526 and recovers once it is finite again, so "Width" in the title is overstated.
- preDelay is harmless: std::max(0.0f, NaN) returns 0 at :433.
- Besides setActive and a preset reload, the tank also clears when the reverb is toggled off or the type is switched away.

Severity: the trigger needs a corrupt or crafted state blob, since the factory presets are generated finite. The outcome, though, is permanent total silence until a reset, and the handler and loader are inconsistent. Medium stands.

**Note 2.** The mechanism is real and I found nothing that guards it. plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/reverb_params.h:176-184 (loadReverbParams) stores size, damping, width, preDelay and modRate exactly as read, while handleReverbParamChange (30-65) clamps them. Both setState (processor_state.cpp:171) and the preset-snapshot path (processor_state.cpp:337) call it. No finiteness sanitizer exists anywhere in plugins/ruinae/src: a grep for isFinite, sanitiz and isNaN finds only engine/voice setter guards, and those are not on the reverb path. applyReverbParams (processor_params.cpp:643-653) forwards the raw atomics to engine_.setReverbParams (ruinae_engine.h:692), which calls RuinaeEffectsChain::setReverbParams (ruinae_effects_chain.h:672-676) and so fdnReverb_.setParams. FDNReverb::setParamsInternal (fdn_reverb.h:553-554) uses only std::clamp, and std::clamp(NaN, 0, 1) returns NaN because both comparisons are false. That NaN reaches fbGain (558), every feedbackGains_ entry (566-568), and t60dc, gDC, gNyq and filterCoeffs_ (576-599). In processBlock, the input guard covers only the input samples (421-422). Feedback (fdnApplyFeedbackSIMD at 491) and delayBufWrite (495-497) then write NaN into all eight delay lines. Nothing clears them when the parameters become finite again, so the tank recirculates NaN. The chain's dry/wet mix (ruinae_effects_chain.h:1087-1092) gives NaN even at wetGain 0, because 0*NaN is NaN, and ruinae_engine.h:985-990 then flushes the whole output to zero. The only recoveries are effects-chain reset (218), a reverb slot fade-out to Off (1097-1099) and a reverb type swap reset (1160-1164). Turning the knob back does not help, as the finding says. One small correction: switching the reverb off recovers as well as setActive. I found no prior finding in specs/ruinae-audit that matches loadReverbParams, so it is not a repeat. Severity: I recommend a downgrade. Ruinae's own getState writes only values the handler has already clamped (saveReverbParams 162-172), so a NaN can reach the reverb only from a corrupted or hand-crafted state or preset file. A normal host round-trip cannot produce it.

**Note 3.** The core mechanism is real, but the finding overstates three things: width, the recovery path and severity. Downgrade to low.

Confirmed from source:
1. reverb_params.h:176-184 stores size, damping, width, preDelay and modRate exactly as read from the stream.
2. processor_params.cpp:644-653 passes them through every block. ruinae_effects_chain.h:672-676 forwards them to fdnReverb_.setParams; only mix is forced to 1.
3. fdn_reverb.h:553-554 clamps roomSize and damping with std::clamp, which lets NaN through. Then fbGain is NaN (558) and is written to every feedbackGains_ entry (566-568). gDC and gNyq go NaN (585-586), so filterGainDC_ and filterCoeffs_ become NaN through std::clamp (590, 597-599).
4. processBlock snapshots those gains (404-407) and writes NaN into every delay line (491-497). The NaN guard covers only the input sample (421-422).
5. Once the size is finite again, the tank still holds NaN. The delay reads are NaN and the one-pole filter state recurses on itself, so NaN times any gain plus input stays NaN. The NaN is permanent until the tank is reset.
6. The reverb output is NaN, and the external mix at ruinae_effects_chain.h:1089-1092 gives NaN even when wetGain is 0. ruinae_engine.h:985-990 then zeroes every sample, so the whole plugin is silent, as claimed.

What the finding gets wrong:
(a) Width never enters the tank. width_ is used only in the output stage (fdn_reverb.h:523-526), so a NaN width silences output only while it stays NaN. preDelay is harmless here: std::max(0.0f, NaN) returns 0 at 432-433. Only size and damping cause the permanent poisoning.
(b) Recovery does not need setActive or a preset reload. Turning the reverb off resets both tanks once the fade reaches Off (ruinae_effects_chain.h:1097-1100). Switching to Plate also resets the outgoing FDN when the crossfade completes (1160-1164).
(c) The trigger is narrow. Ruinae never writes NaN to its own state, because saveReverbParams writes atomics that the handler fed with in-range floats (reverb_params.h:162-172). Only a corrupted or hand-made state reaches this, or a host that sends a NaN normalized value. The handler's clamp at reverb_params.h:31-41 is also std::clamp, so it passes NaN too.

Net effect: total silence, but only from invalid input, and toggling the reverb clears it. The fix is still worthwhile: an isFinite guard in loadReverbParams and the handler, or in FDNReverb::setParamsInternal.

</details>

### R-172

**Envelope Bezier control points from state are unclamped, and the engine's Bezier setters have no NaN guard: a NaN Filter Env control point permanently kills each voice's SVF**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** followup:state-load-unclamped-sweep · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_engine.h:1431-1441, 1492-1498`

**Problem.** loadEnvParams stores all 20 fields, including bezierEnabled and the 12 control points, raw (env_params.h:285-301). RUINAE_APPLY_ENVELOPE forwards the control points when bezierEnabled >= 0.5 (processor_params.cpp:104-113). The scalar curve setters are NaN-guarded (ruinae_engine.h:1416-1419, 1477-1480), but setAmp/Filter/Mod*BezierCurve are not (1431-1441, 1492-1498), and ADSREnvelope::set*BezierCurve has no guard either (adsr_envelope.h:182-203). generateBezierCurveTable evaluates `3*(1-t)^2*t*p1y`, which is NaN even at t=0, so every table entry is NaN (curve_table.h:110-163). In table mode the attack, decay and release output is `logStart + (peak - logStart) * tableVal` = NaN (adsr_envelope.h:276-286, 314-324, 351-359).

**Why it is wrong.** In the voice, filterEnvVal feeds totalSemitones and effectiveCutoff, and `std::clamp(effectiveCutoff, 20, maxCutoff)` passes NaN into setActiveFilterCutoff on every sample (ruinae_voice.h:519-527). The SVF coefficients and then its integrators become NaN (svf.h:204-212, 371-377). Filter state is deliberately not reset at noteOn (ruinae_voice.h:256-271), and the SVF resets only on a NaN input (svf.h:360-363), so every voice that has played one note stays NaN-poisoned. The voice output is flushed to 0 (ruinae_voice.h:626-628).

**Consequence.** A preset with Bezier mode on and one NaN Filter Env control point plays silence. Each of the 16 voices goes dead the first time it is used and stays dead after the Bezier data is fixed, until an engine reset. A NaN Amp Env control point silences the attack, decay and release segments of every note, so only the sustain portion is audible.

**Suggested fix.** Clamp the control points to [0,1] with finite checks in loadEnvParams (and BezierEnabled to 0/1). Add `if (!detail::isFinite(cp...)) return;` to the engine Bezier setters (or to ADSREnvelope::set*BezierCurve). Test: a dsp_ieee_tests case where generateBezierCurveTable with a NaN cp leaves the table finite, or the setter rejects it. Also a Ruinae voice test that sets the filter env decay Bezier cp1y = NaN, plays two notes on the same voice, restores finite points, plays again, and expects non-zero output.

**Evidence.** env_params.h:294-297 `if (streamer.readFloat(v)) { (params.*fields[i].member).store(v, ...); }` (no clamp; handler 164-166 stores raw too); ruinae_engine.h:1416-1418 `void setAmpAttackCurve(float amount) { if (detail::isNaN(amount) || detail::isInf(amount)) return; ...` vs 1431-1432 `void setAmpAttackBezierCurve(float cp1x, ...) { for (auto& voice : voices_) { voice.getAmpEnvelope().setAttackBezierCurve(...` (no guard), 1492-1493 same for Filter; curve_table.h:138-139 `yValues[i] = oneMinusT3 * p0y + 3.0f * oneMinusT2 * t * p1y + ...`; ruinae_voice.h:523-527 `float effectiveCutoff = filterCutoffHz_ * semitonesToRatio(totalSemitones); effectiveCutoff = std::clamp(effectiveCutoff, 20.0f, maxCutoff); setActiveFilterCutoff(effectiveCutoff);`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I traced every link in the claimed chain and each one holds.

1. Load: env_params.h:285-301 `loadEnvParams` stores every float raw, with no finiteness check or clamp. That includes bezierEnabled and the 12 control points. The handler at env_params.h:164-166 also stores the control points raw. Its BezierEnabled branch at 161-162 does binarize, but that does not matter here. The only callers are processor_state.cpp:162-164 (setState) and 328-330 (snapshot).

2. Forwarding: processor_params.cpp:104-113 (RUINAE_APPLY_ENVELOPE, used at 418-420) pushes the four control points per segment to the engine whenever bezierEnabled >= 0.5. Nothing in plugins/ruinae/src/processor calls isNaN/isFinite on these values.

3. Engine: ruinae_engine.h:1416-1429 and 1477-1490 guard the scalar curve setters with `detail::isNaN || detail::isInf`. setAmp/Filter*BezierCurve at 1431-1441 and 1492-1502 loop straight into the voices with no guard.

4. DSP: adsr_envelope.h:182-203 calls generateBezierCurveTable with no guard. In curve_table.h:112, p1y = startLevel + range*cp1y = NaN. Line 138 makes yValues[i] NaN for every i, including i=0, because 3*1*0*NaN = NaN. The resample at 144-164 then copies or lerps NaN into all 256 entries. Table mode (useTableProcessing_ = true) makes processAttack, processDecay and processRelease output logStart + (peak - logStart)*NaN = NaN (adsr_envelope.h:284-285, 322-323, 358-359).

5. Voice: filterEnvVal = filterEnv_.process() (ruinae_voice.h:462) feeds totalSemitones (519) and then effectiveCutoff (523). std::clamp passes NaN through at 524. setActiveFilterCutoff (1371-1390) calls SVF::setCutoff (svf.h:204). There, clampCutoff (690-695) uses `<` / `>` comparisons that NaN fails, so cutoffHz_ = NaN, and computeG = tan(NaN) gives g_/gTarget_ = NaN. SVF::process (353-391) resets only when the INPUT is NaN (360-363). The input is the finite oscillator mix, so ic1eq_/ic2eq_ become NaN at 376-377 and stay NaN.

6. Persistence: noteOn re-snaps the coefficients (ruinae_voice.h:262-271, snapToTarget at svf.h:309-318) but deliberately leaves the integrators alone. voice.reset() is called only from the engine reset (ruinae_engine.h:191) and on a filter type switch (resetActiveFilter, ruinae_voice.h:1323ff). A poisoned voice therefore stays NaN for later notes even after finite Bezier points are restored. Its output is flushed to 0 by the guard at ruinae_voice.h:626-628, which matches the claimed silence.

7. Amp variant: ampEnvVal NaN gives ampLevel NaN, and the output is flushed to 0 during attack, decay and release. Sustain is finite because the decay end sets output_ = sustainTarget (adsr_envelope.h:318), and release still reaches Idle through logPhase >= 1. This matches the claim.

Caveats that justify a downgrade: the only way in is a malformed or corrupted state stream (setState or a preset file). Normal operation cannot write NaN. A normal save serializes values that came from finite normalized host values, so a factory or user preset made by the plugin never contains a NaN control point. The voices do recover on a filter-type change or on an engine reset (setActive), not only on an engine reset. The finding is a real gap in state-load hardening, inconsistent with the guarded scalar setters, but its trigger is narrow.

**Note 2.** The defect is real in the code, but only a corrupted or hand-crafted state can trigger it, so I am confirming it and downgrading it to low.

What the code shows:
- **Load is unclamped.** env_params.h:294-297 stores the optional curve and Bezier fields straight from the stream. The BezierCp handler at env_params.h:164-166 also stores `static_cast<float>(value)` with no clamp.
- **The setters are not guarded.** processor_params.cpp:104-113 forwards the control points whenever bezierEnabled >= 0.5. In ruinae_engine.h the scalar curve setters have NaN/Inf guards (1416-1429, 1477-1490), but setAmp/Filter/Mod*BezierCurve do not (1431-1441, 1492-1502, 1553-1562). The guards on the scalar setters suggest a guard was intended, so the Bezier setters are a gap, not a design choice. ADSREnvelope::set*BezierCurve (adsr_envelope.h:182-203) passes the values straight to generateBezierCurveTable.
- **One NaN fills the table.** At curve_table.h:112 and 138, a NaN cp1y gives NaN p1y, and `3*oneMinusT2*t*p1y` is NaN even at t=0. So every yValues entry, and with it every table entry, is NaN. The table-mode stages then compute their output from the table, so it is NaN too (adsr_envelope.h:284-285, 322-323, 358-359).
- **The voice filter is poisoned.** At ruinae_voice.h:519-524, `filterEnvAmount_ * NaN` is NaN even when the amount is 0. `std::clamp(NaN, 20, max)` returns NaN. SVF clampCutoff (svf.h:690-694) uses `<`/`>` comparisons, so NaN passes through. The integrators at svf.h:371-377 go NaN, and the reset at svf.h:360-363 only fires on a NaN input, never on NaN state.
- **No reset on retrigger.** noteOn deliberately does not reset the filter (ruinae_voice.h:256-271). resetActiveFilter runs only from reset() (ruinae_voice.h:184, 201). The voice output is flushed to 0 (ruinae_voice.h:626-628), so the result is silence, not NaN at the output.
- **No test covers it.** A grep for a NaN Bezier test found none.

What limits it:
- **Reachability.** getState can only write values that came in through setState or a parameter change. VST3 hosts do not send NaN normalized values. The factory presets come from the generator. So the trigger is a corrupted or hand-edited preset or project.
- **Recovery.** applyPresetSnapshot calls engine_.reset() (processor_state.cpp:364), and processor.cpp:206 resets the engine too. Loading another preset therefore clears the poisoned voices. The claim that voices stay dead after the Bezier data is fixed holds only when the fix comes through parameter changes.

Downgrade to low: it is a robustness gap against bad state data, not something normal use reaches.

**Note 3.** The mechanism is confirmed from source.

How the NaN gets in and spreads:
- env_params.h:285-301: loadEnvParams stores every optional field raw, including bezierEnabled and the 12 control points. There is no finite check or clamp.
- The host-param path only clamps BezierEnabled. BezierCp is stored raw via static_cast (env_params.h:164-166).
- processor_params.cpp:104-113: RUINAE_APPLY_ENVELOPE forwards the control points when bezierEnabled >= 0.5.
- ruinae_engine.h:1431-1441, 1492-1501 and 1553-1562: the Amp, Filter and Mod Bezier setters have no isNaN/isInf guard. The scalar curve setters right next to them do (1417, 1478, 1539).
- The only isNaN/isFinite hits in plugins/ruinae/src are in the engine and voice, so nothing sanitises the values after load.
- curve_table.h:112 and 138-139: a NaN cp*y makes p1y/p2y NaN, so every yValues entry is NaN, including at t=0, because 0*NaN is NaN. A NaN cp*x makes xValues NaN, so `frac` is NaN at 161-162. Either way the whole 256-entry table is NaN.
- adsr_envelope.h:184-201 regenerates the tables without a guard. In table mode, attack, decay and release output NaN (285, 323, 359). Release with NaN never crosses the `< kEnvelopeIdleThreshold` test at 360, so it runs its full time.
- ruinae_voice.h:462 and 519-527: filterEnvVal (NaN) times filterEnvAmount_ is NaN even when the amount is 0. std::clamp passes NaN through.
- svf.h:690-694: clampCutoff also passes NaN, because both comparisons are false.
- svf.h:204-211 and 469-491: g_ and the a1/a2/a3 coefficients become NaN, so ic1eq_ and ic2eq_ become NaN (371-377).
- svf.h:360-363: the SVF resets only on a NaN input. The oscillator input stays finite, so the integrators stay NaN.
- ruinae_voice.h:256-271: noteOn deliberately does not reset the filter.
- ruinae_voice.h:626-628: the voice output is flushed to 0, so the voice is silent.

Where the claim overstates the impact:
1. Reachability. NaN cannot reach these fields through any conformant path. Host values are normalized [0,1] doubles. getState writes back what was stored, which is finite. The 168 factory presets come from tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp with finite constants. The only trigger is a corrupted or hand-crafted state blob or .vstpreset.
2. Persistence. The voice is not dead "until an engine reset" only. Switching the filter type resets the SVF via the reset block at ruinae_voice.h:1323-1339, and a setActive/reset also clears it.
3. Output safety. The failure mode is silence: no blast, no NaN at the output, no crash. The per-voice flush (ruinae_voice.h:626) and the engine flush (ruinae_engine.h:985-988) both hold.

Conclusion: this is a real missing input-validation and robustness gap. It repeats the pattern of the other unclamped-state-load findings. Its trigger is limited to malformed state and its result is recoverable silence, so medium severity is too high. Downgrade to low.

</details>

### R-173

**loadArpParams 'clamps' with std::clamp, which passes NaN, and lane speeds are not clamped at all: NaN rate or gate gives undefined size_t casts in ArpeggiatorCore, and a NaN lane speed freezes that lane permanently**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** followup:state-load-unclamped-sweep · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/arpeggiator_params.h:1285, 1288, 1306-1307, 1317-1318, 1402, 1444-1459`

**Problem.** The arp loader clamps every float with std::clamp, which returns NaN for a NaN input: freeRate (1285), gateLength (1288), velocity and gate lane steps (1306-1307, 1317-1318), and humanize (1402). The v8 lane speeds are stored with no clamp at all (1447-1449). applyArpParams forwards them every block: `std::clamp(baseRate * (1 + 0.5*rateOffset), 0.5, 50)` passes NaN to setFreeRate (processor_params.cpp:905-907, or 953 when the arp is Off), gate lane steps go through ArpLane::setStep unchecked (processor_params.cpp:997-1003, arp_lane.h:78-82), and lane speeds go through setLaneSpeed (processor_params.cpp:1129-1136). ArpeggiatorCore stores them via std::clamp again (arpeggiator_core.h:438-445, 700-703).

**Why it is wrong.** calculateStepDuration does `static_cast<size_t>(sampleRate_ / static_cast<double>(freeRateHz_))` (arpeggiator_core.h:1096), and calculateGateDuration casts `currentStepDuration_ * gateLengthPercent_ / 100 * gateLaneValue` to size_t (1158-1162). Converting a NaN double to size_t is undefined behaviour: depending on codegen it yields 0, which the guards turn into a 1-sample step or a 1-sample note, or 2^63, so the step never fires. For lane speed, `accum += speed` makes the accumulator NaN, and `while (accum >= threshold)` is never true again (arpeggiator_core.cpp:532-539). The repo's macOS fast-math rules require finite classification through detail::isFinite, not std::clamp, for values that feed casts.

**Consequence.** A corrupt arp state produces one of three platform-dependent failures: an arp that fires a step every sample (128-event cap per block, flooding the engine and MIDI out), an arp that never fires (silence in MIDI mode, because keys reach only the arp), or 1-sample, inaudible arp notes. A NaN lane speed freezes that lane (velocity, gate, pitch, chord and so on) on one step until arpCore reset, and it freezes again on the next block because the atomic is still NaN.

**Suggested fix.** Add a `finiteClamp(v, lo, hi, def)` helper (detail::isFinite, else def) to the loader. Use it for every float in loadArpParams, including the lane speeds (clamp 0.25-4). This also belongs in the shared-prefix discussion with Gradus, whose loader is separate. Also make ArpeggiatorCore::setFreeRate, setGateLength and setLaneSpeed ignore non-finite input. Test (dsp_ieee_tests): setFreeRate(NaN) leaves the previous rate, and setLaneSpeed(0, NaN) keeps the lane advancing. Ruinae: a state with freeRate=NaN and the arp in MIDI mode, a held chord, and an expected note count in 1 s between the rate's expected bounds.

**Evidence.** arpeggiator_params.h:1285 `params.freeRate.store(std::clamp(floatVal, 0.5f, 50.0f), ...)`, 1288 `std::clamp(floatVal, 1.0f, 200.0f)`, 1317-1318 `std::clamp(floatVal, 0.01f, 2.0f)`, 1447-1449 `if (streamer.readFloat(speed)) target.store(speed, ...);`; arpeggiator_core.h:1096 `baseDuration = static_cast<size_t>(sampleRate_ / static_cast<double>(freeRateHz_));`, 1159-1162 `static_cast<size_t>(static_cast<double>(currentStepDuration_) * static_cast<double>(gateLengthPercent_) / 100.0 * static_cast<double>(gateLaneValue))`, 702 `laneSpeedMultipliers_[laneIndex] = std::clamp(speed, 0.25f, 4.0f);`; arpeggiator_core.cpp:532 `accum += speed;` 539 `while (accum >= threshold) {`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Every link in the claimed chain holds in the source. (1) arpeggiator_params.h:1285, 1288, 1306-1307, 1317-1318 and 1402 clamp with std::clamp. std::clamp(v, lo, hi) returns v when both `v < lo` and `hi < v` are false, so a NaN comes back out. At 1444-1450 the v8 lane-speed lambda stores `speed` with no clamp at all. (2) The loader's only caller is Processor::setState (processor_state.cpp:285), with no finite check before or after it. (3) processor_params.cpp:905-907 computes `std::clamp(baseRate*(1+0.5*rateOffset),0.5f,50.0f)`, which stays NaN, and passes it to setFreeRate. 953-954 (arp Off) pass the raw atomics. 912-915 clamp the gate in the same NaN-transparent way. 997-1003 pass gateLaneSteps[i] straight to ArpLane::setStep, which only clamps the index (arp_lane.h:78-82). 1129-1136 pass the raw lane-speed atomics to setLaneSpeed. (4) In ArpeggiatorCore, setFreeRate and setGateLength (arpeggiator_core.h:438-445) and setLaneSpeed (700-703) use std::clamp again, so a NaN is stored. (5) calculateStepDuration does `static_cast<size_t>(sampleRate_ / (double)freeRateHz_)` (1096), and calculateGateDuration casts `step*gate/100*gateLaneValue` to size_t (1158-1162). A NaN converted to size_t is undefined behaviour. The `swungDuration > 0 ? : 1` guard and `std::max(size_t{1}, ...)` turn a result of 0 into a 1-sample step or note, and a huge result means the step never fires. (6) arpeggiator_core.cpp:532 `accum += speed` and 539 `while (accum >= threshold)`: once accum is NaN the comparison is always false, so the lane never advances again. Fixing the param would not help either, because NaN + x stays NaN until a reset. The atomic stays NaN, so the same thing happens on every block. The prior findings.json has no NaN or isFinite entry, so this is not a repeat of an earlier finding. Downgrade: the only trigger is a corrupt or crafted state blob, or a NaN normalized value from the host. getState never writes a non-finite value, because every live path clamps a finite value. The result is a misbehaving arp (timing UB, a frozen lane), not NaN audio: the engine flushes NaN/Inf at the output and note pitches are integers. That makes it robustness hardening rather than a medium user-facing defect.

**Note 2.** I could not refute this. Every link in the chain is in the source, and I found no guard anywhere along it.

1. The loader stores NaN unchanged. plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/arpeggiator_params.h:1285 (freeRate), 1288 (gateLength), 1306-1307 (velocity steps), 1317-1318 (gate steps), 1351 (slideTime), 1399/1402 (spice/humanize) and 1407 (ratchetSwing) all use std::clamp. With IEEE comparisons std::clamp returns NaN for a NaN input, because both `v < lo` and `hi < v` are false. The v8 lane speeds at 1446-1458 are stored raw: `if (streamer.readFloat(speed)) target.store(speed, ...)`.

2. Nothing upstream catches it. setState calls loadArpParams directly (processor_state.cpp:285). Grep finds no isFinite, sanitize or finite helper anywhere under plugins/ruinae/src.

3. The audio thread passes the values on every block without a check:
   - processor_params.cpp:905-907 computes `std::clamp(baseRate*(1+0.5*rateOffset),0.5,50)`, which is still NaN, and calls setFreeRate. Line 953 does the same when the arp is Off.
   - Line 913 does the same for gate length.
   - Lines 997-1002 forward the gate lane steps raw.
   - Lines 1129-1136 forward the lane speeds.

4. ArpeggiatorCore does not catch it either:
   - setFreeRate, setGateLength and setLaneSpeed use std::clamp only (arpeggiator_core.h:438-445 and 700-703).
   - calculateStepDuration does `static_cast<size_t>(sampleRate_ / static_cast<double>(freeRateHz_))` (arpeggiator_core.h:1096). This is reached whenever tempoSync is off.
   - calculateGateDuration casts a product that includes gateLengthPercent_ and gateLaneValue to size_t (1159-1162).
   - Converting a NaN double to size_t is undefined behaviour. In practice x86 cvttsd2si gives 2^63, so the step never fires, and arm64 fcvtzu gives 0, which the guard turns into 1 sample.

5. A NaN lane speed sticks. arpeggiator_core.cpp:532 does `accum += speed`, so accum becomes NaN. At line 539, `while (accum >= threshold)` is never true again, so that lane freezes. The atomic is still NaN, so it is fed back in every block.

None of the context defences apply:
   - No code comment, spec or prior finding covers this. Grep for NaN or non-finite in specs/ruinae-audit finds nothing, so this is not a repeat of an F-id.
   - The Gradus loader has the same std::clamp pattern (plugins/gradus/src/parameters/arpeggiator_params.h:2190), so this is not a Ruinae-only design divergence.

Why I downgrade the severity: the only source of NaN is a corrupt or crafted state stream. getState writes the atomics, which only receive finite values on the normal parameter path, so no normal save produces NaN. There is no audio NaN, no crash and no stuck voice, only arp timing that is broken until the state is reloaded. Also, the same std::clamp-on-load pattern runs through all the Ruinae packs, so this is one case of a general robustness gap and not a defect specific to the arp.

**Note 3.** The mechanism is real in the source, but only a state blob that is already corrupt or hand-crafted can trigger it. That makes it low severity, not medium.

What the source confirms:
- **Loader:** plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/arpeggiator_params.h:1285 (`std::clamp(floatVal, 0.5f, 50.0f)` for freeRate), 1288 (gateLength), 1306-1307 (velocity steps), 1317-1318 (gate steps) and 1402 (humanize) all clamp with std::clamp. std::clamp is `v<lo?lo:hi<v?hi:v`, so a NaN input comes out as NaN. Lines 1446-1449 store the v8 lane speeds with no clamp at all (`if (streamer.readFloat(speed)) target.store(speed, ...)`).
- **processor_params.cpp:** 883 loads freeRate. 905-907 does `std::clamp(baseRate * (1 + 0.5*rateOffset), 0.5, 50)`, and NaN stays NaN; setFreeRate receives it at 907, or at 900 or 953. 912-915 does the same for the gate length. 1129-1136 forwards the lane speeds.
- **arpeggiator_core.h:** 438-445 (setFreeRate/setGateLength) and 702 (setLaneSpeed) clamp with std::clamp again, so NaN passes. 1096 does `static_cast<size_t>(sampleRate_ / static_cast<double>(freeRateHz_))`, which converts a NaN double to size_t (undefined behaviour; on x86-64 it typically comes out as 0x8000000000000000, so the step never fires). 1158-1162 casts the gate duration the same way.
- **arpeggiator_core.cpp:** 532 `accum += speed` makes the accumulator NaN, and `while (accum >= threshold)` at 539 (and 1276) is then never true, so the lane freezes. The curve clamp at 526 is also std::clamp and does not rescue it.
- No test injects NaN into the arp state. The only corrupt-stream test, arp_integration_test.cpp:1997, covers truncation, not NaN.

Why the impact is lower than claimed:
- **No normal path writes NaN into these atomics.** getState only writes back what the atomics already hold. Factory presets are generated by tools/ruinae_preset_generator.cpp from finite values. The UI and host reach them through normalized parameter changes that are denormalized with finite math.
- **The only triggers are a corrupted or maliciously crafted .vstpreset or project chunk, or a host that sends a NaN normalized value.** A NaN normalized value is a host bug.
- **The effect is limited to the arp.** The arp misbehaves (MIDI-mode silence, or 1-sample notes or a flood capped at 128 events per block, depending on what the cast yields), and one lane can freeze. Nothing NaN reaches the audio output, because the engine's NaN/Inf flush is downstream and this path only produces note events.
- **It does persist:** the NaN is saved back by getState, so it survives a save/reload.

This is a robustness gap for corrupt input, worth a finite-guard fix, but it does not justify medium severity.

### R-174

**Trance Gate attack, release, depth and rate from state are unclamped: TranceGate::setParams lets NaN into the smoother coefficients and into an undefined size_t cast, and gated voices go silent**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** low · **Dimension:** followup:state-load-unclamped-sweep · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/trance_gate.h:153-171, 452-462, 269-285`

**Problem.** loadTranceGateParams stores rateHz, depth, attackMs and releaseMs raw (trance_gate_params.h:308-315); only numSteps, phase, step levels and retrigger are clamped (325-348). applyTranceGateParams passes them every block (processor_params.cpp:388-402). TranceGate::setParams clamps with std::clamp only (154-164), which passes NaN, and then configures both OnePoleSmoothers with it (169-170). calculateOnePolCoefficient's clamp also passes NaN, so the coefficient is exp(NaN) (smoother.h:82-90). updateStepDuration does `static_cast<size_t>(sampleRate_ / static_cast<double>(clampedRate))` with a NaN clampedRate (458-459).

**Why it is wrong.** A NaN depth fails the `depth == 0` bypass (242) and makes finalGain NaN on every sample (285). A NaN attack coefficient makes every rising step's gain NaN (276), and the voice flushes that to 0 (ruinae_voice.h:617-628). The NaN-to-size_t cast is undefined behaviour on every block, even though the engine later overwrites the rate per sub-block.

**Consequence.** With the trance gate enabled, a preset carrying a NaN depth silences every voice for as long as the value stays loaded. A NaN attack produces gated output made of NaN-flushed zeros and clicks on each rising step. The undefined cast executes on the audio thread every block.

**Suggested fix.** Clamp rateHz (0.1-100), depth (0-1), attackMs and releaseMs with finite checks in loadTranceGateParams, matching handleTranceGateParamChange. Make TranceGate::setParams ignore non-finite fields. Test: a dsp test where setParams{depth=NaN, attackMs=NaN} followed by process gives finite output, and a Ruinae state test with trance gate depth NaN gives non-zero output.

**Evidence.** trance_gate_params.h:308-315 `params.rateHz.store(floatVal, ...)`, `params.depth.store(floatVal, ...)`, `params.attackMs.store(floatVal, ...)`, `params.releaseMs.store(floatVal, ...)`; trance_gate.h:154 `const float clampedAttack = std::clamp(params.attackMs, kMinAttackMs, kMaxAttackMs);` 169 `attackSmoother_.configure(params_.attackMs, ...)`, 242 `if (params_.depth == 0.0f)`, 285 `const float finalGain = 1.0f + (smoothedGain - 1.0f) * params_.depth;`, 459 `samplesPerStep_ = static_cast<size_t>(sampleRate_ / static_cast<double>(clampedRate));`; smoother.h:82 `const float clampedTime = std::clamp(smoothTimeMs, ...)`, 89-90 `exponent = -5000.0f / (clampedTime * sampleRate); return detail::constexprExp(exponent);`.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** I could not refute this. I traced the path and confirmed each step.

1. The state load stores raw floats. `plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/trance_gate_params.h:308-315` stores `rateHz`, `depth`, `attackMs` and `releaseMs` with no clamp and no finiteness check. Only `numSteps` (325), the euclidean fields (331/333), `phaseOffset` (335), the step levels (341) and `retriggerDepth` (348) are clamped. The normal parameter path, `handleTranceGateParamChange` (lines 64-84), does clamp all four. `processor_state.cpp:161/327` calls the loader and does no sanitising afterwards: a grep of `processor/` for `isFinite`, `isNaN` or `sanitiz` finds nothing.

2. The values reach the gate on every block. `processor_params.cpp:252` calls `applyTranceGateParams()`. Lines 390-393 copy the atomics into `TranceGateParams`, and line 402 calls `engine_.setTranceGateParams`. `ruinae_engine.h:1317-1318` passes them to every voice. `ruinae_voice.h:1080` does `tranceGateDepth_ = std::clamp(params.depth, 0, 1)`, which lets NaN through, and line 1081 calls `tranceGate_.setParams(params)`.

3. `TranceGate::setParams` clamps only with `std::clamp`, which returns NaN for a NaN input (`trance_gate.h:154-162`). Lines 169-170 then configure both smoothers with that value. `OnePoleSmoother::configure` (`smoother.h:158-161`) calls `calculateOnePolCoefficient`. Its `std::clamp` at line 82 passes NaN, so the exponent at line 89 is NaN, and `constexprExp` returns NaN for a NaN argument (`db_utils.h:221`). The coefficient is therefore NaN.

4. In `updateStepDuration` (`trance_gate.h:458-459`), `std::clamp(NaN)` returns NaN, so `sampleRate_/NaN` is NaN. `static_cast<size_t>(NaN)` is undefined behaviour, and it runs on the audio thread every block. The engine later calls `setRate` with a clamped value, but only for active voices (`ruinae_engine.h:1977`). The undefined cast has already happened by then.

5. A NaN depth fails the `params_.depth == 0.0f` bypass at `trance_gate.h:242`. `finalGain` at line 285 becomes NaN. The voice block-rate modulation at `ruinae_voice.h:588-590` does not repair it, because NaN plus an offset, clamped, is still NaN. `ruinae_voice.h:618` multiplies by that gain, and lines 626-628 flush the NaN to 0. The gated voices go silent.

6. A NaN attack is worse than the finding says. At line 276, `attackSmoother_.process()` gives `target + NaN*(...)`, which is NaN. Line 277 copies that NaN into the release smoother. After that, the comparison `targetLevel > NaN` at line 274 is always false, so every later sample takes the release path. That path computes `target + c*(NaN - target)`, which is still NaN. The gain stays NaN, and the voice stays silent until the gate is reset.

The only precondition is a NaN float in a host state or preset blob: a corrupted or crafted file, never a normal save. Low severity is therefore right as filed.

**Note 2.** I read every link in the chain and could not refute it. Nothing in the chain catches a NaN.
- plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/trance_gate_params.h:308-315 stores rateHz, depth, attackMs and releaseMs straight from the stream. Only numSteps (325), euclidean hits/rotation (331-333), phaseOffset (335), step levels (340-341) and retriggerDepth (348) are clamped.
- processor_state.cpp:161 (setState, phase 1) and :327 both call loadTranceGateParams with no sanitising step.
- processor_params.cpp:388-402 (applyTranceGateParams) copies the raw atomics into TranceGateParams and calls engine_.setTranceGateParams.
- ruinae_engine.h:1317-1319 forwards to each voice. Unlike setTranceGateRate at :1321-1323, which does have an isNaN/isInf guard, it has no finite check.
- ruinae_voice.h:1080-1081 calls std::clamp(params.depth, 0, 1) and then tranceGate_.setParams. std::clamp returns NaN unchanged, because every comparison with NaN is false.
- trance_gate.h:154-164 clamps with std::clamp only. Lines 169-170 configure both smoothers from the possibly-NaN times. Lines 458-459 cast sampleRate_/NaN to size_t, which is undefined behaviour. Line 242's `depth == 0.0f` bypass fails for NaN, so finalGain at 285 (and at 436 in processGain) is NaN.
- ruinae_voice.h:626-628 flushes NaN output to 0, so the voice goes silent instead of passing NaN on.
The voice's depth-mod path at 587-591 cannot fix this either, because it clamps NaN+offset to NaN.
I found no design note, no upstream sanitiser, and no test that pins the behaviour. trance_gate_test.cpp has NaN checks only for output under normal params, and those use std::isnan.
The defect is real, but only a corrupted or crafted state chunk reaches it. Normal getState writes values that already went through handleTranceGateParamChange's clamps, so no ordinary session produces a NaN here. The NaN-to-size_t cast is genuine UB on the audio thread, but in practice it gives a huge or zero step length, not a crash. That makes "low" the right severity.

**Note 3.** Confirmed from source. plugins/ruinae/src/parameters/trance_gate_params.h:308-315 stores rateHz, depth, attackMs and releaseMs from the stream with no clamp and no finite check. Only numSteps, the Euclidean fields, phaseOffset, step levels and retriggerDepth are clamped (325-348). processor_state.cpp:161 and :327 call it, and nothing sanitizes the values afterwards. Processor::applyTranceGateParams (processor_params.cpp:382-402) copies the raw atomics into TranceGateParams every block and calls engine_.setTranceGateParams. That calls RuinaeVoice::setTranceGateParams (ruinae_voice.h:1079-1081), whose own `std::clamp(params.depth, 0, 1)` passes NaN through, and then TranceGate::setParams (trance_gate.h:153-171). There the std::clamp calls at 154/155/159/162 also pass NaN.

Impact, path by path:

(1) Depth NaN. The `params_.depth == 0.0f` bypass (242) is false, so finalGain = 1 + (g-1)*NaN = NaN (285). The voice NaN flush at ruinae_voice.h:626-628 zeroes every sample. The block-rate depth-mod path (584-590) cannot rescue it, because clamp(NaN + offset) is still NaN. Result: every voice is silent while the gate is enabled. This consequence is correct.

(2) Attack NaN. OnePoleSmoother::configure calls calculateOnePolCoefficient (smoother.h:82-90): its clamp passes NaN and constexprExp returns NaN for a NaN argument (db_utils.h:221), so coefficient_ is NaN. On a rising step, process() (smoother.h:195-203) gives current_ = NaN. releaseSmoother_.snapTo(NaN) turns that into 0 (smoother.h:262). On the next sample `targetLevel > NaN` is false, so the release path runs and attackSmoother_.snapTo(finite) runs. The output therefore alternates NaN-flushed zeros with finite samples on every rising transition, a buzz or click there. A release NaN does the same on falling steps (not claimed, but it is symmetric).

(3) Rate NaN. `static_cast<size_t>(NaN)` at trance_gate.h:459 is real UB on the non-tempo-sync path, and it runs every block. But std::max(...,1) bounds it, and RuinaeEngine overwrites the rate for active voices through setTranceGateRate, with a finite clamped value, at ruinae_engine.h:1973-1977. I found no audible consequence for rate, so this part is UB hygiene only.

Severity stays low. The only trigger is a corrupt or crafted state or preset blob carrying NaN float bytes. Normal edits go through handleTranceGateParamChange, which clamps. Inf and out-of-range finite values are handled correctly by the existing std::clamp. Severity is unchanged because the real consequence (a silent instrument or a gritty gate from such a state) is genuine but needs malformed input.

</details>

### R-178

**F026 only half fixed: muted or removed harmonizer voices are still cut in one sample, and the 1/sqrt(N) wet scale steps instantly when the audible voice count changes**

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Severity:** medium → low · **Dimension:** followup:harmonizer-wiring-and-shared-engine · **Source:** followup (verify round followup)
- **Location:** `dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/harmonizer_engine.h:243-246, 383-386, 466-469, 547-555, 576-598, 657-670`

**Problem.** F026 ('Muted harmonizer voices freeze their smoothers and cut abruptly in non-PhaseVocoder paths'): the smoother-freeze half is fixed. advanceMutedVoiceSmoothers (789-797) is now called in all three paths. The cut half is still present. setVoiceLevel sets linearGain = 0 the moment the level reaches -60 dB, and every path then does `continue` on linearGain == 0. The voice's output disappears in one sample at whatever level its smoother currently holds, and the 5 ms level ramp toward 0 is never heard. setNumVoices lowering the count just stores numActiveVoices_ = newCount, so the removed voices vanish mid-sample with no fade-out (only an increase gets a fade-in). voiceCountScale = 1/sqrt(audibleVoices) is recomputed every block from linearGain (the target, not the smoothed level) and applied with no smoothing.

**Why it is wrong.** Gain changes on a sounding signal must be ramped. The engine itself states that a stepped level 'clicks' (comment at 785-787) and smooths every other level. A preset change or stepped automation (voice level 0 dB -> -60 dB, Voices 4 -> 2) is a normal user action. The compensation scale is a gain on all remaining voices, so stepping it is a gain step on the whole harmony bus.

**Consequence.** Lowering Voices 4->3 drops voice 4 at full level instantly (click), and the remaining three jump +1.25 dB (0.5 -> 0.577). 2->1 is a +3 dB jump. Muting a voice by automating its level to -60 dB, or loading a preset that does, cuts it at its current level instead of fading, and the other voices step up in level at the same instant. Unmuting steps them down.

**Suggested fix.** Keep processing a voice until its level smoother's current value is below about 1e-4. Base 'muted' on the smoothed level, not on linearGain. Fade out voices removed by setNumVoices: keep them rendering with a fade-out ramp until it reaches 0, then drop them. Compute voiceCountScale from the smoothed per-voice levels, or run it through its own 10 ms smoother. Regression test (also closes the missing F026 test): sustain a sine through HarmonizerEngine with 2 voices, step voice 1's level to -60 dB, then step numVoices 2->1, and assert the maximum |y[n]-y[n-1]| near each change stays below the steady-state bound.

**Evidence.** harmonizer_engine.h:466-469: `if (voice.linearGain == 0.0f) { advanceMutedVoiceSmoothers(voice, numSamples); continue; }` (same at 243-246, 383-386). :664-669: `if (clampedDb <= kMinLevelDb) { voice.linearGain = 0.0f; } ... voice.levelSmoother.setTarget(voice.linearGain);`. :582-597: the fade only runs `if (newCount > numActiveVoices_ && numActiveVoices_ > 0)`, and a decrease just does `numActiveVoices_ = newCount;`. :547-555 `voiceCountScale = (audibleVoices > 1) ? 1.0f / std::sqrt(...) : 1.0f;` applied per sample at 561-562 with no smoothing. specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json F026 title quoted above.

<details><summary>Verifier notes</summary>

**Note 1.** Every code claim checks out against the source. The defect is real.

1. Muted voices are cut, not faded. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/harmonizer_engine.h, setVoiceLevel (657-670) sets linearGain = 0 when the clamped dB is at or below kMinLevelDb (-60, line 86). It then calls levelSmoother.setTarget(0). All three paths skip a voice whose linearGain == 0: PhaseVocoder at 243-246, 285 and 306; PitchSync at 383-386; Simple/Granular at 466-469. A skipped voice only gets advanceMutedVoiceSmoothers (789-797), which advances the smoothers but adds nothing to outputL/outputR. So in the first block after the level is stepped to -60 dB, the voice contributes nothing, even though its level smoother still holds the previous level (about 1.0 after a 0 dB to -60 dB step). The 5 ms ramp down is never heard. The smoother-freeze half of F026 is fixed (the helper is called in all three paths). The abrupt-cut half is not.

2. Lowering the voice count cuts voices instantly. setNumVoices (576-598) fades only when newCount > numActiveVoices_ && numActiveVoices_ > 0 (582). A decrease just runs numActiveVoices_ = newCount (597). Every loop is bounded by numActiveVoices_, so a removed voice stops at full level within one sample.

3. The compensation scale steps. voiceCountScale is computed per block from linearGain, which is the target, not the smoothed level (547-555). It is applied at 561-562 with no smoother. 4->3 voices moves it from 0.5 to 0.577 (+1.25 dB). 2->1 moves it from 0.707 to 1.0 (+3 dB).

4. Ruinae reaches this with nothing smoothing on top. processor_params.cpp:729 and :736-737 pass numVoices and voiceLevelDb straight to engine_.setHarmonizerNumVoices / setHarmonizerVoiceLevel. Those forward unchanged through ruinae_engine.h:719/723 and ruinae_effects_chain.h:772-774/786-788. Only enable/disable gets a crossfade (ruinae_effects_chain.h:738-754).

5. The finding correctly repeats F026 (specs/ruinae-audit/findings.json:203-208, harmonizer_engine.h:466, rated low).

Severity: I suggest downgrading to low, to match F026. The harmonizer is an optional effect. The muted-voice cut matters only when the level is stepped to exactly the -60 dB floor: automation that sweeps down reaches about 1e-3 gain before linearGain hits 0, so that cut is inaudible. The count-change click and the scale step are real, but they come only from discrete Voices changes or preset loads while sound is passing through the harmonizer.

**Note 2.** The code matches the finding. Two of its three parts are real defects. The "F026 only half fixed / regression" framing is wrong, because the mute-side cut was excluded on purpose.

What the code does (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/harmonizer_engine.h):
- setVoiceLevel (657-670): at clampedDb &lt;= kMinLevelDb it sets linearGain = 0, then levelSmoother.setTarget(0).
- All three paths skip a voice when linearGain == 0. PhaseVocoder: 243-246, 285, 306. PitchSync: 383-386. Standard: 466-469. They only advance the smoothers (advanceMutedVoiceSmoothers 789-797) and add nothing to the output. A step from 0 dB to -60 dB therefore drops the voice at whatever level the smoother holds, possibly 1.0.
- setNumVoices (576-598): the fade only runs when `newCount > numActiveVoices_ && numActiveVoices_ > 0`. A decrease just assigns `numActiveVoices_ = newCount`, so a removed voice stops within one sample at full level.
- voiceCountScale (547-555): counted from linearGain, the target rather than the smoothed level. It is applied per sample at 561-562 with no smoother. Going from 4 to 3 voices steps it 0.5 -> 0.577, and from 2 to 1 it steps 0.707 -> 1.0.

Why it is reachable in Ruinae:
- processor_params.cpp:729 and 736 forward numVoices and voiceLevelDb on every apply.
- They go through ruinae_engine.h:719/723 and ruinae_effects_chain.h:772-774 and 786-788 straight to the engine. The chain adds no crossfade on a voice-count change; its crossfade covers enable only (738-744, 1002-1005).
- No test in dsp/tests/unit/systems/harmonizer_engine_test.cpp covers lowering numVoices or a voiceCountScale step. Every setNumVoices call there is a setup call (1 or 2).

Context against the framing:
- Plan T5.2 (implementation-plan.md:909-923) scoped F026 to the unmute discontinuity. It says outright: "Do NOT: do NOT add a mute-side ramp -- the instant mute crosses -60 dB is already inaudible."
- So the remediation did what the plan asked. The mute-side cut is a documented design decision, not a half-done fix. Its rationale only holds for a continuous fader sweep to -60 dB, where the smoother is already near 1e-3, and not for a stepped preset or automation jump.
- The numVoices-decrease cut and the unsmoothed voiceCountScale step are not covered by F026 or by any comment or spec. They are new, real click sources.

Severity: lower it to low. That matches the original F026 rating, and the parts that survive are clicks on discrete user or preset changes to the harmonizer bus, not a sustained artifact. The "prior-audit-regression" category should become anti-pattern or click.

**Note 3.** I confirmed the defect from source. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/harmonizer_engine.h, setVoiceLevel (657-670) sets linearGain = 0 whenever clampedDb &lt;= kMinLevelDb (-60, line 86) and only then retargets the level smoother. All three paths skip a voice on linearGain == 0, at 243-246 (PV step 2), 285 and 306 (PV analysis and output, a plain `continue`), 383-386 (PitchSync) and 466-469 (Simple/Granular). advanceMutedVoiceSmoothers (789-797) only advances the smoothers and adds no audio, so the voice drops out of the sum at the block boundary at whatever level its smoother held. setNumVoices (576-598) fades only on an increase (`newCount > numActiveVoices_ && numActiveVoices_ > 0`). A decrease just stores numActiveVoices_ = newCount, so voices at or above the new count stop contributing in the next block at full level, with no fade-out. voiceCountScale (547-555) is recomputed each block from linearGain, the target rather than the smoothed level, and multiplied in per sample at 561-562 with no smoother. So 4->3 voices is 0.5 -> 0.577 (+1.25 dB), 2->1 is 0.707 -> 1.0 (+3.0 dB), and an increase steps the other voices down by the same amount even though the new voice fades in.
